000c7f50-ff95-5a24-b26f-2c2401107ffd.name: *Mosque of the Sultan, Cairo*
000c7f50-ff95-5a24-b26f-2c2401107ffd.dimensions: Height: 161 mm photograph, Width: 210 mm photograph
000c7f50-ff95-5a24-b26f-2c2401107ffd.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
000c7f50-ff95-5a24-b26f-2c2401107ffd.keywords: Albumen process; Grand Tour; Holy Land; Victorian; Egypt; travel; history of photography
000c7f50-ff95-5a24-b26f-2c2401107ffd.description2:
During the 1850s and 1860s, Francis Frith was one of England's most celebrated photographers. In September 1856, he set sail for Alexandria. This was the first of three trips that Frith would take to the Near East. The model was that of the 'Grand Tour'.  
Any analysis of Frith's work leads to the discourse of the tension between empirical knowledge and spiritual awareness in Victorian England. The photograph operated as a tool that could have moral influence upon those who viewed them with their ability to bring viewers to the locations of holy events.  
But even from a purely secular point of view, Frith's photographs become operators within an ideology specific to the era. Frith's thematic choices are manifest of the Victorians' tendency to regard themselves in relation to the larger history of mankind.

00c2f038-d775-56aa-a8e0-bba81f9f6642.name: Façade of the Palace of Mushatta
00c2f038-d775-56aa-a8e0-bba81f9f6642.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
00c2f038-d775-56aa-a8e0-bba81f9f6642.dates: AD 743–744; given by the Ottoman sultan ‘Abd al-Hamid II to Emperor Wilhelm II in 1903
00c2f038-d775-56aa-a8e0-bba81f9f6642.author: Stefan Weber
00c2f038-d775-56aa-a8e0-bba81f9f6642.second_name: Decorative entrance facade of the Umayyad caliphal palace
00c2f038-d775-56aa-a8e0-bba81f9f6642.description2: The Umayyad palace façade of Mushatta – gifted by Ottoman sultan `Abd al-Hamid II – is one of the key works of Islamic art and a prime example of shared heritage. The monument shows the origins of a cultural era rooting in the various local traditions of Late Antiquity and also its early development. It hence became seminal for the Islamic art department, whose very establishment by Wilhelm von Bode in 1904 is due to this gift.

00dfb034-7745-571e-9003-aff48bf346d0.name: Talismanic necklace
00dfb034-7745-571e-9003-aff48bf346d0.type: Amulet; cultic object; talismanic object; jewellery
00dfb034-7745-571e-9003-aff48bf346d0.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
00dfb034-7745-571e-9003-aff48bf346d0.author: Huda Kilani
00dfb034-7745-571e-9003-aff48bf346d0.keywords: Talisman; triangular; silver; pendant; Ottoman coins; heal of Gazalle; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics
00dfb034-7745-571e-9003-aff48bf346d0.description2: A triangular silver pendant decorated with small circles on the top and five blue beads with five silver Ottoman coins dangling at the end, and a silver chain known traditionally as “heal of gazelle”. Silver was the most common jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom.

01309821-1550-570d-b610-d7e90337db0f.name: Çırağan Palace
01309821-1550-570d-b610-d7e90337db0f.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; Pascal Sebah
01309821-1550-570d-b610-d7e90337db0f.description2: Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. In 1857 he opened his first photography studio in Istanbul. Çırağan Palace, built by Sultan Abdülâziz, was designed by the palace architect Nigoğayos Balyan and constructed by his sons Sarkis and Hagop Balyan between 1863 and 1867. This was a period in which all Ottoman sultans used to build their own palaces rather than using those of their ancestors. Çırağan Palace is the last example of this period. The inner walls and the roof were made of wood, the outer walls of colourful marble. The palace is connected with a beautiful marble bridge to the Yıldız Palace on the hill behind. A very high garden wall protects the palace from the outer world.

01436bcc-073d-529a-9751-7349d0fd45fc.name: Wooden Qur’an Stand
01436bcc-073d-529a-9751-7349d0fd45fc.type: Hardwood Qur'an Stand with bone and mother-of-pearl inlay
01436bcc-073d-529a-9751-7349d0fd45fc.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
01436bcc-073d-529a-9751-7349d0fd45fc.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
01436bcc-073d-529a-9751-7349d0fd45fc.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
01436bcc-073d-529a-9751-7349d0fd45fc.description2: Items like this Qur’an stand were popular props in Orientalist painting. On the inside, this hard wood Qur’an stand, which is inlaid with ebony, bone and mother-of-pearl, is decorated with two large square geometric panels, surrounded by a wide zig-zag border. The two squares are in turn subdivided into four small squares, filled with abstract star motifs. On the underside, the stand has two large geometric roundels. Two narrow, rectangular mashrabiyyah panels occupy the upper part of the feet. The remaining surfaces surrounding them are filled with chequerboard designs.

022636e4-0dfa-5ef8-9246-5b40c6f3adf2.name: Chest
022636e4-0dfa-5ef8-9246-5b40c6f3adf2.author: Houria Cherid
022636e4-0dfa-5ef8-9246-5b40c6f3adf2.archival: Marçai, G, *L'Exposition d'Art Musulman d'Alger*, April 1905
022636e4-0dfa-5ef8-9246-5b40c6f3adf2.description2: Bridal chest painted with gold paste on a coloured background, and a chiselled copper hinge.

02992f2b-3701-5bc3-ba32-d5f6226b56ef.name: Bowl (*Sakızlık*)
02992f2b-3701-5bc3-ba32-d5f6226b56ef.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
02992f2b-3701-5bc3-ba32-d5f6226b56ef.keywords: minor arts, applied arts, silver objects
02992f2b-3701-5bc3-ba32-d5f6226b56ef.description2: From historical sources, we learn that vessels made of gold and silver were widely used in the Ottoman palace. Starting from the end of the 18th century, Baroque and Rococo forms of Western style replaced classical Ottoman designs. We find roses in relief, the Ottoman coat-of-arms, architectural compositions, casted flowers, birds and animals on a multitude of the vessels of the era. This cylindrical cup with pedestal foot and cupola-like hinged lid was made of vermeil silver. On the body of the cup we see a floral pattern and hanging lambs placed alternatingly. Flowers, buds and leaves are made from rubies and diamonds nailed into gold and silver contours. On the lid – instead of lamb motif on the body – a chalice was used. The foot of the chalice is in the form of a cherub from which a bundle of rays projects.

02c575a0-6154-582b-a588-2ae094079d0d.name: *Calligrapher Rıfat Efendi*
02c575a0-6154-582b-a588-2ae094079d0d.description2: Feyhaman Duran was particularly interested in portrait painting and went to Paris in 1910 through the patronage of the Egyptian Prince Abbas Halim Pasha to further his studies in this genre. He greatly profited from the teaching of Paul Richet, professor of anatomy in the School of Fine Arts in Paris. He also attended the Julian Academy where he learned a great deal from Jean-Paul and Albert Laurens. In 1913-14 he worked in the Cormon studio in the School of Fine Arts. Although devoting most of his time to portrait painting, Feyhaman Duran also did paintings of flowers and nudes, but he was definitely most interested in the portrayal of people, and he had very little time for non-figurative painting.

03fa93d0-4ba6-5345-9362-3c66f5efb5d1.name: Necklace
03fa93d0-4ba6-5345-9362-3c66f5efb5d1.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
03fa93d0-4ba6-5345-9362-3c66f5efb5d1.keywords: zebra fish; concave; Ottoman; coins; silver
03fa93d0-4ba6-5345-9362-3c66f5efb5d1.description2: A zebra fish chain with a concave silver Turkish coins and two metal circles at the end to fix the necklace on the hat and dangle down the neck. Silver was the most common jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom. Jordan's economy relied on trade and crafts; new waves of people started to come to Jordan and began to settle for these purposes. This object reflects the diverse population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It also demonstrates personal attire, fashion, local costumes and rites.

04672ba4-7861-5eb6-ae9c-d793731c3fe9.name: Three drawings: *View of the Throne Salon at the Alcazar of Segovia*; *Kiosk* and *View of the Mudéjar Room at The Royal Convent of Las Huelgas (Burgos)*
04672ba4-7861-5eb6-ae9c-d793731c3fe9.description: These three drawings by Carderera, painter of the Queen Isabel II, illustrated the Mudéjar architecture. He travelled around Spain drawing and documenting the remains and monuments of the Spanish Muslim period and Mudéjar style. These designs had an important influence in the development in the Neo-Mudéjar style.
04672ba4-7861-5eb6-ae9c-d793731c3fe9.author: Ámparo López
04672ba4-7861-5eb6-ae9c-d793731c3fe9.keywords: Mudejar art; Neo-mudejar style; islamic influence; orientalism
04672ba4-7861-5eb6-ae9c-d793731c3fe9.materials: Drawing on paper; pen, watercolour, gouache
04672ba4-7861-5eb6-ae9c-d793731c3fe9.third_name: Tres dibujos: *Sala de Reyes del Alcázar de Segovia*; *Pabellón de las Huelgas de Burgos*; *Interior del monasterio de las Huelgas de Burgos*

04c6becd-fdd7-5c20-9596-b48f8a6ce25a.name: Traditional bridal costume and jewellery
04c6becd-fdd7-5c20-9596-b48f8a6ce25a.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
04c6becd-fdd7-5c20-9596-b48f8a6ce25a.keywords: Costume; accessories; headdress; fez; wedding; marriage
04c6becd-fdd7-5c20-9596-b48f8a6ce25a.description2: This set of traditional clothing gives an overall picture of the universally recognized aesthetics displayed in the festive women’s outfits in Macedonia in the 19th century. Bridal costumes worn in the area of Dolni Polog were distinctive for the great number of varied garments they comprised. The costume, consisting of a *fusta*, a kind of undershirt; a *bunda*, a thicker undergarment; chemise; tunic; vest and other garments, was abundantly decorated with embroidery. It was also richly embellished with jewellery and accessorized with distinctive headdress. Even the headdress included more than one article: a fez made of red baize, a hair band called a *votus* adorned with strings of coins as well as a transparent silk scarf decorated with embroidery, fringes and sequins.

04e56c00-ff8a-5334-9dea-eb0e9fc10644.name: *Kjustek* for men's watch
04e56c00-ff8a-5334-9dea-eb0e9fc10644.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
04e56c00-ff8a-5334-9dea-eb0e9fc10644.keywords: Men's jewellery; kjustek; metalwork; accessories; silver; filigree
04e56c00-ff8a-5334-9dea-eb0e9fc10644.second_name: Men's ornament worn on the chests
04e56c00-ff8a-5334-9dea-eb0e9fc10644.description2: Unlike the diversity of women’s jewellery, there was smaller number of articles of adornment used by men. Male jewellery was, however, rather massive, more precious and more costly in its production. Besides rings, especially impressive were massive silver *kjusteks* (watch chains), which were worn suspended on the chests. This *kjustek* is a nice piece of the jewellery worn by men, showing clearly some elements of Oriental influence. *Kjusteks* and other pieces of metal jewellery used to be worn by men in towns, whereas the jewellery of men in villages was mostly made of tiny beads (*monistra*).

057b0a91-5753-5a0f-a506-60b096d9eeb0.name: Saliha Sultan Fountain
057b0a91-5753-5a0f-a506-60b096d9eeb0.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
057b0a91-5753-5a0f-a506-60b096d9eeb0.description2: Robertson’s photographs of landscapes and monuments were usually printed in a roughly 25 by 30cm format. In the early years of his career as a photographer, he appears to have preferred the albumen-on-glass method of taking negatives, switching to the wet collodion process around 1855. For his positive prints, he used salt paper until about 1858; after that, prints were made on albumen paper even if they were made from negatives taken before that year. Robertson’s photographs are concentrated mainly in and around the districts known as Sultanahmet, Beyoğlu, Galata and Tophane today. This photo captures the Saliha Sultan Fountain in Galata.

057cb072-73f1-5597-b0c3-f4145e5d0880.name: *British Soldiers Near Selimiye Barracks in Scutari Waiting to be Dispatched to Crimea*
057cb072-73f1-5597-b0c3-f4145e5d0880.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
057cb072-73f1-5597-b0c3-f4145e5d0880.keywords: Crimean War; war photojounalism; British forces in Crimean War
057cb072-73f1-5597-b0c3-f4145e5d0880.description2: Robertson's photographs of the Crimean War represent an important chapter in his career. The Crimean War was the first war in history to be extensively covered by press correspondents. The photographs taken by James Robertson and Roger Fenton put them in the ranks of the world’s first war photojournalists. James Robertson’s first photographs related to the Crimean War were actually taken in Istanbul. After England’s declaration of war on 27 March 1854, British and colonial forces dispatched to the front by sea began gathering at Selimiye in Üsküdar and neighbouring districts in April and May.

072d1017-5755-51e9-a465-680b0053022c.name: Two cups
072d1017-5755-51e9-a465-680b0053022c.description: Two glass cups made by Lobmeyr in Oriental style.
072d1017-5755-51e9-a465-680b0053022c.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
072d1017-5755-51e9-a465-680b0053022c.artist: Design Johann Machytka & Franz Schmoranz für J&L Lobmeyr, Vienna
072d1017-5755-51e9-a465-680b0053022c.materials: Tansparent glass with coloured and gilded decoration

073cada1-b5a8-5fa6-bce4-4879f04d6814.name: Iznik jug
073cada1-b5a8-5fa6-bce4-4879f04d6814.author: Mina Moraitou
073cada1-b5a8-5fa6-bce4-4879f04d6814.keywords: Iznik; Egypt; Greeks; collecting; exhibition; dealer
073cada1-b5a8-5fa6-bce4-4879f04d6814.description2: An Iznik jug with one handle decorated with tulips and stems carrying small blue flowers. It was bought by Alexander Benaki in 1919 by the Cairo based dealer Boghos Ispenian whose name is handwritten in ink under the base, next to an etiquette indicating that it was part of the 1925 Alexandria exhibition.

077c68fe-2e6b-58e1-8e7b-c457e2fe3a33.name: Belt of *monistra* – tiny beads
077c68fe-2e6b-58e1-8e7b-c457e2fe3a33.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
077c68fe-2e6b-58e1-8e7b-c457e2fe3a33.keywords: Monistra – tiny beads in different colours; costume; accessories
077c68fe-2e6b-58e1-8e7b-c457e2fe3a33.description2: Unlike the metal jewellery worn in towns, which was produced by goldsmiths, jewellery and other articles of adornment from rural areas were made by women themselves, mostly of canvas, *monistra* (tiny beads in varied colours) and by use of the fruits of the nature, flowers, etc.

07fa4973-f69d-57f4-8e6d-caeb88f75252.name: Belt with buckles
07fa4973-f69d-57f4-8e6d-caeb88f75252.dimensions: Belt: 88 x 7.5 cm, buckles: 27 x 12 cm
07fa4973-f69d-57f4-8e6d-caeb88f75252.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
07fa4973-f69d-57f4-8e6d-caeb88f75252.materials: Cotton fabric, *srma* – silver and gold-wrapped thread, braids. Buckles: silver, hammering, decorative stones
07fa4973-f69d-57f4-8e6d-caeb88f75252.second_name: Articles of adornment worn at the waist – *pafti*
07fa4973-f69d-57f4-8e6d-caeb88f75252.description2: Buckles were the most prominent articles of adornment worn by Macedonian women. They were also the most frequently worn pieces of jewellery, having been an inevitable element of folk costumes in all parts of Macedonia. Combining functionality and aesthetics, buckles were also considered to play a protective role. The diverse shapes – round, rectangular, leaf-shaped, etc., as well as the exquisite style of their decorating, show the remarkable skill and talent of goldsmiths producing them. These buckles consist of two slightly concave round plates joined with a little round piece used for fastening. They are adorned with decorative stones and decorated with geometric patterns applied by hammering. The belt is made of cotton fabric decorated with geometric and floral patterns by application of silver and gold-wrapped thread and braids.

08d3aed6-3599-5046-816b-66df7858d6a8.name: *The Sultan’s Horses* (Drawing 19 for the *XX Dessins* album)
08d3aed6-3599-5046-816b-66df7858d6a8.description: This drawing by Amadeo de Souza-Cardoso forms part of an album, *XX Dessins*, which was published in 1912 and represents a key point of breakthrough for the artist. The context of the work can be explained by his interest in the Western primitivists, the influence of African art, the experiences that he exchanged with Brancusi and Modigliani, and his study of Henri Rousseau’s work. The artist aims to present a demarcated image of his own identity: in an elegantly sophisticated picture replete with medieval imagery, he produces an original work that explores volumes, dynamic forms, and the sense of speed. It was this clearly defined image that Amadeo presented at the Armory Show in 1913, where his work achieved great success in both critical and market terms.
08d3aed6-3599-5046-816b-66df7858d6a8.holder: Modern Art Centre, Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation

08d3aed6-3599-5046-816b-66df7858d6a8.keywords: Amadeo Sousa Cardoso; breaks; avant-garde; medieval; primitivists; african art
08d3aed6-3599-5046-816b-66df7858d6a8.holding_institution_org: Centro de Arte Moderna, Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian

09551850-4b0e-5e89-a902-5605adcd0825.name: Ring
09551850-4b0e-5e89-a902-5605adcd0825.description: A ring made in Fez in the 19th century. Its style, an elaborate floral design in gold set with three emeralds, reveals a European influence.
09551850-4b0e-5e89-a902-5605adcd0825.keywords: Applied arts; precious stones; inscription; floral decoration; floral motifs; vegetal motifs; vegetal decoration; craftsmanship; traditional craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmen; European influence; fashion

097719cc-6187-5302-96cc-c309d799ec93.name: Parapet well
097719cc-6187-5302-96cc-c309d799ec93.author: Ámparo López
097719cc-6187-5302-96cc-c309d799ec93.keywords: Nasrid art; islamic influence; orientalism; collectionism
097719cc-6187-5302-96cc-c309d799ec93.description2: This parapet could be from Granada. It could be the only example from the Nasrid period. It has an inscription with the Nasrid motto: "Only God wins".

0a232d6e-3ce2-5412-be8a-b9cb0af2bff7.name: Tile
0a232d6e-3ce2-5412-be8a-b9cb0af2bff7.description2: Kütahya was the second most important ceramic production centre after İznik due to the rich clay deposits in the area. Although there was a decline in ceramic production at the beginning of the 19th century, in the last quarter of that same century production was revived and new designs inspired by İznik ceramics were produced.

0a489e52-7566-5a35-a21d-e7338d8cc6b4.name: Jar with enamel decoration
0a489e52-7566-5a35-a21d-e7338d8cc6b4.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
0a489e52-7566-5a35-a21d-e7338d8cc6b4.author: Marina Minozzi
0a489e52-7566-5a35-a21d-e7338d8cc6b4.keywords: Applied arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; motifs; collection; collector; glasswork; Murano; Islamic art; production of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode; minor arts; enamelling
0a489e52-7566-5a35-a21d-e7338d8cc6b4.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century and as a training school for specializing artisans. The idea was part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history passed down from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic traditions in the Middle Ages. In the 19th century there was also a rebirth of the Murano glass for different reasons. The jar with enamelled decorations, white flowers and green leaves was made in Murano and dates from the beginning of the 20th century. It shows evolution of forms and techniques through the new ideas coming from Art Nouveau and the diffusion of polychrome enamels.
0a489e52-7566-5a35-a21d-e7338d8cc6b4.holding_institution_org: Museo Artistico Industriale presso la Galleria nazionale d’arte antica in Palazzo Barberini

0ba121fb-d876-5f66-b258-176f999c7959.name: *Seated Moor*
0ba121fb-d876-5f66-b258-176f999c7959.description: This small oil painting was painted in Valencia in a very early date (1880–1884) and is an example of Sorolla’s early works, when he still painted small pieces that follow the taste of the time. This Orientalist topic was very popular in Europe at the end of the century and the paintings sold very well. The inspiration was not from travel or cultural knowledge, but instead was the result of studying engravings, watercolours, and other paintings of the time. The production of this type of topic in Sorolla is very short and almost all of it dates to his early years.
0ba121fb-d876-5f66-b258-176f999c7959.author: Covadonga Pitarch
0ba121fb-d876-5f66-b258-176f999c7959.keywords: Orientalist painting; Spain; Formation of painters

0ba2e663-9318-562e-9c2a-099d167e8112.name: Earrings
0ba2e663-9318-562e-9c2a-099d167e8112.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
0ba2e663-9318-562e-9c2a-099d167e8112.author: Huda Kilani
0ba2e663-9318-562e-9c2a-099d167e8112.keywords: 23 karat gold; rosettes; coral; Ottoman coins
0ba2e663-9318-562e-9c2a-099d167e8112.description2: 23-karat gold earrings from South Palestine (Beer Sheba), with red stones, blue talismans mounted on rosettes of coral, and gold Ottoman coins (dated 1808). Silver jewellery was the most common because only rich people could afford gold jewellery. Silver or gold jewellery was part of the dowry given by the groom to the bride. The material (gold or silver) and even the coins used as pieces of jewellery were an indirect statement of the financial status of the groom.

0c62c358-069e-5101-ad0e-063173c5eefc.name: Chair
0c62c358-069e-5101-ad0e-063173c5eefc.description: This chair, known as *jamuga* in the Spanish tradition, is most certainly a Moresque European piece designed from a combination of pattern books. The chair consists of a great widely decorated back and a curved seat with two arms. The four legs are delicately ornamented. The inscriptions probably have been taken from a design book or other visual model too, rather than being designed by an Arab master calligrapher. The decorated panels, aesthetically pleasing, are imprecise in terms of execution and calligraphic style.
0c62c358-069e-5101-ad0e-063173c5eefc.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes, Cristina Giménez
0c62c358-069e-5101-ad0e-063173c5eefc.keywords: Production of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode; Orientalism

0c74ae54-ebaf-5ed2-bc1e-2921c31f8219.description: Illustration from the book edited by C. Lützow: *Kunst und Kunstgewerbe auf der Wiener Weltausstellung 1873*, 1875, S 101.
0c74ae54-ebaf-5ed2-bc1e-2921c31f8219.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

0da75e4a-673b-56b3-9555-3d8c859156b3.name: Glass hookah base
0da75e4a-673b-56b3-9555-3d8c859156b3.description2: Glass produced in Bohemia with a strong Middle Eastern influence. Acquired by Franks.

0db4a4c1-61f8-578b-9b95-99cacaf89afb.name: Astrolabe
0db4a4c1-61f8-578b-9b95-99cacaf89afb.keywords: Franks; scientific object; astronomy; astrology; science; constellation; zodiac

0dda7d39-b57f-5849-bcea-6897a0d0d4be.name: Amulet
0dda7d39-b57f-5849-bcea-6897a0d0d4be.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
0dda7d39-b57f-5849-bcea-6897a0d0d4be.description2: Throughout the 19th century in Macedonia, jewellery was not used only for adornment; it also served an apotropaic function. People used to wear various kinds of reliquaries for the purpose of personal protection from evil spirits. These protective items used to be worn in pockets or sewn to the garment. This amulet is made of silver using the techniques of hammering and engraving. The rectangular plate depicts the Virgin and Child flanked by two angels above them. The rings on the sides show that the amulet must have been worn suspended on a chain.

0e7a0149-6b93-507e-b4df-dc55cdc5bd9f.name: Iron coffee roasting spoon
0e7a0149-6b93-507e-b4df-dc55cdc5bd9f.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
0e7a0149-6b93-507e-b4df-dc55cdc5bd9f.author: Huda Kilani
0e7a0149-6b93-507e-b4df-dc55cdc5bd9f.keywords: coffee; coffee roasting; coffee beans; domestic furnishing; domestic vessels
0e7a0149-6b93-507e-b4df-dc55cdc5bd9f.description2: Iron coffee roasting spoon used to turn coffee beans while roasting them. Coffee-drinking in a communal setting is an essential part of traditions in Bedouin communities to celebrate or mourn.

0eb45a82-3f02-52db-8222-86625075ccdf.name: Bridal coat (*Klashenik*)
0eb45a82-3f02-52db-8222-86625075ccdf.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
0eb45a82-3f02-52db-8222-86625075ccdf.keywords: klashenik; broad cloth; textile; embroidery; geometric patterns; geometric motifs; costume; wedding; marriage
0eb45a82-3f02-52db-8222-86625075ccdf.materials: Thick woollen fabric, twill-weave, embroidery with *srma* and decoration with wool braids
0eb45a82-3f02-52db-8222-86625075ccdf.description2: A *klashenik* is a kind of over-garment women used to wear in winter. It is split in the front and made of thick woollen broadcloth called *klashna*. This piece is long to the hips. It is adorned with red braids along the hems. It is also decorated with embroidery of geometric patterns on the sleeves and at the breasts. Every ethnic area in Macedonia had distinct style of traditional costume, yet all of them show undeniable influence of Oriental art.

0f8914a6-32b8-5c6c-8562-d748aa45552b.name: *Fountain of Sultan Ahmed III*
0f8914a6-32b8-5c6c-8562-d748aa45552b.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
0f8914a6-32b8-5c6c-8562-d748aa45552b.description2: Although essentially a realist painter, Şevket Dağ worked with free brush stokes in the style of Corot. He is celebrated for his paintings of the interiors of mosques. He took lessons from Osman Hamdi Bey, and followed his master in painting genre pictures reflecting various aspects of Ottoman life. In addition to mosque interiors he would also paint scenes in market places, still-life compositions and the interiors of houses. Over time, Şevket Dağ's work began to be appreciated abroad following exhibitions in European art centres such as Munich and Paris, and he was awarded a gold medal in the Munich International Exhibition of 1909. He later came under the influence of the impressionists.

0fca5a3a-17d8-542b-bada-abe14d89b5ed.name: Carved wooden chest
0fca5a3a-17d8-542b-bada-abe14d89b5ed.description: A carved wooden chest with painted geometric and floral decoration, it illustrates the decorative styles that began to appear in the 19th century and also how industrial colours, imported from Europe, were being used.
0fca5a3a-17d8-542b-bada-abe14d89b5ed.keywords: Craftsmanship; traditional craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmen; woodwork; carving; trade; raw material; industrial colours; geometric decoration; floral decoration; geometric motifs; floral motifs; vegetal decoration; vegetal motifs; furniture

109ed34a-507a-5652-bb30-736569eca0ac.name: Drum
109ed34a-507a-5652-bb30-736569eca0ac.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
109ed34a-507a-5652-bb30-736569eca0ac.author: Huda Kilani
109ed34a-507a-5652-bb30-736569eca0ac.keywords: drum; animals skin; linen rope; wooden stick; Ramadan; to wake up
109ed34a-507a-5652-bb30-736569eca0ac.description2: Small round drum, pointed on the bottom, covered on the top with leather, and fastened with a linen rope. It was played with a wooden stick to create special sounds of music, and it was used during the Muslim holy month of Ramadan to wake up people to eat (*suhur*) before sunrise. Some people used to volunteer to go around before dawn to wake people up during Holy Ramadan, reflecting community spirit.

11568132-d5af-54cf-9a3f-f663abfb4f5b.name: Winter jacket
11568132-d5af-54cf-9a3f-f663abfb4f5b.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
11568132-d5af-54cf-9a3f-f663abfb4f5b.author: Huda Kilani
11568132-d5af-54cf-9a3f-f663abfb4f5b.materials: Wool, cotton and silk; hand weaving and hand embroidered
11568132-d5af-54cf-9a3f-f663abfb4f5b.description2: Sleeveless jacket made of woollen fabric of red and black stripes, decorated with floral motifs of orange and purple colour with couching in silk threads on the shoulders and the bottom. This object illustrates the variegated population composition of the Jordanian territory in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, influenced by the local economy. The main activities were trade and crafts that influenced population movements and the coexistence of various local and foreign communities.

1182b4e7-198f-51a0-b819-4ec5360c27f8.name: Casket
1182b4e7-198f-51a0-b819-4ec5360c27f8.description: This casket was displayed in the exhibition about Islamic Art held in Munich in 1910. Afterwards it was acquired by Lázaro Galdiano, one of the most important Spanish art collectors. It is important to note Lazaro Galdiano's interest in and art appraisal of objects from the Spanish Muslim period. He was one of the earliest collectors of Arab art in Spain.
1182b4e7-198f-51a0-b819-4ec5360c27f8.dates: 1100–1199; exhibited in 1910 and then acquired by Lázaro Galdiano
1182b4e7-198f-51a0-b819-4ec5360c27f8.author: Ámparo López
1182b4e7-198f-51a0-b819-4ec5360c27f8.materials: Ivory, wood and copper; gilded, painted, carved

123030ca-d6ea-5a9d-b948-0601ad74e192.name: Dish (*ghtar*)
123030ca-d6ea-5a9d-b948-0601ad74e192.description: Glazed, blue, terracotta dish, dated 1894 and made in Fez.
123030ca-d6ea-5a9d-b948-0601ad74e192.keywords: Applied arts; craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmanship; kitchen ware; domestic ware; terracotta; earthenware; bleau de Fez; glaze; floral decoration; floral motifs; vegetal decoration; vegetal motifs

13a6be55-80b1-576f-be99-bfc3e15b7c3f.name: *Casket from San Isidoro of León*
13a6be55-80b1-576f-be99-bfc3e15b7c3f.description: This casket was donated by the Dean of Leon Cathedral to the National Museum of Archaeology in 1869. It was part of the Cathedral Treasury and it is an example of the importance of Arab workshops in the Iberian Peninsula in Middle Ages.
13a6be55-80b1-576f-be99-bfc3e15b7c3f.artist: Drawing by José María Casado del Alisal; lithograph: A. Fortuny; chromolithograph: Eusebio de Lettre and Teo Rufflén
13a6be55-80b1-576f-be99-bfc3e15b7c3f.third_name: *Arqueta de San Isidoro de León (Estilos persoarábigo)*

147b289f-3d6e-58be-8aa0-db105cfb150f.name: *National Museum of Archaeology No. 9 (Arab Courtyard) Monuments and Epigraphy of Islamic Spain*
147b289f-3d6e-58be-8aa0-db105cfb150f.description: View of the courtyard in the National Museum of Archaeology, also known as "Arab courtyard", between 1917-1936. This room displayed different pieces such as the Alfajería arch, a copy of the fountain of the Lions and the bronze lamp from the Alhambra palace. This room was one of the first museum galleries focusing on Arab or Islamic pieces in Europe.
147b289f-3d6e-58be-8aa0-db105cfb150f.artist: FOTOTIPIA DE HAUSER Y MENET.- MADRID
147b289f-3d6e-58be-8aa0-db105cfb150f.keywords: Museums; Spanish Muslim art and Archaoelogy; Madrid
147b289f-3d6e-58be-8aa0-db105cfb150f.third_name: *Museo Arqueológico Nacional de Madrid N.º 9. (Patio árabe) Arte monumental y Epigrafia hispanomahometanos*

159f7828-e467-5f3d-b3ba-96aafc6f5b7c.name: Postcard: *Colonial Exhibition 1907, Tuareg caravan*
159f7828-e467-5f3d-b3ba-96aafc6f5b7c.description:
This postcard (not franked or used) is part of a collection donated by the anthropologist Manuel Antón.  
During the second half of the nineteenth century in Europe and America there were held countless ethnological and colonial exhibitions that showed groups of individuals from distant exotic territories, to make them public and available to anthropologists and scholars. They were put on show alongside exotic animals and recreations of the structures inhabited by these people in their places of origin.  
These exhibitions were a result of the intensification of colonial imperialism of the West and also the relative popularity of two young scientific disciplines (physical anthropology and ethnology) and the development of new and intense forms of consumerism among the European bourgeoisie. Actually these exhibitions got to transmit a sense of lower and "savage" status of the colonised people (Sánchez Gómez, L. “Espectáculos demasiado humanos”, 2008, 88-89).

16c4b489-744b-54ba-b2f9-e9d429647ac5.name: Bracelet in French Egyptian Revival style
16c4b489-744b-54ba-b2f9-e9d429647ac5.author: Marina Minozzi
16c4b489-744b-54ba-b2f9-e9d429647ac5.keywords: Revivalism; Egyptomania; Egyptian motifs; applied arts; jewellery; exploration; archaeology; excavation; scientific expedition; Campaign in Egypt; Campaign in Syria; Enlightenment; science; technique; Egyptology; Orientalism; travel; botany; epigraphy
16c4b489-744b-54ba-b2f9-e9d429647ac5.description2: This bracelet, owned by Princess Paolina Bonaparte (1780–1825), wife of Camillo Borghese, was made by one of the most famous goldsmiths in Paris, Jean Baptiste Claude Odiot, as identified by the trademark on the safety lock of the bracelet. The elegant Egyptian decoration made by hieroglyphics and triangles alternating with little palms is inspired to the book *Voyage dans le Basse et Haute Égypte*, written by Dominique Vivant Denon (1745–1825) during Napoleon’s campaign along the Nile river in 1798 and published between 1802 and 1810. The ancient Egyptian fashion, popular in Italy since the second half of the 18th century, influenced furniture design and works of art following publication of Denon’s book, which popularized a “retour d’Egypte”.

en: Costamagna, A., *La raffinatezza e il lusso: lo "stile" Borghese dal cardinale Scipione ai principi Camillo e Paolina in quattro piccoli "tesori" artistici*, Rome: Galleria Borghese, 2005: 23–27.

174a686d-d71c-5900-ac66-c2dba02914eb.name: Jug
174a686d-d71c-5900-ac66-c2dba02914eb.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
174a686d-d71c-5900-ac66-c2dba02914eb.description2: It is known that there were workshops producing glass vessels around Beykoz in Istanbul in the 19th century. The first glass workshop was founded by Mevlevi Dervish Mehmed Dede during the reign of Selim III (1789–1807). There were European glass craftsmen working in those workshops as well. Cups, bottles, jugs etc. made of colourful, colourless and opal glass were among Beykoz's productions. *Çeşm-i bulbul* is the name of the technique used to make this glass jug. In this technique, the glass bars are immerged into transparent glass. On the body of the jug we see spirally placed opaque white, opaque purple and blue glass bars immerged into colourless ground. It is of pear-shaped with a short neck and a lid. The handle was attached later. The lid handle is in the shape of a *Mevlevi sikke* (Mevlevi Sufi headwear).

176c309e-be45-54b8-81a1-917857d46338.name: Textile
176c309e-be45-54b8-81a1-917857d46338.description: This textile was displayed in the exhibition about Islamic Art held in Munich in 1910, as part of the Miquel i Badia collection. Afterwards it was acquired by Lázaro Galdiano, one of the most important Spanish art collectors. It is important to note Lazaro Galdiano's interest in and art appraisal of objects from the Spanish Muslim period. He was one of the earliest collectors of Arab art in Spain. The decoration is similar to the Golden Room of the Alhambra palace and it could be the Mohammad V period.
176c309e-be45-54b8-81a1-917857d46338.author: Ámparo López
176c309e-be45-54b8-81a1-917857d46338.keywords: Nasrid art; islamic influence; orientalism; collectionism
176c309e-be45-54b8-81a1-917857d46338.materials: Silk and metallic threads; lampas weave

178d2db5-fbc1-5e5a-8ce8-245dc22c7cea.name: Arabian *bisht*
178d2db5-fbc1-5e5a-8ce8-245dc22c7cea.description2: Arabian *bisht* made from black cloth and gold thread.

17a114d9-989f-52a9-85d5-689485ba21f6.name: Icon *The Holy Seven Slav Teachers*
17a114d9-989f-52a9-85d5-689485ba21f6.author: Viktorija Popovska Korobar, art historian
17a114d9-989f-52a9-85d5-689485ba21f6.description2: This icon represents icon-painting in Macedonia in the 19th century. This painted variant of the motif of the seven Slav teachers was enriched by Dimitar Dicho Zograf with the romantic awareness of the Macedonian Revival. The style of the most popular and most productive Macedonian painter in the 19th century follows the experience of the painters from that period. It was commissioned by the Robev family for the church of St. Nicholas Gerakomia in Ohrid. It was painted on wood with oil. It represents the Slav missionaries Ss. Cyril and Methodius and their most prominent disciples Clement, Nahum, Gorazd, Sabbas and Angelariy, in a sole composition entitled as “Sedmochislenitzi” (The Seven Holy Teachers). The saints' names are inscribed in the Old Church Slavonic language.

17a2df03-43c9-5803-92e9-9cff69d81432.name: Mosque lamp
17a2df03-43c9-5803-92e9-9cff69d81432.keywords: Orientalism; Mamluk Revival; trade; calligraphy; inscription; glass; furniture; decorative arts
17a2df03-43c9-5803-92e9-9cff69d81432.description2: ‘Mosque lamp’ reproducing well known examples from the Middle East. Produced by Philippe-Joseph Brocard, Faubourg Saint-Honoré. Brocard was inspired by his collection of Mamluk glass.

17e0e95e-14d7-5aeb-b21f-b18091757a69.name: *Mr. Byzantoine et son ex-libris*, by the Greek cartonist Kem
17e0e95e-14d7-5aeb-b21f-b18091757a69.author: Mina Moraitou
17e0e95e-14d7-5aeb-b21f-b18091757a69.description2: Antonis Benakis in Byzantine dress holds his ex-libris and golf clubs, with his dog Mangas and his boat at his feet; on the right, the Russian painter I. Bilibin, below, K. Synadinos, and, top left, ceramics glued together, probably from sherds. Kem’s drawing is a satire on the artistic and athletic interests of Benaki, in the style of Bilibin’s illustrations to Russian legends, for example *The Tale of the Tzar Saltan* (1905).

184eef10-6e1e-5cd3-9d3c-79a146221593.name: Amelia del Valle y Serrano
184eef10-6e1e-5cd3-9d3c-79a146221593.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo (politician, historian, and collector of art and antiques) and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This albumen portrait of Amelia del Valle y Serrano is delicate and quiet, with outstanding deep chocolate colour which reveals the quality of the photographic technique and the good condition of the object.
184eef10-6e1e-5cd3-9d3c-79a146221593.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes

185ba5fa-c953-5b73-a895-436fd368117e.name: Ottoman Clothing Album
185ba5fa-c953-5b73-a895-436fd368117e.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
185ba5fa-c953-5b73-a895-436fd368117e.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
185ba5fa-c953-5b73-a895-436fd368117e.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
185ba5fa-c953-5b73-a895-436fd368117e.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

18e02623-b9ad-5163-8ba9-d958a15a6f01.name: Dagger
18e02623-b9ad-5163-8ba9-d958a15a6f01.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
18e02623-b9ad-5163-8ba9-d958a15a6f01.dimensions: Length without sheath 28 cm, sheath length 19.5 cm
18e02623-b9ad-5163-8ba9-d958a15a6f01.author: Huda Kilani
18e02623-b9ad-5163-8ba9-d958a15a6f01.keywords: Thin silver; Hammering; sheath; geometric motifs; turquoise; arms; armours; metalwork; fashion; accessories
18e02623-b9ad-5163-8ba9-d958a15a6f01.materials: Thin silver, wood, metal; casting handmade
18e02623-b9ad-5163-8ba9-d958a15a6f01.description2: Wooden handled dagger with thin silver sheath; incurved geometric designs on the obverse side; inset with turquoise and black stones. The dagger was used by both Bedouins and villagers as part of men’s traditional garb. This object reflects the diverse population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It also demonstrates personal attire, fashion, local costumes and rites.

19148556-ea6b-5b21-8cbd-bc83909a1343.name: Binding/Book cover
19148556-ea6b-5b21-8cbd-bc83909a1343.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
19148556-ea6b-5b21-8cbd-bc83909a1343.description2: Arabian leather binding bought for the Museum of Applied Arts in Vienna.

1aa20f81-288f-5491-bfba-4d0a1e219f27.name: Qur’an
1aa20f81-288f-5491-bfba-4d0a1e219f27.holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts
1aa20f81-288f-5491-bfba-4d0a1e219f27.keywords: Floral decoration; religious objects; waqf; Qur’an; Turkish Baroque-Rococo
1aa20f81-288f-5491-bfba-4d0a1e219f27.description2: Illumination is a natural part of Qur'ans. Illuminators used naturalistic floral motifs influenced by Europe alongside classical elements to illuminate the Qur'ans during the AH 12th–13th / AD 18th–19th centuries.

1b1e3ef8-5e29-5178-ac83-8c4cb0d8ce8c.name: Invitation from Egyptian Sultan Fuad I to Joaquín Sorolla
1b1e3ef8-5e29-5178-ac83-8c4cb0d8ce8c.description: Sultan Fuad I’s letter was sent to Sorolla by Garcia Herreros. It is an invitation to spend one year with his family in the palaces of Cairo, where the painter could reside and work freely. All this is part of the artistic policy that was intended to attract well-known Western artists to the Egyptian sultan's court. Unfortunately, Sorolla was never able to take this trip, but from a letter to his wife we know the excitement that was caused by the idea of spending time in Egypt.
1b1e3ef8-5e29-5178-ac83-8c4cb0d8ce8c.author: Covadonga Pitarch
1b1e3ef8-5e29-5178-ac83-8c4cb0d8ce8c.third_name: Carta del Sultán de Egipto Fyad I

1b350001-5006-5f24-bc12-29f7589319af.name: *Country West of Algiers from the British Consul General's Garden*
1b350001-5006-5f24-bc12-29f7589319af.author: Houria Cherid
1b350001-5006-5f24-bc12-29f7589319af.third_name: *Country West of Algiers from the British Consul General's Garden*
1b350001-5006-5f24-bc12-29f7589319af.description2: A lithograph depicting the countryside to the west of Algiers, as seen from the garden of the British General Consul's garden.

1c205c93-bc85-56c7-bb96-3f280389af94.name: *Comares Courtyard at the Alhambra*
1c205c93-bc85-56c7-bb96-3f280389af94.description: The monument of the Alhambra, the last palace of the kingdom of Granada, fascinated travellers to Spain during the nineteenth century. Sorolla saw it for the first time in 1902 and in his successive trips to Granada during 1909, 1910 and 1917 he painted it, away from the Orientalist clichés, focusing on its corners, and especially in its gardens and fountains. In this view of the Patio de Comares, he highlights the reflection of the arches over the pond and a set of mirrors that is repeated in successive rooms of the palace.
1c205c93-bc85-56c7-bb96-3f280389af94.author: Covadonga Pitarch
1c205c93-bc85-56c7-bb96-3f280389af94.third_name: *El Patio de Comares, la Alhambra de Granada*

1c7eb8dd-c27a-55e4-b4bd-256860c07387.name: Types of Cairo
1c7eb8dd-c27a-55e4-b4bd-256860c07387.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
1c7eb8dd-c27a-55e4-b4bd-256860c07387.author: Vito Lattanzi, Marina Minozzi
1c7eb8dd-c27a-55e4-b4bd-256860c07387.keywords: Woman; photograph; anthropology; ethnology; geography; travel; exploration; scientific expedition; ethnography; museums; model; genre picture; portrait; representation of the other; costume; material culture; collection; Egypt
1c7eb8dd-c27a-55e4-b4bd-256860c07387.description2: The historical photos, belonging to Enrico H. Giglioli's collection, were collected by the Florentine naturalist during his travel around the world in 1865–68 on the Magenta's steam corvette, with the purpose to start diplomatic and commercial relations. The "genre" images seem to be created "ad hoc" to represent human diversity along the different ages. The ethnographic photographs in the Giglioli's collection are part of the historical archive of the Pigorini Museum, and are very important for the history of anthropological science and history of photography. The origins in terms of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

1ca4ae5b-e753-59d1-a5de-423460efb5d1.name: Iconostasis in the Church of the Holy Saviour
1ca4ae5b-e753-59d1-a5de-423460efb5d1.type: Work of art executed in wood-carving; iconostasis
1ca4ae5b-e753-59d1-a5de-423460efb5d1.holder: The Church of the Holy Saviour
1ca4ae5b-e753-59d1-a5de-423460efb5d1.author: Nada Andonovska
1ca4ae5b-e753-59d1-a5de-423460efb5d1.artist: Petre Filipovski Garkata and his group of artisans from village Gari near Debar
1ca4ae5b-e753-59d1-a5de-423460efb5d1.description2: This iconostasis was created by one of the greatest Macedonian masters of woodcarving, Petre Filipovski Garka, who formed his own group of artisans and developed his outstanding style of wood-carving, which was widely recognizable in the Balkans in the early 19th century. This exquisite piece of wood-carving was made from walnut in the technique of high relief. The iconostasis depicts scenes from the Old and the New Testament in which biblical figures are rendered wearing traditional costumes worn in Macedonia. The detail shows the self-portraits of Petre Filipovski and his associate artisans.

1caa0741-193b-5ce9-9a9c-423846c3eeff.name: Small bucket
1caa0741-193b-5ce9-9a9c-423846c3eeff.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
1caa0741-193b-5ce9-9a9c-423846c3eeff.author: Marina Minozzi
1caa0741-193b-5ce9-9a9c-423846c3eeff.keywords: Applied arts; minor arts; manufacture;  craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; decoration; motifs; collection; collector; glass; Murano glass; glasswork; gold leaf; cobalt-blue; crystal; zoomophysm; zoomorphic; eastern influence
1caa0741-193b-5ce9-9a9c-423846c3eeff.description2: M.A.I. was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. The small bucket in glass cobalt-blue is decorated with crystal animal-shaped applications and gold leaves recalling ancient eastern motifs. The object was made according to the 18th century taste and recalls 15th century models of aspersoriums, or holy water basins, from Venice dating from the 16th and 17th centuries. These objects were depicted in paintings by Veronese and Carpaccio.
1caa0741-193b-5ce9-9a9c-423846c3eeff.holding_institution_org: Museo Artistico Industriale presso la Galleria nazionale d’arte antica in Palazzo Barberini

en: Zaccagnini, M., *Arti decorative: Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini*, Rome: L'Erma di Bretschneider, 2011: 23.

1deb708b-ab5d-5f99-8702-421204b044cf.name: Berber woman (Nailiya) lying down
1deb708b-ab5d-5f99-8702-421204b044cf.description: The image depicts a Nailiya, a woman of the Berber tribe of the Ouled Naïl, in the south of Algeria. She is lying on her side like an odalisque, wearing a colourful silk dress and the rich jewels used to perform their traditional dance. The Nailiyat were independent women, free to marry men of their choosing. They moved to the cities in the North to earn money as dancers, in order to maintain their families in their community of origin. All this was not fully understood by Europeans. With the emergence of sex-tourism these women were forced to introduce sexual content in their originally hieratic performance, and finally they were even considered as prostitutes by the French administration, which in turn led to them being repudiated in their villages. Early photography contributed to forge this image of the Nailiyat in the European imagination.

1f016872-92d0-54fb-b596-c44b25a26d1a.name: Plate
1f016872-92d0-54fb-b596-c44b25a26d1a.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
1f016872-92d0-54fb-b596-c44b25a26d1a.description2: Kütahya was the second most important ceramic production centre after İznik due to the rich clay deposits in the area. This plate has flat rim, is slightly deep in body and has a circular bottom. It was made of white clay and coated in white on which there are patterns in cobalt blue, yellow, turquoise, purple and red covered with transparent glaze. In the middle of the plate there is an Ottoman coat-of-arms while both sides of the plate are decorated with curtains. Above the coat-of-arms, “Long Live My Sultan” is written in Turkish in Arabic letters forming a crescent and there is a *tuğra* (monogram) of Abdülhamid II (1876-1909) in the middle of the sun covering both the *tuğra* and the crescent.

1f14a324-c1e9-5296-b0e9-2ac16800da16.name: Old wooden slippers
1f14a324-c1e9-5296-b0e9-2ac16800da16.description2: Slippers made out of wood that was usually worn for comfort.

1fb1726f-8870-520a-9b34-30b69dacfc97.name: *The Encyclopaedia of Islam*, edited by M. Th. Houtsma (and others)
1fb1726f-8870-520a-9b34-30b69dacfc97.author: Mina Moraitou
1fb1726f-8870-520a-9b34-30b69dacfc97.description2: The first of four volumes of the *Encyclopaedia of Islam*, a dictionary of the georgraphy, ethnography and biography of the Muhammadan peoples by Th. Houtsma and others. It was published by Brill in Leiden and Lyuzac in London. It contains the ex libris of Antonis Benakis.

1fc5fe5c-fbfa-5316-9126-a887d85076f6.name: *Description de l'Arménie la Perse*
1fc5fe5c-fbfa-5316-9126-a887d85076f6.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Félix Marie Charles Texier was a French historian, architect and archaeologist. Texier published a number of significant works involving personal travels throughout Asia Minor and the Middle East. These books included descriptions and maps of ancient sites, reports of regional geography and geology and descriptions of artwork and architecture.

1fe23b95-31f5-5b9a-b2ab-2854193671c7.name: *The Outcast*
1fe23b95-31f5-5b9a-b2ab-2854193671c7.author: DGPC
1fe23b95-31f5-5b9a-b2ab-2854193671c7.description2: This sculpture by António Soares dos Reis was made in Italy and it rapidly became an icon of romanticism, as it symbolises a young man who has been forced into exile.  The classic contours of the human body, the position of the model and the remarkable sculpture led to the recognition of the author as one of Portugal’s main exponents of sculpture and this piece a National Treasure.
1fe23b95-31f5-5b9a-b2ab-2854193671c7.holding_institution_org: Museu Nacional de Soares dos Reis

1fe2bf0f-28b8-574f-bc6b-664e988fdf29.name: Pitcher
1fe2bf0f-28b8-574f-bc6b-664e988fdf29.description2: Çanakkale was a pottery production centre between the end of 17th century and first quarter of the 20th century where pottery with interesting and original forms was produced. Mostly coarse red clay and occasionally beige-coloured paste was used. This jug with a pear-shaped body and long neck has green, brown, dark yellow, under-glazed purplish brown, dark blue and white decorations made by a brush. In front there is a single raised pattern of a flower. On either side there are painted flowers.

204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.name: A Druse Bride from Lebanon
204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.author: Vito Lattanzi, Marina Minozzi
204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.keywords: Woman; photograph; anthropology; ethnology; geography; travel; exploration; scientific expedition; ethnography; museums; model; genre picture; portrait; representation of the other; costume; material culture; collection; Lebanon; Druze
204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.description2: The bride wears a tantur, a head ornament worn along with a white veil by the women from Antilibano. The photo belonging to Enrico H. Giglioli's collection was collected by the Florentine naturalist on his world travels in 1865 to 1868 as he advanced diplomatic and commercial affairs between the newborn Italian state and the other nations. The images seem to have been created spontaneously to show ethnocentric diversity. The ethnographic photographs in the Giglioli's collection are part of the historical archive of the Pigorini Museum and are important for the histories of anthropological science and photography. The origins of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome can be traced back to the 1875 foundation of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

213b0fb4-e0c5-55f3-9d6e-bd61b0fcc5ae.name: Ottoman Clothing Album
213b0fb4-e0c5-55f3-9d6e-bd61b0fcc5ae.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
213b0fb4-e0c5-55f3-9d6e-bd61b0fcc5ae.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
213b0fb4-e0c5-55f3-9d6e-bd61b0fcc5ae.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
213b0fb4-e0c5-55f3-9d6e-bd61b0fcc5ae.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

214be064-96bb-55b5-a13e-9888c7b4d009.name: Cup of early-Christian inspiration
214be064-96bb-55b5-a13e-9888c7b4d009.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
214be064-96bb-55b5-a13e-9888c7b4d009.author: Marina Minozzi
214be064-96bb-55b5-a13e-9888c7b4d009.keywords: Applied arts; minor arts; reproduction; model; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; motifs; collection; collector; glasswork; Murano glass; early Christian art; Romanticism; gold leaf; smoked glass
214be064-96bb-55b5-a13e-9888c7b4d009.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century. In the second half of the 19th century the tradition of Murano glass experienced a revival and a museum in Murano was created with an archive to offer models to artisans to copy. Objects included archaeological glasses of Phoenician, Egyptian, Alexandrian, Roman and Byzantine origin. Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. In Venice, one of the most popular glass factories was the Salviati Society, which was awarded with several prizes at National and International Exhibitions. The Venice-Murano Company made the smoked glass cup with gold leaf and biblical scenes (Inv. n.3046) recalling Early Christian tradition dating to the second half of the 19th century. Aquamarine glass and gold leaf medals are applied on the cup.
214be064-96bb-55b5-a13e-9888c7b4d009.holding_institution_org: Museo Artistico Industriale presso la Galleria nazionale d’arte antica in Palazzo Barberini

en: Zaccagnini, M., *Arti decorative: Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini*, Rome: L'Erma di Bretschneider, 2011: 22.

21713372-5487-5c79-91b5-f6b64a308116.name: Palais Kobbet el-Nhas
21713372-5487-5c79-91b5-f6b64a308116.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
21713372-5487-5c79-91b5-f6b64a308116.history: To the West of Bardo the fresh air and cultivated fields of the Manouba plain attracted royalty and nobility who were moving to their springtime residences. The presence of a revered saint, Lalla Manoubiya, added to the attraction of the area. The Palais Kobbet el-Nhas, built by Mohamed Errachid Bey (Muhammad al-Rashid Bey) c. 1756 and reorganised by Hammouda Pacha Bey in the late 19th century, is located amongst these residences. The palace itself is named after him, a reference to his brass domed pavilion which had originally been built for the beylical harem. The neighbouring Palais de la Rose, which seems to have been connected to it originally, is equally vast and luxurious.
21713372-5487-5c79-91b5-f6b64a308116.keywords: Architecture; art; painting; stucco; mosaic; marble; ceramics
21713372-5487-5c79-91b5-f6b64a308116.description2: This palace is located at the end of a great courtyard, lined with trees and featuring a large elevated façade and gallery, sitting above an annex, accessed via a grand staircase. The full beauty of this palace is evident even from the patio, which leads to a double driba (vestibule), with a vaulted ceiling embellished with Andalusian motifs carved in stucco, and paved with marble and decorated with earthenware tiles, which leads to a great hall. The wall decorations are made from luxurious earthenware and refined marble, and the floor is decorated as a black and white checkerboard. The domed ceilings, like the vaulted ceilings, are decorated with carved stucco with geometric and arabesque patterns. Other rooms are attached to every corner of this great hall, which, like the second reception hall in the right wing of the palace, has a wooden ceiling painted gold in an Italian style.

21fbb370-0706-50de-a10a-ae6eb3f6cb65.name: Portrait Album – Ottoman State Officers
21fbb370-0706-50de-a10a-ae6eb3f6cb65.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
21fbb370-0706-50de-a10a-ae6eb3f6cb65.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
21fbb370-0706-50de-a10a-ae6eb3f6cb65.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah; Joaillier
21fbb370-0706-50de-a10a-ae6eb3f6cb65.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

22b59916-1001-5666-873e-2d7a62f3d991.name: *Keswa kabbous (wedding outfit)*
22b59916-1001-5666-873e-2d7a62f3d991.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
22b59916-1001-5666-873e-2d7a62f3d991.keywords: Wedding outfit; embroidery with silver thread.
22b59916-1001-5666-873e-2d7a62f3d991.description2: Worn by the bride during the wedding ceremony, the keswa kabous el-Jaraq weighs more than ten kilograms. It consists of a large, billowing pair of trousers secured at the waist by a tekka (similar to a ribbon), with a matching top, short enough to leave the waist uncovered, both made of silk taffeta. Its air of great wealth and elegance comes particularly from the contrast between the floral motifs, embroidered with a flat silver thread, and the sequins, also sewn on with a gold and silver thread. When worn by a seated bride, the trousers resemble a large hoop-skirt, connected to a low-necked bodice, which together give the impression of being a robe de cour (grand habit). The upper section of these trousers, hemmed at the waist but open at the front, consists of almost four metres of fabric, and the legs alone have a circumference of one and a half metres and are a metre long. The end of the legs is hemmed with some robust percale fabric, which contains the hemming and rises up the leg to create an even larger swell around the ankle.

23916cb8-b949-51f4-9771-383db0e095cb.name: Single dish
23916cb8-b949-51f4-9771-383db0e095cb.description: The dish, while inspired by European blue-and-white models with intricate floral designs, also displays the *Shahada* (“La Ilaha Illa ALLAH") and thus its calligraphic decoration is a reminder of Islamic architectural decor.
23916cb8-b949-51f4-9771-383db0e095cb.keywords: Ceramic; blue-and-white; calligraphy; calligraphic decoration; applied arts; European influence; Moroccan craftsmen; craftsmanship; Islamic architecture; architectural decoration; model; reproduction

23e1371d-e17b-5b84-a037-47dc18e8eb2f.name: *Qittan*
23e1371d-e17b-5b84-a037-47dc18e8eb2f.description2: A very rare piece purchased from Sheikh Sa\`ud in 2002. This was his personal *thawb* and he said he found wearing it very relaxing. Called *qittan*, which means 'cord', the piece is embroidered around the neck up until the ends of sleeves, with silk thread. It also contains silk ball buttons.

23edfc09-0c9b-59bb-960f-61e8838f93b3.name: Shoes
23edfc09-0c9b-59bb-960f-61e8838f93b3.description: White and blue satin shoes. They are flat and have a sharply raised toecap. The sole is made of leather. The surface is partially covered in yellow silk; they are adorned with gold sequins and a yellow tassel.
23edfc09-0c9b-59bb-960f-61e8838f93b3.holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
23edfc09-0c9b-59bb-960f-61e8838f93b3.dimensions: Height 5 cm, Length 27,2 cm, Width 6,3 cm
23edfc09-0c9b-59bb-960f-61e8838f93b3.author: Elena Vázquez

2462e2d8-8762-51dd-918c-0c13489c5218.name: Powder box
2462e2d8-8762-51dd-918c-0c13489c5218.description: A powder box of the horn type decorated with geometric motifs and crafted in Marrakesh in the early 20th century. While maintaining an old-style form, European influences are apparent in the decoration and production technology.
2462e2d8-8762-51dd-918c-0c13489c5218.type: Fittings; metalwork; arms and armour; munitions
2462e2d8-8762-51dd-918c-0c13489c5218.keywords: Metalwork; copper; European influence; geometric motifs; geometric decoration; Applied arts; craftsmanship; traditional craftsmanship; arms; armours; weapons; war; warfare; military objects; Moroccan craftsmen

24e0347f-f9f3-5254-ba16-aef618e16ba6.name: Flag
24e0347f-f9f3-5254-ba16-aef618e16ba6.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
24e0347f-f9f3-5254-ba16-aef618e16ba6.author: Huda Kilani
24e0347f-f9f3-5254-ba16-aef618e16ba6.description2: A piece of green Syrian silk fabric, inset on the top of the mast, which used to be carried during religious ceremonies. Trade and crafts were common activities in Jordan between the late 19th century and the earlier 20th century. These activities depended on migration and attracted groups of people who travelled or settled in the Jordanian territory to produce or sell products. Thus, the exchange of goods among different areas was very common, as exemplified by this object and many traditional dresses. Silk textiles were very common products in the Jordanian and Palestinian areas and were purchased from Syria, being an element in local fashion, both in Jordan and in Palestine.

25019945-0006-566a-b1cc-e378a23e92ea.name: Farrokh Khan, Persian ambassador
25019945-0006-566a-b1cc-e378a23e92ea.description2: Diplomatic relations between France and Persia were strained at the beginning of the 19th century, so Persia began to turn more and more to Great Britain. However, following a disagreement with Great Britain over the city of Herat, Persia re-established its diplomatic relationship with France. The ambassador Farrokh Khan was sent to Paris in the midst of the Anglo-Persian war (1856–57), and Napoléon III's diplomatic aid led to the Treaty of Paris (1857) and successfully ended the conflict. Félix Nadar, one of the most famous portrait photographers in Paris, photographed Farrokh Khan for the occasion.

251b2b7e-e8f3-5697-9d6d-a33a6facc5ca.name: *Details and ornaments from the Alhambra by Owen Jones, Architect*
251b2b7e-e8f3-5697-9d6d-a33a6facc5ca.description: The influence of the Islamic art also arrived through different publications as the well-known Owen Jones's books and the pieces displayed in the International Exhibitions, as in the first one in London where Owen Jones displayed the Lion fountain of the Alhambra Palace in a building dedicated to master works of art. This book was well-known for many of the Orientalist artists as an example for decoration and the use of the colour.
251b2b7e-e8f3-5697-9d6d-a33a6facc5ca.author: Ana Cabrera
251b2b7e-e8f3-5697-9d6d-a33a6facc5ca.archival: *Plans, elevations, sections and details of the Alhambra from drawings taken on the spot 1834 by the late M. Jules Goury and in 1834 and 1837 by Owen Jones, Archt. With a complete translation of the Arabic inscriptions and an historical notices of the Kings of Granada, from the conquest of that city by Arab to the expulsion of the Moors, by Mr. Pascual de Gayangos, vol. II.*
251b2b7e-e8f3-5697-9d6d-a33a6facc5ca.keywords: Alhambra; International exhibitions; Diffusion of models; Architecture; colour

254ea7af-536e-5a78-8206-f0d4cc517b93.name: *Study of an Arab*
254ea7af-536e-5a78-8206-f0d4cc517b93.description2: *Study of an Arab* by Frederick Lewis, and important orientalist painter and etcher.

25cc99b8-ea3d-5a36-aad3-2fdf4e0f6ac5.name: Wedgwood ‘drabware’
25cc99b8-ea3d-5a36-aad3-2fdf4e0f6ac5.description2: Illustrates the influence of Egyptian motifs on Victorian ceramics. Part of the second wave of Egyptianisation, related to the construction of the Suez Canal.

26bb48d2-0468-5e95-b709-f3f74817bef6.name: Man's trousers (*Chakshiri*)
26bb48d2-0468-5e95-b709-f3f74817bef6.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
26bb48d2-0468-5e95-b709-f3f74817bef6.description2: There used to be around fifty diverse styles of folk costumes worn in different ethnic areas throughout Macedonia in the 19th century and in the early 20th century. Among the most prominent were the costumes of Gorni Polog. Unlike the diverse and numerous women’s garments, men’s outfits were much simpler and rather unified. These men's trousers of white canvas are decorated plainly with black braids.

26ea850d-69fb-528e-98a1-2e8e7c4ad533.name: Glass scent vessel
26ea850d-69fb-528e-98a1-2e8e7c4ad533.description2: Glass produced in Bohemia with a strong Middle Eastern influence. Acquired by Franks.

274e910c-7ec1-5f20-8460-292341da7d08.name: Headdress
274e910c-7ec1-5f20-8460-292341da7d08.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
274e910c-7ec1-5f20-8460-292341da7d08.author: Huda Kilani
274e910c-7ec1-5f20-8460-292341da7d08.keywords: silver chains; coins; decorated; Ottoman coins; Venice coins
274e910c-7ec1-5f20-8460-292341da7d08.description2: Three silver chains formed into a hat with beaded frontispiece decorated with coins. On the back, a long fabric with gold and silver Ottoman and Venice coins. Silver jewellery was the most common, because only rich people could afford gold jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom. The Jordanian economy relied on trades and crafts and new waves of people started to come to Jordan and began to settle for these purposes. This object is an example of how traditional fashion reflected the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is also an example of local personal attire, fashion, costumes and rites.

279e1f50-df40-5f44-a5e0-e9a46ddf29b7.name: Bridal coat (*Klashenik*)
279e1f50-df40-5f44-a5e0-e9a46ddf29b7.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
279e1f50-df40-5f44-a5e0-e9a46ddf29b7.keywords: klashenik; broad cloth; textile; embroidery; costume; wedding; marriage
279e1f50-df40-5f44-a5e0-e9a46ddf29b7.materials: Thick twill-weave woollen fabric decorated with braids
279e1f50-df40-5f44-a5e0-e9a46ddf29b7.description2: A *klashenik* is a kind of over-garment in varying lengths and split on the front made of thick woollen broadcloth called *klashna*. This knee-length piece comes from the Veles Region. It is abundantly adorned with embroidery above the lower hem and at the breasts. Embroidery was an inevitable part of decorating the majority of Macedonian folk costumes. The exquisite, meticulously executed embroidery applied on this tunic makes it a real work of art.

2879dbdc-ef5b-53f4-b8f7-d3ae618cfb30.name: Rose sprinkle flask in Persian style
2879dbdc-ef5b-53f4-b8f7-d3ae618cfb30.description: Flask produced in Paris in Oriental style.
2879dbdc-ef5b-53f4-b8f7-d3ae618cfb30.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

295e748a-0245-55df-9c43-f50f0272c148.name: Painting on glass
295e748a-0245-55df-9c43-f50f0272c148.holder: Musée des Arts et Traditions Populaires
295e748a-0245-55df-9c43-f50f0272c148.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
295e748a-0245-55df-9c43-f50f0272c148.description2: This image, painted on glass, is a reference to the famous legend of Abla and 'Antar ibn Shaddad a legend which was very much alive in the Tunisian popular imagination of the time. The well-loved Abla is painted here as a queen, with regal clothes and a crown on her head. The horse, a symbol of virility and strength, is a reference to the legendary character of 'Antar.

29723c0f-a1c2-5bb3-aa6b-3b7ef63ed1af.name: Ceramic vase
29723c0f-a1c2-5bb3-aa6b-3b7ef63ed1af.description2: Kütahya was the second most important ceramic production centre after İznik due to the rich clay deposits in the area. Although there was a decline in ceramic production at the beginning of the 19th century, in the last quarter of the same century production was revived and new designs inspired by İznik ceramics were produced. This is a Kütahya-produced vase whose body enlarges toward the top. It has a floral design on a blue base. The inner part of the notched mouth is white.

29f9716b-3b17-5ea5-b1e6-06de5e5b0e3e.name: *Funda* (pin)
29f9716b-3b17-5ea5-b1e6-06de5e5b0e3e.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
29f9716b-3b17-5ea5-b1e6-06de5e5b0e3e.keywords: decorative pin; funda; filigree; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; silver; wedding; marriage; fashion; costume
29f9716b-3b17-5ea5-b1e6-06de5e5b0e3e.description2: Over the course of the centuries-long existence of Macedonia in the shadow of the Ottoman Empire there was apparent reflection of Oriental-Islamic influences in its arts and crafts. This also applies to the jewellery of Macedonians and all other ethnic communities. In the east of Macedonia, young women and brides within the Vlach population used to wear exquisite articles of adornment in the area of the temples. This type of jewellery was called *funda*. It was usually in trapezoid or semi-oval shape. *Funda* was made in filigree technique richly adorned with lace and tiny silver coins.

2a226eef-1a17-51ae-9e21-911b78e227e7.name: The Builders
2a226eef-1a17-51ae-9e21-911b78e227e7.author: Marina Minozzi
2a226eef-1a17-51ae-9e21-911b78e227e7.keywords: Sculpture; Italian sculptors; reform; social change; work; post-unitarian Italian society; working class; working class condition; social topics; realism; Verismo; social verismo; artistic exchanges; France
2a226eef-1a17-51ae-9e21-911b78e227e7.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
2a226eef-1a17-51ae-9e21-911b78e227e7.description2: Arturo Dazzi was the son of the owner of a marble quarry and remained attracted to this raw material throughout his life. He attended the Academy of Fine Arts in Carrara and then won two national contests. The group of *The Builders*, as stated by the artist, was made for his final examination during the four years he spent at the Pensionato Nazionale di Scultura between 1904 to 1907. For this reason, the sculpture is very complicated and needed a lot of study and work in order to be completed. Nonetheless it gave great satisfaction to the artist: exhibited in 1907 in Italy and in 1909 in Munich the group was awarded both times with gold medals. The work shows an idealized version of the social “verism”, or truth, a concept common among young Italian sculptors of the time, and shows the influence of the painting of Constantin Meunier, *Enlèvement d’un creuset brisé*, done in 1884.

2ae3984e-4d68-5007-ab52-077d0d39f896.name: Alhambra vase
2ae3984e-4d68-5007-ab52-077d0d39f896.dimensions: Height: 107.0 cm, Width: 51.0 cm, Depth: 48.0 cm, Weight: 28.5 kg
2ae3984e-4d68-5007-ab52-077d0d39f896.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
2ae3984e-4d68-5007-ab52-077d0d39f896.keywords: Ceramic; earthenware; vase; geometric patterns; exhibition; revival; lusterware; Nasrids; Spain; workshop; decorative arts; Neo-Mudéjar
2ae3984e-4d68-5007-ab52-077d0d39f896.materials: Earthenware, inlaid with coloured clays and, possibly, painted
2ae3984e-4d68-5007-ab52-077d0d39f896.description2: The Alhambra, the palace and fortress of the Moorish Kings of Granada, Spain, was founded in 1248 and largely completed by 1354. After three hundred years of neglect and destruction, restoration work began in 1828. Its sumptuous architecture excited a great deal of interest, dissemninated most notably by the *Plans, Details and Sections of the Alhambra* published by Owen Jones from 1836. Of the original furnishings of the Palace, some vases survive. The most famous was made before 1400 and is here copied relatively accurately by Deck. This vase was probably shown in the International Exhibition, London, 1862.

2b2f8bbd-a9f5-5da8-a561-886281458b0f.name: Jewellery case
2b2f8bbd-a9f5-5da8-a561-886281458b0f.description: The influence (on decoration, in fabrication techniques or in the typology) of the Islamic artworks from the Middle Ages or Modern period can be seen in this piece.

2d85c81f-8fff-5170-9719-df9f41dbd763.name: Socks (*Chorapi*)
2d85c81f-8fff-5170-9719-df9f41dbd763.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
2d85c81f-8fff-5170-9719-df9f41dbd763.keywords: home-made attire; knitting; silver; gold; embroidery; floral decoration; costume
2d85c81f-8fff-5170-9719-df9f41dbd763.materials: Knitted of wool and silver and gold-wrapped threads. Decoration with embroidery of varied wool
2d85c81f-8fff-5170-9719-df9f41dbd763.description2: In the 18th, 19th and early 20th centuries, all garments for the entire family were made by women themselves. They used to weave all the fabrics, except for the broadcloth, as well as to cut and sew the clothes, decorate them by embroidery and apply varied ornaments for embellishing. Women also used to knit the socks to match the outfit. These men’s socks belong to the set of traditional men’s costume from the Gorni Polog area. They are knitted from black wool and *srma* (silver and gold-wrapped threads). They have been additionally decorated with embroidered floral patterns in different colours.

2df6225e-8ea7-5fef-a311-cc29307168e3.name: *Excavation of Samarra*
2df6225e-8ea7-5fef-a311-cc29307168e3.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
2df6225e-8ea7-5fef-a311-cc29307168e3.author: Stefan Weber
2df6225e-8ea7-5fef-a311-cc29307168e3.second_name: Great Mosque with the famous minaret (Malwiya) of the caliphal city of Samarra, groundbreaking excavation by E. Herzfeld 1911–13
2df6225e-8ea7-5fef-a311-cc29307168e3.description2: Of great importance for the collection of the first Museum of Islamic Art in the western world are the findings made during the excavations in Samarra, which were conducted by Ernst Herzfeld and the museum’s first director, Friedrich Sarre, between 1911 and 1913. The study of the Abbasid’s temporal second capital has contributed to an understanding of the developments and changes in Islamic art at the time.

2e1b7a1f-87a3-5357-a286-a3e13417e1ea.name: *Catalogue Raisonné des monuments exposés dans le Musée National de l'art Arabe*
2e1b7a1f-87a3-5357-a286-a3e13417e1ea.author: Mina Moraitou
2e1b7a1f-87a3-5357-a286-a3e13417e1ea.description2: The *Catalogue Raisonné des monuments exposés dans le Musée National de l'art Arabe* by Max Herz Bey is an illustrated catalogue of the collections at the Museum of Islamic Art in Cairo. It contains an introduction with the history of the different periods from the Umayyads to the Ottomans and chapters following the galleries of the museum and according to material: chapters on stucco and stone, woodwork, metalwork, ceramics, textiles, bookbindings and glass.

2e2c6f60-7eec-5d13-9b2d-03e45b5cd72a.name: *Burqu\` rayyasi*
2e2c6f60-7eec-5d13-9b2d-03e45b5cd72a.description2: Face mask (also known in Arabic as *batula*) decorated with small embossed gold discs all around the forehead and sides. There are two matching gold clasps on each side of the forehead.
