307c3b5c-a525-55c7-89a1-8342e6da903a.name: Dolmabahçe Palace Imperial Gate
307c3b5c-a525-55c7-89a1-8342e6da903a.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; James Robertson
307c3b5c-a525-55c7-89a1-8342e6da903a.description2: James Robertson arrived in Istanbul in 1840 and started work as head etcher in Ottoman Mint. He began taking photos of Istanbul soon after. Dolmabahçe Palace was built by Sultan Abdulmecid (1839-1861), who was the thirty first Ottoman Sultan. The palace, whose construction commenced on 13 June 1843, was brought into use on 7 June 1856, upon completion of its surrounding walls. The palace mainly consists of three parts: the Imperial Mabeyn (State Apartments), Muayede Salon (Ceremonial Hall) and the Imperial Harem. Evident Western influences, observed in the style, details and ornaments, are reflections of the aesthetic values as they changed through the last period of the Imperial. On the other hand, it is a building complex in which traditional Turkish House style was applied on a large scale with respect to spatial organization and the relationships between the rooms and salons.

30b613c8-c840-5eba-a2ea-3334a058e6c5.name: *The Temptations of Saint Antony*
30b613c8-c840-5eba-a2ea-3334a058e6c5.author: Marina Minozzi
30b613c8-c840-5eba-a2ea-3334a058e6c5.keywords: Realism; France; La tentation de Saint-Antoine; Orientalism; Orientalist painting; religious topics; exoticism; eroticism; woman; international exhibitions; universal exposition; national exposition; exoticism in fine arts and literature
30b613c8-c840-5eba-a2ea-3334a058e6c5.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
30b613c8-c840-5eba-a2ea-3334a058e6c5.description2:
The painting by Domenico Morelli shown at the Universal Exposition in Paris, it’s among the artist’s most complex artworks. Both realistic and symbolic elements characterise the painting, as well as a strong mystic, but at the same time erotic, tension. Inspired by *La Tentation de Saint-Antoine* by Gustave Flaubert from 1874, the painting shows realism in the imaginary setting influenced by oriental elements. The work was finished in 1878 and sent to the French merchant Goupil to be shown at the Universal Exposition in Paris. It was also presented at the National Exposition in Turin in 1880 and completely misunderstood by contemporaries who blamed Morelli for having resigned to make fashionable art.  
A smaller version of it was painted by the artist while making a lot of preparatory drawings in which Saint Anthony is standing next to the rock wall. In the final version the Saint is seated on the ground trying to resist the temptations embodied by the two half-naked women on the left.
30b613c8-c840-5eba-a2ea-3334a058e6c5.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

The immigration of the Circassians to the Eastern Arab countries (they have spiritual and religious links with these countries) started in the middle of 19th century and continued until 1900.

30efc219-29fa-5f32-b34b-24791540a5c9.name: Astrolabe
30efc219-29fa-5f32-b34b-24791540a5c9.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
30efc219-29fa-5f32-b34b-24791540a5c9.description2: This portable astrolabe consists of a suspension device with a 18cm diameter disk, divided up into degrees, and a handle. Two moving parts are used for measurements: the spider on the front, and the alidade (a flat ruler revolving round a point) on the back. The astrolabe remained in use as the primary tool for navigation until the 18th century. However, it was also used as an astronomical tool, to measure the height of stars from the horizon, or the angle separating one star from another.

316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.name: *Mohamed Sadok Pacha Bey* (painting)
316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.keywords: Oil on canvas; B. de Moynier; Mohamed Sadok Pacha Bey
316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.materials: Canvas, wood, coloured pigments, gold leaf
316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.description2: This 1861 oil on canvas by B. de Moynier shows the Mohamed Sadok Pacha Bey in front of the throne in the great hall of the Palais du Bardo, his right hand on the Tunisian constitution (which he has just proclaimed), his left holding his sword. He is dressed in official uniform, with red trousers with a gold stripe and a short black coat with a gold belt and epaulets, in addition to the Nichan al-Amen medal and a green sash with a double red stripe. On his chest the Nichan al-Dam, the Légion d'Honneur and the Nichan al-Iftikhar (classe majeur) medals can be seen, as well as a Légion d'Honneur and Nichan al-Iftikhar on a sling. This painting is evidence of an active diplomatic relationship between the Palais du Bardo and the European chancelleries.

316cb158-b737-5946-b4f5-2c1e7c67bb07.name: Textile

31b5f52e-c220-58fe-a02b-2b22d317bc2b.name: *Description of the Arab monuments of Granada, Seville and Córdoba: the Alhambra, the Alcazar and the Great Mosque*
31b5f52e-c220-58fe-a02b-2b22d317bc2b.description: The publications about the Spanish Muslim Antiquities, including monuments can be retraced to the end of the 18th century. Interest in these monuments is related to the interest in this unique heritage in Europe, as part of the Alhambresque and Neo-Mudéjar styles in Spain and Europe. The publication of the monument’s descriptions aided in their conservation.
31b5f52e-c220-58fe-a02b-2b22d317bc2b.author: Ana Cabrera
31b5f52e-c220-58fe-a02b-2b22d317bc2b.third_name: *Estudio descriptivo de los monumentos árabes de Granada, Sevilla y Córdoba o sea, La Alhambra, El Alcazar y la gran Mezquita de Occidente*

328d4cd7-8859-5b3d-96c3-05fe9c191bbc.description: These textiles were part of the famous Alhambra wall hangings that decorated different Alhambra rooms. Each is from a different Nasrid king: Yusuf I (textile 1607), Muhammad III (textile 1606) and Muhammad V (textile 1719).

32fb3761-3d91-5ac8-b9e9-d93cf46f8c28.name: Lamp from a mosque
32fb3761-3d91-5ac8-b9e9-d93cf46f8c28.keywords: Exploration; Aden; travel; traveller; mosque interior decoration
32fb3761-3d91-5ac8-b9e9-d93cf46f8c28.description2: This lamp from a mosque was purchased from a Yemenite from Saana by Franz Steindacher in Aden in 1896. Steindacher was part of an Austrian expedition to explore the Red Sea.

3339a22b-fc28-5c69-a302-f09a3d0a84b5.name: *View of Mers el-Kebir, Fort Lamoune*
3339a22b-fc28-5c69-a302-f09a3d0a84b5.author: Dalila Orfali
3339a22b-fc28-5c69-a302-f09a3d0a84b5.description2: This small watercolour was made during the artist's short break in Algeria in 1832, during his visit to Morocco with the Count de Mornay. Delacroix only made a small number of Algerian works, as he spent a very short time in the country. He only stayed in Algiers for three days, where he had the oppurtunity to see the inside of *rais*'s palace. Alazard believes that the watercolour of the museum is only drawing from his brief stay at Oran, and this is corroborated by the art historian Arlette Sérullaz, a specialist of Delacroix. The watercolour is also mentioned in Robaut's book *L’œuvre complet de Delacroix*, and was exhibited at the Louvre in 2003 for the "Chefs d'Œuvre du Cabinet des Estampes" exhibition.

3385951b-c80c-5d8e-8659-f32b8e5ee6a7.name: Bridal coat
3385951b-c80c-5d8e-8659-f32b8e5ee6a7.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
3385951b-c80c-5d8e-8659-f32b8e5ee6a7.keywords: upper garment; broad cloth; costume; textile; accessories; wedding; marriage
3385951b-c80c-5d8e-8659-f32b8e5ee6a7.materials: Klashna – thick woollen fabric adorned with balze, silver and gold-wrapped thread, silver string, sequins, beads and pompons of wool
3385951b-c80c-5d8e-8659-f32b8e5ee6a7.description2: Analysis of the evolution path of traditional costumes in the Republic of Macedonia have shown apparent influences of the Old Slav, Old Balkan, Byzantine and Turkish-Oriental cultures. This piece of traditional overcoat is an exquisite example of the application of *srma* – gold and silver-wrapped thread used widely in the Oriental handicraft of decorating garments. A *gornik* is a sleeveless upper garment made of white broadcloth called *klashna*. It has false sleeves hanging on the back. They are actually strips of white broadcloth richly adorned with pompoms of fluffy red wool, silver thread braids, a silver twisted ribbon, red baize, a silver string, sequins and beads. The lower part of the back is decorated in the same manner. Its rims and seams are also decorated with red and black braids.

33c78378-09b9-5e76-bb0d-85f0948fe81c.name: Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, Marquise of Cerralbo, and Amelia del Valle y Serrano, in Oriental garment
33c78378-09b9-5e76-bb0d-85f0948fe81c.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This albumen portrait of Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, Marquise of Cerralbo, and her daughter Amelia del Valle y Serrano is delicious thanks to the typical Turkish costume, the apparently easy pose and the scenography and the absolute harmony with the idea of aesthetic orientalism.
33c78378-09b9-5e76-bb0d-85f0948fe81c.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes
33c78378-09b9-5e76-bb0d-85f0948fe81c.third_name: Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, marquesa de Cerralbo, y Amelia del Valle y Serrano, con atuendo oriental

33daf898-afb6-58bd-95bf-60b7472151c4.name: Illuminated Qur’an manuscript
33daf898-afb6-58bd-95bf-60b7472151c4.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
33daf898-afb6-58bd-95bf-60b7472151c4.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
33daf898-afb6-58bd-95bf-60b7472151c4.artist: Calligrapher Ali Shukri, known as Nadherzadeh
33daf898-afb6-58bd-95bf-60b7472151c4.materials: European paper, black ink, pigments, gilding, pasteboard, leather
33daf898-afb6-58bd-95bf-60b7472151c4.description2: 19th-century Qur’an manuscripts produced in Istanbul and the Ottoman Empire continued many Islamic art traditions, but could not entirely escape the increasing taste for Western aesthetics.Ssingle-volume Qur’ans like this one became increasingly popular and were completed in large numbers. This example – which appears to have remained unfinished judging by the empty title cartouches above the chapters, begins – as is customary – with a lavishly decorated double page, showing – on the right - the first chapter ‘Al-Fatiha’ and – on the left - the beginning of the second chapter ‘Al-Baqara’. Both texts are contained within broad geometric borders and framed with colourful illuminations with vegetal detailing. The remainder of the all in all 114 chapters of the Holy Qur’an are written in black naskhi and red detailing, with 15 lines to each page. As was customary, the verse markers are rendered as golden circles and each page is confined within delicate gilt borders. Colourful medallions in some of the margins mark important subdivisions of the text.

35645306-e708-561a-ae81-24e697df6d15.name: *Woman In Oriental Dress*
35645306-e708-561a-ae81-24e697df6d15.author: Petar Petrovic
35645306-e708-561a-ae81-24e697df6d15.description2: In order to evoke and convey the spirit of the Balkans and the Orient as faithfully as possible, Paja Jovanović meticulously recorded each detail of the interior of a typical Balkan or Eastern house. He also collected props that made up a family’s inventory of furniture (e.g. the hexagonal decorative table to the left), and carefully studied the physiognomies and characters of the men and women he encountered in the southern Balkans, in Egypt, Constantinople, the Caucasus and elsewhere. The precision of draughtsmanship and freshness of colour in this painting by Paja Jovanović ranks it among his more successful works from the mid-1880s.

356abb7a-adfb-5423-8a02-b389733f2355.name: Textile
356abb7a-adfb-5423-8a02-b389733f2355.description: Velvet with silver stencilled decorations of arabesques with starts of six points. These decorations recalled the plaster decorations of the Spanish Muslim interiors.
356abb7a-adfb-5423-8a02-b389733f2355.holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
356abb7a-adfb-5423-8a02-b389733f2355.author: Lucina Llorente

3578fea3-edb8-5ff7-a0a7-aea81c138ad2.name: Gold brooch
3578fea3-edb8-5ff7-a0a7-aea81c138ad2.description2: Gold brooch based closely on Assyrian reliefs. Illustrates Assyrian influence on 19th century jewellery.

3583d624-13fa-58e9-9d82-9ef1b2d476f5.name: *Beethoven at the Palace*
3583d624-13fa-58e9-9d82-9ef1b2d476f5.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
3583d624-13fa-58e9-9d82-9ef1b2d476f5.description2: Caliph Abdulmecid was interested in art in addition to administration. He opened many art exhibitions. He was chosen as honorary president of the Society of Ottoman Painters, which was founded in 1909, and he gave considerable financial support to the monthly journal published by the society. He took part in the Galatasaray Art Exhibitions with his paintings. For example, one of his paintings was accepted for an exhibition held at Galatasaray during the first years of the First World War. His works reveal him as a colourist and an accomplished portrait painter. Caliph Abdulmecid showed his paintings at the Viyana Exhibition, which was the first exhibition opened by Turkish painters in Europe in 1918.

35b02f89-4d68-5272-8b1d-532de4511f6a.name: Pottery coffee-cup from Saudi Arabia
35b02f89-4d68-5272-8b1d-532de4511f6a.description2: Cups like these were used predominantly to serve both *qishr* a drink made from the outer shells of coffee beans flavoured with cardamom or cinnamon as well as coffee made from toasted and ground coffee beans. They were frequently glazed in shades of green and yellow. Earthenware cups such as these were gradually replaced by finer porcelain cups during the middle and later parts of the 20th century.

366a9ff1-e485-57a9-ad1c-a5eb7cf07698.name: Chest of drawers
366a9ff1-e485-57a9-ad1c-a5eb7cf07698.author: Ana Cabrera
366a9ff1-e485-57a9-ad1c-a5eb7cf07698.keywords: Orientalism; Applied Arts; Westernization of the arts and design
366a9ff1-e485-57a9-ad1c-a5eb7cf07698.description2: This chest has a European shape and the decoration is near to Indian or Near-Eastern motifs. It has an Arab inscription, but only the date could be read it. This chest was probably made in India or in Egypt for the European customers who lived there.

36773e08-5d5d-510b-9eaf-d6bc145e39d8.name: Cigarette case
36773e08-5d5d-510b-9eaf-d6bc145e39d8.description: The Orientalism or Neo-Mudéjar style gave new light to old motifs as decoration in ivory or bone, with flowers and interlaces, as in this cigarette case. The decoration is strongly influenced by Arab pieces.
36773e08-5d5d-510b-9eaf-d6bc145e39d8.author: Ana Cabrera
36773e08-5d5d-510b-9eaf-d6bc145e39d8.keywords: Neo-mudejar style; Applied Arts; Production of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode

36a5f8c4-91af-5cb4-9bf8-37f9eb7b40ac.name: *Sadness*
36a5f8c4-91af-5cb4-9bf8-37f9eb7b40ac.description: Amadeo de Sousa-Cardozo (1887–1918) was a famous Portuguese artist from the beginning of the 20th century. His career, which ended at the age of 30, is an example of international dialogue with contemporary artistic trends of his time such as cubism, futurism and expressionism.

36d231d4-e722-5471-936b-e81fdd08dc11.name: Coffee pot
36d231d4-e722-5471-936b-e81fdd08dc11.description2: Coffee formed the basis of all hospitality rituals in the Arabian Peninsula. The coffee beans were freshly roasted, ground and brewed in coffee pots whenever guests were received, and a strict etiquette was followed in the serving of coffee, with offence easily taken if any breach of the expected procedure occurred. Hospitality was a source of tremendous pride and no respectable host would be seen without a variety of coffee pots with which to honour his guests. In the Arabian peninsula, coffee pots were originally made of earthenware, but were replaced by more durable and ostentatious copper coffee pots.

36d58a55-2db8-5fb1-a95f-93e3fa5513d2.name: Ottoman Clothing Album
36d58a55-2db8-5fb1-a95f-93e3fa5513d2.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
36d58a55-2db8-5fb1-a95f-93e3fa5513d2.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
36d58a55-2db8-5fb1-a95f-93e3fa5513d2.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
36d58a55-2db8-5fb1-a95f-93e3fa5513d2.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

372e3810-b18e-5d0c-b107-9bd837cefb1e.name: Hijaz Railway Medal
372e3810-b18e-5d0c-b107-9bd837cefb1e.description: Medal of the Hijaz Railway fund. In September 1900, (the 25th anniversary of Sultan Abdul Hamid’s accession to throne) he addressed a call for all the Muslims all over the world to collect donations for establishing a railway between Damascus and the holy places to facilitate transporting the pilgrims. The call was responded to enthusiastically and with great support from all Muslims. Sultan Abdul Hamid II began the donations with 300,000 Ottoman gold lira, then kings and heads of Islamic world donated money or materials for setting the railway. The donations continued till 1907. On this occasion the sultan issued gold, silver and nickel medals to donors – for instance a nickel medal given to whoever donated 5-50 Lira, a silver medal for whoever donated 50-100 Lira and named them bey, and for donations of more than 100 Lira a gold medal and the title of Pasha. After that the donation become compulsory in which the officials disclaim a one month salary. This is a gilt nickel medal issued AH 1318 / AD 1900. On its obverse, within a wreath: tuğra of sultan Abdul Hamid II with "al-Ghazi" and form of locomotive and the date ١٣١۸ (AH 1318) below. On reverse, حميديه حجاز تيمور يولنه خدمت ايدن حميتمندانه مخصوص مدالية در ("Medal reserved to patriots who have served the Hamidiye Hijaz Railway") written in Divan script.

3854487a-c60c-5835-adc0-fa6fe0ed8d59.third_name: *Mobili egiziani del'italiano Giuseppe Parvis dimorante al Cairo*
3854487a-c60c-5835-adc0-fa6fe0ed8d59.description2: Giuseppe Parvis, who emigrated from Italy to Egypt, began extensive production of elegant furniture adapted to Arabian taste and decorated with mother-of-pearl and metal inserts. He won awards for his work at the Universal Exhibitions of Paris in 1867, Vienna and Philadelphia. Giuseppe Parvis is an example of successful businessman who successfully adapted to the Egyptian market. He was able to run laboratories with 50 workers and trained a large number of students in ebony furniture making. Over the span of 20 years he introduced and sold furniture to Arabian people who traditionally did not possess such furniture, using an Arabic style and taste and by using woods found in the East, Egypt and China.

3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.name: Headdress
3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.author: Huda Kilani
3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.keywords: cotton; embroidered; gold coins; Ottoman coins
3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.materials: Gold, silver, cotton fabric, silk; casting; hand embroidered
3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.description2: A rectangular piece of cotton cloth embroidered with cross-stitching forming a bonnet with a line of 70 gold coins (*ghawasi*) sewn together on the front, with two pieces of cloth on the top sides with silver Ottoman coins and red stuffed velvet pursed from the back side with 7 silver Ottoman coins. The silver coins were used as money and as jewellery given by the groom to the bride, thus being an indication of his financial status. This object reflects the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It illustrates common elements and traditions in the area in fashion, costumes and social rites. There were no political boundaries at that period between the Jordanian and Palestinians territories. Some cities were like twins because of their close proximity and the exchange of trade goods and business.

3a9203b3-ee28-58a5-9738-28760f62fc9b.name: Photograph
3a9203b3-ee28-58a5-9738-28760f62fc9b.dimensions: Height: 27.5 cm album, Width: 80 cm album open
3a9203b3-ee28-58a5-9738-28760f62fc9b.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
3a9203b3-ee28-58a5-9738-28760f62fc9b.description2:
This photograph is taken from a family photograph album. Most of the photographs in it are printed on platinum paper, which was introduced in 1879.  
Throughout most of the 19th century women had few legal rights to property, money, children, or even, after marriage, their own bodies. However, there were great changes in attitudes during the last decade of the century. The traditional role of women was questioned and some women openly defied convention. They educated themselves by reading widely and took up what were seen as 'un-ladylike' activities such as smoking and cycling. The free movement of the bicycle was seen as a symbol of equality and personal freedom.

3abe2459-c22d-5b5d-907a-4be0147c9eec.name: Seated Berber woman (Nailiya)
3abe2459-c22d-5b5d-907a-4be0147c9eec.description:
The image depicts a Nailiya, a woman of the Berber tribe of the Ouled Naïl, in the south of Algeria. She is sitting among rich cushions, wearing a colourful silk dress and the jewels used to perform their traditional dance.  
The Nailiyat were independent women, free to marry men of their choosing. They moved to the cities in the North to earn money as dancers, in order to maintain their families in their community of origin. All this was not fully understood by Europeans. With the emergence of sex tourism these women were forced to introduce sexual content in their originally hieratic performance, and finally they were even considered as prostitutes by the French administration, in turn leading to being repudiated in their villages.  
Early photography contributed to forge this image of the Nailiyat in the European imagination.

3bc9a9b0-a7fe-59d9-9819-5e3a9265f4a4.name: Egyptianising necklace
3bc9a9b0-a7fe-59d9-9819-5e3a9265f4a4.description2: Gold fringe necklace in the  form of cast alternating lotus flowers and buds. Illustrates the influence of Egyptian motifs on 19th French jewellery. As was typical, this necklace is not derived from an original, but a more free creation based on patrern books.

3c18dfa3-8e52-5116-bf41-c9550b769ba0.keywords: Applied arts; minor arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; decoration; motifs; collection; collector; glass; Murano glass; glasswork; zoomorphysm; zoomorphic; floral decoration; floral motifs; vegetal motifs
3c18dfa3-8e52-5116-bf41-c9550b769ba0.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, and was part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. The Crystal cup with curved stem and appliqued aquamarine glass flowers and leaves dates from the second half of the 19th century. Baroque repertory inspired its form and use of floral decoration. A tendency toward abstract form is noticeable.

3c3428ad-e6d9-50dc-93c0-7e7ab1c900d2.author: Marina Minozzi
3c3428ad-e6d9-50dc-93c0-7e7ab1c900d2.keywords: Orientalism; painting; Orientalist painting; Italian painters; exoticism; artistic exchanges; France; international exhibitions; universal exposition; travel; imaginary trips; travelling artist; natural sciences
3c3428ad-e6d9-50dc-93c0-7e7ab1c900d2.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
3c3428ad-e6d9-50dc-93c0-7e7ab1c900d2.description2: In 1891 Filippo Palizzi donated more than 300 paintings to the National Gallery of Modern Art of Rome in order to describe his entire career through his artworks. All of them are cited in the Chronological List of 1853, which includes 12 studies depicting exotic animals done in The Jardin des Plantes in Paris. The series is considered the preparatory base for the amazing painting *Dopo il Diluvio. Uscita degli animali dall’Arca* (*After the Flood. The Animals Exiting the Ark*), commissioned by King Vittorio Emanuele II for the Museum of Capodimonte and presented in 1867 at the Universal Exposition in Paris. Other animals, like the Indian ox, the antelope and the dromedary were depicted in the Jardin des Plantes in Paris with the same aim.

3cce65e9-b5bd-5b53-9b90-2b8d522d809b.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. The motif of glass filaments worked with pincers to look like crests, typical of the 17th century objects is used also in the ruby-red glass cup with snake-shaped stem of neo-baroque inspiration and dating from the second half of the 19th century. Its form is inspired by snake goblets common in Venice and Germany in the 17th century.

3e0c77fe-e569-53cb-a6e6-0d26f3ac626b.name: Coffee pot
3e0c77fe-e569-53cb-a6e6-0d26f3ac626b.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
3e0c77fe-e569-53cb-a6e6-0d26f3ac626b.description2:
This copper pot has been covered in a thin layer of silver and lavishly decorated. Its swelling shape shows the influence of the European Baroque style on the Ottoman decorative arts. Most metal coffee pots were made of cheaper materials such as tinned copper. In richer homes, coffee was served to honoured guests in pots like this one, made of precious metals (or imitations of them) and decorated in the latest taste.  
The Ottoman Baroque style developed from the 1740s as artists and designers began to apply non-figurative European motifs to Ottoman forms. It flourished until the 1820s, when new types of European ornament were introduced.

3e51e99d-8ff0-545e-95fc-52a15be8b042.name: *A Coffee House in Tophane*
3e51e99d-8ff0-545e-95fc-52a15be8b042.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
3e51e99d-8ff0-545e-95fc-52a15be8b042.keywords: Thomas Allom; Jivanian; Orientalism; painting; İstanbul
3e51e99d-8ff0-545e-95fc-52a15be8b042.description2: A Thomas Allom composition which appears in the first volume of Robert Walsh’s book *Constantinople and Scenery of Seven Churches of Asia Minor* is *The Coffee-House*. This is an oil copy of the composition by Civanyan. Written by Robert Walsh, who served as the private priest of British ambassador Lord Strangford after 1820, the book was published in two volumes in London in 1838. It includes engravings and the book, which was later published in French, acted as an important visual resource on Istanbul and its engravings were used as models by numerous artists. In the corresponding text, Robert Walsh provides information on the interior organisation and decoration of the coffeehouse and relates various details ranging from making music and smoking pipes to the plays of the *meddah* (storytellers).

3eac8587-105c-522d-ac26-54e2094512db.description2: Glass produced in Bohemia with a strong Middle Eastern influence. Acquired by Franks.

3f6f9fb2-a5df-53ef-ab7b-89496d344816.description: A sword and scabbard decorated with geometric and floral motifs and crafted in southern Morocco in the 19th century. Sword blades were imported from Europe, especially from Toledo in Spain, or from Damascus in Syria.

40cc028f-a362-5724-b6be-dad14e9c2277.name: *Dagla zabun*
40cc028f-a362-5724-b6be-dad14e9c2277.materials: Cream twill, weave wool fabric, polychrome wool, embroidery threads, brown cotton knit braid, knotted brown silk buttons.
40cc028f-a362-5724-b6be-dad14e9c2277.description2: Men’s ceremonial coat style gown. Full-length A-line coat made from fine cream wool that was embroidered prior to being cut. It is likely that the coat was made from embroidered Kashmiri shawls decorated on corners and edges. Materials are cream twill, weave wool fabric, polychrome wool, embroidery threads, brown cotton knit braid, and 2 knotted brown silk buttons. This type of un-dyed wool is very fine, and we have only one. When this type of coat came back in to popularity, this specific design and color never appeared again. It is very rare. Lined with un-dyed silk in a natural color. There is a slit on the side for a pocket.

40ef2328-28fd-59f1-96b3-b75abf4e6c58.name: *Bedouin of the Houran*
40ef2328-28fd-59f1-96b3-b75abf4e6c58.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
40ef2328-28fd-59f1-96b3-b75abf4e6c58.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
40ef2328-28fd-59f1-96b3-b75abf4e6c58.description2: The constant movement of large Bedouin confederations regularly impacted on the history of the Middle East, in particular when it intersected with settled societies and cities. The bedouins of Hauran lived in the Hauran plain in what is now SW Syria/ NW Jordan at the time. The Sheikh of the Hauran bedouins was employed by the Ottoman pasha of Damascus to collect tribute from all tribes in the area and help in its defence. Philip Meeder was a British wood engraver, who died in 1913. The image is taken from ’Picturesque Palestine, Sinai and Egypt’, Charles William Wilson ed., 1881. The accompanying text in the book reads: 'A bedouin of the Haurân. Bedouins occupy the north-west district of the Haurân; the plain is inhabited by peasants, and the Druses for many centuries have colonised the mountain range.

412af98f-597f-5bd8-9bce-18aac056c045.name: Jars from the Company of Glass and Mosaic of Venice and Murano [Paris Exhibition, 1878]
412af98f-597f-5bd8-9bce-18aac056c045.author: Marina Minozzi
412af98f-597f-5bd8-9bce-18aac056c045.archival: *L'Esposizione di Parigi del 1878 illustrata*, Sonzogno Editore, 1878, p. 340.
412af98f-597f-5bd8-9bce-18aac056c045.keywords: Applied arts; minor arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; decoration; motifs; collection; collector; glass; Murano glass; glasswork; Venice; Salviati; book; International exhibitions; market; trade
412af98f-597f-5bd8-9bce-18aac056c045.copyright: Copyright image: Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale, Roma.
412af98f-597f-5bd8-9bce-18aac056c045.third_name: *Vasi della Compagnia di Vetri e Mosaici di Venezia e Murano*
412af98f-597f-5bd8-9bce-18aac056c045.description2: “The Chronicle of the Universal Exhibition of Paris” of 1878 celebrates the city of Murano’s commercial success in glass production. A large number of these objects reside in the collection of the Museum of Industrial Arts in Rome (M.A.I.), now part of the acquisitions of the National Museum of Antique Art on display at Palazzo Barberini. M.A.I. was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. These jars were manufactured by the famous glass company Salviati, founded in 1866 and established in Venice and Murano. In presenting these objects they claimed the rebirth of a long-forgotten antique art and the rebirth of glass industries in Italy. Tomb excavations brought to light a series of vases. New objects based on those excavated were made on the occasion of the International Exhibition in Paris in 1878.

41a2680e-8cf9-5ee5-a679-4297b5a1558c.name: Fındıklı
41a2680e-8cf9-5ee5-a679-4297b5a1558c.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; Pascal Sebah
41a2680e-8cf9-5ee5-a679-4297b5a1558c.description2: Pascal Sébah (1823-1886) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. In 1857 he opened his first photography studio, *El Chark Societe Photographic*, in Istanbul and by 1873 was successful enough to open another studio in Cairo. In 1860 he moved to another studio next to the Russian Embassy in order to work with A. Laroche, who worked in Paris. He continued to work with Laroche until 1873.

423021cf-ae6a-5fd5-a257-4aa4a79ded1d.name: *Pedestal of the Obelisk in the Ancient Byzatine Hippodrome*
423021cf-ae6a-5fd5-a257-4aa4a79ded1d.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
423021cf-ae6a-5fd5-a257-4aa4a79ded1d.keywords: Istanbul photography; Byzantine and Ottoman architecture
423021cf-ae6a-5fd5-a257-4aa4a79ded1d.description2: A frequently employed device in Robertson's Istanbul photographs is the inclusion of the one or more human figures in the foreground – indeed, this is something of a trademark of Robertson’s work. There were two main reasons for the inclusion of these figures. For one thing, the artist used them as a way of creating a more natural scene. The other was to provide one or more reference points so that the photograph’s viewers could get an idea of the dimensions of the scene they were looking at and of the elements contained therein.

42a12e5a-4f49-5af5-9a9c-e5db696bbced.name: Portrait of a Lady
42a12e5a-4f49-5af5-9a9c-e5db696bbced.description: The decoration of the cabinet represented in this painting is clearly influenced by Islamic art in the details of the arches and the motifs in Neo-Mudéjar style. This decoration is related to the different publications about the Alhambra or the drawings by Carderera, in which the designers and artists found new inspiration for their works.

43a8c5d9-b3aa-529b-a3f9-5e64b5b32a48.name: The Pearl Carpet
43a8c5d9-b3aa-529b-a3f9-5e64b5b32a48.materials: Pearls, silk, deer hide, beads, gems
43a8c5d9-b3aa-529b-a3f9-5e64b5b32a48.description2: The foundation of silk and fine deer hide is densely embroidered overall with a design worked in strings of natural ‘Basra’ pearls, measuring approximately 1-3 mm, and English coloured glass beads. There are on average 78 pearls and beads per vertical dm. (10 cm), and 68 per horizontal dm., equaling a density of c.4,990 pearls and beads per dm2. The total area of the carpet is c. 45,670 cm2. The 32 smaller rosettes cover an area of c. 400 cm2 with smaller gems, and the total area embroidered with pearls and is beads is approximately 44,500 cm2. Therefore, over 2.2 million pearls and beads have been used to decorate the field. In our estimation, the number of pearls employed in the design is therefor at least 1.2-1.5 million.

459c2899-4ce2-5ffd-a17b-a43ffa91c9bc.name: *Milos Obrenovic, prince of Serbia*
459c2899-4ce2-5ffd-a17b-a43ffa91c9bc.author: Petar Petrovic
459c2899-4ce2-5ffd-a17b-a43ffa91c9bc.description2: Milos Obrenović (1783-1860) was Prince of Serbia from 1815 to 1839, and again from 1858 to 1860. He participated in the First Serbian Uprising, led Serbs in the Second Serbian Uprising, and founded the dynasty of Obrenović. Under his rule, Serbia became an autonomous duchy within the Ottoman Empire. He is credited with starting the process of re-establishing Serbian statehood, as well as shaping the domestic and foreign policies of the modern Serbian state. Prince Milos ruled autocratically, permanently refusing to share power. During his rule, he was the richest man in Serbia and among the richest in the Balkans. In the portrait that was painted by Pavel Djurkovitch in Kragujevac, prince Milos is dressed in Oriental costume and has on the top of the head a turban. It is a typically Oriental piece of costume and this was of significance for the attitude and dignity of the Serbian sovereign at the beginning 19th century, who was by all means respecting an Ottoman empire and his Sultan.

45cab7c7-4fad-588f-ae17-e78354e7fd67.name: *Exposition d’Art Musulman*
45cab7c7-4fad-588f-ae17-e78354e7fd67.author: Mina Moraitou
45cab7c7-4fad-588f-ae17-e78354e7fd67.keywords: photo; Egypt; Greeks; Iznik; collecting; exhibition
45cab7c7-4fad-588f-ae17-e78354e7fd67.description2: A photo depicting a showcase with Iznik ceramics belonging to Greek and European collectors such as Benakis, Nomico, Lagonico and Salvago. Many of the works were collected by Greeks in Egypt and were included in the *Exposition d’Art Musulman*, organised by Gaston Migeon and held in Alexandria in 1925 while a number more were shown in the earlier great Islamic exhibition in Munich in 1910.

45ccc1b2-62ae-540c-ba7c-d71565ea58c3.name: Palestine Gendarmerie badge
45ccc1b2-62ae-540c-ba7c-d71565ea58c3.description: The Palestine Gendarmerie, established on 1 July 1921, consisted of Arabs and Jews under British officers. It consisted of cavalry, camelry and infantry units. Enlistment of recruits was regulated so as to maintain a certain proportion amongst the various sects and religious creeds, which comprised Arabs, Jews, Circassians and Druse. In 1922, the strength of the Palestine Gendarmerie was as follows: 234 Arabs, 157 Jews, 72 Circassians and 27 Druses, of whom 250 were mounted on horses and 50 on camels, the remainder consisting of infantry. The badge was usually seen worn on black kalpak hats. It consists of the British imperial crown leaned on the letters PG, the abbreviation of Palestine Gendarmerie written in capital French script. Two crossed flags in the middle of the letters PG, based on a band that displays the full name of the PALESTINE GENDARMERIE and below the date 1921 written on a small band. The flag in the right side is broken.
45ccc1b2-62ae-540c-ba7c-d71565ea58c3.author: Aida Naghawi
45ccc1b2-62ae-540c-ba7c-d71565ea58c3.keywords: Gendarmerie; Arabs; Jews; British officers; cavalry; camelry and infantry; Circassians and Druse

4656ec61-9406-5e34-94e3-612bfbb2e88c.name: *Persian carpet from Haas & Söhne*
4656ec61-9406-5e34-94e3-612bfbb2e88c.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
4656ec61-9406-5e34-94e3-612bfbb2e88c.dates: Photograph from the World Trade Exhibition 1873 in Vienna
4656ec61-9406-5e34-94e3-612bfbb2e88c.description2: Persian carpet made by Haas & Söhne in Vienna following the pattern of an original Persian carpet preserved in the Munich National Museum.

46e5760e-4ca7-5891-b293-149dd73cdb25.name: *View of Jaffa*
46e5760e-4ca7-5891-b293-149dd73cdb25.description: Travel illustrations in the 19th century, with their images of life, history and topography, had a great influence over Orientalism. This engraving appeared in a publication about the history of Turkey. Jaffa was a very important port in East Mediterranean.
46e5760e-4ca7-5891-b293-149dd73cdb25.author: Carmen Linés Viñuales

471bc9ed-d220-539b-b302-0835391b4214.name: *The Lookouts*
471bc9ed-d220-539b-b302-0835391b4214.author: Dalila Orfali
471bc9ed-d220-539b-b302-0835391b4214.description2:
After his short, initial trip to Algeria in 1846 when he stayed at Blida, the artist returned in 1847 and 1848, staying in Constantine and Biskra. From then on Algeria became his primary source of inspiration, thanks to which he created these Algerian "impressions", as well as a number of paintings and drawings and two pieces of travel writing in 1857 and 1858. The emotions evoked by experience of such a different landscape fill the first account, *Une Année dans le Sahel* (1874), as well as the writer's admiration for the people, their simplicity and their attentiveness, their habits and their customs. He also deplores the Western urbanism which has already begun to destroy the country's authenticity.  
He also visited Egypt for the inauguration of the Suez Canal. He is one of the many artists who brought a degree of humanity back to Orientalist art.

47365132-f164-5764-a7d6-518e266d0b96.name: *Arab Vase*
47365132-f164-5764-a7d6-518e266d0b96.description: Drawing of a vase known as "The Alhambra vase". The ceramic vase is a good example of the development of the Nasrid workshops. This vase came from the church of Nuestra Señora de la Asunción in Hornos (Jaén) and it was acquired by the National Museum of Archaeology in 1875. This type of vase is very rare and few of them have survived.
47365132-f164-5764-a7d6-518e266d0b96.artist: Drawing by Francisco Contreras; chromolithograph: Mariano Fuster
47365132-f164-5764-a7d6-518e266d0b96.keywords: Spanish Muslim art; applied arts; Alhambra
47365132-f164-5764-a7d6-518e266d0b96.third_name: *Jarrón Árabe recientemente adquirido por el Museo*

476f71b7-f16d-54c8-85e4-ed053fa70b87.name: Pen box
476f71b7-f16d-54c8-85e4-ed053fa70b87.description2: Penbox from Mosul. Acquired by Augustus Wollaston Franks, a curator at the British Museum who played a key role in the building of the Mediaeval collection.

478abce7-afc2-532d-82bd-fbecf067ac32.name: *One Thousand and One Nights*: decorative sketch of the palace gardens. Façade of an
478abce7-afc2-532d-82bd-fbecf067ac32.keywords: Orientalism; one thousand and one nights
478abce7-afc2-532d-82bd-fbecf067ac32.description2: The collection *One Thousand and One Nights* was translated into French in the early 18th century. The rise of Orientalism caused it to become extremely popular, appearing as the subject of numerous editions, adaptations, etc. In the 19th century, a tale from the collection was staged in one of Paris' most famous theatres (the Théâtre du Châtelet), and, as this image shows, the theatre was redecorated as an "Oriental palace" for the occasion.

47ae1491-a4bf-5c5f-98f7-d10504afcb6c.name: *Hagia Sophia. General view*
47ae1491-a4bf-5c5f-98f7-d10504afcb6c.description: Photographic print that is part of an album of different Istanbul images taken by the studio of the three Armenian brothers who, in 1880, opened a headquarters in this city. It shows the central nave of the Mosque of Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya Camii), under the main dome, facing the Eastern apse where the altar has been replaced by a *mihrab*. On the left, in the transept, the pavilion for the sultan's personal prayer. A group of men are sitting on the ground, on carpets that cover the entire surface, listening attentively. This kind of album had great success with 19th century European travellers.
47ae1491-a4bf-5c5f-98f7-d10504afcb6c.author: Rebeca C. Recio

48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.name: Portrait Album – Ottoman State Officers
48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

48d3809b-e5eb-56eb-9a31-568dd0718ce7.name: *The African*
48d3809b-e5eb-56eb-9a31-568dd0718ce7.author: DGPC
48d3809b-e5eb-56eb-9a31-568dd0718ce7.description2: As a result of the movement of artists and the attention paid along the 19th century to the traditional habits of the Portuguese people, the arts in Portugal became also focused on different cultural pluralism references, as shown in this oil painting by João António Correia.
48d3809b-e5eb-56eb-9a31-568dd0718ce7.holding_institution_org: Museu Nacional de Soares dos Reis

4a617bed-3c19-5563-b98a-4cd98cda144d.name: *Scene in the Desert*
4a617bed-3c19-5563-b98a-4cd98cda144d.description: This painting was made around 1863 when the author travelled to Morocco with Mariano Fortuny. The reason of his travel was to paint the characters and “picturesque” garments as the way of life of the people from Morocco. His experiences can be seen in his paintings and drawings. During his travels he brought exotic artworks as Egyptian sarcophagi.
4a617bed-3c19-5563-b98a-4cd98cda144d.author: Carolina Miguel Arroyo

4ae45f56-80f0-5f31-82a5-680fa0d249f9.name: Bathroom pot
4ae45f56-80f0-5f31-82a5-680fa0d249f9.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
4ae45f56-80f0-5f31-82a5-680fa0d249f9.description2: The top of this semi-open bathroom pot is decorated with a band of perforated floral motifs beneath a rounded rim. A strip of maghrebi calligraphy covers the rest of the pot's surface, reading: "Wisdom is the crown of the young, which has become a golden blindfold. Honesty is daybreak."

4b1cc99c-bdcc-51e9-bf03-770c80101277.name: Men's coat (*Mintan*)
4b1cc99c-bdcc-51e9-bf03-770c80101277.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
4b1cc99c-bdcc-51e9-bf03-770c80101277.description2: There used to be around fifty diverse styles of folk costumes worn in different ethnic areas throughout Macedonia in the 19th century and in the early 20th century. Among the most prominent were the costumes of Gorni Polog. Unlike the diverse and numerous women’s garments, men’s outfits were much simpler and rather unified. This upper garment called a *mintan* is of plain cut. It is made of silk in a striped pattern. Its only decorations are pieces of black cloth applied to the sleeves.

4b354c59-a5bb-5836-b87b-32109e77b5d3.name: Ivory box
4b354c59-a5bb-5836-b87b-32109e77b5d3.keywords: Franks; collection; collector; museums; calligraphy; inscription; exhibition
4b354c59-a5bb-5836-b87b-32109e77b5d3.description2: Acquired by Augustus Wollaston Franks, a curator at the British Museum who played a key role in the building of the Mediaeval collection.

4b5af6a4-7de4-5e18-87de-8bf5e62763db.name: Dish
4b5af6a4-7de4-5e18-87de-8bf5e62763db.description: The Orientalism or Neo-Mudéjar style gave new light to old techniques such as ceramic with lustre decoration; the Manises workshops begun again to use lustre decorations and shapes from the Middle Age period.
4b5af6a4-7de4-5e18-87de-8bf5e62763db.author: Manuel Alonso

4b603a95-53d0-5a95-be2d-d52aff93ad2c.name: Sprinkler
4b603a95-53d0-5a95-be2d-d52aff93ad2c.author: Mina Moraitou
4b603a95-53d0-5a95-be2d-d52aff93ad2c.description2: A sprinkler made of brownish glass with enamel decoration of sprigs with flowers. The sprinkler is made in a Bohemian workshop and imitates the glass production of the Istanbul workshops – the Beykoz glass. The shape with the screw stopper is identical to the Ottoman prototypes while the decoration is different and more naturalistic. Made in Bohemian workshops. A complex and well organized sales network was spread in the eastern Mediterranean and constituted a binding link between western knowledge and Islamic aesthetics preserving a lucrative market for European works of glass with shapes and decoration of oriental inspiration.

4b63a853-7b5d-5c93-8ec7-7348d5091101.name: Model in plaster
4b63a853-7b5d-5c93-8ec7-7348d5091101.description: Following on the European fascination for the oriental world and for the famous Nasrid Palace of the Alhambra (Granada), a lot of reproductions of its remarkable architecture and decorations were made and spread. José Contreras was commended as restorer and decorator and his son, Rafael (1824–1890), was the leading pioneer of this trend in 1847. His work was continued by the grandson and by a huge number of plaster-cast workshops in Granada, and very likely, in other cities. His plasterworks were very successful in the International Exhibitions and were kept in private collections and museums like South Kensington (London). These delightful polychrome models, accentuated with a black frame, represents different rooms form the Alhambra Palace as the Comares Room, with its double horseshoe.
4b63a853-7b5d-5c93-8ec7-7348d5091101.dimensions: 68 x 41 cm; 72 x 53 and 54 x 49 cm
4b63a853-7b5d-5c93-8ec7-7348d5091101.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes, Cristina Giménez

4b6b4cd7-723b-5fc1-9d39-214740318d2a.name: Panel
4b6b4cd7-723b-5fc1-9d39-214740318d2a.dimensions: Height: 61.4 cm panel, Width: 40.5 cm panel, Depth: 1.9 cm, Height: 20.6 cm each tile, Width: 20.6 cm each tile
4b6b4cd7-723b-5fc1-9d39-214740318d2a.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
4b6b4cd7-723b-5fc1-9d39-214740318d2a.keywords: Ceramic; earthenware; collector; collection; ceramic tile; tile panel; tilework; vegetal decoration; floral decoration; revival; Syrian tiles
4b6b4cd7-723b-5fc1-9d39-214740318d2a.materials: Buff-coloured earthenware, with painting over a white slip
4b6b4cd7-723b-5fc1-9d39-214740318d2a.description2:
William De Morgan designed and produced pictorial tile panels. The smaller versions were sometimes framed for display as pictures, or used in fireplaces. Larger panels, would have been used in architectural settings, grander fireplaces, bathroom walls, and for the decoration of smoking rooms on ocean liners of the P&O company.  
De Morgan had a great interest in Islamic tilework, much of which was thought to be Persian in the 19th century. The Islamic-inspired patterns and the dominant range of colours (turquoise, blue, green, purple), were also often termed 'Persian'. They were in fact more closely related to the tilework of Syria and Turkey. The different regional types of Islamic tile were little understood, despite the acquisition of large quantities of Islamic tiles by European collectors.

4b719ab5-caa8-53d7-a185-809f12af918c.name: Venetian mirror
4b719ab5-caa8-53d7-a185-809f12af918c.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
4b719ab5-caa8-53d7-a185-809f12af918c.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
4b719ab5-caa8-53d7-a185-809f12af918c.description2: This magnificent wooden mirror, carved and decorated with gold leaf, is deeply moulded (14cm) and engraved with floral patterns. Two different tones of gold leaf, matte and gloss, were used. This Italian style carving was very fashionable with the 19th century nobility.

4ba698dd-340a-5068-ac6e-53bd809620f8.name: *Old Oriental Gilt and Enamelled Glass Vessels extant in Public Museums and Private Collections*
4ba698dd-340a-5068-ac6e-53bd809620f8.author: Mina Moraitou
4ba698dd-340a-5068-ac6e-53bd809620f8.description2: An illustrated publication by Gustav Schmoranz on the history of Mamluk enamelled glass and example from public and private collections. It was published with the sanction and assistance of the imperial Austrian Ministry of Education by the Imperial Handels- Museum of Vienna. It contains the ex libris of Antonis Benakis.

4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.name: Antonio del Valle y Serrano, Marquis of Villa-Huerta
4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This vignetted bust shot albumen portrait shows the elegance and the character of Antonio del Valle y Serrano, marquis of Villa-Huerta and stepson of the marquis of Cerralbo.
4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes
4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.third_name: Antonio del Valle y Serrano, marqués de Villa-Huerta

4cb2c7b0-e6c5-5421-ba04-8e3b26cad183.name: Purse
4cb2c7b0-e6c5-5421-ba04-8e3b26cad183.description: Miser’s purses, also known as ring or string purses, were very popular feminine accessories during the 19th century and even the first decades of the following century. The Cerralbo Museum has a small collection of these kinds of pieces, souvenirs from Istanbul. This Turkish and colourful beadwork one, with its traditional geometric pattern and the promise of a fashionable outfit, would have surely delighted any lady.
4cb2c7b0-e6c5-5421-ba04-8e3b26cad183.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes

4d5b7131-33fe-5c5d-8076-ab9568f98e94.name: Iron coffee roaster
4d5b7131-33fe-5c5d-8076-ab9568f98e94.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
4d5b7131-33fe-5c5d-8076-ab9568f98e94.author: Huda Kilani
4d5b7131-33fe-5c5d-8076-ab9568f98e94.keywords: coffee; coffee roasting; coffee beans; domestic furnishing
4d5b7131-33fe-5c5d-8076-ab9568f98e94.description2: Circular iron coffee roaster with long handle decorated with zigzag and triangle motifs. Coffee-drinking in a communal setting is an essential part of traditions in Bedouin communities to celebrate or mourn.

4e27b872-ecb5-5764-8ab4-12316b90ca21.name: *Marketplace, Morocco*
4e27b872-ecb5-5764-8ab4-12316b90ca21.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
4e27b872-ecb5-5764-8ab4-12316b90ca21.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
4e27b872-ecb5-5764-8ab4-12316b90ca21.description2: This imposing oil painting shows a caravan apparently leaving the gate of a North African city, perhaps Fez, with much commotion going on on either side of the camels and their guides. Although the title of the painting suggest a market scene, in reality little trading activity can be seen apart from an old hooded man sitting next to a large basket with shoes on the right. On the left a group of African men and a little child in a burnous admire the skills of a snake charmer, while his monkey next to him looks on intently. In the background, large numbers of men, apparently both of Arab and Berber origin, and dressed in a variety of traditional dress, walk along or stand together in groups conversing, oblivious to the camels, donkeys and horses moving inbetween them. Ferenc Eisenhut was an Austro-Hungarian painter, known for his monumentally conceived genre scenes of Eastern life and vistas. He was the only internationally acclaimed, Hungarian Orientalist painter.

4e4b02a5-e3a8-5005-84bb-56a2cfc8b07a.name: Sword with scabbard
4e4b02a5-e3a8-5005-84bb-56a2cfc8b07a.description: A sword and scabbard decorated with geometric and floral motifs and crafted in southern Morocco in the 19th century. Sword blades were imported from Europe, especially from Toledo in Spain, or from Damascus in Syria.
4e4b02a5-e3a8-5005-84bb-56a2cfc8b07a.keywords: Trade; arms; armours; metalwork; geometric motifs; geometric decoration; floral decoration; vegetal motifs; vegetal decoration;craftsmanship; war; warfare; military objects

4ef4f4cf-3d12-58c3-8cc2-6c635b02100f.name: Plate
4ef4f4cf-3d12-58c3-8cc2-6c635b02100f.description2: Plain inverted rim, shallow body, ring base. Light brown paste, white slip, transparent glaze. Under glaze decoration in cobalt blue, turquoise, dark green, yellow, red and black with black outlines. At the centre of a scalloped sun-shaped medallion formed by intertwined *rumi* and palmette motifs is a star and crescent motif, itself at the centre of a scalloped nine-petal medallion. The remaining surface is covered with a geometric design composed of eight-pointed stars, and the rim is decorated with a wide border of rumi-palmette motifs. The reverse of the plate bears the inscription, *Kütahya Azim Çini Fabrikası Mamulatı* (Product of the Kütahya azim Tie Factory).

4fba9c3c-f84d-510f-bba6-f6a6783a23b3.name: Nusretiye Mosque and the Imperial Gun Foundry in Tophane
4fba9c3c-f84d-510f-bba6-f6a6783a23b3.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
4fba9c3c-f84d-510f-bba6-f6a6783a23b3.description2: A frequently employed device in Robertson's Istanbul photographs is the inclusion of the one or more human figures in the foreground – indeed, this is something of a trademark of Robertson’s work. There were two main reasons for the inclusion of these figures. For one thing, the artist used them as a way of creating a more natural scene. The other was to provide one or more reference points so that the photograph’s viewers could get an idea of the dimensions of the scene they were looking at and of the elements contained therein.

50c3aa93-d400-5d9f-824f-b394e33b63a6.name: Beylical salon
50c3aa93-d400-5d9f-824f-b394e33b63a6.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
50c3aa93-d400-5d9f-824f-b394e33b63a6.keywords: Palace; Husainid dynasty; carved wood; mashrabiya
50c3aa93-d400-5d9f-824f-b394e33b63a6.description2: This beylical salon is furnished with carved wood from the beylik era, and consists of three large double-seater benches and four smaller benches with full armrests and topped with a pediment. The set is decorated with rectangular panels in the middle and square panels on the sides, all decorated with a mashrabiya. A wood carved table completes the set.

522f2144-3034-5e4d-9bc3-6ef8c6f5ecd0.name: Veil
522f2144-3034-5e4d-9bc3-6ef8c6f5ecd0.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
522f2144-3034-5e4d-9bc3-6ef8c6f5ecd0.author: Huda Kilani
522f2144-3034-5e4d-9bc3-6ef8c6f5ecd0.keywords: Linen fabric; natural cotton; embroidered patterns
522f2144-3034-5e4d-9bc3-6ef8c6f5ecd0.materials: Linen, silk; hand weaving, hand embroidered, natural dyes
522f2144-3034-5e4d-9bc3-6ef8c6f5ecd0.description2: Three natural cotton and linen fabrics sewn and decorated with cross-stitch with embroidered folkloric patterns (known as “cypress trees”, “amulets”, “keys”, “saw” and “Shuayb teeth”). They are mainly in red with some green colour; a small linen fringe dangles from two sides. The veil was an essential piece of women’s dress. Girls started preparing their trousseau (clothes, shawls, and other belongings collected for marriage) at the age of ten. Married women had various embroidered costumes worn for special occasions. As the economy of the Jordanian territory in the late 19th century-early 20th century relied on trades and crafts, new waves of traders and artisans started to arrive and to settle. Thus, traditional costumes reflect a variegated population composition, demographic changes, personal attire and local rites.

5250886a-a6a0-5674-9156-a5f133b9cfe8.name: Kerosene lamp
5250886a-a6a0-5674-9156-a5f133b9cfe8.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
5250886a-a6a0-5674-9156-a5f133b9cfe8.author: Huda Kilani
5250886a-a6a0-5674-9156-a5f133b9cfe8.description2: A cylindrical container filled with gas and injected with air heats a group of emerging pipes from the cylinder, which are surrounded by glass to shield them from air and assist in hashing its light into place. Kerosene lamps were used to light the streets of Amman until the first electricity generator began to operate. The beginning of the 20th century marked the re-urbanisation of Amman after 500 years of abandonment.

52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.name: *The Virgin at the Nile*
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.author: Marina Minozzi
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.keywords: Egyptomania; Orientalism; painting; Orientalist paintings; artistic exchange; Egyptology; archaeology; imaginary trips; reinvention; historical events in painting; exoticism; architectural trends in painting; Italian painters; travel
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.description2: Federico Faruffini made his debut as a painter at the 1856 annual exposition of Brera. In his works the artist breaks away from the academic rule of ‘disegno’, or artistic drawing, and focuses on colour. The painting *The Virgin at the Nile* shows a sacrifice. Numerous study sketches survive. They attest that the artist was well educated on customs, traditions and architecture of ancient Egypt. In the painting the artist proposes the integration of two separate themes through different rendering styles: on the brighter upper part he sets the historic characters and in the lower zone the more narrative one, of obvious academic inspiration. The painting was brought to Paris by the artist after he decided to leave Italy because he was having difficulty finding work. After the artist committed suicide, *The Virgin at the Nile* was on display at the retrospective exhibition in Rome in 1883 where Faruffini’s entire portfolio was reconsidered, and the painting was declared his undiscussed masterpiece.
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

en: Villari, A., in Elena di Majo and Matteo Lafranconi (eds), *Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Moderna. Le Collezioni. Il XIX secolo*, Milan: Electa, 2006, cat. 1.21.

52bc1f5c-19f1-5c15-8794-630ecd367289.name: Amulet
52bc1f5c-19f1-5c15-8794-630ecd367289.type: Cultic Object; ornament; talismanic object; jewellery
52bc1f5c-19f1-5c15-8794-630ecd367289.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
52bc1f5c-19f1-5c15-8794-630ecd367289.author: Huda Kilani
52bc1f5c-19f1-5c15-8794-630ecd367289.keywords: Talisman; crescent; tusks; wild boar; heal of Gazalle
52bc1f5c-19f1-5c15-8794-630ecd367289.description2: This object is a piece of horse jewellery, an amulet worn around the horse's neck to ward off misfortune. Horse jewellery was used among Bedouins and villagers communities. This amulet consists of a silver-cased crescent composed of two joined tusks of wild boar. A ¼ Majidi Ottoman gold coin dangles from the crescent with three crescents and stars at the end. The silver chain is called “heal of gazelle”.

52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.name: Lithographs after the panoramic photograph taken by Robertson and Beato, *Faust: Poligrafisch Illustrirte*, Zeitschrift, 1857, Vienna
52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.keywords: Istanbul panorama; Faust; tower of War Ministry in Beyazıt
52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.description2: James Robertson is the first Istanbul photographer known to have taken 360 degree panoramic photographs of the city. The first panorama, which was taken in May 1854 from the War Ministry tower in Beyazıt, consists of twelve separate photographs. The most successful printed reproductions based on Robertson’s photographs curiously enough were produced in Vienna. Issues of *Faust* published during 1857 report fascinating bits of information as well as pictures that are important to the history of printing and visual arts in the Ottoman Empire. A plate published in *Faust* contained a panoramic view from the Istanbul Beyazıt tower that is made from Robertson’s panorama.

532b4aae-3420-5fef-ba89-4653325f00d7.name: *A young and an old Turk*
532b4aae-3420-5fef-ba89-4653325f00d7.description2: Carol Popp de Szathmari was born in Transylvania, but later settled in Bucharest, Wallachia, where he worked as court painter of princes Alexandru Dimitrie Ghica, Gheorghe Bibescu and Alexandru Ioan Cuza. During the reign of prince Carol of Hohenzollern, he was also court photographer. He is the author of five photographic albums with images of people and places from Bucharest and other regions in Romania, among which there are depictions of people belonging to the ethnic minorities of Romania, such as the Turks. He travelled twice to Istanbul, in 1860 and 1864, as member of prince Alexandru Ioan Cuza’s suite. During the Crimean War (1854-1855) he photographed the Russian and Turkish armies that occupied Wallachia and then went to Crimea, where he took more than 200 photos of the fights.

5401f2b8-18f4-599c-b201-a2d99f1b35ce.name: Dar Zarrouk
5401f2b8-18f4-599c-b201-a2d99f1b35ce.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
5401f2b8-18f4-599c-b201-a2d99f1b35ce.history: This palace was built in the early 19th century on a huge plot of land in La Manouba belonging to 'Ali Zarrouk, the great-grandson of Hammouda Pacha Bey's minister, 'Ali Arbi Zarrouk. The architectural style chosen by 'Ali Zarrouk is evidence for the fashion amongst the urban elites of the time for comfortable, luxurious, houses in a European (and particularly Italian) style. The palace is currently the seat of the La Manouba local government.
5401f2b8-18f4-599c-b201-a2d99f1b35ce.keywords: Architecture; art; painting; stucco; mosaic; marble; ceramics
5401f2b8-18f4-599c-b201-a2d99f1b35ce.description2: This tall white façade with shuttered windows and a curved Italian-style door sits at the heart of a lush garden. Inside, a series of hallways on the ground floor, all leading to different rooms, are built with stunning Italian marble door frames and paving. The flat ceiling is decorated with pendant vaults. On the first floor, an innovative covered patio is beautifully lit by a Venetian crystal chandelier. Four reception rooms surround a central hall. The imported marble and faience pottery contrast with the shining gold gilding on the furnishings and the reflection from the huge windows and mirrors.

54061b49-5654-5a34-bb57-ed20127e9164.name: Gülabdan
54061b49-5654-5a34-bb57-ed20127e9164.description2: It is known that there were workshops producing glass vessels around Beykoz in Istanbul in the 19th century. The first glass workshop was founded by Mevlevi Dervish Mehmed Dede during the reign of Selim III (1789-1807). There were European glass craftsmen working in those workshops as well. Cups, bottles, jugs, etc. made of colourful, colourless and opal glass were among Beykoz' productions. This *gülabdan* (a small flask for sprinkling rose water) is a Beykoz production. Its body is milk white on which floral patterns in dark pink, green and yellow were placed.

541e7afc-c735-5bac-ad3a-928530f9d141.name: Horse adornment used in wedding ceremonies (*Gushnik*)
541e7afc-c735-5bac-ad3a-928530f9d141.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
541e7afc-c735-5bac-ad3a-928530f9d141.keywords: Horse ornament; monistra; horse jewellery; accessories; marriage; wedding
541e7afc-c735-5bac-ad3a-928530f9d141.description2: A *gushnik* is an article used for the adornment of horses. This item shows the tradition of decorating horses on some festive occasions, particularly on weddings. The decoration consists of a string and numerous ornaments made of *monistra* (tiny beads in varied colours) applied on canvas. The pendants are decorated with varied patterns and have fringes at the bottom.

54310c6d-87ca-585e-b552-bcb1c5951fe3.name: Dress
54310c6d-87ca-585e-b552-bcb1c5951fe3.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
54310c6d-87ca-585e-b552-bcb1c5951fe3.author: Huda Kilani
54310c6d-87ca-585e-b552-bcb1c5951fe3.materials: Silk, cotton; hand woven Syrian silk fabric (brocade)
54310c6d-87ca-585e-b552-bcb1c5951fe3.description2: This dress of al-Druze (Druse) women is made of a long grey with green and silver brocade, pursed narrow sleeves, wide, open square shaped chest, pursed at the middle and wide at the bottom with ruffles and a cotton liner. This object illustrates the variegated social composition and demographic changes in the Jordanian territory in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The al-Druze tribes migrated from Syria (Hawran) to north east Jordan in the early twentieth century because of their support for the Syrian revolution against the French occupation. The traditional Druse and other Jordanian costumes were influenced by the local trade and economic activities: as illustrated in this case, they were often made of silk textiles, produced in Syria and traded to Jordan and Palestine.

5451b48d-8d64-533c-b7e9-be06d8f670ea.name: Water Carrier’s Portable Water Jug
5451b48d-8d64-533c-b7e9-be06d8f670ea.type: Copper alloy and ceramic water ewer with fibre rope netting
5451b48d-8d64-533c-b7e9-be06d8f670ea.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
5451b48d-8d64-533c-b7e9-be06d8f670ea.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
5451b48d-8d64-533c-b7e9-be06d8f670ea.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
5451b48d-8d64-533c-b7e9-be06d8f670ea.materials: Engraved and punched sheet copper alloy; ceramic base; fibre rope
5451b48d-8d64-533c-b7e9-be06d8f670ea.description2: This large ovoid ewer consists of a metal top and ceramic base. From the hemispherical shoulder rises a tall, waisted cylindrical neck with central collar. The mouth is covered by a bulbous, domical lid. The ewer has a strong, angular handle of roughly square section and a tall, obliquely rising body spout, which is connected to the neck by a curved tube and tapers towards the prominent, slightly waisted mouth section. The entire upper part of the ewer is decorated with incised horizontal bands of plaiting, abstract floral decoration, pseudo-inscriptions and running animals. The spout shows a dense system of punched, arched lines and incised decorative bands near its base. The undecorated ceramic base of the ewer is secured by netting created from fibre ropes. Thicker ropes of the same material, probably used for carrying the ewer, are attached. A ewer identical to this one appears in Ludwig Deutsch’s painting of the Al-Azhar mosque (SH_66).

54a75fca-9a38-5dc2-9f8e-80faf09f8470.name: *The Artist Girl and Her Studio*
54a75fca-9a38-5dc2-9f8e-80faf09f8470.keywords: Painting; Halil Pasha; orientalist Turkish painters
54a75fca-9a38-5dc2-9f8e-80faf09f8470.description2: The basis of Turkish painting drawing influence from western tradition was laid when *Mühendishane-i Berr-i Hümayun* (the Naval Academy) opened in 1795. Halil Pasha, who had been a student of the painting courses held at the Academy, was foremost among the painters with a military background who founded a western style art tradition in Turkey. He worked with Jean Leon Gerome in his atelier in Paris. He provided a unique distinction to the analysis of impressionist light and colour, and was an example of artists dealing with impressionist technique. Because of his qualified knowledge about anatomy and his interest in depicting the human figure, Halil Pasha had a unique place in Turkish Art History.

554cc278-49e0-58cd-8147-15ce5f2c7002.name: Lady Layard’s jewellery
554cc278-49e0-58cd-8147-15ce5f2c7002.description2: Layard, excavator of Nineveh and other sites, had this necklace made as a wedding present for his wife. It combines ancient cylinder seals in contemporary gold settings. Said to have been much admired during dinner with Queen Victoria in 1873.

555612b1-3b0e-5939-af4c-dcd61c208ab2.name: *Reading The Qu'ran*
555612b1-3b0e-5939-af4c-dcd61c208ab2.keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters
555612b1-3b0e-5939-af4c-dcd61c208ab2.description2: Osman Hamdi focused on dilemmas such as East and West, love and hate, life and death. While stylistically reminiscent of western Orientalist painters, his works reflect a more nuanced appreciation of Ottoman society and culture. He also gave importance to details while reflecting the colourful scenes of Turkish culture, traditional architecture, Ottoman fashion and domestic and social life of the women in the Ottoman Empire. And it’s obvious that he is the first painter who used human figures in the western style.

55d4b6d2-fc7e-5bc6-a971-7a640559de05.name: *A Muslim man praying*
55d4b6d2-fc7e-5bc6-a971-7a640559de05.author: Ámparo López
55d4b6d2-fc7e-5bc6-a971-7a640559de05.description2: One of the drawings by Fortuny, one of the most important European painters of the last quarter of the 19th century. He travelled to Morocco in 1863 and he was taken by the light, colour and characters of the country. He was an important collector of Islamic artworks, some of them depicted in his paintings.

55e346ff-6f0e-5e17-90fe-1d309d2d7056.name: Painted chest
55e346ff-6f0e-5e17-90fe-1d309d2d7056.author: Xenia Politou
55e346ff-6f0e-5e17-90fe-1d309d2d7056.description2: The main façade of the chest is adorned with a composition of flowers, branches and fruits in curvilinear compartments, while the corners depict female figures flanked by columns. The interior of the lid shows a landscape with five male figures: a man with a European garment sitting on the ground observing another figure dressed in European clothes, two figures on horseback with Ottoman costumes and a European traveller. The panels in the style of rocailles that adorn both the main and the side views of the chest, the compositions of fruit and flowers and the soft colours refer to the prevailing influence of the rococo style that is dominant in the frescos of the mansions of Lesvos the late 18th century. Both the structure of the mansions and the decorative repertoire follow Ottoman aesthetic as these were by influenced by European art but blending baroque, rococo and neoclassical styles.

56669d0c-f1dc-5ef6-92fc-a676c2150aa7.name: Wooden shelving unit
56669d0c-f1dc-5ef6-92fc-a676c2150aa7.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
56669d0c-f1dc-5ef6-92fc-a676c2150aa7.description2: This shelf belonged to a traditional house in the town of Ksar Hellal. It would been hung from a wall as decoration, holding vases and perfume sprinklers, as well as weapons. It is characterized by its floral patterns with birds, flowers and leaves painted in stylised colours on a pale green background, all surrounding a multicolour fish.

56bae231-ad09-5568-8e83-1f1aa7115444.name: Buckles (*Pafti*)
56bae231-ad09-5568-8e83-1f1aa7115444.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
56bae231-ad09-5568-8e83-1f1aa7115444.keywords: Buckles; live gold-plating; wedding; marriage; accessories; costume
56bae231-ad09-5568-8e83-1f1aa7115444.materials: Silver, filigree, granulation. Decoration with semi-precious stones, pearls and live gold plating
56bae231-ad09-5568-8e83-1f1aa7115444.description2: Buckles were distinctive articles of adornment used throughout the centuries by Macedonian women. They were the most frequently worn and most exquisite articles of adornment in Macedonian women’s folk attire. Buckles used to be adorned with stylized geometric and floral patterns, the artistic effect having been emphasized by the application of decorative stones, filigree ornaments, gold-plating, pearls, mother-of-pearl, corals, chains and other embellishments. This outstanding set of buckles in leaf shapes is decorated with pearls and semi-precious stones, by application of the technique of "live" gold-plating.

56ca4b0e-6b96-51e1-9a41-815aad91e661.name: Geomantic instrument
56ca4b0e-6b96-51e1-9a41-815aad91e661.description2: Geomantic instrument. Signed by the craftsman Muhammad b.Khutlukh al-Mawsili. Acquired by Augustus Wollaston Franks, a curator at the British Museum who played a key role in the building of the Mediaeval collection.

5714f381-6e11-56d5-9801-fef85803c128.name: Wedding dress
5714f381-6e11-56d5-9801-fef85803c128.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
5714f381-6e11-56d5-9801-fef85803c128.author: Huda Kilani
5714f381-6e11-56d5-9801-fef85803c128.materials: Linen and silk; hand woven and hand embroidered
5714f381-6e11-56d5-9801-fef85803c128.description2: Long black dress, wide at the bottom with narrow sleeves, rounded neck and open chest. Silk linen appliqué, hand embroidery with cross-stitch on the sides, back panel, chest, and sleeves with embroidered folkloric patterns. On the chest: necklace, cypress tree. Side: ivy, amulets, “feathers”. Front: small cypress tree on silk. Back: ivy, cypress tree, pillows, pasha tents. Sleeve: ivy, feather, triangle (amulets). Palestinian women's costumes varied according to each Palestinian city and geographical area. Costumes in the mountain regions were different from those of coastal and desert areas, and had a distinguished embroidery. This costume represents village style. Girls started preparing their trousseau (clothes, shawls and other belongings they collected for their marriage) at the age of ten. Married women's costumes were heavily embroidered. Palestinian weavers used traditional spinning processes using manual spindles to prepare the cotton and linen threads imported from Egypt. Ashkelon city weavers used light vertical hand looms (*Majdalawi* looms) to produce linen fabrics, while silk fabrics were spindled and woven in Syria.

571c2e73-e0f1-5b98-b748-e41a5e7ff2b7.name: Door carved on wood
571c2e73-e0f1-5b98-b748-e41a5e7ff2b7.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
571c2e73-e0f1-5b98-b748-e41a5e7ff2b7.description2: This door from the interior of the museum of the Palais du Bardo is made of carved and studded oak, with two panels on either side. The frames are studded along their horizontal axis, and the panels are richly decorated with flower vase motifs.

5737c1ee-cc7f-51c5-a3a0-7d7bf8615842.name: Iznik bottle
5737c1ee-cc7f-51c5-a3a0-7d7bf8615842.author: Mina Moraitou
5737c1ee-cc7f-51c5-a3a0-7d7bf8615842.keywords: Iznik; Egypt; Greeks; collecting; exhibition; London
5737c1ee-cc7f-51c5-a3a0-7d7bf8615842.description2: An Iznik flask, with a spherical body and a long neck, is decorated with polychrome flowers: roses, hyacinth and carnations and the neck displays vertical panels. Bought by A. Benakis in Cairo in 1920 and according to the etiquettes under the base it was part of the 1885 exhibition at the Burlington Arts Club in London and of the 1925 exhibition in Alexandria. Ottoman c. 1575.

5742022d-5251-5bf2-9309-1b5f081234cd.name: *A Costume from Capri*
5742022d-5251-5bf2-9309-1b5f081234cd.author: DGPC
5742022d-5251-5bf2-9309-1b5f081234cd.description2: Until the 19th century, Portuguese painting focussed on landscape and local habits. The new interest for travelling and for other cultures can be seen in this oil painting by Silva Porto portraying a girl from the Island of Capri and her costume.
5742022d-5251-5bf2-9309-1b5f081234cd.holding_institution_org: Museu Nacional de Soares dos Reis

576f26e0-f45e-5486-860f-0324e1f36b51.name: Bracelet
576f26e0-f45e-5486-860f-0324e1f36b51.description: This silver bracelet is decorated with cobalt blue and enamel and bears an inscription from an Arabic poem. Crafted in Essaouira in the 20th century, it is very likely to have been made for a European woman. Cobalt was a European import.
576f26e0-f45e-5486-860f-0324e1f36b51.keywords: Trade; raw materials; finished products; cobalt-blue; applied arts; enamelling; inscription; decorative inscription; Moroccan craftsmanship for European market; craftsmanship; traditional craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmen

57952ce7-c1d9-5593-a21a-cd6480d6eec9.name: Illuminated Qur’an manuscript
