57952ce7-c1d9-5593-a21a-cd6480d6eec9.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
57952ce7-c1d9-5593-a21a-cd6480d6eec9.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
57952ce7-c1d9-5593-a21a-cd6480d6eec9.materials: European paper, black ink, pigments, gilding, pasteboard, leather
57952ce7-c1d9-5593-a21a-cd6480d6eec9.description2: 19th-century Qur’an manuscripts produced in Istanbul and the Ottoman Empire continued many Islamic art traditions, but could not entirely escape the increasing taste for Western aesthetics. The quality of this Qur’an manuscript suggests that it might have been executed for a member of the Imperial household. The radiant opening double-page shows two delicate cartouches with ‘Al Fatiha’ and the beginning of ‘Al Baqara’ set into a majestic framework of gilt floral arabesque cartouches. The main body of the text is executed in finest black naskh, 15 lines to the page, the sura headings written in white riqa' on a solid golden ground. Beyond the gold margins, delicated medallions mark important subdivisions in the text. The last double page shows the end of sura 113 and sura 114 on the right and the dedication page on the left. Both texts are embedded in rectangular panels accentuated with richly gilt and blue ornamentation. Beyond, the entire page is covered with delicate sprays and leaves painted in solid gold.

57d9ec8b-2100-527f-abb2-8188927bef19.name: *The Gate of a Mosque, Istanbul*
57d9ec8b-2100-527f-abb2-8188927bef19.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
57d9ec8b-2100-527f-abb2-8188927bef19.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
57d9ec8b-2100-527f-abb2-8188927bef19.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
57d9ec8b-2100-527f-abb2-8188927bef19.description2: This oil painting shows the entrance gate to an Ottoman mosque or mausoleum complex, set in a lush shaded garden with majestic trees, its tall pointed minaret soaring high above the tiled awnings of the surrounding wall. Two turbaned old men, one seated on the pavement at the gate, the other standing to face him, accentuate the scene on the street outside. The painter of this somewhat melancholy scene, Halil Bey, was trained under Gerome and Courtoix. Under the influence of European artists and encouraged by the tastes of the Ottoman court, the arts underwent a great deal of transformation in the 13th/ 19th century. Painting in western styles gained increasing acceptance, and several local artists now concentrated on depicting their surroundings in a manner and style which they had learned in painting and drawing classes given by European instructors, either in Ottoman cities, or - as in the case of Halil Bey - in the prominent European centres of art.

57e870a3-328c-5454-8a46-128fb0cb4e2a.name: Pair of vases and pedestals
57e870a3-328c-5454-8a46-128fb0cb4e2a.description: The interlacing and the flower decoration of this pair of glass vases can be considered an example of the great influence exerted by the Turkish or Orientalist revival. The glass factories of the Austro-Hungarian Empire played an important role in the spreading of this style.
57e870a3-328c-5454-8a46-128fb0cb4e2a.author: Ana Cabrera
57e870a3-328c-5454-8a46-128fb0cb4e2a.keywords: Turkish style; Applied Arts; Production of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode

582735bb-91b8-5a1b-b50e-a4d74176b7d7.name: Knife
582735bb-91b8-5a1b-b50e-a4d74176b7d7.holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée
582735bb-91b8-5a1b-b50e-a4d74176b7d7.author: Bechir Yazidi
582735bb-91b8-5a1b-b50e-a4d74176b7d7.keywords: Tunisian army; Musée de l'Armée; Palais de la Rose
582735bb-91b8-5a1b-b50e-a4d74176b7d7.description2: The surface of this silver-plated bronze knife is covered in beautiful engravings, and the handle is decorated with floral motifs. Various coats of arms are engraved on the blade, along with a stylised ship with an Arabic inscription on the other side. The handle is 65 cm long and the blade is 21 cm long.

58d8569e-9dce-5ab4-bed2-63c6b0b22bb0.name: Cabinet on stand
58d8569e-9dce-5ab4-bed2-63c6b0b22bb0.description: The Neo-Mudéjar style gave new light to different workshops and techniques. As a consequence of this revival woodwork technique for furniture, such as the inlay in Granada style, was recreated in different pieces of furniture such as this cabinet. The decoration of stars and interlacing arabesques at the front of the cabinet shows the influence of the Mudéjar art.
58d8569e-9dce-5ab4-bed2-63c6b0b22bb0.author: Ana Cabrera
58d8569e-9dce-5ab4-bed2-63c6b0b22bb0.keywords: Neo-mudejar style; Applied ArtsProduction of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode

593969dc-7368-5182-961d-c81a464474fc.name: Bridal headdress (*Kiska*)
593969dc-7368-5182-961d-c81a464474fc.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
593969dc-7368-5182-961d-c81a464474fc.keywords: Decorative pin; kiska; apotropaic intention; amulet; talisman; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; wedding; marriage
593969dc-7368-5182-961d-c81a464474fc.description2: Hairpins and other articles of adornment worn on the head were inevitable elements of Macedonian women's attire in the 19th century and at the beginning of the 20th century. This distinctive decorative pin – *kiska* – was used for supporting the hat or scarf. This type of jewellery also conveyed a symbolic meaning and served an apotropaic purpose in addition to its decorative function. The pear-shaped ornament was made by application of filigree and granulation techniques. It is adorned with pellets and decorative stones in varied colours. Tiny coins are suspended on chains at the bottom of the ornament.

59c2a789-38b6-526c-8c2e-10450f77128f.name: Long Moorish musket
59c2a789-38b6-526c-8c2e-10450f77128f.description: This musket, along with other pieces, was taken by Salvador de Foronda, a member of the Spanish Army, awarded for his actions in battle. He was a relative of the Marquis of Cerralbo and donated to his uncle’s museum these exceptional pieces in 1918. The Moorish musket, a long firearm that could be shot with a single arm while riding the horse, was described by Salvador as “one of the most ancient and authentic", a truly beauty with damascene work, romantically infused with the testimony of the war.
59c2a789-38b6-526c-8c2e-10450f77128f.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes
59c2a789-38b6-526c-8c2e-10450f77128f.materials: Wood, metal, fabric; handmade, damascene work

59e106e1-b0a2-5505-af4e-7abfde04a90a.name: Belt
59e106e1-b0a2-5505-af4e-7abfde04a90a.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
59e106e1-b0a2-5505-af4e-7abfde04a90a.author: Huda Kilani
59e106e1-b0a2-5505-af4e-7abfde04a90a.keywords: Leather; belt; embellished; niello; rosette buckles; silver
59e106e1-b0a2-5505-af4e-7abfde04a90a.description2: Leather belt embellished with silver pieces decorated in niello with patterns and symbols at the end. Two silver rosette buckles at the end form a locking mechanism. This is an object produced by Circassian craftsmen. The immigration of the Circassians to the Ottoman Empire started in the middle of 19th century and continued until 1900. The Circassian communities migrated mostly to the eastern Arab countries, with which they had spiritual and religious links. They brought with them their traditional activities, crafts and decorative patterns. All these elements soon mingled with the local Arab society and became part of the social and economic landscape of the Arab countries.

59e91077-81f0-5cb2-9fc1-2e7eb98c95ab.name: Turkish woman
59e91077-81f0-5cb2-9fc1-2e7eb98c95ab.description2: The Zangaki brothers were a pair of photographers working in Egypt who sold "Orientalist" photos to Western tourists. This photograph for example, responds to Western stereotypes by depicting a Turkish woman lying nonchalantly by shisha pipe.

5adbfb98-b45f-586e-9adf-ca2c828986da.name: A photograph of the Arms Factory in Fez (*Dar al-makina*)
5adbfb98-b45f-586e-9adf-ca2c828986da.description: A photograph depicting workers at the Arms Factory in Fez.
5adbfb98-b45f-586e-9adf-ca2c828986da.holder: The Inspection of the Historic Monuments
5adbfb98-b45f-586e-9adf-ca2c828986da.keywords: Industrialisation; industrialists; Italians in Morocco; social changes; work; labour; workers; machine; technical innovation; urban life; urban space; urbanisation; changes in warfare; protectorate; weapons; arms; armours; firearms; market

5c6bfb8e-5045-5559-8078-f4e37350944b.name: Pillowcase
5c6bfb8e-5045-5559-8078-f4e37350944b.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
5c6bfb8e-5045-5559-8078-f4e37350944b.description2: Textiles and embroidery found a wide array of uses which reflect the imaginations of Turkish women. In these textiles, silk, golden and silver threads were used for embroidery. From the 18th and 19th century on – when Western influence started – almost every colour found use and by using different tones of the same colour, the illusion of light and depth was created. Instead of human and animal figures, floral design, fruits, or calligraphy, ship and architectural patterns became more popular. This piece was made in the Hereke Plant, founded in 1843. There is one big star and crescent in the middle while there are four smaller ones in the corners. The base is covered with plenty of stars and dots.

5cf8b622-bc23-5c90-a393-46a79bb0514b.name: Reliquary of St-George Chiopolites from Aivali
5cf8b622-bc23-5c90-a393-46a79bb0514b.author: Ballian 1992, 84, no. 44
5cf8b622-bc23-5c90-a393-46a79bb0514b.description2: The reliquary contained the head of George Chiopolites, who was martyred in Aïvali / Kydonies in 1807. The container made for the head has intricate rococo decoration with ribbons, bows, roses, blank heraldic shields and St George holding the attributes of a neomartyr under the imposing two-headed eagle of ecclesiastical authority. From the mid-eighteenth century, thanks to special administrative treatment or privileges, the inhabitants of Aïvali transformed what had been a small fishing village into a flourishing commercial centre on the Aeolian coast. The inscription on the reliquary refers to the goldsmith and to the Guild of Soap-Makers, which was one of the biggest trade associations in the town. It also refers to Sophronios, who oversaw the commissioning, and has been identified to the parish priest and a close relative of Theophilos Kaïris, a teacher at the Academy of Kydonies who was later expelled from the Church under the free Greek state for his revolutionary ideas and was to die in prison, the last ideologue of the Enlightenment.

en: Ballian, Anna, *Treasures from the Greek Communities of Asia Minor and Eastern Thrace. Collections from the Benaki Museum*, Athens: Benaki Museum, 1992.

5e131b15-3042-5b4a-bc07-e72c9fb0b7fb.name: Figures in Turkish style
5e131b15-3042-5b4a-bc07-e72c9fb0b7fb.description: In these two porcelain figures, it is showed through the clothes, and combined with the Rococo style of the bases. Produced by many European manufactures at the time, this kind of objects could be easily found in rooms as the *fumoir*, usually decorated in an Orientalist style to recreate exoticism.
5e131b15-3042-5b4a-bc07-e72c9fb0b7fb.author: Isabel Ortega Fernández
5e131b15-3042-5b4a-bc07-e72c9fb0b7fb.keywords: Production of applied art in Europe in the Islamic mode; Turkish influence
5e131b15-3042-5b4a-bc07-e72c9fb0b7fb.materials: Moulded; enamelled, painted and gilded porcelain

5e51433f-c353-5de6-8d1d-14dc9459c3f2.name: *Moors of Tetouan*
5e51433f-c353-5de6-8d1d-14dc9459c3f2.description:
This painting was made around 1863 when the author travelled to Morocco with Mariano Fortuny. The reason for his travel was to paint the characters and picturesque garments as the way of life of the people from Morocco.  
His experiences can be seen in his paintings and drawings.  
During his travels he bought exotic artworks as Egyptian sarcophagi.  
Harem and markets are considered a genre painting in Orientalism.
5e51433f-c353-5de6-8d1d-14dc9459c3f2.author: Ámparo López

5f3b539e-1d3b-5ad6-9c3f-11df8f1f7e2f.name: *Thebes. Hypogea. Pictures drawn after the covering of the mummies*
5f3b539e-1d3b-5ad6-9c3f-11df8f1f7e2f.second_name: Taken from *Description de l'Egypte, ou, Recueil des Observations et des Recherches qui ont été faites en Egypte pendant l'Expédition de l'Armée Française*, vol. 2
5f3b539e-1d3b-5ad6-9c3f-11df8f1f7e2f.description2: During the Egyptian expedition (1798–1801), Napoléon Bonaparte brought with him a group of scholars, engineers and artists, charged with collecting as much scientific information as possible. This was then used in a publication (of exceptional quality and execution) entitled Description de l'Égypte, in which the observations and enquiries made by the military expedition in Egypt were collected. The collection comprises of 10 volumes of illustrations and 9 volumes of texts published betwen 1809 and 1826.

5fa7cbde-981a-5031-afe4-3cc242fd75c7.name: *Remains of the Garments of Prince Philip of Castile, son of Ferdinand III*
5fa7cbde-981a-5031-afe4-3cc242fd75c7.description: Drawing of part of the garment of Prince D. Felipe, son of the King of Castile Ferdinand III. These garments are a good example of the rich silk textile from the Arab workshops of the Al-Andalus.
5fa7cbde-981a-5031-afe4-3cc242fd75c7.artist: Chromolithograph: Teo. Rufflé; lithograph: José Mª Mateu
5fa7cbde-981a-5031-afe4-3cc242fd75c7.keywords: Spanish Muslim art; applied arts; Textiles; Trade
5fa7cbde-981a-5031-afe4-3cc242fd75c7.third_name: *Restos del trage* \[sic\] *del Infante D. Felipe, hijo de Fernando III el Santo (Museo Arqueológico Nacional)*

602e2e1a-614b-533b-b171-c2a7bb60bc72.name: Bridal apron
602e2e1a-614b-533b-b171-c2a7bb60bc72.dates: End of the19th – beginning of the 20th century
602e2e1a-614b-533b-b171-c2a7bb60bc72.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
602e2e1a-614b-533b-b171-c2a7bb60bc72.keywords: Plain weave; warp; weft; sequins; sash; costume; accessories; textile; shell; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; wedding; marriage
602e2e1a-614b-533b-b171-c2a7bb60bc72.materials: Plain weave of cotton warp and weft consisting of wool and silver and gold wrapped thread. Decoration with sequins – *svetlinke*, *puloi*, and beads
602e2e1a-614b-533b-b171-c2a7bb60bc72.second_name: Apron with sash and bead chain
602e2e1a-614b-533b-b171-c2a7bb60bc72.description2: Belts, sashes and aprons were unavoidable accessories of folk costumes in all areas of Macedonia. This sash was made of white hand-woven cotton cloth, which was decorated at the front with embroidery of pink wool, silver-wrapped thread, silver string, sequins and multi-coloured beads. It has a hook and a loop on the ends for fastening. The apron was made in the technique of plain-weave. The warp of cotton and the weft of red wool and silver and gold-wrapped threads was embellished with sequins – *svetlinke* – and beads. The apron has two strips on the left and right sides woven and decorated in the same manner with shells and coins suspended at the bottom.

60799836-0950-5426-b9f2-6f8fbdaa9f72.name: Silver coin (twenty piasters)
60799836-0950-5426-b9f2-6f8fbdaa9f72.description: On obverse: "*amara bi-ta'amul al-husayn bin 'ali 1338 'abduhu wa ibn 'abdihi*" ("It is ordered to deal with by Al Hussein b. Ali 1334, God servant"). On reverse: "*duriba bi-makka al-mukarrama sana 8 / al-hukuma al-'arabiyya al-hashimiyya / 'ishruna / hashimi / qurushan*" ("20 piasters of Arab Hashemite Government, minted at Makka al-Mukarrama in reign year 8).
60799836-0950-5426-b9f2-6f8fbdaa9f72.author: Aida Naghawi
60799836-0950-5426-b9f2-6f8fbdaa9f72.keywords: Hussein bin Ali; twenty piasters; Arab Hashemite Government; Mecca al Mukarrama; coin; currency; coinage; numismatics

60bef031-ec19-5d57-8b30-278d1bbc2dd6.name: Glass bottle
60bef031-ec19-5d57-8b30-278d1bbc2dd6.description2: Glass produced in Bohemia blending European and Middle Eastern styles. Acquired by Franks.

60c41d82-4ce0-5ec0-9037-67792716aba8.name: Tunic (*'aba'a*)
60c41d82-4ce0-5ec0-9037-67792716aba8.description: Aba or man’s robe is inspired in the North African ones. It is made in cream velvet with a stencilled decoration related with Safavid motifs. This kind of garment that Fortuny discovered in his travels for North Africa is related to Spanish Muslim “aljubas” of the Medieval Spain.
60c41d82-4ce0-5ec0-9037-67792716aba8.holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
60c41d82-4ce0-5ec0-9037-67792716aba8.author: Elvira González
60c41d82-4ce0-5ec0-9037-67792716aba8.keywords: Costumes; Design; North African influence; Spanish Muslim influence

60d42b24-3acf-5ae0-ab4f-e3aae453f313.name: *Still-life with Calligraphic Panel*
60d42b24-3acf-5ae0-ab4f-e3aae453f313.keywords: Painting; Feyhaman Duran; orientalist painters; still life
60d42b24-3acf-5ae0-ab4f-e3aae453f313.description2: Feyhaman Duran was particularly interested in portrait painting and went to Paris in 1910 through the patronage of the Egyptian Prince Abbas Halim Pasha to further his studies in this genre. He greatly profited from the teaching of Paul Richet, professor of anatomy in the School of Fine Arts in Paris. He also attended the Julian Academy where he learned a great deal from Jean-Paul and Albert Laurens. In 1913-14 he worked in the Cormon studio in the School of Fine Arts. Although devoting most of his time to portrait painting, Feyhaman Duran also did paintings of flowers and nudes, but he was definitely most interested in the portrayal of people, and he had very little time for non-figurative painting.

60e43904-297f-56d1-af8b-fa4776b2ccb3.name: Pitcher
60e43904-297f-56d1-af8b-fa4776b2ccb3.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
60e43904-297f-56d1-af8b-fa4776b2ccb3.description2: Çanakkale was a pottery production centre between the end of the 17th century and first quarter of the 20th century where pottery with interesting and original forms was produced. Mostly coarse red clay and sometimes beige-coloured paste was used. There are green, brown, dark yellow and under-glazed purplish brown, yellow, dark blue and white decorations made by a brush. This Çanakkale-produced pitcher is made of red clay; it has green and dark yellow glaze and a bulgy body with long, narrow neck. Its mouth has a stylized bird shape. It has a flat bottom and round handle. On the head, neck and body of the bird, there are raised rosette flower patterns. On the front part of the body, there is a cat and some cypress tree figures. The details were made with the barbotine technique.

61d517e1-9410-5522-abb9-809bf66d22a5.name: Ewer
61d517e1-9410-5522-abb9-809bf66d22a5.description2: It is known that there were workshops producing glass vessels around Beykoz in Istanbul in the 19th century. The first glass workshop was founded by Mevlevi Dervish Mehmed Dede during the reign of Selim III (1789-1807). There were European glass craftsmen working in those workshops as well. Cups, bottles, jugs etc. made of colourful, colourless and opal glass were among Beykoz' productions. This is an ewer made of dark blue opaline with a water-drop-shaped lid. On its body there are raised flower patterns and *kabaras*.

635f5f5e-120a-51d8-b033-3d0504a831cb.name: Rumelihisarı İskelesi
635f5f5e-120a-51d8-b033-3d0504a831cb.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; Abdullah Brothers
635f5f5e-120a-51d8-b033-3d0504a831cb.description2: Abdullah Brothers is the name given to three men with Armenian origin, Viçen (1820-1902), Hovsep Abdullahyan (1830-1908) and Kevork (1839-1918) who started the art of photography in Turkey. For 40 years they photographed the people of Istanbul, landscapes, various political and social events, and prepared albums of historical and cultural values, as well as monuments.

6361ef20-5b25-59b2-bd56-7f7ed9244291.name: Reed pipe
6361ef20-5b25-59b2-bd56-7f7ed9244291.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
6361ef20-5b25-59b2-bd56-7f7ed9244291.author: Huda Kilani
6361ef20-5b25-59b2-bd56-7f7ed9244291.description2: A pair of blank reeds opened from both sides, of moderate thickness. Each has six holes on the surface attached together with a type of gum. Playing the *mijwiz* requires some ability because it is played by blowing into both reeds at the same time and pushing the air strongly with the cheeks. Shepherds used to play it while taking their flocks of sheep and goats to graze. It is a popular traditional musical instrument in the Middle East.

640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.name: Municipal theatre
640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.history: This building, which was once the Municipal Casino and often affectionately known as the "bonbonnière Resplandy", was built in the early 20th century in the Art Nouveau style by the French Architect Jean-Émile Resplandy and located on Avenue Jules-Ferry (now Avenue Habib-Bourguiba) in the heart of the European quarter. It has been constantly active since its birth, clearing the way for new artistic talent. The biggest names in Tunisian and Arab performing arts stood on its stage, performing ballet, opera, dramatic performances, classical concerts and more. In 2011 it became an important symbol of the Tunisian revolution; protestors, martyrs and rebels from all sides stood on its steps at some point.
640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.keywords: Art Nouveau; theatre; stucco; bas reliefs; Apollo
640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.description2: This theatre, the last remnant of a municipal artistic complex, can hold up to 1,350 seats. An immense white building, it reflects the style of Art Nouveau with evidence for some baroque influences. The bas-relief decorations, showing a scene with Apollo and the two muses, dominate the façade. The interior, from the vestibule to foyer, is notable for its modern structure and the richness of the carved stucco decorations. The bas-reliefs, moulds, cornices and balconies were all made by famous French and Italian artists.

65d5d950-d069-5d9e-989f-ca9b3eb57b29.name: *Harem*
65d5d950-d069-5d9e-989f-ca9b3eb57b29.description2: Pascal Sébah (1823–1886) was a French photographer working in the Ottoman Empire. This photo of a harem is interesting insofar as it  differs from the mainstream representations of harems in the Western imagination, which were influenced by the painter Gérôme. Indeed, many local customs - both real and imagined - captured the interest of European artists, and their Orientalist art then fuelled both the Western fascination with and revulsion towards the East.

66051236-e6f5-50e1-94a9-729e97d849a2.name: Tea tray (*siniyya*)
66051236-e6f5-50e1-94a9-729e97d849a2.description: A tea tray, known as a *siniyya*, made in Fez in the 19th century. It’s geometric and floral decoration – a fusion of old and new styles – suggests that it was made before products, especially those of Richard Wright (“RR”) from Manchester, entered the Moroccan market.
66051236-e6f5-50e1-94a9-729e97d849a2.keywords: S'ni; applied arts; craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmanship; kitchen ware; domestic ware; metalwork; geometric decoration; geometric motifs; floral decoration; floral motifs; vegetal decoration; vegetal motifs; British in Morocco; Richard Wright

6737216e-9ec0-5301-bc44-aa17e6e3cff5.name: Yıldız Ceramic panel
6737216e-9ec0-5301-bc44-aa17e6e3cff5.description2: Sultan Abdülhamid II founded in 1891 the *Yıldız Çini Fabrika-i Hümâyûnu* (Yıldız Royal Tile Factory) in the garden of Yıldız Palace in order to revive Turkish tile art and give it a new direction and momentum. Vases, hanging wall plates and many sorts of daily-use wares were produced in the factory, including writing and dinner table utensils, card plates, lidded bowls, pans, *aşure* (a kind of dessert) trays, sugar bowls, tea and coffee cups. Many native and foreign artists have worked in the tile factory of Yıldız. One of them, Halid Naci received training in tile painting in Sevres, France after his education at the *Sanayi-i Nefise Mektebi* (School of Fine Arts) and he was assigned to be head painter of the tile factories after his return. In the middle of the porcelain plate are a herd of sheep, its shepherd and his dog, all drawn using natural colours.

6752ea88-0922-5aae-a9a3-d9e93a4c8c57.name: Embroidery
6752ea88-0922-5aae-a9a3-d9e93a4c8c57.author: Ámparo López
6752ea88-0922-5aae-a9a3-d9e93a4c8c57.keywords: Nasrid art; islamic influence; orientalism; collectionism
6752ea88-0922-5aae-a9a3-d9e93a4c8c57.description2: This rich embroidery in the Mudéjar style showed the importance of these goods in the Italian and Spanish Renaissance. The influence of the Arab art in the Renaissance has been overlooked many times, but the Mediterranean ceramics and textiles of this period were influenced, in technique and decoration, by this art.

67aa0756-7dec-5fdf-a48c-f7c56bbd3c48.name: *Souvenir of Algeria*
67aa0756-7dec-5fdf-a48c-f7c56bbd3c48.author: Dalila Orfali
67aa0756-7dec-5fdf-a48c-f7c56bbd3c48.description2: This painting, made during one of the artist's many trips to Algeria, shows the ancient aqueduct of Cherchell. Algeria, for Fromentin, remained and endless source of inspiration to be constantly reinterpreted, as we can see from this painting's slightly personal touch. This famous work was first exhibited at the Salon in 1859, then again in 1874. It belonged to the old Delagrade collection and was published in *La Gazette des Beaux-Arts* in 1859 along with the following commentary: "This group of brightly dressed horsemen, who stand out like rubies against the green hills of the valley under the acqueduct, is above all the work of a colourist artist who has succeeded in uniting science with audacity.".

685a2ad1-af1f-51a1-a4f2-d4dc7fc2a7f0.name: Wooden Sideboard with Mother of Pearl Inlay
685a2ad1-af1f-51a1-a4f2-d4dc7fc2a7f0.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
685a2ad1-af1f-51a1-a4f2-d4dc7fc2a7f0.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
685a2ad1-af1f-51a1-a4f2-d4dc7fc2a7f0.dimensions: Height 2485 mm, width 1100 mm, depth 415 mm
685a2ad1-af1f-51a1-a4f2-d4dc7fc2a7f0.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
685a2ad1-af1f-51a1-a4f2-d4dc7fc2a7f0.description2: This tall, intricately carved sideboard consists of two parts, the mirror section with intricately carved openwork and mashrabiya ornamentation enhanced with mother-of-pearl inlay, and the narrow table section decorated with similar elements and with its four front legs supporting an elaborate system of lobed arches. the sideboard is further enhanced by religious inscriptions, some of which seem to suggest a Christian context. Sideboards and other European-style furniture were unknown in the Middle East until the second half of the12th/ 18th century. By the 13th/ 19th century, the urban elites in Ottoman cities enthusiastically imported domestic furniture from Italy, France and England or bought locally-made hybrid pieces that combined European and traditional Islamic elements like the item shown here. Many European entrepreneurs like the Italian Furino Brothers, based in Cairo, set up shop in Ottoman cities and specialised in this so-called Arabesque style, especially fashionable for furniture.

68a95c99-7986-5df2-8af1-8a9cc45a55e6.name: The Damascene Hall
68a95c99-7986-5df2-8af1-8a9cc45a55e6.holder: Wilhelma, Zoological and Botanical Garden Stuttgart
68a95c99-7986-5df2-8af1-8a9cc45a55e6.history:
King Wilhelm I of Württemberg commissioned to Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1837 the design of Moorish style buildings for his Wilhelma garden. The architect planned and built all the buildings with the exception of the Damascene Hall.  
The idea was not to reproduce faithfully the Islamic art but to lend an “oriental” flair to the garden. The mention of an “oriental garden” conjured up visions of elegance, luxury, colourful brilliance, seduction and eroticism.  
The Moorish style recalls the Islamic art of Spain and North Africa between the 12th and 15th centuries which reached its zenith in the Alhambra. It was fashionable in 19th century: Wilhelma is also known as the “Alhambra on the river Neckar” and other buildings – synagogues in Berlin and Vienna for example – were built in the Moorish style.
68a95c99-7986-5df2-8af1-8a9cc45a55e6.description2: In the eastern part of Wilhelma, towards the R. Neckar, is the Damascene Hall. It is the only one of the historical buildings that was not built by the royal architect Karl Ludwig von Zanth, but, after his death, by Professor Wilhelm Bäumer in 1864. It served Wilhelm I as a building for keeping pheasants and chickens. The name comes from that of the inhabitants of the town of Damascus, which used to be a centre of the Moorish style of building. The Damascene Hall was the only one of the historical buildings at Wilhelma to have survived the war undamaged. Despite this it was still very carefully restored in 1992. A small part of the old Moorish splendour of Wilhelma is to be seen here in the sumptuous ceiling painting, the stucco marble of the walls and the wonderful chandelier.

696bbefe-4763-59bf-ad00-3b86378355df.name: Pin, plaque
696bbefe-4763-59bf-ad00-3b86378355df.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
696bbefe-4763-59bf-ad00-3b86378355df.author: Huda Kilani
696bbefe-4763-59bf-ad00-3b86378355df.description2: A gold pin with three gold ¼ rashadi Ottoman coins welded together; at the end of two chains hang ¼ gold rashadi coins (Sultan Rashadi, 1909), each with a heart shape dangling from it. Ottoman coins were used as decorative objects for jewellery. Gold jewellery was usually bought only by the rich, while most people used silver jewellery. Pieces of gold or silver jewellery were given by the groom to the bride as a dowry, thus the choice of a piece of jewellery indicated the financial status of the groom.

6a6e9eb9-6672-5c93-a85f-f911188ec1ce.name: Tankard
6a6e9eb9-6672-5c93-a85f-f911188ec1ce.description: This tankard follows the pattern of Persian jugs of the 15th century. Its rich figurative decoration is reminiscent of the decorative strips used in book painting. The decor gives this tankard a special position in the context of Ottoman silver works, which in most cases present ornamental decoration only.
6a6e9eb9-6672-5c93-a85f-f911188ec1ce.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

6b3e84b4-acb3-5d73-a5b0-e7455c527cf6.name: Map of the different types of housing in East Beirut
6b3e84b4-acb3-5d73-a5b0-e7455c527cf6.holder: *Maisons traditionnelles de Beyrouth: Typologie, culture domestique, valeur patrimoniale. Le secteur de Rmeil-Médawwar* (Book)
6b3e84b4-acb3-5d73-a5b0-e7455c527cf6.author: Jeff El-Msanne, David Andos
6b3e84b4-acb3-5d73-a5b0-e7455c527cf6.description2: This map indicates the different types of housing found in the East Beirut with a system of coloured dots.

6c0ec863-e0e7-5b08-9c07-4fe22fc9d7ae.name: *Oriental perfumes*
6c0ec863-e0e7-5b08-9c07-4fe22fc9d7ae.description: This advertisement shows that the influence of Orientalism was telegraphed to the public as a synonym for exotic places, buildings and dresses. This advertisement also could be related to the Russian ballets of Sergéi Diágilev.
6c0ec863-e0e7-5b08-9c07-4fe22fc9d7ae.author: Ana Cabrera

6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.name: The Palace of Porto Trade Association Headquarters, the Arabian Room
6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.history: During the siege of Porto (1832-33) by Miguelist Army led by absolutist Prince Miguel (1802-66) against the Liberal troops of his brother Prince Pedro (1798-1834), S. Francisco convent was burnt only surviving the church.  Porto Trade Association’s headquarters was erected over these ruins. Queen Maria II issued the law concession letter of 19th June 1841 to order the establishment of the Stock Exchange and the Trial Court. The solemn placing of the first stone took place on 6 October 1842.
6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.keywords: Oporto; Trade Association; cultural heritage; trade; Queen Maria II; Cabralism
6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.architects: Architects: Joaquim da Costa Lima (1840–1860), Gustavo Adolpho Gonçalves e Sousa (1860–1879), Thomaz Augusto Soller (1879–1883), José de Macedo Araújo Júnior (1883–1890), Joel da Silva Pereira (1894–1899) and José Marques da Silva (1889–1910); Painting and sculptures: Luigi Maninin, António Ramalho, António Carneiro, Veloso Salgado, Marques de Oliveira, Soares dos Reis, Eduardo Malta, Teixeira Lopes and Henrique Medina, among others.
6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.description2: The Arabian Room (1862–1880) is considered as the most emblematic of all the Palace’s rooms, embodying the Neo-Moorish art in Portugal. Inspired by the Palace of Alhambra in Granada combines the Arab ornament grammar and the fertile imagination of the engineer/architect, Gustavo Adolpho Gonçalves e Sousa. The Hall of Nations is decorated with the national shield and the coat of arms of the countries with which Portugal had the closest ties of friendship and trade; consolidating the idea that the greatness of a nation, country or region is not a singular effort, but one of union, strength and the cooperation among people of different nations.

6db232a1-1948-537d-8bad-3c92a264c7c0.name: Stucco panel
6db232a1-1948-537d-8bad-3c92a264c7c0.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
6db232a1-1948-537d-8bad-3c92a264c7c0.keywords: Carved plaster; capitals; palaces; Ottoman style; Italian-esque style
6db232a1-1948-537d-8bad-3c92a264c7c0.description2: "Stucco" is a term used to describe the vast majority of decorations in Islamic Arts. White stucco, made from plaster stones, was used for column capitals, arcs, as well as sloped constructions such as roofs, as it is an incredibly supple, yet strong, adherent, durable and light material. Muslim artisans made countless constructions decorated with stucco. The 18th and 19th centuries, however, saw many constructions in carved golden plaster - both palaces and houses were elaborately decorated in this way. Floral motifs, closer to the Ottoman and Italian styles, soon overtook the geometric designs of previous centuries.

6e1d143a-f28c-5e23-bd94-fbe16124f587.name: Crown (*taj*)
6e1d143a-f28c-5e23-bd94-fbe16124f587.description: A crown (*taj*) made in Fez, with geometric and floral decoration, crafted from gold, and set with emeralds and rubies. It illustrates the decorative style that appeared in the early 20th century influenced by French designs, which is notable especially in the three small crowns at the top.
6e1d143a-f28c-5e23-bd94-fbe16124f587.keywords: Applied arts; precious stones; French design; floral decoration; floral motifs; vegetal motifs; vegetal decoration; craftsmanship; traditional craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmen; European influence; fashion

6e335928-9fa2-5b6f-93cb-9088b371f464.name: *Zabun*
6e335928-9fa2-5b6f-93cb-9088b371f464.description2: The *zabun* is similar to a European coat and the Turkish *qaftan* (a European inspired coat). It is speculated that it first arrived in the eastern part of Saudi Arabia through the Hajj, at the time of the Turkish empire, and later became popular in Qatar and Bahrayn. The *zabun* is made out of fine Indian Kashmiri brown wool with intricate embroidery. Decoration: made of light brown wool embroidered with *boteh* design, motif across the coat – paisley, Islamic decorative arts. Imitated because the shape is Kashmiri, shaped like cashew nut, pronounced ‘Gazorah.’ Colours are red, yellow, and edges are lined with metal silk thread – round neck opening. Narrow Nehru collar, or Chinese collar is known in Qatar. Buttons are handmade metal balls down the front. It is worn with the *thawb ishlahat*.

6eca5184-69aa-5866-8c8d-9b32d60fd187.name: *The gardens of the Dey's palace*
6eca5184-69aa-5866-8c8d-9b32d60fd187.archival: Lessore, E. et Wild, W., *Voyage Pittoresque dans la Régence d'Alger*, Paris: J.Delahaye, 1835.

6f1eea68-18d9-59b6-a602-617d05d6a7ae.name: Sprinkler
6f1eea68-18d9-59b6-a602-617d05d6a7ae.author: Mina Moraitou
6f1eea68-18d9-59b6-a602-617d05d6a7ae.description2: A sprinkler with a low base, spherical body and a narrow tapering neck. The body is decorated with a fish-scale motif anf four stylised leaves. The neck bears a dotted motif and blue motifs. A product of a workshop in France specialising in Islamic shapes and decoration.

6f8705b6-8b55-55ab-a02e-52dedab4e4de.name: Long-sleeve women's coat (*Mintan*)
6f8705b6-8b55-55ab-a02e-52dedab4e4de.author: Nada Andonovska
6f8705b6-8b55-55ab-a02e-52dedab4e4de.keywords: Mintan; srma; silk; silver; costume; Yörük community; nomads; Turkish; marriage; wedding
6f8705b6-8b55-55ab-a02e-52dedab4e4de.materials: Decoration with braids and cords of gold wrapped thread
6f8705b6-8b55-55ab-a02e-52dedab4e4de.description2: The enclave of the Turkish Yoruk community in Macedonia living in the mountain villages of Dojran – Valandovo and Radovish – and the Shtip region is a genuine treasure of tangible and intangible heritage that adds to the diversity of traditional culture in Macedonia. This bridal attire preserves some of the traditions in clothing and embellishment of Yoruk women in Macedonia in the 19th century and the early 20th century. A *mintan* is a short upper garment worn over the tunic. This piece is made of red silk. It is decorated with braids and cords of *srma* – gold-wrapped thread applied on the hems and over the front.

701d0273-bf02-5200-8f32-6dab9287106b.name: Bridal apron jewellery (*Mangura*)
701d0273-bf02-5200-8f32-6dab9287106b.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
701d0273-bf02-5200-8f32-6dab9287106b.keywords: Mangura; filigree; perforation; silver; costume; accessories; wedding; marriage
701d0273-bf02-5200-8f32-6dab9287106b.materials: Silver, silver alloy, tiny beads, hammering, casting, filigree, perforation
701d0273-bf02-5200-8f32-6dab9287106b.description2: The influences of Eastern art in Macedonia were largely expressed in the jewellery of the 19th century through the so-called Levantine Baroque style. This piece preserves evidence of the exceptional diversity of the jewellery. Worn on the apron, it also shows that articles of adornment used to be applied on many different items of clothing. A *mangura* consists of a string of tiny beads adorned with ornaments. The larger central pendant has been made in the filigree technique and embellished with decorative stones. It is flanked by minor ornaments decorated by perforation.

70b73c8c-526f-5ae3-901a-f7ef4dbf4ea8.name: Arabs listening to a story in their camp
70b73c8c-526f-5ae3-901a-f7ef4dbf4ea8.artist: Engraver: Jean-Pierre Marie Jazet; artist: Horace Vernet
70b73c8c-526f-5ae3-901a-f7ef4dbf4ea8.description2: Horace Vernet (1789–1863), the official painter of both Napoléon III and Louis-Philippe, was tasked with painting the "discovery" and conquest of Algeria. Various images of Algeria were published in the illustrated press in order to acquaint the French with Algeria and feed the narrative of a peaceful conquest. This idyllic painting of a group storytelling was very popular in the Salon des Beaux-Arts in 1834, and was reproduced by the engraver Jean-Pierre Marie Jazet in order to ensure its wider diffusion in the national press.

70fdcb57-1eeb-5564-b13a-e80bde43f3ba.name: *Courtyard of Justice at the Alhambra Palace, Granada*
70fdcb57-1eeb-5564-b13a-e80bde43f3ba.description: Sorolla depicted the Alhambra palace often. In this painting he chose the entry to the golden room. The beauty and exoticism of the Alhambra Palace fascinated European painters during the 19th century. Sorolla painted this monument in successive trips in 1909, 1910 and again in 1917. He was interested in architecture and especially in the Arab gardens, the play of light and water in their pools, and not so much in other topics.
70fdcb57-1eeb-5564-b13a-e80bde43f3ba.author: Covadonga Pitarch
70fdcb57-1eeb-5564-b13a-e80bde43f3ba.third_name: *Patio de la Justicia, la Alhambra de Granada*

7145d9d7-3f20-55d9-a385-486cd31761ab.name: Women's pants (*Don*)
7145d9d7-3f20-55d9-a385-486cd31761ab.author: Nada Andonovska
7145d9d7-3f20-55d9-a385-486cd31761ab.keywords: costume; embroidery; geometric patterns; geometric motifs; Yörük community; nomads; Turkish; marriage; wedding
7145d9d7-3f20-55d9-a385-486cd31761ab.materials: White canvas decorated with embroidery og varied wool, as well as silver and gold wrapped thread
7145d9d7-3f20-55d9-a385-486cd31761ab.description2: The enclave of the Turkish Yoruk community in Macedonia living in the mountain villages of Dojran – Valandovo and Radovish – and the Shtip region is a genuine treasure of tangible and intangible heritage that adds to the diversity of traditional culture in Macedonia. In general terms, the traditional outfit of Yoruk women in Macedonia is distinguished with exceptional colouring and application of varied elements in all articles of clothing. This bridal attire preserves some of the traditions in clothing and embellishment of Yoruk women in Macedonia in the 19th century and the early 20th century. This piece of trousers shows decoration of embroidery with geometric patterns applied on the lower front part of the trousers.

721353f1-5e28-56da-9787-f6334515d373.name: Memorial of Sultan Husayn Kamil’s visit to the Islamic Arts Museum
721353f1-5e28-56da-9787-f6334515d373.keywords: Sultan Hussein Kamel; Arabian Archeology Museum; Islamic Arts Museum
721353f1-5e28-56da-9787-f6334515d373.description2: The Islamic Arts Museum in Cairo is the biggest Islamic museum in the world, and it encompasses a wide collection of Islamic arts from India, China, the Arab Peninsula, the Levant, Egypt, North Africa and Andalusia. Sultan Husayn Kamil’s visit to the Museum in 1916 is considered one of the more important visits received by the Museum.

736574db-9cd1-5e72-95d5-f1860d3596ad.name: *Mashrabiyya*
736574db-9cd1-5e72-95d5-f1860d3596ad.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
736574db-9cd1-5e72-95d5-f1860d3596ad.description2: The *mashrabiyya* is a decorative architectural element characteristic of residences in the Arab world. It was generally used on windows or balconies on the second floor or above. As well as being a natural ventilation device, the *mashrabiyya* served the purpose of shielding the occupant from the vision of passers' by, whilst still allowing natural light to pass through the gaps. This particular piece is square shaped and made of limestone, sculpted in floral patterns.

73a8c1a7-47a7-5ac2-8219-524e45f2889c.name: Basin
73a8c1a7-47a7-5ac2-8219-524e45f2889c.holder: Musée de la Céramique Sidi Kacem Jelizi
73a8c1a7-47a7-5ac2-8219-524e45f2889c.description2: This large basin with a flat base and curved, sloping sides is also called a *maajna*. The feet of the basin are circular, and the centre is decorated with a highly stylised floral pattern with palms and winged shapes overlapping. The walls are mainly painted with a *tawq* (collar) motif. This style indicates a symbiosis between Ottoman influences and local traditions. The dominant colours are: yellow, green, brown, and violet. This basin was used to knead dough, roll semolina and as a serving bowl for certain ingredients, and shows traces of both Ottoman and Andalusian influences.

73c32255-eecb-5121-b674-c388b401bbb6.name: Charcoal iron
73c32255-eecb-5121-b674-c388b401bbb6.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
73c32255-eecb-5121-b674-c388b401bbb6.author: Huda Kilani
73c32255-eecb-5121-b674-c388b401bbb6.description2: A heavy iron box with a triangle-shaped lid with a handle and a hollow interior that could hold smouldering charcoal to keep the iron hot. This object of everyday use illustrates how the changes in mundane life affected society at a global level. Objects like this were traded locally within Jordan.

73e736ab-49ec-5eea-8f27-af65046fe133.name: Headdress
73e736ab-49ec-5eea-8f27-af65046fe133.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
73e736ab-49ec-5eea-8f27-af65046fe133.author: Huda Kilani
73e736ab-49ec-5eea-8f27-af65046fe133.keywords: silver; prominent dome; disk; al- Druz women
73e736ab-49ec-5eea-8f27-af65046fe133.description2: A silver circular disk with filigree work and prominent dome above; chains dangling with triple petal and filigree work at the end; placed on the top of a high hat worn by al-Druze (Druse) women. Silver was the most common jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom. This object illustrates the variegated social composition and the demographic changes in the Jordanian territory in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The al-Druze tribes migrated from Syria (Hawran) to north east Jordan in the early twentieth century because of their support for the Syrian revolution against the French occupation.

7474b893-ab5b-5cb0-8dbf-1f03e7b4dcb1.name: Egyptianising pendant
7474b893-ab5b-5cb0-8dbf-1f03e7b4dcb1.description2: The pendant's rich design illustrates the influence of Egyptian motifs on Victorian jewellery. This piece was based on one made for the British Princess Alexandra.

74cb07f0-79d7-57eb-be13-fe55793125ae.name: Milk jar
74cb07f0-79d7-57eb-be13-fe55793125ae.description2: This butter jar with a *dagra* lid has a spherical body and rests on a small pedestal. It is decorated with a polychromatic pattern, organised in rows. Medallion shapes filled with flowers cover the lower half of the body, and the lid is also densely decorated with flowers, and framed by a lattice.

75ba6380-c797-5b14-a144-d7546e1f3572.name: *Album de la Dobrudgea* by Anatol Magrin
75ba6380-c797-5b14-a144-d7546e1f3572.description2: In 1878 Anatole Magrin was appointed secretary of the French consul to Constanța and then became vice-consul and consul. He married a Romanian woman and eventually settled in Constanța. He was the owner of the first photo studio in the city and later became the official photographer of king Carol I, who decorated him with the Romanian order of the Crown. He is considered to be the first artist to take photographs of Dobruja, a province in the south-east of Romania which was restored to Romania in 1878, after more than three centuries of Ottoman domination. Magrin’s photo album dedicated to Dobruja contains 56 photos of landscapes and people, some of which depict Turkish and Tatar communities (the Tatars and Turks represent one of Dobruja’s main ethnic minorities).

75ecd1ca-690e-54ec-ae5c-583c92e90430.name: *Street Scene in Cairo*
75ecd1ca-690e-54ec-ae5c-583c92e90430.description2: *Street Scene in Cairo* from the Austrian painter Alphons Mielich. Mielich specialized in Oriental scenes, which he sold to aristocratic Austrian tourists as mementos of their trips to Egypt.

75ede8fe-76f3-5385-bdc5-f85fce889190.name: Quran
75ede8fe-76f3-5385-bdc5-f85fce889190.holder: Musée des Arts Islamiques de Kairouan
75ede8fe-76f3-5385-bdc5-f85fce889190.description2: These are two pages from a calligraphic Quran written in maghrebi script, dating to the 18th century, and a good example of the symbiosis between Hispano-Islamic and Ottoman influences. Although the script and the colour of the diacritics are typically maghrebi, the decoration and the frontispiece of the fatiha, which is adorned with floral motifs, shows the clear influence of the Ottoman school, which was itself inspired by Iranian art. The vowels are written in red, the *sukun* and the *shadda* in blue, the *hamza* in yellow or gold and the *hamza al-wasl* in green.

760fa584-9cdb-54e9-a484-39638db07064.name: Moorish dagger
760fa584-9cdb-54e9-a484-39638db07064.description: This dagger, along with other pieces, was taken by Salvador de Foronda, a member of the Spanish Army, awarded for his actions in battle. He was a relative of the Marquis of Cerralbo and donated to his uncle’s museum these exceptional pieces in 1918. This piece is enriched with damascene work, and the fabric rope still holds some metallic threads. This dagger was a traditional self-defence tool for North African men.
760fa584-9cdb-54e9-a484-39638db07064.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes

7625cc1a-04cd-541e-97b3-01fa3eac5fdf.name: *Dolmabahçe Palace Portal Under Construction*
7625cc1a-04cd-541e-97b3-01fa3eac5fdf.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
7625cc1a-04cd-541e-97b3-01fa3eac5fdf.keywords: Dolmabahçe Palace; Ottoman architecture; close-up from Dolmahçe Palace portal
7625cc1a-04cd-541e-97b3-01fa3eac5fdf.description2: Lacan heaps particular praise on the artist's panorama taken from Beyazıt Tower as well as on his photograph of the architectural elements of Galata Tower, the Hagia Sophia, the Mosque of Sultan Ahmed I, and Dolmabahçe Sarayı. Robertson’s Istanbul photographs are concerned primarily with the city’s historical monuments. They reveal the city’s magnificent Byzantine and Ottoman structures from different angles and with close-ups taken in an approach that is usually quite aesthetic.

763ee7df-878c-58a5-84f4-122b7dc9a7e0.name: Helmet
763ee7df-878c-58a5-84f4-122b7dc9a7e0.holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée
763ee7df-878c-58a5-84f4-122b7dc9a7e0.author: Bechir Yazidi
763ee7df-878c-58a5-84f4-122b7dc9a7e0.keywords: Tunisian army; Musée de l'Armée; Palais de la Rose
763ee7df-878c-58a5-84f4-122b7dc9a7e0.description2: This Islamic helmet, known as a "casque de Rostem", has Persian origins. It is 21 cm long from its tip to the joint at the front, the serrated iron mesh is 30 cm long, and the front perimeter is 70 cm long. This helmet is lavishly decorated, coming to two points on either side, and with an Ottoman point at the front and floral motifs all over the surface.

77fc77a2-454c-58fa-aa16-959029610bb1.name: Women's tunic (*Gomlek*)
77fc77a2-454c-58fa-aa16-959029610bb1.author: Nada Andonovska
77fc77a2-454c-58fa-aa16-959029610bb1.keywords: Yörük community; nomads; Turkish; tunic; costume; embroidery; wedding; marriage
77fc77a2-454c-58fa-aa16-959029610bb1.materials: White canvas decorated with embroidery og varied wool, as well as silver and gold wrapped thread
77fc77a2-454c-58fa-aa16-959029610bb1.description2: The enclave of the Turkish Yoruk community in Macedonia living in the mountain villages of Dojran – Valandovo and Radovish – and the Shtip region is a genuine treasure of tangible and intangible heritage that adds to the diversity of traditional culture in Macedonia. In general terms, the traditional outfit of Yoruk women in Macedonia is distinguished with exceptional colouring and application of varied elements in all articles of clothing. This bridal attire preserves some of the traditions in clothing and embellishment of Yoruk women in Macedonia in the 19th century and the early 20th century. The tunic is made of white canvas and modestly decorated by embroidery of two short vertical strips above the lower hem.

7878caf5-22b7-5137-93bb-b21eeb4df6c5.name: Earrings
7878caf5-22b7-5137-93bb-b21eeb4df6c5.description: Earrings form triple crescent, central lamellar and mobile; the side streets are filigree, stuffed with coils of wire, each with small mounts. It is decorated with filigree fans.
7878caf5-22b7-5137-93bb-b21eeb4df6c5.holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
7878caf5-22b7-5137-93bb-b21eeb4df6c5.author: Mª Antonia Herradón

789458d3-49a6-51d8-9be2-897051433c19.name: Layard Freedom Casket
789458d3-49a6-51d8-9be2-897051433c19.description2: A commemorative piece custom made to honour Austen Henry Layard. Layard was famous for excavating Nineveh. Closely modelled on the sculptures discovered by Layard.

78eecb65-6040-5c83-8995-b8c35cb4d3a6.name: Nusretiye Mosque and Tophane Square
78eecb65-6040-5c83-8995-b8c35cb4d3a6.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; James Robertson
78eecb65-6040-5c83-8995-b8c35cb4d3a6.description2: James Robertson arrived in Istanbul in 1840 and started work as head etcher in Ottoman Mint. He began taking photos of Istanbul soon after. There was previously a mosque located on the site of the current Mosque, which was known as the Mosque of the Artillery Barracks (Tophane-i Amire Arabacilar Kislasi Camii) built by Selim III (1789-1807). When that mosque was destroyed by the Firuzaga fire, the Nusretiye Mosque, located on Meclis-i Mebusan Street in the Tophane District of Beyoglu, was built on the order of Sultan Mahmud (1784-1839), and was constructed by the Krikor Amira Balyan. The construction lasted from 1823 to 1826 and was broadly restored between the years of 1955 and 1958, and partially again between 1980 and 1992. While its architecture is influenced by Islamic elements, it retains a Baroque style, making it unique to the city.

7935012a-92f2-5749-a878-3506ddbb8dc4.name: *The Temple of Venus*
7935012a-92f2-5749-a878-3506ddbb8dc4.author: Marina Minozzi
7935012a-92f2-5749-a878-3506ddbb8dc4.keywords: Italian painters; genre scene; Naples; Rome; Florence; Macchiaioli; Verismo; history painting; celebration of the past; Roman past; archaeology; documentation; post-unitarian Italian society; exhibition; exposition; exoticism
7935012a-92f2-5749-a878-3506ddbb8dc4.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
7935012a-92f2-5749-a878-3506ddbb8dc4.description2: Giuseppe Sciuti initially worked in his hometown as a decorator, then moved to Naples and Florence. In Florence, the artist works with the Macchiaioli painters upon subjects linked to the “Verismo”, or realist, movement, and while in Naples he worked on history paintings. In Rome he decorated public and private buildings with historical and allegorical themes, pagan rituals and scenes from the Greek and Roman tradition, highly valued by the international market. *The Temple of Venus* is an archeological reconstruction of a sacred interior showing an offering to the goddess Venus for the beginning of Spring. The painting is part of the group of works by the artist presented at the Exposition in Milan in 1871, Nice in 1884 and London in 1888.
7935012a-92f2-5749-a878-3506ddbb8dc4.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

en: Di Majo, E., in Elena di Majo and Mateo Lafranconi (eds), *Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Moderna. Le Collezioni. Il XIX secolo*, Milan: Electra, 2006, cat. 7.21.

795bacd6-ac66-5eca-9599-838de1b288ee.name: *Natürmort*
795bacd6-ac66-5eca-9599-838de1b288ee.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
795bacd6-ac66-5eca-9599-838de1b288ee.keywords: Painting; Halil Paşa; orientalist Turkish painters; still life
795bacd6-ac66-5eca-9599-838de1b288ee.description2: The foundation of Turkish painting drawing influence from western tradition was laid when the Naval Academy opened in 1795. In the period of Selim II, painting lessons were given at the academy. And course attendees were sent abroad after to develop their painting techniques and skills. These painters, who were known as the soldier-painters, worked in Gerome’s, Cabanel’s and Boulanger’s workshops in Paris. Halil Paşa provided a unique distinction to the analysis of impressionist light and colour. Because of his qualified knowledge about anatomy and his interest in depicting the human figure, Halil Paşa has a unique place in Turkish Art History.

79fded3c-fc12-5fa3-bff4-6820a231b3e4.name: Marriage shawl
79fded3c-fc12-5fa3-bff4-6820a231b3e4.holder: Musée des Arts et Traditions Populaires
79fded3c-fc12-5fa3-bff4-6820a231b3e4.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
79fded3c-fc12-5fa3-bff4-6820a231b3e4.description2: This loose marriage shawl is decorated with various symbols of fertility. Two large rectangles of red wool are sewn together, and their joining seam is ornately decorated with gold embroidery. The decorations are spread out across the whole cloth, forming a strip of finely woven motifs in the centre, which is surrounded by various traditional figures and patterns. The human figures are characteristic of the (often enigmatic) decorative arts of the towns of El Jem and Ouerdanine, and feature here in addition to the more common motifs such as the fish, the hand, disks, circles, diamonds, crescents, the dove and the camel.

7a66ac7e-e537-5099-bcf6-d574ade2e10c.name: Egyptianising vase
7a66ac7e-e537-5099-bcf6-d574ade2e10c.description2: Glass vase with stylised lotus leaves and buds decoration. Inspired by an Egyptian faience lotus cup in the British Museum.

7a6f5cad-f74c-5502-95b2-2068560418a6.name: The Port From The Galata Tower
7a6f5cad-f74c-5502-95b2-2068560418a6.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; Abdullah Brothers
7a6f5cad-f74c-5502-95b2-2068560418a6.description2: Abdullah Brothers is the name given to three men of Armenian origin, Viçen (1820-1902), Hovsep Abdullahyan (1830-1908) and Kevork (1839-1918) who started the art of photography in Turkey. For 40 years they photographed the people of Istanbul, landscapes, various political and social events, and prepared albums of historical and cultural values, as well as monuments.

7bdd779c-2cc5-578c-a095-d2093ad30ce0.name: *Ornements turcs: Recueil de dessins pour l' art et l' industrie*
7bdd779c-2cc5-578c-a095-d2093ad30ce0.author: Mina Moraitou
7bdd779c-2cc5-578c-a095-d2093ad30ce0.description2: A large portofolio on the ornament of the Turks as seen by potter Eugène Collinot and the designer Adalbert de Beaumont. The illustrations concern architecural details as well as building interiors, fountains and gates. It contains the ex libris of Antonis Benakis.

7c5b0aa9-383a-5b52-bc5a-91c986d3c9eb.name: Toiletries
7c5b0aa9-383a-5b52-bc5a-91c986d3c9eb.holder: Musée des Arts et Traditions Populaires
7c5b0aa9-383a-5b52-bc5a-91c986d3c9eb.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
7c5b0aa9-383a-5b52-bc5a-91c986d3c9eb.description2: In the 19th century the wealthy families of Tunis invented the notion of the knastrou l'aroussa (marriage basket) as a mark of their wealth. Made of engraved or watermarked silver, this basket would contain various toiletries for the bride: a perfume sprinkler (mrach), a khol phial with applicator for the eyes (mokhala), a round or rectangular-framed mirror with engraved floral motifs, and a knife and plate for henna. A pair of clogs (qobqabs) made of wood and covered in silver worn by the bride. As a traditional bath (hammam) was the bride's first event on her wedding day, all her toiletries were set out ready for her, with a series of tools for exfoliation, depilation, application of a clay face mask, and more.

7c6c4813-f135-5843-8f48-660e13714964.name: The Covered Walkway in the Moorish Garden (Wilhelma Park)
7c6c4813-f135-5843-8f48-660e13714964.holder: Wilhelma, Zoological and Botanical Garden Stuttgart
7c6c4813-f135-5843-8f48-660e13714964.history:
King Wilhelm I of Württemberg commissioned to Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1837 the design of Moorish style buildings for his Wilhelma garden. The architect planned and built all the buildings with the exception of the Damascene Hall.  
The idea was not to reproduce faithfully the Islamic art but to lend an “oriental” flair to the garden. The mention of an “oriental garden” conjured up visions of elegance, luxury, colourful brilliance, seduction and eroticism.  
The Moorish style recalls the Islamic art of Spain and North Africa between the 12th and 15th centuries which reached its zenith in the Alhambra. It was fashionable in 19th century: Wilhelma is also known as the “Alhambra on the river Neckar” and other buildings – synagogues in Berlin and Vienna for example – were built in the Moorish style.
7c6c4813-f135-5843-8f48-660e13714964.description2:
Planned as a bathhouse by Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1846, the Moorish Villa was then, however, built as living quarters with a glasshouse. It was first intended to be a bathhouse because mineral springs had been discovered in the adjacent Rosenstein Park. Rosenstein Palace was already standing in Rosenstein Park, and served the King as a summer residence.  
The Covered Walkaway marks the perimeter of the Moorish Garden at Wilhelma.

7cb05e6b-507b-594c-9ddd-3e9a0460ae93.name: Tent panel
7cb05e6b-507b-594c-9ddd-3e9a0460ae93.type: Islamic, Indian & Southeast Asian works of art; textile
7cb05e6b-507b-594c-9ddd-3e9a0460ae93.holder: Shangri La, Doris Duke Foundation for Islamic Art
7cb05e6b-507b-594c-9ddd-3e9a0460ae93.keywords: tent panel; Mamluk Revival; Egypt; cotton; applique; geometric motifs; inscription; textile; calligraphy
7cb05e6b-507b-594c-9ddd-3e9a0460ae93.description2: This appliqué is one of a set of six featuring designs that echo the bold geometry of Egypt’s period of Mamluk rule (1250–1517). The format of calligraphy above a central roundel with trefoils is similar to other works of art created during the Mamluk Revival period. This particular textile features the following verse from the Qur’an: “That man can have nothing but what he strives for...” (53:39). Appliqués of this type were often used to embellish tents.

7db8c87e-01d9-50ac-b044-887244457a35.name: Cup with lid
7db8c87e-01d9-50ac-b044-887244457a35.description: Cup with lid made in London in Oriental style.
7db8c87e-01d9-50ac-b044-887244457a35.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

7e87a4ee-76a2-59b0-995b-b76a7a6ee825.name: *Woman with mimosa*
7e87a4ee-76a2-59b0-995b-b76a7a6ee825.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
7e87a4ee-76a2-59b0-995b-b76a7a6ee825.keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters
7e87a4ee-76a2-59b0-995b-b76a7a6ee825.description2: Osman Hamdi focused on dilemmas such as East and West, love and hate, life and death. While stylistically reminiscent of western Orientalist painters, his works reflect a more nuanced appreciation of Ottoman society and culture. In the art of his paintings, he depicted unique details so diligently that he made us recognize our environment and Turkish culture. He illustrated carpets, tile panels, calligraphies, decorative arts, shrines, mosques and human figures in his paintings. He also gave importance to details while reflecting the colourful scenes of Turkish culture, traditional architecture, Ottoman fashion and domestic and social life of the women in the Ottoman Empire. And it’s obvious that he is the first painter who used human figures in the western style.

7ecaa27d-f3a4-5a6b-941d-8b655a5c543d.name: *Ewer in Turkish style*
7ecaa27d-f3a4-5a6b-941d-8b655a5c543d.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
7ecaa27d-f3a4-5a6b-941d-8b655a5c543d.dates: Photograph from the World Trade Exhibition 1873 in Vienna
7ecaa27d-f3a4-5a6b-941d-8b655a5c543d.description2: Illustration from C. Lützow (editor), *Kunst und Kunstgewerbe auf der Wiener Weltausstellung 1873*, 1875, p. 219.

7f9082fe-da75-56c9-8c44-bba718558f12.name: Ottoman Clothing Album
7f9082fe-da75-56c9-8c44-bba718558f12.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
7f9082fe-da75-56c9-8c44-bba718558f12.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
7f9082fe-da75-56c9-8c44-bba718558f12.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
7f9082fe-da75-56c9-8c44-bba718558f12.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

80035f13-53d6-5c24-82f4-b515c60d1e91.name: Portrait Album – Ottoman State Officers
80035f13-53d6-5c24-82f4-b515c60d1e91.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
