80035f13-53d6-5c24-82f4-b515c60d1e91.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
80035f13-53d6-5c24-82f4-b515c60d1e91.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

80775105-576a-504c-b3ae-7ae96a26ce22.name: Wedgwood pilgrim flask
80775105-576a-504c-b3ae-7ae96a26ce22.description2: Illustrates the influence of Egyptian motifs on Victorian ceramics. Part of the second wave of Egyptianisation, related to the construction of the Suez Canal. Shown at the Paris exhibition of 1878.

8096854b-be45-5588-b075-3b50e753c3ac.name: Writing Box
8096854b-be45-5588-b075-3b50e753c3ac.type: Woodwork; domestic furniture; Calligraphy; lacquered on wood
8096854b-be45-5588-b075-3b50e753c3ac.holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts
8096854b-be45-5588-b075-3b50e753c3ac.keywords: Calligraphy; Edirnekari technique; lacquer, Sultan Abdülmecid I; tughra
8096854b-be45-5588-b075-3b50e753c3ac.description2: Writing boxes were made to store the tools of calligraphers and scribes. They were decorated according to the taste of the period, in this case in a lacquer technique known as *Edirnekari*. Its owner was Sultan Abdülmecid I, who was himself a calligrapher.

81c95e16-5933-5305-af8a-2c4021985089.name: *The so-called Rhodian Pottery*
81c95e16-5933-5305-af8a-2c4021985089.author: Mina Moraitou
81c95e16-5933-5305-af8a-2c4021985089.description2: A  book on the Iznik pottery of the Ottoman period by the Greek collector and amateur scholar Chr. Nomiko. It contains a dedication by the author to Antonis Benakis.

81ebd0c7-807d-5447-9cf3-c2bec3c89a89.name: *Matériaux pour un Corpus inscriptionum Arabicum*
81ebd0c7-807d-5447-9cf3-c2bec3c89a89.author: Mina Moraitou
81ebd0c7-807d-5447-9cf3-c2bec3c89a89.third_name: *Mémoires publiés par les membres de la Mission Aarchéologique Francais du Caire, tome XIX*
81ebd0c7-807d-5447-9cf3-c2bec3c89a89.description2: One of a number of volumes on Arabic epigrapphy by the scholar Max van Berchem (1863-1921) who studied inscriptions from a number of areas in the Middle East.

82377c81-2aca-5c1e-8a4c-f15d8d08fec5.name: *Armed Guard of a House*
82377c81-2aca-5c1e-8a4c-f15d8d08fec5.description2: Painting by Eduard Charlemont showing an Egyptian guard in front of a door. Charlemont graduated from the Academy of Fine Arts in Vienna and travelled widely. He specialized in painting in the Oriental style.

82540953-196e-5dad-808a-f0bd9b908d16.name: *The Royal Palaces of Seville*
82540953-196e-5dad-808a-f0bd9b908d16.description: In this case the author lived in Seville and he knew very well the place. The scene is also historicist because the figures are dressed in a Renaissance style. Some of the decorations in the arch were invented by the artist.
82540953-196e-5dad-808a-f0bd9b908d16.author: Carolina Miguel Arroyo

82635f79-7381-59a0-8cbe-e72a1b631f83.name: Dish
82635f79-7381-59a0-8cbe-e72a1b631f83.description: The Orientalism or Neo-Mudéjar style gave new light to different workshops, as Fajalauza in Granada. Following this revival, this workshop produced dishes and other object decorated with Alhambra motifs, in this case the gazelles from the very well-known "Gazelle Vase" from the Alhambra Palace, the inscriptions and interlaces.
82635f79-7381-59a0-8cbe-e72a1b631f83.keywords: Neo-mudejar style; Applied Arts; Production of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode

8341e914-3245-5e20-9233-8addfbd06386.name: Mohamed Bey Mosque
8341e914-3245-5e20-9233-8addfbd06386.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
8341e914-3245-5e20-9233-8addfbd06386.history: Built in the late 18th century, this mosque is also known as the Sidi Mehrez mosque, probably due to its location facing the mausoleum to the saint Sidi Mehrez in the Bab Souika quarter. It is the only multiple-domed mosque in Tunisia. With clear Turkish influences, this mosque is reminiscent of the Hagia Sofia in Istanbul and the Pêcherie in Algiers.
8341e914-3245-5e20-9233-8addfbd06386.description2: The mosque is accessible through three doors, the most important of which opens up onto the *suq*, on one of the medina's most important streets. When seen from the outside, the mosque dominates the city, with its grouped domes and cupolas painted with a white wash. The Anatolian ceramic tiles covering the walls were an innovative addition at the time. The square-based prayer room is bordered on three sides by galleries, which each face onto three V-shaped courtyards. These galleries rest on marble columns with Turkish-style capitals. The richly decorated *mihrab* is covered in Iznik ceramic tiles. This mosque, also known as the Sidi Mahrez Mosque, is notable for being the only mosque in Tunisia with Turkish influences.

83550dcd-d5fe-53bf-ba81-33534dbf86ed.name: Lace skirt
83550dcd-d5fe-53bf-ba81-33534dbf86ed.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
83550dcd-d5fe-53bf-ba81-33534dbf86ed.author: Huda Kilani
83550dcd-d5fe-53bf-ba81-33534dbf86ed.description2: Skirt of light pink lace with black flowers, pursed from the middle, worn over a woman’s dress. This object illustrates the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, the various local costumes and rites, fashion and personal attire. This skirt was used by al-Druze women in Jordan. The al-Druze tribes migrated from Syria (Hawran) to north east Jordan in the early twentieth century because of their support for the Syrian revolution against the French occupation.

8469840c-c735-573f-aef2-fdf1fcbc3556.name: Bottle-shaped vase
8469840c-c735-573f-aef2-fdf1fcbc3556.description2: This nipple or bottle-shaped vase, with its central ring-shaped handle and turned-up base, resembles a closed coffin when seen from the side. Vases in this shape are very rare, and this particular one, which is decorated with the image of a great yellow and brown bird, was used for bottle-feeding infants.

8483f56d-4097-5e63-a47a-8a53aa99f289.name: *Hilye*
8483f56d-4097-5e63-a47a-8a53aa99f289.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
8483f56d-4097-5e63-a47a-8a53aa99f289.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
8483f56d-4097-5e63-a47a-8a53aa99f289.artist: Ali Al-Shukri; his work is certified by Al-Hajj Hafedh Muhammad Al-Wahbi and Khalil Al-Safi
8483f56d-4097-5e63-a47a-8a53aa99f289.materials: Black ink, pigments, gilding on board; ebru (marbling)
8483f56d-4097-5e63-a47a-8a53aa99f289.second_name: Calligraphic composition describing the noble qualities of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh)
8483f56d-4097-5e63-a47a-8a53aa99f289.description2: Despite the steady advance of western-style artworks, traditional Ottoman arts and crafts did not disappear entirely. This hilye or word portrait of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) has been rendered on tripartite, foldable cardboard, decorated on the outside with elaborate ebru paper marbling. Its composition follows a layout current since the 11th/17th century when it was devised by the famous Ottoman calligrapher Hafiz Osman (1052-1110 H/1642-1698CE). Traditionally, the hilye presents Hadith recounting the noble physical and spiritual attributes of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), often embellished with rich illumination. A large oval cartouche, with the hadith in black naskhi, appears in the centre, surrounded by four roundels naming the four rightly-guided caliphs Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali. Above the cartouche, the Bismillah is written in thuluth style. Below, a verse from the Holy Qur'an (68:4) is followed by the last lines of the hadith, a prayer, the names of the artist and two individuals certifying his work, and the date. All calligraphic elements are set against a stippled gold background enhanced with European-style floral elements.

84f5327f-428b-5355-b4b7-9d4e62a12ef9.name: *Bashi Bazouk*
84f5327f-428b-5355-b4b7-9d4e62a12ef9.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
84f5327f-428b-5355-b4b7-9d4e62a12ef9.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
84f5327f-428b-5355-b4b7-9d4e62a12ef9.description2: This colourful watercolour, executed by the Istanbul-based, Maltese painter V. A. Preziosi, shows a Bashi Bazouk, a member of the irregular forces of the Ottoman army that came into use in the late 18th century. The bashi bazouk were mercenaries of great ethnic diversity, often from the Balkans, who fought for the Ottomans in hope of plunder, as they were not paid. An attempt by Husrev Pasha in Egypt to disband his Albanian bashi bazouks in favor of his regular forces began the rioting which led to the establishment of Muhammad Ali's rule. The bashi bazouk did not wear regular uniforms. In this case, the flamboyant character depicted here with his formidable moustache wears an astonishing array of clothing: a towering turban with tassles, an embroidered shirt and waistcoat with large open sleeves, a voluminous waistband and trousers. The outfit is finished off by elaborate footwear. A large yatagan dagger is secured in the waistband across the soldier's front, a gun slung across his chest.

84f69ff8-6c1a-5173-a0c7-4b706dba6ef1.name: Arabian Fantasy
84f69ff8-6c1a-5173-a0c7-4b706dba6ef1.author: Marina Minozzi
84f69ff8-6c1a-5173-a0c7-4b706dba6ef1.keywords: Orientalism; reinvention; historical events in paintings; Orientalist topics; exoticism; diplomatic mission; Morocco; Mulay al-Hasan; travel; travelling artist; Italian travellers; Italian painters; Edmondo de Amicis; Marocco; travel book
84f69ff8-6c1a-5173-a0c7-4b706dba6ef1.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
84f69ff8-6c1a-5173-a0c7-4b706dba6ef1.description2: Stefano Ussi lived between Florence and Rome, studied at the Academy of Fine Arts of Florence and then enrolled as a volunteer in the first Italian War of Independence, during which he was taken prisoner by the Austrian troops. He developed a model of historic painting characterized by a quick application of layers (almost a rough draft) and by a sharp chiaroscuro. In 1875 he followed a diplomatic delegation to Morocco, in which the painter Biseo and the writer De Amicis also took part. The Arabian Fantasy documents the "Lab-el-barode", a game with the dust played in honor of the Italian delegation. This episode was masterly described by the writer Edmondo De Amicis.
84f69ff8-6c1a-5173-a0c7-4b706dba6ef1.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

en: Villari, A., in Elena di Majo and Mateo Lafranconi (eds), *Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Moderna. Le Collezioni. Il XIX secolo*, Milan: Electa, 2006, cat. 8.31.

85128cd9-af17-5141-b661-afa4f41e6438.name: *Kusejr Amra*
85128cd9-af17-5141-b661-afa4f41e6438.author: Mina Moraitou
85128cd9-af17-5141-b661-afa4f41e6438.description2: An early illustrated publication on the Umayyad Qusayr Amra in Jordan by the Austrian Alois Musil and drawings by the artist A.L. Mielich.

85842d41-d3a1-5921-ac88-903643f0147a.name: Moorish Kiosk in Linderhof Palace Park
85842d41-d3a1-5921-ac88-903643f0147a.type: Pavillion; Park building in Linderhof Palace Park
85842d41-d3a1-5921-ac88-903643f0147a.history:
Linderhof Palace Park was laid out from 1870 to 1880 from plans by Carl von Effner. Ludwig II decorated the park and its environs with architectural features conjuring up the world of the Orient, such as the Moorish Kiosk and the Moroccan House, or scenes from Wagner's operas, such as the Venus Grotto. Hunding's Hut and the Gurnemanz Hermitage.  
The Moorish Kiosk was built in 1867 as the Prussian contribution to the World Exhibition in Paris. In 1870 the "railway king" Henry Strousberg bought the pavilion. After Strousberg's bankruptcy, Ludwig II bought the building in 1876 for Linderhof Palace Park and had it rebuilt and reappointed to his specifications.
85842d41-d3a1-5921-ac88-903643f0147a.keywords: King Ludwig II; Linderhof Palace; Ettal; Moorish style; Romanticism; gardens
85842d41-d3a1-5921-ac88-903643f0147a.description2: The Moorish Kiosk is located high above the park on two terrace levels. A colourful, exotic arrangement of palms, pomegranate trees and numerous flowering shrubs extends the foreign atmosphere of the Kiosk outside the walls and also distinguishes its surroundings from the rest of the park. – Between 1972 and 1983 the kiosk was completely restored.

859283ff-dbce-5eca-aab7-fe1bee0640a1.name: Dagger
859283ff-dbce-5eca-aab7-fe1bee0640a1.description: A dagger decorated with geometric and floral motifs and crafted in southern Morocco in the 19th century. Dagger blades were imported from Europe.
859283ff-dbce-5eca-aab7-fe1bee0640a1.keywords: Trade; arms; armours; metalwork; European influence; geometric motifs; geometric decoration; floral decoration; vegetal motifs; vegetal decoration; craftsmanship; war; warfare; military objects
859283ff-dbce-5eca-aab7-fe1bee0640a1.materials: Gold; precious stones; horn, enamel; steel; cord

8609522c-18c6-5b1c-9149-7c3bb976c5b7.name: Neo-Mamluk, metal-inlaid copper alloy Table
8609522c-18c6-5b1c-9149-7c3bb976c5b7.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
8609522c-18c6-5b1c-9149-7c3bb976c5b7.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
8609522c-18c6-5b1c-9149-7c3bb976c5b7.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
8609522c-18c6-5b1c-9149-7c3bb976c5b7.keywords: Mamluk; blazon; kufi; thuluth; al-Nasir ibn al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun
8609522c-18c6-5b1c-9149-7c3bb976c5b7.materials: Sheet copper alloy with metal inlay
8609522c-18c6-5b1c-9149-7c3bb976c5b7.description2: In 13th/ 19th- century Egypt, the political, cultural and social climate increasingly encouraged a nationalistic reappraisal of indigenous heritage. The era of the Mamluks, who had ruled Egypt and Syria between the later 7th/13th and the early 10th/ 16th centuries, was particularly celebrated as a golden age in national history. As a result, artisans now turned their efforts to reviving the glories of Mamluk artefacts, and particularly their celebrated, silver- and gold-inlaid metalwork. This stand or table is an exquisite example of such revivalist work. It copies a famous Mamluk Qur’an stand in the Museum of Arab Art in Cairo, inscribed with the name of the Mamluk Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun (r. 1294-1340) and made by Muhammad ibn Sunqur al-Baghdadi.

86c2720a-384b-58d3-92a2-3fc1aefd7f1c.name: Small earthenware jar
86c2720a-384b-58d3-92a2-3fc1aefd7f1c.holder: Musée de la Céramique Sidi Kacem Jelizi
86c2720a-384b-58d3-92a2-3fc1aefd7f1c.description2: This double-handled and oval-shaped *qolla* has a long neck and a bulging lip. The decoration is polychromatic and organised in rows. On vase's belly, a row of medallions filled with flowers are bordered by a lattice strip and a herringbone strip on either side. The neck is decorated with alternating yellow, blue and green vertical lines. This item shows traces of both Ottoman and Andalusian influences.

8719dd85-f9ef-50c8-9dad-04384401d5ca.name: *The Revolt of the Dolls*
8719dd85-f9ef-50c8-9dad-04384401d5ca.holder: National Museum of Contemporary Art – Chiado Museum
8719dd85-f9ef-50c8-9dad-04384401d5ca.author: DGPC
8719dd85-f9ef-50c8-9dad-04384401d5ca.description2: This painting by Eduardo Viana is a landmark of the first modernism in Portuguese painting, even though it is influenced by naturalist themes such as landscape and traditions.
8719dd85-f9ef-50c8-9dad-04384401d5ca.holding_institution_org: Museu Nacional de Arte Contemporânea – Museu do Chiado

884ca90f-561a-57c1-913d-b4aab82da583.name: Pendant necklace
884ca90f-561a-57c1-913d-b4aab82da583.description: This beautiful triangular pendant necklace shows a loop chain decorated with four little floral ornaments and the main pendant decorated small red and green mounted crystals. This also has a shared connection with the traditional Fátima Hand motif.
884ca90f-561a-57c1-913d-b4aab82da583.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes, Cristina Giménez

888046f7-3ef2-5941-9017-769431669b16.name: Ring
888046f7-3ef2-5941-9017-769431669b16.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
888046f7-3ef2-5941-9017-769431669b16.author: Huda Kilani
888046f7-3ef2-5941-9017-769431669b16.keywords: Floral decoration; religious objects; waqf; Qur’an; Ottoman Baroque-Rococo
888046f7-3ef2-5941-9017-769431669b16.description2:
Thin silver ring with a squared black stone set in silver. Silver jewellery was the most common, because only rich people could afford gold jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom.  
Jordan's economy in the late 19th and early 20th centuries relied on trades and crafts and new waves of people started to come to Jordan and began to settle for this purpose. This object is an example of how traditional fashion reflected the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is also an example of local personal attire, fashion, costumes and rites.

89d4c66b-a374-55e7-8284-7f6b427b03c0.name: Portrait of Abel Acácio Botelho
89d4c66b-a374-55e7-8284-7f6b427b03c0.description: This painting by António Ramalho (1859–1916) portrays European fascination for eastern cultures. As well as wearing a Japanese costume, the figure in the painting is surrounded by oriental objects in a clear reference to his aesthetic preferences.
89d4c66b-a374-55e7-8284-7f6b427b03c0.holder: National Museum of Contemporary Art – Chiado Museum
89d4c66b-a374-55e7-8284-7f6b427b03c0.author: DGPC
89d4c66b-a374-55e7-8284-7f6b427b03c0.holding_institution_org: Museu Nacional de Arte Contemporânea – Museu do Chiado

8a11b8a8-3b2f-5ba0-8118-5ec32059a75d.name: Book cover
8a11b8a8-3b2f-5ba0-8118-5ec32059a75d.holder: Musée des Arts Islamiques de Kairouan
8a11b8a8-3b2f-5ba0-8118-5ec32059a75d.provenance: La zaouia de Sidi Sahbi, Kairouan
8a11b8a8-3b2f-5ba0-8118-5ec32059a75d.description2: This book cover from Rabat is decorated with a red and gold moulded pattern. The central medallion contains various florets, with two teardrops in a similar pattern emanating from it. The rectangular borders are made of a geometric interlaced pattern, whereas the four concave corners are surrounded by a curved border and floral motifs. This cover is evidence of the influence of the Ottoman school on Tunisian book covers.

8ad123be-79dd-59a7-84a8-ffc0f7c6d8e7.name: *James Robertson and His Brother-in-Law Felice Beato in Turkish Costume*
8ad123be-79dd-59a7-84a8-ffc0f7c6d8e7.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
8ad123be-79dd-59a7-84a8-ffc0f7c6d8e7.keywords: self-portrait; watercolour on photographs; Felice Beato
8ad123be-79dd-59a7-84a8-ffc0f7c6d8e7.description2: A self-portrait of James Robertson and his brother-in-law Felice Beato standing side by side and dressed in Turkish costume is an important work in the history of photography. This picture is in every sense a coloured counterpart of two other portrait photographs by Robertson first brought to light by Bahattin Öztuncay in 1991. The image of Felice Beato in this identical photograph is the only known picture of him in his youth.

8b5de31f-f1e0-5ddc-9d8a-dd777ed6d387.name: Mosaic for the inauguration of the Musée du Bardo
8b5de31f-f1e0-5ddc-9d8a-dd777ed6d387.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
8b5de31f-f1e0-5ddc-9d8a-dd777ed6d387.description2: This mosaic was made for the inauguration of the Musée Alaoui, now the Musée du Bardo, on 7 May 1888. At the top right-hand side we can see the Tunisian flag, on the left the the initials of the French General Residence in Tunisia, and in the centre the words  "Le Musée Alaoui"  in red letters. The inauguration was hosted by 'Ali Pacha Bey and the Resident-General M. J. Massicault. The names of the French civil servants who had accompanied the Resident-General and supervised the creation of the museum are written in two colums: M. Georges Perrot and M. Edouard Delpeuch, delegates from the Ministre de l'Instruction Publique des Beaux-Arts, M. Henri Wallon and M. Héron de Villefosse, from l’Académie des Inscriptions et Belles Lettres, and M. R. de la Blanchére, director of the Service des Antiquités et des Arts. Finally, the Arabic text at the bottom of the mosaic celebrates the inauguration of the museum.

8c7b0235-6bb9-503d-ac59-f73f7984f36b.name: *Le général Khaireddine* (painting)
8c7b0235-6bb9-503d-ac59-f73f7984f36b.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
8c7b0235-6bb9-503d-ac59-f73f7984f36b.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
8c7b0235-6bb9-503d-ac59-f73f7984f36b.keywords: Oil on canvas; Simil; General Khayr al-Din
8c7b0235-6bb9-503d-ac59-f73f7984f36b.materials: Canvas, wood, coloured pigments, gold leaf
8c7b0235-6bb9-503d-ac59-f73f7984f36b.description2: This 1852 oil on canvas by Simil depicts the General Khaireddine (Khayr al-Din) on horseback in official uniform. This brigadier-general uniform from the latter half of the 19th century comprises a full suit, a short coat, a shirt, a checia, a chemla and a pair of shoes. The brigadier-general also wore two crossed capes and a sword, with the Nichan al-Iftikhar (1st class) medal on the right-hand side of the chest, next to the insignas, and the Légion d'Honneur and the Ordre des Saints Maurice et Lazare medals on the left-hand side.

8ca42471-fa97-56f9-94ac-a3f4088b69ff.name: Cannon
8ca42471-fa97-56f9-94ac-a3f4088b69ff.holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée
8ca42471-fa97-56f9-94ac-a3f4088b69ff.author: Bechir Yazidi
8ca42471-fa97-56f9-94ac-a3f4088b69ff.keywords: Tunisian army; Musée de l'Armée; Palais de la Rose
8ca42471-fa97-56f9-94ac-a3f4088b69ff.description2: This cast bronze cannon is 156 cm long, has a front diameter of 50 cm and a back diameter of 85 cm. The Beylik of Tunis' coat of arms can be seen near the muzzle, and the Kingdom of Italy's near the back, as well as the name of the manufacturer, Fonderia di Torino, and the date, 1867.

8d188108-655f-550e-b130-a0eb24f32b9c.name: Headdress
8d188108-655f-550e-b130-a0eb24f32b9c.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
8d188108-655f-550e-b130-a0eb24f32b9c.author: Huda Kilani
8d188108-655f-550e-b130-a0eb24f32b9c.description2: Three bands of silver (800) chain fitted around the sides and over the crown of the head; 1/4 Ottoman coins (*barah*s) are fixed in the inner section of the band. This kind of jewellery was part of the dowry the groom gave to the bride. Dowries consisted mostly of silver jewellery because only the rich could afford gold jewellery. Thus, the financial status of the groom was highlighted by the jewellery he could give as a dowry and by the use of coins as pieces of jewellery for his wife.

8d76b341-a93b-5d3a-8003-baf0071d63f7.name: Vase
8d76b341-a93b-5d3a-8003-baf0071d63f7.description: The Orientalism or Neo-Mudéjar style gave new light to old techniques like decorating ceramic with lustre; new ceramic artisans such as Pickman, in Seville, produced pieces in Neo-Mudéjar or Orientalist style. This piece won an award in one of the International Exhibitions. It reproduces the shape of the vase known as "The Alhambra vase" in lustre decoration.
8d76b341-a93b-5d3a-8003-baf0071d63f7.author: Ana Cabrera
8d76b341-a93b-5d3a-8003-baf0071d63f7.materials: Moulded porcellaneous earthenware; painted with enamel and gilded

8eb7973a-8c9e-5910-83bd-ad5e77872aba.name: *Algerians*
8eb7973a-8c9e-5910-83bd-ad5e77872aba.author: Dalila Orfali
8eb7973a-8c9e-5910-83bd-ad5e77872aba.description2: This study consists of a series of sketches depicting various Algerians. The subjects are mostly women, whose faces, wrapped in a traditional *haik*, are particularly interesting. According to experts only two paintings of this kind exist today. Before being acquired by the museum this study belonged to an important collection from the late 19th century. In 2003 it was published in the Australian scholar Roger Benjamin's collection dedicated to Auguste Renoir's Algerian period, *Renoir and Algeria*.

905cb8f2-54fa-520a-b0bc-209a26809787.name: Ottoman Clothing Album
905cb8f2-54fa-520a-b0bc-209a26809787.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
905cb8f2-54fa-520a-b0bc-209a26809787.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
905cb8f2-54fa-520a-b0bc-209a26809787.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Vassilaki Kargopoulo
905cb8f2-54fa-520a-b0bc-209a26809787.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in 19th century. Vassilaki Kargopoulo was of Greek descent. His first studio was opened in 1850 near the Russian Consulate. Between the years of 1859 and 1860, he began to attract the attention of customers from all sections of society. He focused on Ottoman clothing and street vendors in 1860.

90e3fb5e-2f89-5468-82a4-55ad1ae995cf.name: Pair of panels, possibly from a door to a shrine
90e3fb5e-2f89-5468-82a4-55ad1ae995cf.type: Islamic, Indian & Southeast Asian works of art; Metalwork
90e3fb5e-2f89-5468-82a4-55ad1ae995cf.holder: Shangri La, Doris Duke Foundation for Islamic Art
90e3fb5e-2f89-5468-82a4-55ad1ae995cf.dates: Hegira 10th century / AD 16th century or later
90e3fb5e-2f89-5468-82a4-55ad1ae995cf.keywords: panels; Safawid; Mughal; Iran; India; silver; arabesque; inscription; Muhammad Amin al-Kirmani; door; calligraphy; geometrical decoration; geometrical motifs
90e3fb5e-2f89-5468-82a4-55ad1ae995cf.description2: This pair of small metal hinged doors is of rectangular shape and is elaborately ornamented on the interior. At the centre of each door is a field of dense arabesques and stars. The lengthy and exquisite Arabic inscription adorning the perimeter of each of these panels proclaims the sanctity of a shrine and requests permission to enter into it. It is signed by one Muhammad Amin al-Kirmani. On the reverse sides of each door are repeating engraved, peaked crosses with studs inset down the centre.

9107cee6-86c6-50d5-afa3-39c67845bd31.name: Cup stand (*zarf*)
9107cee6-86c6-50d5-afa3-39c67845bd31.description: These delicate silver pieces known as *zarf* are an important part of the coffee ritual in Turkey, as they work as a protection and stand for the hot cups. We can admire those pieces as a part of the scenography in the portrait of the marquise of the Cerralbo and his daughter in Turkish costume made by Abdullah Fréres.
9107cee6-86c6-50d5-afa3-39c67845bd31.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes

91c9008b-704b-5717-93d7-868bfaa22521.name: *Asia. Athalide*
91c9008b-704b-5717-93d7-868bfaa22521.description: In this lithography, Asia is represented as a woman dressed in Turkish style. She is Athalide, the lover of Bayaceto, in a 1762 play by Jean Racine. She wears Circassian clothes. Orientalist painting usually represents Circassian women in the seraglios or harems.
91c9008b-704b-5717-93d7-868bfaa22521.author: Carmen Linés Viñuales

9241049c-6cdf-5701-af96-c463f9661bf7.name: *Mosque Gate*
9241049c-6cdf-5701-af96-c463f9661bf7.description2: Caliph Abdulmecid was interested in art in addition to administration. He opened many art exhibitions. He was chosen as honorary president of the Society of Ottoman Painters, which was founded in 1909, and he gave considerable financial support to the monthly journal published by the society. He took part in the Galatasaray Art Exhibitions with his paintings. For example, one of his paintings was accepted for an exhibition held at Galatasaray during the first years of the First World War. His works reveal him as a colourist and an accomplished portrait painter. Caliph Abdulmecid showed his paintings at the Viyana Exhibition, which was the first exhibition opened by Turkish painters in Europe in 1918.

92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.name: Palais de la Rose
92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.history: The Palais de la Rose was built in the late 18th century, within La Manouba's royal gardens. Although originally used as a recreational palace for the Husainid beys, it soon began to receive many famous guests or persons visiting Tunisia, such as Queen Caroline of Brunswick in 1816. During the reign of Ahmed Pacha Bey (1837–1855) the palace became a residence for foreign teachers at the École Militaire du Bardo, among whom was the famous hero of Italian independence, Giuseppe Garibaldi. From 1881, the beginning of the French protectorate in Tunisia, the palace became the occupying army's headquarters. Following independence, the palace was restored and thus regained its original splendour and the became home to the Musée Militaire National.
92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.keywords: Architecture; art; painting; stucco; mosaic; marble; ceramics
92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.description2: The Palais de la Rose is an example of "Moorish" architecture from Spain and North Africa with Italian influences. Its most notable features are the grand staircase, the great hall surrounded by a marble gallery, and the huge, luxurious courtrooms. It is richly decorated in a variety of styles, with Italian marble in rare colours and an elegant rococo style, as can be seen from the Neapolitan faience pottery, the vaulted ceilings, and the tympanums finely carved from stucco or naqsh hadida in one of the styles popular at the time, such as an eight-point star between two stylised cypress trees. Finally, palace-museum's four great rooms invite its visitors to learn about the history of the Tunisian army from antiquity to the War of Independence.

92edd2fe-ef09-5e83-baba-8f729535104a.name: Dolmabahçe Mosque and Square
92edd2fe-ef09-5e83-baba-8f729535104a.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; Abdullah Brothers
92edd2fe-ef09-5e83-baba-8f729535104a.description2: Dolmabahçe Mosque’s original construction was initiated by Bezm-i Alem Valide Sultan, the mother of Sultan Abdülmecid (1823-61). Upon her death, its construction was continued by her son. It is located in the southern part of the Dolmabahce Palace, situated on the coast. The mosque was opened for prayer services on 23 March 1855. Its architect is Garabet Balyan, a member of the Balyan family, who built various structures for the Ottoman Empire. The Dolmabahçe Mosque is adorned with various items of both Baroque and Ampir styles, which are reflected in the architectural design of that period. Also, an emergent architectural modernity in the mosque is its circular window design. Such a design had rarely been seen in mosques and civil architecture before this time.

93ae9a92-2eeb-5864-aa3f-f804d80d9877.name: The Moorish Villa (Wilhelma Park)
93ae9a92-2eeb-5864-aa3f-f804d80d9877.holder: Wilhelma, Zoological and Botanical Garden Stuttgart
93ae9a92-2eeb-5864-aa3f-f804d80d9877.history:
King Wilhelm I of Württemberg commissioned to Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1837 the design of Moorish style buildings for his Wilhelma garden. The architect planned and built all the buildings with the exception of the Damascene Hall.  
The idea was not to reproduce faithfully the Islamic art but to lend an “oriental” flair to the garden. The mention of an “oriental garden” conjured up visions of elegance, luxury, colourful brilliance, seduction and eroticism.  
The Moorish style recalls the Islamic art of Spain and North Africa between the 12th and 15th centuries which reached its zenith in the Alhambra. It was fashionable in 19th century: Wilhelma is also known as the “Alhambra on the river Neckar” and other buildings – synagogues in Berlin and Vienna for example – were built in the Moorish style.
93ae9a92-2eeb-5864-aa3f-f804d80d9877.description2:
The "Moorish Villa" at Wilhelma indicates either the whole construction of the botanical section or its central building. The glasshouses are impressive constructions of glass and cast iron adjoined to the central living quarters already during the reign of Wilhelm I of Württemberg.  
The overall construction accommodate five autonomous plant houses, each of them displaying plants according to a super-ordinate theme. From the northern entrance, one first reaches the Cactus Cupola House, then the room with the Tropical Crop Plants. In the centre there follows the Moorish Villa (central part of the construction), with the famous giant titan plant. The next section is the glasshouse with tropical ferns, and in the final room, also with a glass cupola, the tree ferns.  
In the central room of the Moorish Villa construction there is the Department for Nocturnal Animals with nocturnal birds.

94535829-1f7a-57f3-91f8-a5b331e4d1a1.name: Stalactites
94535829-1f7a-57f3-91f8-a5b331e4d1a1.second_name: *Précis de l'Art Arabe et Matériaux pour servir à la Théorie et à la Technique des Arts de l'Orient Musulman*
94535829-1f7a-57f3-91f8-a5b331e4d1a1.description2: The artist and architect Jules Bourgoin travelled to Egypt many times. Between 1880 and 1884 he took part in a French archaeological campaign to Cairo, directed by Gaston Maspéro, from which he brought back a number of drawings of Egyptian monuments and Arab architecture.

94a92e7a-86a2-564b-a1ed-f8bdaf4ad23c.name: Capsule-charge handgun
94a92e7a-86a2-564b-a1ed-f8bdaf4ad23c.description: A capsule-charge gun crafted in southern Morocco in the early 19th century.
94a92e7a-86a2-564b-a1ed-f8bdaf4ad23c.keywords: craftsmanship; arms; armours; metalwork; weapons; war; warfare; military objects; bone; copper; ivory; silver

94c59dc9-5032-599d-bcf3-18eec377e4fa.name: Velvet embroidered kaftan
94c59dc9-5032-599d-bcf3-18eec377e4fa.holder: Musée des Arts et Traditions Populaires
94c59dc9-5032-599d-bcf3-18eec377e4fa.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
94c59dc9-5032-599d-bcf3-18eec377e4fa.materials: Velvet fabric, braided trimmings, silver thread with white and gold
94c59dc9-5032-599d-bcf3-18eec377e4fa.description2: This purple velvet kaftan is decorated with gold and silver braided trimmings and embroidered with silver and golden metal thread. It is fitted with mid-length sleeves embellished with a large "lyonnais" ribbon. The chest is covered by a large breastplate, split into two symmetrical halves, and adorned with large buttons of gold lace. The embroidery on the breastplate features two peacocks facing, on each side, a bowl with floral motifs. The kaftan is lined with a pale blue satinette on the outer rims with a pattern of swallows' wings sewn on. The kaftan, a particularly lavish item in the 19th century, was typically worn for marriage ceremonies, usually with calf-length trousers.

94d92226-8356-5023-81bd-a96c6c114974.name: Design for book cover: *Tres morillas me enamoran*
94d92226-8356-5023-81bd-a96c6c114974.description: The influence of the Spanish Muslim art can be seen in this design that references the illuminated books of Alfonso X, King of Castile (1252–1284). The arches, the dresses and the general decoration recall the illuminated pages of the 13th century illuminated books preserved in the Royal Collection and Library.
94d92226-8356-5023-81bd-a96c6c114974.author: Ana Cabrera
94d92226-8356-5023-81bd-a96c6c114974.third_name: Diseño para portada del libro *Tres morillas me enamoran*

95cff7a3-4aaf-5c15-8a93-e9f1eb66d9e1.name: *Oriental Landscape with Classical Ruins*
95cff7a3-4aaf-5c15-8a93-e9f1eb66d9e1.description: This painter who made this landscape never travelled to Egypt, but he knew how the Oriental landscapes looked like thanks to the different books with engravings. It is important to noted that most of these landscapes mixed different view or were invented by the artist, in basis of different engravings.
95cff7a3-4aaf-5c15-8a93-e9f1eb66d9e1.author: Carolina Miguel Arroyo

9647edd4-27e5-5ed4-a0ce-9b56a5dfc3ea.name: Coffee mortar and pestle
9647edd4-27e5-5ed4-a0ce-9b56a5dfc3ea.description2: Coffee mortar and pestel from Egypt/Morocco.

96d75b79-58ff-5945-b11e-11a08e7dd7b9.name: *Typical North African interior*
96d75b79-58ff-5945-b11e-11a08e7dd7b9.archival: Berbrugger, *Algérie Historique Pittoresque et Monumentale*, Paris: J. Delahaye, 1843.

97234026-b759-5b5b-ada5-8fc567b89260.name: Four-poster bed
97234026-b759-5b5b-ada5-8fc567b89260.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
97234026-b759-5b5b-ada5-8fc567b89260.description2: This four-poster bed was made for a Muslim market in a pseudo-baroque style and shows evidence of European influences. The metalworkers who made this kind of furniture worked with both copper and iron, and were organised in their own guild, with their workshops located in the lower kasbah.

9729e384-0aab-59c6-bb73-2a5621d81218.name: Bridal headdress (*Tepelak* – tas)
9729e384-0aab-59c6-bb73-2a5621d81218.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
9729e384-0aab-59c6-bb73-2a5621d81218.keywords: Head-dress; tepelak; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; tughra; marriage; wedding; fashion; costume
9729e384-0aab-59c6-bb73-2a5621d81218.materials: Gilt silver, casting, filigree, adornment with small coins
9729e384-0aab-59c6-bb73-2a5621d81218.description2: Jewellery worn on the head included diverse types of metal articles which served to support the hat or scarf and also had an apotropaic function in addition to their decorative one. Especially noteworthy head-pieces were *tepelaks*. These are headdresses of round form, sometimes slightly concave, abundantly adorned with chains, smaller or larger silver coins and with *trepkas* (tiny ornaments in diverse forms – round, leaf-shaped, rectangular, heart-shaped, etc.). *Tepelaks* used to be worn everywhere in Macedonia, particularly in the Kumanovo, Skopje, Gostivar and Gevgelija regions, as well as within Vlachs. This piece of bridal *tepelak-tas* was made by application of filigree technique. It is abundantly decorated with coins suspended on tiny chains.

97603dc7-78b0-567d-995d-706683438f46.name: Wedding dress
97603dc7-78b0-567d-995d-706683438f46.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
97603dc7-78b0-567d-995d-706683438f46.author: Huda Kilani
97603dc7-78b0-567d-995d-706683438f46.materials: Linen with silk; hand weaving, hand embroidered, natural dyes
97603dc7-78b0-567d-995d-706683438f46.description2: The main fabric of this wedding dress is linen with silk selvedge stripes, with red and yellow taffeta inserts in the sleeves and skirt; the chest panel is couched with gilt cord and yellow, green and purple silk cord, and filled with multi-coloured stain and herringbone stitches. Palestinian weavers used manual spindles to prepare the cotton and linen threads imported from Egypt. Ashkelon weavers used light vertical hand looms (*Majdalawi* looms) to produce linen fabrics, while silk fabrics were spindled, died and woven in Syria. The Jordanian economy in the late 19th and early 20th centuries relied on trade and crafts; new waves of people started to come to Jordan to participate in those industries. This object shows the diverse population composition of Jordan at that time, through personal attire, fashion, local costumes and rites.

98176d85-368c-5bcb-9ca0-e03314e1aa13.name: Amulet band
98176d85-368c-5bcb-9ca0-e03314e1aa13.keywords: Franks; collection; collector; museums; amulet; talisman; inscription

982f1ac5-a37a-57db-93bb-493e4513bd14.name: *Zarf*
982f1ac5-a37a-57db-93bb-493e4513bd14.description2: *Zarf* made entirely of silver-gilt filigree with granulation. Used to hold a small porcelain coffee-cup. From Syria.

98c3852e-4d88-54fc-b204-73d1b0245994.name: Fan
98c3852e-4d88-54fc-b204-73d1b0245994.description: This fan was used by the Queen Maria Cristina of Spain and showed that the influence of the Orientalism or Neo-Mudéjar style had arrived in lace design. This lace has pointed arches and interlacing decoration very similar to Arab patterns.
98c3852e-4d88-54fc-b204-73d1b0245994.author: Ana Cabrera
98c3852e-4d88-54fc-b204-73d1b0245994.materials: Lace and tortoiseshell; diamonds and pearls

9a135c4c-830c-5fdd-a5e6-61129754ecfd.name: Bridal breast jewellery (*Chaprag*)
9a135c4c-830c-5fdd-a5e6-61129754ecfd.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
9a135c4c-830c-5fdd-a5e6-61129754ecfd.keywords: Breast ornament; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; accessories; costume; wedding; marriage
9a135c4c-830c-5fdd-a5e6-61129754ecfd.third_name: Chaprag – Nevestinski ukras za na gadi
9a135c4c-830c-5fdd-a5e6-61129754ecfd.description2: This exquisite article called a *chaprag* shows the exceptional skill and inventiveness of the unknown goldsmith, who makes each piece of jewellery a virtual work of art in itself. The *chaprag* is a breast ornament consisting of a round plate and tiny chains. It is executed in filigree technique and adorned with decorative stones. Besides its decorative function, it was applied for the purpose of fastening the cleavage of the tunic. It was characteristic of the Ohrid-Prespa region, that is, the areas of Ohridsko Pole, Strushko Pole and Debarski Drimkol.

9aa9bf06-9414-5502-8c25-a49ce6269462.name: Belt
9aa9bf06-9414-5502-8c25-a49ce6269462.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
9aa9bf06-9414-5502-8c25-a49ce6269462.author: Huda Kilani
9aa9bf06-9414-5502-8c25-a49ce6269462.description2: A Circassian belt with 15 silver and niello-decorated buckles connected together to form the belt; there is a rosette shape at the end with locking mechanism and three dangling silver tassels. This belt, together with the dagger, was an accessory forming the traditional male Circassian dress. The Circassians used to carry daggers which were an essential part of the national dress. The immigration of the Circassians to the Ottoman Empire started in the middle of 19th century and continued until 1900. The Circassian communities migrated mostly to the eastern Arab countries with which they had spiritual and religious links.

9b0fa536-0fe5-5f95-ba19-41b4f81e9fd4.name: Brass head of flagpole
9b0fa536-0fe5-5f95-ba19-41b4f81e9fd4.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
9b0fa536-0fe5-5f95-ba19-41b4f81e9fd4.author: Huda Kilani
9b0fa536-0fe5-5f95-ba19-41b4f81e9fd4.description2: This mast, made of casted brass, bears an Arabic calligraphic decoration with the inscription "Oh God, Oh Muhammad". It is fixed on a pointed piece of copper with a hole at the bottom to install on a long wooden staff. In religious festivities such as a pilgrimage, various activities were organized. They would normally include festivals and rallies under flags and standards. The heads of flagstaffs were decorated with metallic items usually with Arabic calligraphy and some cosmic signs such as the crescent and the star.

9b44e7da-e4ce-51fe-a09e-946b4f817954.name: *View of Istanbul*
9b44e7da-e4ce-51fe-a09e-946b4f817954.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
9b44e7da-e4ce-51fe-a09e-946b4f817954.description2: Felix Ziem, who incorporated the seasons and the changing light of the sun during the day into Venetian scenes, selected Istanbul – another city intertwined with the sea – as a subject for this particular work. Portraying a quiet village at the shores of the Bosporus and the boats on the sea, the painting is dominated by the golden colour of sunset. Ziem is deemed a particularly successful artist in terms of capturing the reflections of sunlight on the water. Recognizing this feature as Ziem’s forte, Theophile Gautier mentions the effects of the changing light of the sun – as part of the movement in the environment – reflecting on the water as “broken into a thousand fractions”. As in his other works, the figures have been transformed into a few colour stains in the picturesque atmosphere.

9b7f13f5-9188-59a0-bf2d-8b4f7c9b66cb.name: Brass head of flagpole
9b7f13f5-9188-59a0-bf2d-8b4f7c9b66cb.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
9b7f13f5-9188-59a0-bf2d-8b4f7c9b66cb.author: Huda Kilani
9b7f13f5-9188-59a0-bf2d-8b4f7c9b66cb.description2: A cultic item with Arabic calligraphy mentioning God and his prophet Muhammad made of casted brass; fixed on a pointed piece of copper with a hole at the bottom to install on a long wooden staff. In religious festivities such as a pilgrimage, various activities were organized that would normally include festivals and rallies under flags and standards. The heads of flagstaffs were decorated with metallic items usually with Arabic calligraphy and some cosmic signs such as the crescent and the star.

9b83a66c-2937-5afb-80f5-4db5f45d441b.name: Slippers
9b83a66c-2937-5afb-80f5-4db5f45d441b.description: The slippers are handcrafted and embroidered by hand, their unique creation emphasizing their value. This type of footwear demonstrates the influence of oriental art in the technical work of 19th century European artisans, and the great fascination with the objects coming from the East that refer to the luxurious craftsmanship of these countries.
9b83a66c-2937-5afb-80f5-4db5f45d441b.author: Mercedes Rodríguez Collado
9b83a66c-2937-5afb-80f5-4db5f45d441b.materials: Silk, metallic thread, leather; velvet, sewn, embroidered, tanning

9c2ac3c9-ddf9-5578-9e26-fad8ec3a615c.name: Dhow collection
9c2ac3c9-ddf9-5578-9e26-fad8ec3a615c.keywords: Boat; ship; dhow; pearling; fishing; trade; transportation
9c2ac3c9-ddf9-5578-9e26-fad8ec3a615c.description2: The National Museum of Qatar holds, in its collection, a fleet comprising of 14 dhows. The growing collection includes a variety of traditional dhows, with several models dating to the early 20th century, as well as more recent replicas of traditional vessels. Originating from Oman, Bahrayn, India and Qatar, among other places traditional dhows represented include *jalbut* (small to medium sized), *shuw\`i* (medium sized, once used for fishing and coastal trade), *sanbuq* (largest type in the Arabian Gulf today) and *baglah* (traditional, deep-sea dhows once used for the long – haul transport of goods.)

9c6f1f64-15f3-5d35-93ad-16dc50cc2b9f.name: Coat
9c6f1f64-15f3-5d35-93ad-16dc50cc2b9f.description: Coat in green velvet completely decorated in flowers and leaves in gold with the stencil technique. It is lined with a silk and has a green velvet belt.
9c6f1f64-15f3-5d35-93ad-16dc50cc2b9f.holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
9c6f1f64-15f3-5d35-93ad-16dc50cc2b9f.author: Elvira González

9c872904-bce3-5aa4-b6f0-1ecfaddfcbd1.name: Mosque lamp
9c872904-bce3-5aa4-b6f0-1ecfaddfcbd1.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
9c872904-bce3-5aa4-b6f0-1ecfaddfcbd1.description2: Imitation of a Syrian-Egyptian mosque lamp made by Philippe-Joseph Brocard in Paris, 1867.

9ee4a0fa-3ad1-5d46-a700-262cfde9d93d.name: Scarab brooch
9ee4a0fa-3ad1-5d46-a700-262cfde9d93d.description2: Illustrates the influence of Egyptian motifs on Victorian jewellery. Part of the second wave of Egyptianisation, related to the construction of the Suez Canal.

9f63568d-d271-5f57-bc5d-a0c73ea5a902.name: Vase
9f63568d-d271-5f57-bc5d-a0c73ea5a902.description: Vase produced in Berlin in Oriental style.
9f63568d-d271-5f57-bc5d-a0c73ea5a902.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
9f63568d-d271-5f57-bc5d-a0c73ea5a902.artist: House of Arts and Crafts of the Hohenzollern family, H. Hirschwald, Berlin

a10695d2-fbb1-56b0-aaa5-5b25ce6071ac.name: Sahib el-Tabaa Mosque
a10695d2-fbb1-56b0-aaa5-5b25ce6071ac.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
a10695d2-fbb1-56b0-aaa5-5b25ce6071ac.history: This mosque was the last great work of the Husainid dynasty of Tunisia. It was built by the powerful Youssef Saheb el-Tabaa between 1808 and 1814. Being the richest man in the country during Hammouda Pacha Bey's reign, he used his wealth to set up a variety of activities around his mosque, such as two madrasas and the tomb of its founder, similar to the Turkish Konya. The décor and ornamentation reflect Western influences, with a narrow and elegant minaret.
a10695d2-fbb1-56b0-aaa5-5b25ce6071ac.description2: This mosque's imposing height dominates the Place Halfaouine. The layout of the mosque is organised around its main prayer room, which is composed of nine naves and seven bays. The barrel-vaulted ceiling is covered in stucco, and decorated with vegetative and floral motifs and with geometric elements, such as stripes and stars, reflecting both its Italian and Turkish influences. It is also boasts of having the only five-domed prayer room in the city. The walls are covered in marble panels imported from Carrara (Italy) and ceramic tiles from Qallaline. The thin tall columns are ribbed and topped with composite capitals. The *mihrab*'s polychromatic decoration is mixed with the pseudo-gothic arches and floral motifs. The Sahib el-Tabaaa mosque is noteable for being one of the clearest examples of the Italian influences on religious architecture.

a15b7e00-538c-5aa8-a826-c4febf856606.name: In the Desert
a15b7e00-538c-5aa8-a826-c4febf856606.author: Marina Minozzi
a15b7e00-538c-5aa8-a826-c4febf856606.keywords: Orientalism; reinvention; historical events in paintings; exoticism; Verismo; diplomatic mission; Morocco; Mulay al-Hasan; travel; travelling artist; Italian travellers; Italian painters; Edmondo de Amicis; Marocco; travel book
a15b7e00-538c-5aa8-a826-c4febf856606.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
a15b7e00-538c-5aa8-a826-c4febf856606.description2: Cesare Biseo was a decorator and a realistic painter. He was sent to Egypt in 1870 to decorate the Theatre of the Opera in Cairo, where the painter Stefano Ussi also was working. In 1877 Biseo took part in the diplomatic delegation in Morocco with Ussi and de Amicis. Biseo’s painting *In the Desert* shows an exotic Verismo style of painting and is an example of the high status oriental paintings had in those years with the rise of Italian interests in colonialisation. The painting was bought by the Italian state in 1890 and displayed in the National Gallery of Modern Art of Rome in 1907.
a15b7e00-538c-5aa8-a826-c4febf856606.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

a237773b-cce0-5972-a24d-1e563fd1cb62.name: Little jar with crested handle
a237773b-cce0-5972-a24d-1e563fd1cb62.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
a237773b-cce0-5972-a24d-1e563fd1cb62.author: Marina Minozzi
a237773b-cce0-5972-a24d-1e563fd1cb62.keywords: Applied arts; minor arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; decoration; motifs; collection; collector; glass; Murano glass; glasswork; zoomorphysm; zoomorphic; glass filaments
a237773b-cce0-5972-a24d-1e563fd1cb62.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century and as a training school for specialising artisans. The concept was part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. The tendency of Murano's industries in using bizarre shapes, often of zoomorphic inspiration, gave life to manufacts not so much functional as extremely representative of the decorative needs, and it was very successful. The motif of glass filaments worked with pincers to look like crests, typical of the 17th century objects, is used also in the little ruby-red jar with gold leaf from the second half of the 19th century and resembling objects from Cinquecento and Seicento.
a237773b-cce0-5972-a24d-1e563fd1cb62.holding_institution_org: Museo Artistico Industriale presso la Galleria nazionale d’arte antica in Palazzo Barberini

a2ba32a3-7747-5b54-b011-e71d3a84e08c.name: Dress
a2ba32a3-7747-5b54-b011-e71d3a84e08c.description: Pink silk twill dress lined with cotton, long-sleeved and high-waisted. The neckline is round in the front and triangle-shaped in the back. The upper bodice area is boned. Both breasts are marked with a U-shaped pleating. The skirt is soberly straight in front but it gains volume towards the back, ending in a short trail. The dress is fastened with invisible hooks at the back and adorned with buttons covered in the same silk fabric. The lower end presents a wide multi-coloured paisley frieze; each drop is composed of minute woven flowers. This elegant dress is a late variation of Empire dresses; the slender high-waisted silhouette is the same, but the fabric is thicker, the neckline has turned more modest and the long sleeves go down to cover part of the hands.
a2ba32a3-7747-5b54-b011-e71d3a84e08c.holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
a2ba32a3-7747-5b54-b011-e71d3a84e08c.dimensions: Width 38 cm, Height (front) 121 cm, Height (back) 112 cm, Sleeve length 61 cm, Diameter 233 cm
a2ba32a3-7747-5b54-b011-e71d3a84e08c.author: Irene Seco
a2ba32a3-7747-5b54-b011-e71d3a84e08c.keywords: Costume; geometric decoration; commerce; Empire dress; 19th century
a2ba32a3-7747-5b54-b011-e71d3a84e08c.materials: Silk, cotton, metal, bone; taffeta, twill, boning

a2f41b51-30af-503a-a290-05cb553751f2.name: Part of a veil
a2f41b51-30af-503a-a290-05cb553751f2.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
a2f41b51-30af-503a-a290-05cb553751f2.author: Huda Kilani
a2f41b51-30af-503a-a290-05cb553751f2.keywords: Gold; Ottoman coins; above the nose; piece of cloth
a2f41b51-30af-503a-a290-05cb553751f2.description2: Five lines of gold ¼ Ottoman lira and other type of coins sewn together on a piece of cloth; such pieces were usually affixed above the nose on the veils, *burqu'*, of women of Beer Sheba. Fashion, local costumes and rites in the territories of Jordan and Palestine show identical elements, as this veil illustrates. It is one of the many examples of jewellery made with Ottoman coins to decorate veils and dresses. Jewellery was an important accessory for married women because pieces of jewellery constituted part of the dowry their husbands gave them for marriage. Jewellery was also a symbol of financial prestige: the more precious it was, the richer the husband’s family. Silver jewellery was the most common because only rich people could afford gold jewellery.

a3383721-0dca-5dd7-9c36-0d0b44bcc62a.name: Plate
a3383721-0dca-5dd7-9c36-0d0b44bcc62a.description: Plate produced in Brussels in Oriental style.
a3383721-0dca-5dd7-9c36-0d0b44bcc62a.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

a34c17e6-990c-5cb0-95c0-c85297eb94e1.name: *A Mamluk Resting with his Horse*
a34c17e6-990c-5cb0-95c0-c85297eb94e1.description: The Mamluks were excellent horsemen and aroused the attention of artists like Carle Vernet and Sebastian of Bourbon, a member of the Spanish Royal family. Artists did not need to have journeyed to the Near East or Arabia to be labelled Orientalists. This is a good example, because the authors did not travel to the Near East.
a34c17e6-990c-5cb0-95c0-c85297eb94e1.author: Carmen Linés Viñuales
a34c17e6-990c-5cb0-95c0-c85297eb94e1.artist: Original: Carle Vernet; copyist and lithographer: Sebastián María Gabriel Borbón y Braganza

a46e70b6-0a07-57b9-ad2a-d974179b2424.name: Water jug
a46e70b6-0a07-57b9-ad2a-d974179b2424.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
a46e70b6-0a07-57b9-ad2a-d974179b2424.author: Huda Kilani
a46e70b6-0a07-57b9-ad2a-d974179b2424.description2: A copper circular-shaped ewer with a very narrow neck, arched handle and strait long nozzle, used in mosques of Jordan and Palestine to wash before praying. This is another example of how the same objects, traditions, and activities were common in territories that now belong to different Arab states. In the late 19th century and early 20th century, there were still no boundaries between the Arab states and this – together with the lack of geographical barriers – made population movements, nomadism and migration a common factor influencing the everyday life and exchanges in the local society. The local economy, which relied heavily on trade and crafts, depended also on travel and migration in order to sell products or find markets for craft products.

a50f8085-8ff8-57a1-9ecc-7536a8854029.name: Sword with scabbard
a50f8085-8ff8-57a1-9ecc-7536a8854029.description: A sword and scabbard decorated with geometric and floral motifs and crafted in southern Morocco in the 19th century. Sword blades were imported from Europe, especially from Toledo in Spain, or from Damascus in Syria.
a50f8085-8ff8-57a1-9ecc-7536a8854029.keywords: Trade; arms; armours; metalwork; geometric motifs; geometric decoration; floral decoration; vegetal motifs; vegetal decoration; craftsmanship; war; warfare; military objects

a57a7875-1547-559b-a57d-6fa92bce59cf.description: A capsule-charge gun called *Bou Habba* and crafted in southern Morocco in the early 19th century.
a57a7875-1547-559b-a57d-6fa92bce59cf.keywords: craftsmanship; arms; armours; metalwork; weapons; war; warfare; military objects
