a5c93080-d37b-5926-ad79-2d9bb61932f2.name: *The Grand Bazaar*
a5c93080-d37b-5926-ad79-2d9bb61932f2.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
a5c93080-d37b-5926-ad79-2d9bb61932f2.description2: Amadeo Preziosi often presented genre scenes from Istanbul in his unique style. Specifically, he incorporated diverse scenes from the Bazaar in a number of his paintings. This venue, particular to Istanbul, has been of great interest to western artists, and in Edmondo De Amicis’s words “is not just a building but a town”. The Grand Bazaar, which housed shops for a wide range of commercial goods and catered to almost all of the needs of customers, offered an incredible visual richness and diversity to the western artist. A reflection of this opulence is also evident in Preziosi’s painting, which includes numerous details from daily life.

a6e38d56-3857-5b4e-a7be-06bb9cacae78.name: *The Petition Writer*
a6e38d56-3857-5b4e-a7be-06bb9cacae78.keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters
a6e38d56-3857-5b4e-a7be-06bb9cacae78.description2: Osman Hamdi focused on dilemmas such as East and West, love and hate, life and death. While stylistically reminiscent of western Orientalist painters, his works reflect a more nuanced appreciation of Ottoman society and culture. He also gave importance to details while reflecting the colourful scenes of Turkish culture, traditional architecture, Ottoman fashion and domestic and social life of the women in the Ottoman Empire. And it’s obvious that he is the first painter who used human figures in the western style.

a6e39000-fe68-56fd-a598-f2bd48c41311.name: Silver brooch pin
a6e39000-fe68-56fd-a598-f2bd48c41311.description: The small collection of Berber jewellery that Sorolla´s family acquired during their visit to Morocco in February of 1919 includes this silver pin. The pins are indispensable parts of female jewellery; headbands, necklaces, bracelets and earrings complete the outfit. This pin served to fasten clothes to the shoulders and pins were always carried in pairs, connected by a string, which in this case was not preserved. The Museum preserves the other twin.
a6e39000-fe68-56fd-a598-f2bd48c41311.author: Covadonga Pitarch

a77f3909-2307-52b5-b2aa-0229a50ed6c5.name: Ceiling
a77f3909-2307-52b5-b2aa-0229a50ed6c5.author: Houria Cherid
a77f3909-2307-52b5-b2aa-0229a50ed6c5.archival: Marye, G., “Période Musulmane”, in *Catalogue d'Exposition du Musée National des Antiquités Algériennes* 1899, p. 22
a77f3909-2307-52b5-b2aa-0229a50ed6c5.description2: Wooden carved ceiling, painted in colour and gold leaf. Taken from the Algerian section of the Paris 1867 Exposition Universelle (world fair). Algerian woodwork.

a7fd98fa-f450-5ba3-b6d2-3909a56326ac.name: Decorated panel featuring a mosque
a7fd98fa-f450-5ba3-b6d2-3909a56326ac.description2: An Ottoman-style mosque, identifiable by its cone-shaped minarets, sits in the middle of this horseshoe arch supported by two columns. The lower panel contains a vase with various flowers emerging from it, such as carnations, tulips, and vine leaves. A dense rinceau pattern with flowers and leaves fills the gaps in the arch and the keystone and decorates the capitals of the columns. The main colours are yellow green and blue, although beige and brown also feature. This item shows traces of both Ottoman and Andalusian influences.

a81b5a25-c516-56c6-b670-eb0ae21f4f03.name: The Moorish Banqueting hall (Wilhelma Park)
a81b5a25-c516-56c6-b670-eb0ae21f4f03.holder: Wilhelma, Zoological and Botanical Garden Stuttgart
a81b5a25-c516-56c6-b670-eb0ae21f4f03.history:
King Wilhelm I of Württemberg commissioned to Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1837 the design of Moorish style buildings for his Wilhelma garden. The architect planned and built all the buildings with the exception of the Damascene Hall.  
The idea was not to reproduce faithfully the Islamic art but to lend an “oriental” flair to the garden. The mention of an “oriental garden” conjured up visions of elegance, luxury, colourful brilliance, seduction and eroticism.  
The Moorish style recalls the Islamic art of Spain and North Africa between the 12th and 15th centuries which reached its zenith in the Alhambra. It was fashionable in 19th century: Wilhelma is also known as the “Alhambra on the river Neckar” and other buildings – synagogues in Berlin and Vienna for example – were built in the Moorish style.
a81b5a25-c516-56c6-b670-eb0ae21f4f03.description2:
The Moorish Banqueting Hall was built in 1851 as a place for royal festivities, receptions and balls. The Moorish Villa and Moorish Banqueting Hall were separated by the Moorish Garden and linked to each other by the Covered Walkway.  
Amongst the absolute social highlights were the Stuttgart Imperial Days in September 1853. King Wilhelm I of Württemberg had invited Tsar Alexander II and the French Emperor Napoleon III to a meeting of reconciliation at Wilhelma. In 1944 the Moorish Banqueting Hall was heavily damaged by bombing. In 1961, after much deliberation – controversial as the decision was – the remains were demolished. Today the Aquarium with the Crocodile Hall is standing at the site. One small section of the original façade has survived. It forms the wall at the side of the Aquarium facing the Water Lily Pond.

a8732393-9f73-5349-bf08-2e06bf17b6f1.name: Jar with animal decorations
a8732393-9f73-5349-bf08-2e06bf17b6f1.description2: This oval-shaped double-handled *charbiya* has a long neck, a curved rim and a flat bottom. The main colours of the decorations are yellow, green and brown. On the shoulders, a strip of leaves in green and yellow are superimposed on a paler green background. A second strip of brown herringbone sits above a yellow and brown spotted cheetah, painted in profile with its head turned in full face and its big green eyes wide open. Its back is raised and topped with a ribbed crest. This item shows traces of both Ottoman and Andalusian influences.

a95b3b6a-66a7-5a79-99bd-6be598fec282.name: Dolmabahçe Palace Theatre under construction
a95b3b6a-66a7-5a79-99bd-6be598fec282.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
a95b3b6a-66a7-5a79-99bd-6be598fec282.description2: James Robertson came to Istanbul in 1841 to assist with modernization of the Imperial Mint and remained for 40 years, during which he served without interruption under no less than four Ottoman sultans. He started as head etcher in the Ottoman Mint. Then he began to take photos of Istanbul. He also painted watercolours, and in the early 1850s became interested in photography and went on to become a leading name among early photographers. Robertson’s Istanbul photographs are concerned primarily with the city’s historical monuments. They reveal the city’s magnificent Byzantine and Ottoman structures from different angles and with close-ups taken in an approach that is usually quite aesthetic. In this photo, Dolmabahçe Palace Theatre is seen under construction.

aa871988-924d-5384-8ea9-bf439584db36.name: Dish
aa871988-924d-5384-8ea9-bf439584db36.description:
The different exhibitions on Islamic Art gave new light to Islamic artworks and increased the interest from collectors about these pieces.  
This ceramic dish from Safi (Morocco) shows the interest for the traditional arts from North Africa.  
Collectors were interested not only in antiquities but also contemporary pieces from North Africa.
aa871988-924d-5384-8ea9-bf439584db36.author: Ana Cabrera
aa871988-924d-5384-8ea9-bf439584db36.keywords: Applied Arts; Formation of the collections in museums

aae1befb-bde5-5b51-b06a-8f5f49582dd4.name: Azulejo (glazed tile)
aae1befb-bde5-5b51-b06a-8f5f49582dd4.author: DGPC
aae1befb-bde5-5b51-b06a-8f5f49582dd4.keywords: Azulejo; glaze tile; armillary sphere; National identity
aae1befb-bde5-5b51-b06a-8f5f49582dd4.description2: Apart from its utility function and use for cladding façades, the azulejo is, at the beginning of the 20th century, an iconic expression of Portuguese art. This panel, produced by the Faience Factory of Caldas da Rainha, depicts tiles made in Seville in the 16th century for the Palace of Sintra.

aaef1d8a-bfc0-52ec-a6fc-9e01b30cc9d4.name: Capsule-charge handgun
aaef1d8a-bfc0-52ec-a6fc-9e01b30cc9d4.description: A capsule-charge gun called *Ida o Semlale* and crafted in southern Morocco in the early 19th century.
aaef1d8a-bfc0-52ec-a6fc-9e01b30cc9d4.keywords: craftsmanship; arms; armours; metalwork; weapons; war; warfare; military objects; bone; copper

ab21cc92-59d1-559f-ab5b-149da55c95bd.name: Vase
ab21cc92-59d1-559f-ab5b-149da55c95bd.description2: In 1891 Sultan Abdülhamid II founded the Yıldız Çini Fabrika-i Hümâyûnu (Yıldız Royal Tile Factory) in the garden of Yıldız Palace for the purpose of reviving Turkish tile art and giving it a new direction and momentum. Vases, hanging wall plates and many sorts of daily-use wares were produced in the factory, including writing and dinner table utensils, card plates, lidded bowls, pans, *aşure* (a kind of dessert) trays, sugar bowls, tea and coffee cups. A vase with conical body with wide mouth and round foot. There is a landscape painted on its body. The rest of its body has an intricate floral design painted on a green base. On the base a stamp of the star and crescent and dates of 1312-13 written in Arabic can be seen.

abc52fc4-de0b-59c4-80c9-078c5a2e0416.name: Topkapı Palace (Fruit Room of Ahmed III)
abc52fc4-de0b-59c4-80c9-078c5a2e0416.description2: By the Westernisation period, the abstract decorative and ornamental features of classical Ottoman art are replaced by naturalistic motifs.

acce08e9-8aba-5eba-b44c-f4bb89218e20.name: *The Grammar of Ornament*
acce08e9-8aba-5eba-b44c-f4bb89218e20.author: Mina Moraitou
acce08e9-8aba-5eba-b44c-f4bb89218e20.description2: A monumental work by Owen Jones on design with 20 chapters dedicated to the traditions of different historical periods ranging from the savage tribes, the arts of the ancient world, the arts of the Middle East and the Far East to European art. The last chapter is devoted to naturalistic ornament.

ad9f5054-4028-51c0-91cb-d8f1179760fa.name: *Two Figures*
ad9f5054-4028-51c0-91cb-d8f1179760fa.description: This little sketch of two female figures represents a typical orientalist-themed image. Sorolla could undertake studies abroad thanks to a grant. During that period he mainly produced two types of Oriental paintings, which were still very popular in that period: great scenes for the Academy where he studied and small works (as the one on display) to sell and augment his income.
ad9f5054-4028-51c0-91cb-d8f1179760fa.author: Covadonga Pitarch
ad9f5054-4028-51c0-91cb-d8f1179760fa.keywords: Orientalist painting; Spain; Formation of painters

ae42a45e-443f-5a1d-aaab-85cd72bce06d.name: *A Greek Mountaineer*
ae42a45e-443f-5a1d-aaab-85cd72bce06d.author: Washington, D.C., 1991, 80-81, no 28
ae42a45e-443f-5a1d-aaab-85cd72bce06d.description2: During the Ottoman occupation, Greek peasants who were dispossessed of their property often retreated to impregnable mountain regions, where they engaged in resistance against the Turks. These mountaineers, who both fascinated and frightened European travellers, were romanticised by artists and poets such as Lord Byron. The man depicted here clearly represents the type of mountaineer described by Byron. To emphasize his costume and his swift movement, he appears in full gear, the sleeves of his jacket falling freely to the back as if to underscore his impulsive gesture. Pistols and knives are tucked in his belt. His right hand rests on his musket; his left hand proudly touches the tip of his sword. Haag chose to place the figure in a grand mountainous landscape, complete with a ruined temple. This sacred monument may be identified as the temple of Apollo Epicurius in Arcadia in the central Peloponnese. This enhances the dignity of the figure, whose nobility and heroism are worthy of the principles of his legendary ancestors.

aed162cf-cef3-52e5-aa78-567138f64d2a.name: Bowl with stand
aed162cf-cef3-52e5-aa78-567138f64d2a.holder: Musée de la Céramique Sidi Kacem Jelizi
aed162cf-cef3-52e5-aa78-567138f64d2a.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
aed162cf-cef3-52e5-aa78-567138f64d2a.keywords: Floral motifs; winged motifs; cermaics from Nabeul
aed162cf-cef3-52e5-aa78-567138f64d2a.description2: This bowl with a bulging rim sits on a stand. The decoration is made of two layers of concentric patterns around a central circle, filled with winged motifs. These green and brown patterns are painted on a yellow background. Although this kind of bowl is usually used to serve couscous, in the town Nabeul, and particularly for the occasion of Islamic New Year, each child is presented with a *methred* bowl, filled with golden couscous, dried fruit, dates, a hard-boiled egg and sweets. This all surrounds a statuette made of sugar, moulded and coloured to resemble an animal (such as a rooster or a gazelle) or a figure, like a doll or cavalier.

af2dcc82-957a-54c2-9a0f-e5e5ba86b4d3.name: Ottoman Clothing Album
af2dcc82-957a-54c2-9a0f-e5e5ba86b4d3.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
af2dcc82-957a-54c2-9a0f-e5e5ba86b4d3.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
af2dcc82-957a-54c2-9a0f-e5e5ba86b4d3.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
af2dcc82-957a-54c2-9a0f-e5e5ba86b4d3.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

af7e1b24-5d7e-5856-900a-6365e01610ba.name: Portrait Album – Ottoman State Officers
af7e1b24-5d7e-5856-900a-6365e01610ba.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
af7e1b24-5d7e-5856-900a-6365e01610ba.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
af7e1b24-5d7e-5856-900a-6365e01610ba.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
af7e1b24-5d7e-5856-900a-6365e01610ba.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

aff0f573-5e91-5646-94a2-26bd51ba0e14.name: *Interior of a Harem*
aff0f573-5e91-5646-94a2-26bd51ba0e14.description: This painting was made around 1863 when the author travelled to Morocco with Mariano Fortuny. The reason for his travel was to paint the characters and picturesque garments as the way of life of the people from Morocco. The influence his experiences had on his works can be found in his paintings and drawings. During his travels he bought exotic artworks, such as Egyptian sarcophagi. Harem and markets are considered a genre painting in Orientalism.
aff0f573-5e91-5646-94a2-26bd51ba0e14.author: Carolina Miguel Arroyo
aff0f573-5e91-5646-94a2-26bd51ba0e14.keywords: North Africa; Orientalism; Travelling; Harem; Women

aff1ae5a-f832-5831-b8c0-8ad91d5e93ec.name: Inkstand
aff1ae5a-f832-5831-b8c0-8ad91d5e93ec.keywords: Arts and Crafts; Daily utilitarian ware; Portugal; Vista Alegre; Factory
aff1ae5a-f832-5831-b8c0-8ad91d5e93ec.description2: Inskstandish shaped like a brigantine, representing young triton blowing on a conch trumpet. Ink wells, lids and edges decorated with flowers in polychrome. Base of the inkstand is rested on waves, painted in shades of green.  The inkstandish reflects the taste for nautical representations, evoking the national maritime glory, while it introduces delicate floral motifs, in the romantic style of that epoch. Painted by Victor Rousseau, master of painting in the Vista Alegre Porcelain Factory, this object is an example of the early decorative tendencies, distinguishable by the virtuosity of the drawings, intricate forms and artistic experimentation.

en: Arez, Ilda, *et al.*, *Vista Alegre Porcelanas*, Lisbon: Inapa, 1989.
Henriques, Paulo, “Ciclos de Modernidade” in Mântua, Ana Anjos (ed), *Cerâmica Portuguesa do século XVI ao século XX*, Geneva: Musée Ariana, 2004.
Valente, Vasco, *Porcelana Artística Portuguesa*, Porto: Imprensa Moderna Limitada, 1949.

b0034e9d-b0b0-5bbc-a3c7-5d26a2e4d496.name: Textile
b0034e9d-b0b0-5bbc-a3c7-5d26a2e4d496.description: Cotton textile made in twill weave. The complete surface is decorated, in different colours, with the writing decoration in silver and white lines.
b0034e9d-b0b0-5bbc-a3c7-5d26a2e4d496.holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
b0034e9d-b0b0-5bbc-a3c7-5d26a2e4d496.author: Lucina Llorente
b0034e9d-b0b0-5bbc-a3c7-5d26a2e4d496.materials: Cotton and silver; tabby or plain weave, twill weave and stecilled decoration

b08652d5-bffa-5858-a142-61103d91cf12.name: *Khayali* necklace and earrings
b08652d5-bffa-5858-a142-61103d91cf12.holder: Musée des Arts et Traditions Populaires
b08652d5-bffa-5858-a142-61103d91cf12.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
b08652d5-bffa-5858-a142-61103d91cf12.description2: Although it was originally used in Tunis as both a necklace and head jewellery (like a diadem), the *khayali* was worn in other Tunisian towns simply as a necklace. It consists of a very thin gold chain with rose-encrusted diamonds pendants. The *khayali* is made of 9-carat gold and inspired by the European style. The *sboulitat* earrings are also made of 9-carat gold and encrusted with roses.

b15011a9-1d5f-5210-be56-0a51595a1b75.name: The King's House on the Schachen
b15011a9-1d5f-5210-be56-0a51595a1b75.type: Hunting lodge; summer manor; royal villa in the mountains
b15011a9-1d5f-5210-be56-0a51595a1b75.location: Bavarian Alps near Garmisch-Partenkirchen; altitude 1,866 meters
b15011a9-1d5f-5210-be56-0a51595a1b75.history: The Turkish Room inside the King's House on the Schachen spreads an Oriental fairytale charm with a gold, blue and red colour combination. The design for the room was based on an engraving by the Englishman Thomas Allom, published in an architectural work on Constantinople. The engraving shows a room built by Sultan Selim III (r. 1789–1807) in the Palace of Eyüb. However, the overall impression created by the furniture and colourfulness derives entirely from contemporary influences.
b15011a9-1d5f-5210-be56-0a51595a1b75.keywords: King Ludwig II; Bavaria; mountain refuge; Schachen; Moorish style; Romanticism; gardens
b15011a9-1d5f-5210-be56-0a51595a1b75.description2: The King's House, built from plans by Georg Dollmann in 1869 to 1872 on the Schachen Alp near Garmisch-Partenkirchen, was King Ludwig II's mountain refuge. The wooden post-and-infill structure in the form of a Swiss chalet has five living rooms downstairs with cembra wood panelling and a mixture of stylistic elements. The whole of the upper floor, however, is taken up by the "Turkish Hall". With its coloured glass windows, opulently embroidered textiles, peacock feathers and candelabra it reflects the fascination of the king and his contemporaries with the Orient.

b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.name: Steam engine building
b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.holder: Prussian Palaces (Stiftung Preussische Schlösser und Gärten Berlin Brandenburg)
b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.history:
In October 1842 the steam engine in the "Mosque," which could reach 81.4 horsepower, was inaugurated, allowing jets of water from the great fountain in front of Sanssouci Palace to rise to an impressive 38 meters. By possessing what was the most powerful machine in Prussia at the time, built by the young entrepreneur August Borsig, King Frederick William IV hoped to compete with the technical supremacy of England.  
Although today's supply of water to the fountains in Sanssouci Park is provided by means of modern electrical pumps, a visit to the "Mosque" allows the visitor to experience a technical marvel from days past that is still in operation.
b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.keywords: Moorish style; Romanticism; Sanssouci; Potsdam; exoticism; steam engine; steam pumping; Frederick William IV; gardens
b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.description2: The Steam Engine Building, located on a bay of the Havel River called the Neustädter Havelbucht, is at once the most charming as well as the most exotic building in Potsdam. Frederick William IV, the "Romantic on the throne," had it built by Ludwig Persius from 1841-1843, "in the style of the Turkish mosques, with a minaret as a smokestack." The building, which could still be seen at that time from Sanssouci Palace, added a picturesque architectural accent to the Potsdam cultural landscape.

b20d222f-63fe-50b9-acfd-a854de63e772.name: Photograph: *A Mohammedan Funeral, Egypt*
b20d222f-63fe-50b9-acfd-a854de63e772.description: Stereoscopic photography that creates the illusion of depth of field from a two-dimensional image by using a specific viewfinder, or stereoscope. The photograph is formed by two apparently identical images mounted on a rigid board. Stereographic cards turned into a popular entertainment medium from the late 1880s until 1970, reaching its peak of popularity in the first decade of the twentieth century. The ceremonies of funeral, studied for example by the British anthropologist Edward William Lane around the time of the dating of the photography, are very similar for men and women: the wailing is produced by the family and community, and is accompanied by a series of prayers from the Qur´an and ritual cleansing of the body. In this photography, within this "farewell ceremony" we can distinguish the coffin and the funeral procession, mostly male, who plays different songs and prayers; after the coffin, the procession would be closed for the mourners.
b20d222f-63fe-50b9-acfd-a854de63e772.keywords: Photography; funeral; ritual; travel; Egypt; scenes of life

b23d072c-13ac-5c66-9709-b4cefd84d692.name: Inkwell with Oriental decoration
b23d072c-13ac-5c66-9709-b4cefd84d692.description2: The use of this type of inkwell was borrowed in the Romanian lands from the Ottomans. This particular inkwell belonged to Ion Ghica, one of the Romanian politicians who prepared the 1848 Wallachian revolution. As member of Wallachia’s revolutionary committee, he was sent to Istanbul before the start of the revolution to have talks with Ottoman officials and the ambassadors of European states, in an attempt to convince them to support the claims of the Romanian revolutionaries. After the revolution was defeated, he remained in Istanbul. Between 1854-1857 he was governor of Samos. In 1866, after the election of Carol of Hohenzollern as prince of the United Principalities, Ghica went to Istanbul (May-July) to try to obtain the recognition of his reign.

b2a64729-0616-53e6-bc8d-4d7583ceac8c.name: Plate
b2a64729-0616-53e6-bc8d-4d7583ceac8c.description2: Sultan Abdülhamid II founded in 1891 the *Yıldız Çini Fabrika-i Hümâyûnu* (Yıldız Royal Tile Factory) in the garden of Yıldız Palace in order to revive Turkish tile art and give it a new direction and momentum. Vases, hanging wall plates and many sorts of daily-use wares were produced in the factory, including writing and dinner table utensils, card plates, lidded bowls, pans, *aşure* (a kind of dessert) trays, sugar bowls, tea and coffee cups. This plate features a dark green background on which there is a *tuğra* (monogram) made of gilding and a border around the edge.

b2d452de-0ae0-577e-b868-f2761e941b26.name: Vase with stand
b2d452de-0ae0-577e-b868-f2761e941b26.description: This vase with stand reproduces the shape of the ceramic vase known as "The Alhambra vase" and the stand recalls the little tables of the Arab cafés. The technique used is damascening and references Arab techniques of metal decoration. It is a good example of the extension of the Neo-Mudéjar style, not only in the decorations, as the interlacing arabesques, or techniques, but also in the shape of the artworks.
b2d452de-0ae0-577e-b868-f2761e941b26.author: Ana Cabrera
b2d452de-0ae0-577e-b868-f2761e941b26.keywords: Neo-mudejar style; Applied Arts; Production of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode

b3ffe5a9-b94e-57b4-815b-88dcdb526256.name: *Tomb of Sultan Selim II*
b3ffe5a9-b94e-57b4-815b-88dcdb526256.description2: Although essentially a realist painter, Şevket Dağ worked with free brush stokes in the style of Corot. He is celebrated for his paintings of the interiors of mosques. He took lessons from Osman Hamdi Bey, and followed his master in painting genre pictures reflecting various aspects of Ottoman life. In addition to mosque interiors he would also paint scenes in market places, still-life compositions and the interiors of houses. Over time, Şevket Dağ's work began to be appreciated abroad following exhibitions in European art centres such as Munich and Paris, and he was awarded a gold medal in the Munich International Exhibition of 1909. He later came under the influence of the impressionists.

b424ad60-28d9-5e2b-8050-b9eeeaa8a7c0.name: *Book bindings*
b424ad60-28d9-5e2b-8050-b9eeeaa8a7c0.description: This illustration shows book bindings made by Wunder und Kölbl (Vienna), in leather-mosaic and hand gilding. The illustration was included in the *Kunst und Kunstgewerbe auf der Wiener Weltausstellung 1873*, edited by Carl Lützow, 1875, p. 188.
b424ad60-28d9-5e2b-8050-b9eeeaa8a7c0.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
b424ad60-28d9-5e2b-8050-b9eeeaa8a7c0.materials: Print showing book bindings made by Wunder und Kölbl

b437a6ed-24fb-56b3-b57f-e110c5ab5d47.name: Plate
b437a6ed-24fb-56b3-b57f-e110c5ab5d47.description: Plate produced in Valencia in Oriental style. This object was part of José Ros’ collection “Fabricación de objetos hispano-árabes en terra cocida”, which was displayed at the Exhibition of Valencia in 1890.
b437a6ed-24fb-56b3-b57f-e110c5ab5d47.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

b474efac-e6f6-5108-a2dd-76d0a7cfc596.name: Metal teapot
b474efac-e6f6-5108-a2dd-76d0a7cfc596.description: A 19th-century metal teapot named simply “Right” in Morocco, after Richard Wright (“RR”) of the Manchester manufactory. Although in the style of Moroccan teapots, its floral decoration is inspired by European designs.
b474efac-e6f6-5108-a2dd-76d0a7cfc596.keywords: Applied arts; craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmanship; kitchen ware; domestic ware; metalwork; floral decoration; floral motifs; vegetal decoration; vegetal motifs; British in Morocco; Richard Wright; trade; finished products

b4f64de8-89f2-5608-a2d6-f642d0ce7827.name: *Cairo, from the Gate of Citizenib, looking towards the Desert of Suez*
b4f64de8-89f2-5608-a2d6-f642d0ce7827.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
b4f64de8-89f2-5608-a2d6-f642d0ce7827.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
b4f64de8-89f2-5608-a2d6-f642d0ce7827.keywords: Fatimah Khatun; Sultan Khalil; Sayidah Nafisah; Madrasah of Sultan Hassan; Khedive Ismail
b4f64de8-89f2-5608-a2d6-f642d0ce7827.description2: Although entitled 'Cairo from the Gate of Citizenib, looking towards the Desert of Suez', this view actually shows Cairo as seen from Tel Zaynum, situated to the south of the city. The monuments depicted include the tombs of Fatimah Khatun and Sultan Khalil on the left and the mosque of Sayidah Nafisah on the right. In the background, one can discern both the Cairo citadel on the right and the Madrasah of Sultan Hassan on the left. Notwithstanding the incorrect identification of this area of Cairo, the scenes gives a good impression of one of its quarters with its traditional urban architecture and historical monuments before major urban development projects were undertaken under the Khedive Ismail (1863-1879), who was determined to turn Cairo into a modern, international city  on a par with European capitals.
b4f64de8-89f2-5608-a2d6-f642d0ce7827.artist_birthplace: David Roberts: Edinburgh, Scotland; Louis Hague: Tournai, Belgium
b4f64de8-89f2-5608-a2d6-f642d0ce7827.artist_deathplace: David Roberts: London; Louis Hague: London

b54a4c02-3027-5de2-965f-2bb5a2395c13.name: Folk costume
b54a4c02-3027-5de2-965f-2bb5a2395c13.author: Nada Andonovska
b54a4c02-3027-5de2-965f-2bb5a2395c13.keywords: Embroidery; apron; Albanians; costume; floral decoration; geometric patterns; geometric decoration; geometric motifs
b54a4c02-3027-5de2-965f-2bb5a2395c13.materials: White canvas, embroidery, woollen home-woven fabric
b54a4c02-3027-5de2-965f-2bb5a2395c13.second_name: Traditional attire worn by Albanian women
b54a4c02-3027-5de2-965f-2bb5a2395c13.description2: The Albanian community is an important element in the multicultural milieu of ethnicities in the Republic of Macedonia. This outfit preserves some distinctive features of the clothing and adornment worn by Albanian women in Macedonia in the 19th century and early 20th century. The cotton canvas tunic is moderately decorated by embroidery of floral patterns on the sleeves and at the front part of the cleavage. The wool apron is embellished with geometric patterns woven of varied wool threads along the left and right hem, which end with woollen fringes in different colours.

b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.name: Drums
b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.dimensions: Upper diameter 12 cm; lower diameter 10 cm; height 28 cm
b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.author: Vito Lattanzi, Marina Minozzi
b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.keywords: Darbuka; ceramic; enamelling; cobalt-blue; bleau de Fez; Morocco; museums; collection; collector; anthropology; ethnology; travel; exploration; scientific expedition; geography; representation of the other; material culture; music; musical instrument
b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.description2: The two drums are part of the flourishing tradition of enamelled ceramic in Fez, in production since the Middle Ages. Cobalt blue and white decorations identify Fez products dating to the second half of the 19th century. The drums belong to the ethnographic collections of the Pigorini Museum founded between the 19th and the 20th century. The origins of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

b65922f4-01d3-5457-a9bc-98f6df701f87.name: Gospel cover of Dorotheos Proios from Edirne
b65922f4-01d3-5457-a9bc-98f6df701f87.author: Ballian 1992, 86-7, no.46
b65922f4-01d3-5457-a9bc-98f6df701f87.description2: The gospel comes from Adrianople, but a handwritten note on the second page notes that: "…it was crafted and decorated here in Smyrna". From around the mid-eighteenth century Smyrna was the second most important port of the Ottoman Empire, and an important part of its economic life was in the hands of Greeks. The “Frankish quarter” and the preponderance of large-scale, foreign trade gave o cosmopolitan air to Smyrniot society. There is strong western European influence on this impressive silver cover made for Dorotheos Proios. Scrolled cartouches, thronging garlands of roses and conch shells in high relief make it a triumph of Rococo art, at least after the fashion in which it was understood in the Ottoman Empire. Smyrna was an important centre of silver production, but the designs were in general circulation and compositions were put together to fit the circumstances.

en: Ballian, Anna, *Treasures from the Greek Communities of Asia Minor and Eastern Thrace. Collections from the Benaki Museum*, Athens: Benaki Museum, 1992.

b69ab8bc-8ca2-5930-bf6d-22951609c373.name: Harness for a British royal carriage
b69ab8bc-8ca2-5930-bf6d-22951609c373.description: Made for a British royal carriage, this harness was manufactured in Morocco in one of the country’s most prestigious workshops. The harness accentuates the skill of Moroccan artisans in a style distinctively *le maroquin* (Moroccan).
b69ab8bc-8ca2-5930-bf6d-22951609c373.holder: Agronomic and Veterinary Institute Hassan II
b69ab8bc-8ca2-5930-bf6d-22951609c373.archival: Sophie Landrin, "Du role actual du cheval au Maroc: etat des lieux et perspectives" (The current role of the horse in Morocco: state and perspectives), PhD. Veterinary science, Alfort: ENVA, 2009.
b69ab8bc-8ca2-5930-bf6d-22951609c373.keywords: Craftsmanship; traditional craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmen; horsemanship; workshop; maroquin; leather; leatherwork; trade; raw material; finished products; Moroccan production for European market

b69b45bc-18ac-5427-86ca-9f760fc47793.name: Qur'an box
b69b45bc-18ac-5427-86ca-9f760fc47793.author: Mina Moraitou
b69b45bc-18ac-5427-86ca-9f760fc47793.description2: A rectangular Quran box on four feet with inlaid decoration which consist of inscriptions on a background with vegetal scrolls.

b7a9c747-adba-50e0-a0a8-312875639e02.name: Gold bracelet
b7a9c747-adba-50e0-a0a8-312875639e02.description2: Based closely on Assyrian reliefs. Illustrates Assyrian influence on 19th century jewellery.

b7d0545b-be32-5c47-ab91-272824042882.name: Headdress
b7d0545b-be32-5c47-ab91-272824042882.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
b7d0545b-be32-5c47-ab91-272824042882.author: Huda Kilani
b7d0545b-be32-5c47-ab91-272824042882.description2: Line of silver Ottoman coins sewn together on a piece of fabric, part of a headdress. This kind of jewellery was part of the dowry the groom gave to the bride. Dowries consisted mostly of silver jewellery because only the rich could afford gold jewellery. The use of coins as pieces of jewellery in particular was an indirect statement of the financial status of the groom, as brides wore those pieces of jewellery in front of relatives and friends.

b814bde1-48f9-5356-8789-4fecae32bde0.name: Bridal tunic (*Veyke*)
b814bde1-48f9-5356-8789-4fecae32bde0.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
b814bde1-48f9-5356-8789-4fecae32bde0.keywords: bridal tunic; embroidery; costume; silver; wedding; marriage
b814bde1-48f9-5356-8789-4fecae32bde0.materials: White canvas, embroidery with variegate threads
b814bde1-48f9-5356-8789-4fecae32bde0.description2: This bridal tunic is abundantly decorated with relief embroidery above the lower hem. The embroidery is very impressive owing to the varied relief techniques applied. It has been created by application of black woollen thread with slight borders in other colours, flat silver string and silver-thread braid. The sleeves are also richly adorned with embroidery in predominantly red nuances. The symbolism of embroidered patterns endow this tunic with universal values distinctive to Macedonian home-made women's attire.

b8eb5a77-e816-5c46-818d-96a032573547.name: *Landscape from Gebze*
b8eb5a77-e816-5c46-818d-96a032573547.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
b8eb5a77-e816-5c46-818d-96a032573547.keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters
b8eb5a77-e816-5c46-818d-96a032573547.description2: Osman Hamdi focused on dilemmas such as East and West, love and hate, life and death. While stylistically reminiscent of western Orientalist painters, his works reflect a more nuanced appreciation of Ottoman society and culture. In the art of his paintings, he depicted unique details so diligently that he made us recognize our environment and Turkish culture. He illustrated carpets, tile panels, calligraphies, decorative arts, shrines, mosques and human figures in his paintings. He also gave importance to details while reflecting the colourful scenes of Turkish culture, traditional architecture, Ottoman fashion and domestic and social life of the women in the Ottoman Empire. And it’s obvious that he is the first painter who used human figures in the western style.

b8fd5a61-6e87-5479-8b87-53c6a66033f2.name: A drawing showing wooden gratings from various mosques
b8fd5a61-6e87-5479-8b87-53c6a66033f2.author: Marina Minozzi
b8fd5a61-6e87-5479-8b87-53c6a66033f2.archival: A. Melani, *L'ornamento policromo nelle arti e nelle industrie artistiche, medievale e moderne per uso delle scuole e degli artisti…*, Milano 1886, tav. 25
b8fd5a61-6e87-5479-8b87-53c6a66033f2.keywords: Applied arts; museums of applied arts; Islamic art; Islamic influence; book; model; crafstmanship; sketch; drawing; Grammar of ornament; Alfredo Melani; Owen Jones; Prisse d'Avennes; Islamic architecture; schools of applied arts
b8fd5a61-6e87-5479-8b87-53c6a66033f2.copyright: Copyright image: Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale, Roma.
b8fd5a61-6e87-5479-8b87-53c6a66033f2.description2: Alfredo Melani, teacher and then director at the school of applied arts in Milan, was one of the main exponents of oriental decorative motifs in Italy. During the 1880s he published a series of works and texts discussing eastern art, often in the form of handbooks and essays. Subsequently, toward the end of the century Camillo Boito pioneered courses in the history of styles at the Accademia of Brera. Dell’ornamento nell’architettura written by Melani, includes a whole chapter about Muslim decorations, from which the drawing showing wooden grills from mosques is taken.

en: Barucci, C., “L'orientalismo nelle fonti bibliografiche e nella manualistica italiana dell'Ottocento”, in Giusti, M.A. and Godoli, E. (eds), *L’ orientalismo nell’architettura italiana tra Ottocento e Novecento*, atti del convegno internazionale di studi (1997), Siena, 1999, pp. 23–30.

b966135b-aa13-5813-b98e-6dab1d391e68.name: Shelf
b966135b-aa13-5813-b98e-6dab1d391e68.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
b966135b-aa13-5813-b98e-6dab1d391e68.description2: The back on this shelf is decorated with a perforated pattern, whereas the rack is decorated with a floral pattern (daisies) and small hooks. The section directly beneath the shelf is also decorated with a floral motif.

b98b5c58-b52f-54a7-85fa-fdea8460caf3.name: *Adornment Of The Bride*
b98b5c58-b52f-54a7-85fa-fdea8460caf3.author: Petar Petrovic
b98b5c58-b52f-54a7-85fa-fdea8460caf3.description2: Bright, folkloristically vivid, technically impeccable and with an abundance of ethnographic detail, this is one of Jovanović’s best paintings, both in this period and as a whole. In a broader sense, this work by Paja Jovanović contains all the relevant characteristics of the poetics of academicism and thus – together with Jovanović’s other works from this period – had a crucial impact on the development of realism in Serbian painting in the late 19th century.

b9ec5638-cdfd-59b1-9665-cf8e39b21d9b.name: *A landscape from Eyüp, Istanbul*
b9ec5638-cdfd-59b1-9665-cf8e39b21d9b.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
b9ec5638-cdfd-59b1-9665-cf8e39b21d9b.description2: At the beginning of the 19th century, romantic painters who appreciated eastern mysticism brought newly discovered eastern landscapes with their paintings which contained fiery colours and interesting landscapes. One of those painters coming to Istanbul from Malta and affected by eastern mysticism was Amadeo Preziosi. He usually painted scenes from daily life, such as shops between streets, coffeehouses, baths, peddlers passing the street, a woman filling water from a fountain and figures from different ethnic groups. Like many of his contemporaries, Preziosi had been lured to the exotic city of Istanbul. He also tried to reflect the cultural diversity of the city in his paintings. Especially in his watercolour paintings he loved expressing the blue water of the Bosporus with its caïques, pavilions, palaces, boats, mansions, residences, bazaars and cemeteries.

ba422441-e1c1-5256-9187-632e779470fd.name: Firearm
ba422441-e1c1-5256-9187-632e779470fd.holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée
ba422441-e1c1-5256-9187-632e779470fd.author: Bechir Yazidi
ba422441-e1c1-5256-9187-632e779470fd.keywords: Tunisian army; Musée de l'Armée; Palais de la Rose
ba422441-e1c1-5256-9187-632e779470fd.description2: This firearm is a French model from 1822. Its total length measures 353 mm, with the barrel measuring 200 mm and the calibre 17.7 mm. All the embellishments, except the ring, are made of brass. It has a hollow-headed ramrod, and an elongated breech which extends to the pommel.

baa15a8e-e8d7-5417-9132-86b970237c10.name: Bowl
baa15a8e-e8d7-5417-9132-86b970237c10.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
baa15a8e-e8d7-5417-9132-86b970237c10.artist: Design: Johann Machytka & Franz Schmoranz für J&L Lobmeyr
baa15a8e-e8d7-5417-9132-86b970237c10.materials: Tansparent glass with coloured and gilded decoration
baa15a8e-e8d7-5417-9132-86b970237c10.description2: Bowl made by Lobmeyr in Oriental style and decorated with the inscription, "Wer sich in fremde Dinge mengt, hat den Schaden davon, Die Klugheut ist die mächtigste Stütze des Menschen und die Rechtschaffenheit ist seine beste Eigenschaft".

baa9427d-f633-556e-9aa9-f175636f895f.name: Bracelet
baa9427d-f633-556e-9aa9-f175636f895f.holder: Musée des Arts et Traditions Populaires
baa9427d-f633-556e-9aa9-f175636f895f.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
baa9427d-f633-556e-9aa9-f175636f895f.description2: This silver bracelet, which is lined with gold and encrusted with roses, is made of a longer chain of openwork rosettes and framed by geometric motifs. A jagged gold leaf lines the inside of the bracelet. All the silver motifs are encrusted with roses. The two identical halves of the bracelet are joined by hinge and pin fastening topped by a large pearl.

baf82baf-93a9-5da4-b22c-8e5e634174fe.name: Miniature
baf82baf-93a9-5da4-b22c-8e5e634174fe.description:
This framed octagonal miniature shows a scene in a portico where men and women talk. A large blue curtain, two ribbed columns and a lobulated arch over another hidden column set the composition where a bearded Arab man with a turban, dressed in traditional Turkish costume in blue, red and white, is seated on a carpet, looking at a woman and a man who is introducing her. On the right and left sides, two couples of Circassian odalisques complete the scene and a standing armed man closes it on our right side.  
In the horizon beyond the harem we can see magnificent palaces by the water, probably the sea in Istanbul.
baf82baf-93a9-5da4-b22c-8e5e634174fe.author: Cristina Giménez

baf9e3e8-08a9-59e2-8c21-17ce2e3a24c6.name: *Moorish Parade*
baf9e3e8-08a9-59e2-8c21-17ce2e3a24c6.description:
This painting was made around 1863 when the author travelled to Morocco with Mariano Fortuny. The reason of his travel was to paint the characters and picturesque garments as the way of life of the people from Morocco.  
His experiences can be seen in his paintings and drawings.  
During his travels he bought exotic artworks as Egyptian sarcophagi.  
Harem and markets are considered a genre painting in Orientalism.
baf9e3e8-08a9-59e2-8c21-17ce2e3a24c6.author: Ámparo López

bb8237ee-e92e-5329-9529-6fd346236dd0.name: *Jaffa from the Camp of Ibrahim Pasha*
bb8237ee-e92e-5329-9529-6fd346236dd0.description: This print shows the Ibrahim Pasha camp at Jaffa during the Egyptian – Ottoman War (1830–1833). Muhammad Ali Pasha demanded control of Greater Syria for the Ottoman Empire. Ali sent his army into Syria under the command of his son Ibrahim Pasha. The Egyptian navy landed at Jaffa.
bb8237ee-e92e-5329-9529-6fd346236dd0.author: Carmen Linés Viñuales
bb8237ee-e92e-5329-9529-6fd346236dd0.third_name: *Jafa. Vista del Campamento de Ibrahin Baja*

bbeb5c8c-87db-5293-acee-f6b517d2244d.name: Box
bbeb5c8c-87db-5293-acee-f6b517d2244d.description: Box made in Paris in Oriental style.
bbeb5c8c-87db-5293-acee-f6b517d2244d.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

bbeb7fe5-88d9-5182-83a9-e637b3a17a0b.name: Tile panel
bbeb7fe5-88d9-5182-83a9-e637b3a17a0b.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
bbeb7fe5-88d9-5182-83a9-e637b3a17a0b.keywords: Ceramic; earthenware; collection; collector; vegetal decoration; ceramic tile; tilework; tile panel; Iznik; Ottoman ceramic; revival
bbeb7fe5-88d9-5182-83a9-e637b3a17a0b.materials: Slip-covered and hand-painted in various colours and glazed, on earthenware blanks
bbeb7fe5-88d9-5182-83a9-e637b3a17a0b.description2:
The architect of Membland Hall in Devon commissioned this sumptuous design for bathroom tiles from William Morris. Morris had the tiles painted in the studios of William de Morgan (1839-1917). They represent a rare collaboration between these two creative geniuses.  
Edward Charles Baring, 1st Baron Revelstoke, was the builder of Membland Hall. He was a merchant banker. The hall was later demolished.

bc05121b-1942-54f8-ba62-84b29282f089.name: Tile Panel
bc05121b-1942-54f8-ba62-84b29282f089.description2: Kütahya was the second most important ceramic production centre after İznik due to the rich clay deposits in the area. Although there was a decline in ceramic production at the beginning of the 19th century, in the last quarter of that same century production was revived and new designs inspired by İznik ceramics were produced.

bc4af44a-740c-54ce-806a-021695934601.name: Yıldız Ceramic vase
bc4af44a-740c-54ce-806a-021695934601.description2: Sultan Abdülhamid II founded in 1891 the *Yıldız Çini Fabrika-i Hümâyûnu* (Yıldız Royal Tile Factory) in the garden of Yıldız Palace in order to revive Turkish tile art and give it a new direction and momentum. Vases, hanging wall plates and many sorts of daily-use wares were produced in the factory, including writing and dinner table utensils, card plates, lidded bowls, pans, *aşure* (a kind of dessert) trays, sugar bowls, tea and coffee cups. The vase has yellow covers and two handles. There is a landscape of a tree and a house near the water on the vase.

bc65e295-73e5-5ae4-84e4-1777b2658828.name: Bracelet
bc65e295-73e5-5ae4-84e4-1777b2658828.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
bc65e295-73e5-5ae4-84e4-1777b2658828.author: Huda Kilani
bc65e295-73e5-5ae4-84e4-1777b2658828.keywords: Bedouin; settler; village; economy; dowry; tradition; marriage; Ottoman Jordan
bc65e295-73e5-5ae4-84e4-1777b2658828.description2:
Hollow domes and welded reliefs with locking mechanism. Silver jewellery was the most common, because only rich people could afford gold jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom.  
The Jordanian economy relied on trades and crafts and new waves of people started to come to Jordan and began to settle for these purposes. This object is an example of how traditional fashion reflected the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is also an example of local personal attire, fashion, costumes and rites.

bc71fd0a-a9bf-5d5a-881e-ff89569de8a9.name: Small pot
bc71fd0a-a9bf-5d5a-881e-ff89569de8a9.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
bc71fd0a-a9bf-5d5a-881e-ff89569de8a9.description2: This small pot is decorated on its base and its neck by a braided band with a red copper outline. Rectangular cartouches on the body, also outlined in red copper, contain silver Arabic inscriptions reading "hard work brings rewards" and "patience wins the race".

bc8e9132-343b-5b7f-a75d-aa8304520a26.name: Tughra of Sultan Osman III
bc8e9132-343b-5b7f-a75d-aa8304520a26.holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts
bc8e9132-343b-5b7f-a75d-aa8304520a26.keywords: Wood; gilding; watercolour; painting; tuğra; tughra
bc8e9132-343b-5b7f-a75d-aa8304520a26.description2: *Tughras*, official monograms of the sultans, are one the first things to come to mind when Ottoman art or history is mentioned. The size of this *tughra* of Sultan Osman III makes it an interesting example and it has features peculiar to the art of the AH 12th / AD 18th century.

bd9ac0b4-17dd-5d2a-86a5-baadbae9f621.name: Jeweller’s tools box
bd9ac0b4-17dd-5d2a-86a5-baadbae9f621.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
bd9ac0b4-17dd-5d2a-86a5-baadbae9f621.author: Huda Kilani
bd9ac0b4-17dd-5d2a-86a5-baadbae9f621.description2: Jeweller’s wooden box to keep tools such as hand drills, punctures and screws, and soldering iron clumps. This tool box belonged to an Armenian jeweller whose family left their country during the First World War and settled in Jerusalem. The jeweller then moved to Amman and settled there in 1948. The Armenians were well known as skilled craftsmen and jewellers. The owner of this box worked as a jeweller since the 1950's, using his tool box until his death. The tool box demonstrates the relationship between different waves of migration and the variegated demographic composition of the Jordanians.

be009de4-94db-5ccd-b043-8e9fe6838bd7.name: *Ma'ara*
be009de4-94db-5ccd-b043-8e9fe6838bd7.description2: Gold necklace with blue stones made of oval beads on a gold chain with coin print discs and heart-shaped leaves attached to them, with a large heart-shaped gold pendant inlaid with a blue stone.

be8c9494-f659-53be-b44a-b763609d1e3d.name: Dawud Pasha’s bedroom
be8c9494-f659-53be-b44a-b763609d1e3d.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
be8c9494-f659-53be-b44a-b763609d1e3d.description2: This bedroom belonged to the first *mutasarrif* (ruler) of the Mount Lebanon *mutasarrifiyya*, Dawud Pasha, who governed from 1861–68). The room is furnished with one double bed, one baldachin bed, two curtains, one rug, two embroidery panels, two bedside tables and a coffer. A thin off-white mattress covered in silk and embroidered in gold thread rests on each bed, and both frames are covered with light blue silk draperies. Three small, rectangular off-white silk pillows rest against the baldachin bed's adjustable headboard. Two square pillows rest on the double bed. The blue silk drapery on the bed frames was also used for the identical silk curtains. The curtains served a purely decorative function and could not be closed, as they were sewn to the valances, which are made with off-white silk and gold embroidery. The curtains are held back with golden tiebacks hooked on golden metal knobs. The embroidery panels on the walls are also made with the same off-white silk, and feature a variety of floral designs. The two dark, wooden bedside tables resemble classical columns and the coffer is made with a lighter wood and decorated with floral bas-reliefs.

c00a74d5-7adc-54fe-85fc-96f35232755e.name: *Justice Room at the Alhambra, Granada*
c00a74d5-7adc-54fe-85fc-96f35232755e.description: This painting copied, almost literally, an engraving by David Roberts, published on the Tourist in Spain series by Roberts in 1835. Roberts travelled from Cordova to Granada in February 1883 and painted many sketches and drawings that were used afterwards, in engravings and paintings.
c00a74d5-7adc-54fe-85fc-96f35232755e.author: Carolina Miguel Arroyo
c00a74d5-7adc-54fe-85fc-96f35232755e.third_name: *La Sala de la Justicia en la Alhambra de Granada*

c0d03656-54de-5836-824e-12905a80c7a5.name: Coffee grinder
c0d03656-54de-5836-824e-12905a80c7a5.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Departmant of Antiquities
c0d03656-54de-5836-824e-12905a80c7a5.author: Huda Kilani
c0d03656-54de-5836-824e-12905a80c7a5.keywords: coffee; coffee grinding; coffee beans; domestic furnishing; domestic vessels
c0d03656-54de-5836-824e-12905a80c7a5.description2: Manual coffee grinder carved out of a hard wood, usually oak. The grinder consists of two parts: the mortar and the pestle. The mortar is highly decorated with floral and geometric designs. After roasting the coffee beans, the local Bedouins use these to grind the beans. The sound of grinding functions as an invitation to others to come and chat while enjoying freshly prepared coffee.

c0dbe8f9-c861-5074-9fb8-b7dfcde583ed.name: *Al Azhar University, Cairo*
c0dbe8f9-c861-5074-9fb8-b7dfcde583ed.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
c0dbe8f9-c861-5074-9fb8-b7dfcde583ed.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
c0dbe8f9-c861-5074-9fb8-b7dfcde583ed.description2: Ludwig Deutsch  (1855-1935) was an Austrian-Jewish Orientalist painter. Here he tries to capture the atmosphere within the courtyard of the Al-Azhar mosque, first built in the 10th century and a major religious, intellectual and political hub of activity ever since. One of the oldest and most revered universities in the Islamic world, it was from here that a revolt against French troops was launched in 1798.  The French general Kleber was assassinated by Suleiman al Halabi, an al Azhar student, and later, Al Azhar was a focal point of protest against the Ottoman occupation of Egypt. Despite Deutsch's near-photographic style, his depiction is not entirely accurate and contains several errors: the arcades under the wooden oriel - their arches in reality wider and squatter - were not blocked up in his time, and the colour of the stonework is exaggerated. The praying men in the background are facing in the wrong direction (the direction of prayer or qibla in fact being to their right), Finally, the tall dark figure in the centre of the painting clutches what appears to be a Holy Qur'an between his dirty shoes, an act any Muslim would consider an absolute sacrilege.

c1679a4a-eb18-5ec1-bd6f-8c176785d5ff.name: Pendant
c1679a4a-eb18-5ec1-bd6f-8c176785d5ff.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
c1679a4a-eb18-5ec1-bd6f-8c176785d5ff.author: Huda Kilani
c1679a4a-eb18-5ec1-bd6f-8c176785d5ff.keywords: triangle; silver; blue beads; Ottoman coins
c1679a4a-eb18-5ec1-bd6f-8c176785d5ff.description2: A thin silver triangular pendant and welded decoration with blue glass beads. Five chains dangle with Ottoman coins at the end. This kind of jewellery was part of the dowry the groom gave to the bride. Dowries consisted mostly of silver jewellery because only the rich could afford gold jewellery. The use of coins as pieces of jewellery, worn by brides in front of their relatives and friends, was an indirect statement of the financial status of the groom.

c16fad3d-de00-51aa-b32f-c08f9761a3dc.name: *Madame X*
c16fad3d-de00-51aa-b32f-c08f9761a3dc.keywords: Painting; Halil Pasha; orientalist Turkish painters
c16fad3d-de00-51aa-b32f-c08f9761a3dc.description2: The basis of Turkish painting drawing influence from western tradition was laid when *Mühendishane-i Berr-i Hümayun* (the Naval Academy) opened in 1795. Halil Pasha was foremost among the painters with a military background who founded a western-style art tradition in Turkey. He worked with Jean Leon Gerome in his atelier in Paris. He provided a unique distinction to the analysis of impressionist light and colour, and was an example of artists dealing with impressionist technique. Because of his qualified knowledge about anatomy and his interest in depicting the human figure, Halil Pasha had a unique place in Turkish Art History.

c183f4c0-12ee-5c65-bc23-c8e71cccb311.name: Qusayr Amra
c183f4c0-12ee-5c65-bc23-c8e71cccb311.dates: AD 8th century; visited by Alois Musil in 1896
c183f4c0-12ee-5c65-bc23-c8e71cccb311.author: Mohammad Najjar
c183f4c0-12ee-5c65-bc23-c8e71cccb311.history: The best-known of the desert castles and a World Heritage Site. This monument was most probably built sometime between 723 and 743, by al-Walid Ibn Yazid, the future Umayyad caliph Walid II. The abandoned structure was re-discovered by Alois Musil in 1898, with the frescoes made famous in drawings by an Austrian artist named Mielich for Musil's book.
c183f4c0-12ee-5c65-bc23-c8e71cccb311.keywords: World Heritage Site; Alois Musil; rediscovery; archaeological investigation
c183f4c0-12ee-5c65-bc23-c8e71cccb311.description2: Qusayr Amra is one of few Jordanian sites that have been listed as a World Heritage site. It represents the formative stage of Islamic art and architecture. It consists of vaulted reception hall and a bath house the walls of which were richly decorated. Its famous figurative wall paintings are proof that figurative art was not prohibited outside religious contexts at least during the first two centuries of Islam.

c1c21018-70eb-5e4f-93fb-c53b4de7b9a0.name: Glass vessel (*cista*) with *fenicio* ('Phoenician') decoration
c1c21018-70eb-5e4f-93fb-c53b4de7b9a0.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
c1c21018-70eb-5e4f-93fb-c53b4de7b9a0.author: Marina Minozzi
c1c21018-70eb-5e4f-93fb-c53b4de7b9a0.keywords: Applied arts; minor arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; motifs; collection; collector; glasswork; Murano glass; Phoenician art; Spanish glassworks; model; reproduction; decoration; Façon de Venise
c1c21018-70eb-5e4f-93fb-c53b4de7b9a0.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. The massive emigrations of Murano's glass workers to Spain during the 1600s spurred the building of many kilns that fused formal training with the strong local glass tradition. The *cista* is part of a series of objects made in Murano in the second half of the 19th century, mainly by the Murano Venetian Glass Society, and inspired to Spanish models called "Façon de Venise", showing a Phoenician decoration. The *cista*, or vessel, has a lid with a pinnacle in aquamarine glass.
c1c21018-70eb-5e4f-93fb-c53b4de7b9a0.holding_institution_org: Museo Artistico Industriale presso la Galleria nazionale d’arte antica in Palazzo Barberini

en: Zaccagnini, M., *Arti decorative: Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini*, Rome: L'Erma di Bretschneider, 2011: 27-28.

c2865a20-07ed-57a6-a434-0d7f2bfbe970.name: Tunic (*'aba'a*)
c2865a20-07ed-57a6-a434-0d7f2bfbe970.description: Tunic in cream ground with stencilled decoration in black showing vegetal and geometrical motifs. Fortuny was son of the well-known Spanish painter Mariano Fortuny. He designed one of the early dresses for women without corsets. Some of his designs were inspired in the Orientalism style, he was influenced by his travels and of the historical textiles that he collected.
c2865a20-07ed-57a6-a434-0d7f2bfbe970.holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
c2865a20-07ed-57a6-a434-0d7f2bfbe970.author: Elvira González
c2865a20-07ed-57a6-a434-0d7f2bfbe970.keywords: Costumes; Design; North African influence; Spanish Muslim influence

c2b2223d-a18d-567f-a3db-ca8e7fcc63f5.name: Decorative ivory plaque
c2b2223d-a18d-567f-a3db-ca8e7fcc63f5.author: Mina Moraitou
c2b2223d-a18d-567f-a3db-ca8e7fcc63f5.description2: This fragmentary plaque, datable to the late Umayyad period is a superb example of high quality craftsmenship. It is carved in high relief allowing the decoration to stand in depth. Its main decoration consists of a vine scroll with five-lobed leaves and bunches of grapes. The vine stalks curl symmetrically creating three large circles. The central circle contains four smaller ones, two with a five-lobed leave and two with a bird, which turns its head backwards so as to pluck the fruit. The upper and lower circles form a spiral with five-lobed leaves and bunches of grapes. Outside the main scroll there are smaller three-lobed leaves and at the edge a hare and another bird. The object was bought by Antoni Benaki in 1919 from the Cairo dealer Maurice Nahman who provided objects for most of the important collectiors at the beginning of the 20th century.

c2d7dded-69f6-5450-9ae1-d5680237968b.name: *Caiques and Sailboats at the Bosporus*
c2d7dded-69f6-5450-9ae1-d5680237968b.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
c2d7dded-69f6-5450-9ae1-d5680237968b.description2: Felix Ziem was able to produce works in many styles such as portraits, still life, genre scenes and historical depictions, though he is primarily renowned as a landscape artist. He was an active member of the Barbizon school, which primarily focused on the depiction of nature. In the painting, Istanbul is represented through a few mosque silhouettes in the background. Nonetheless, as in his Venetian scenes, the painting emphasizes the picturesque union of the city, the sea and human figures, which have been reduced to mere colour stains. Ziem, who produced his own paints from natural pigments, influenced other artists with the use of colour in his paintings. He is known to have used “lapis lazuli” for the dominant blue colour in this painting.

c30744ff-e34a-5568-a818-fa8429cf37a9.name: *East View of the City of Algiers*
c30744ff-e34a-5568-a818-fa8429cf37a9.author: Houria Cherid
c30744ff-e34a-5568-a818-fa8429cf37a9.third_name: *East View of the City of Algiers*
c30744ff-e34a-5568-a818-fa8429cf37a9.description2: A lithograph depicting Algiers, as seen from the east.

c3322b4d-5cf0-5412-aee3-1fd52f0cba22.name: Hat (*Cuculj*)
c3322b4d-5cf0-5412-aee3-1fd52f0cba22.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
c3322b4d-5cf0-5412-aee3-1fd52f0cba22.keywords: Headdress; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; marriage; wedding; costume; textile; fashion
c3322b4d-5cf0-5412-aee3-1fd52f0cba22.materials: Klashna – thick woollen fabric, silver coins, silver alloy. Silversmith's production
c3322b4d-5cf0-5412-aee3-1fd52f0cba22.second_name: Bridal ornament worn on the head
c3322b4d-5cf0-5412-aee3-1fd52f0cba22.description2: In the 19th century and the beginning of the 20th century, metal jewellery and other articles of adornment in Macedonia were made by goldsmiths. They were distinguished with exceptional diversity reflecting the skill and creativity of artisans. This versatility applies particularly to headdresses. The bridal hat is made of broadcloth – *klashna* – which is decorated with small silver coins reminiscent of fish scales. This particular headdress is part of a jewellery set that goes with a piece worn on the breasts, which was called *mingjuska so vot*.

c4179abe-6375-58e2-9109-f22b4b9e5ebd.name: Photograph: *Arabic School, Learning the Koran, Egypt*
c4179abe-6375-58e2-9109-f22b4b9e5ebd.description:
Stereoscopic photography that creates the illusion of depth of field from two apparently identical images mounted on a rigid board by using a specific viewfinder, or stereoscope.  
The arrival of Islam to Africa caused the birth of schools where the Qu'ran was taught in Arabic. Probably Islamic education was the first education system introduced in African populations. Islam establishes education as a key priority for children.  
Universities, *madrasas* (organised institutions with different levels for studying Islamic religion), and Qur'anic schools (first education that children receive) are used by Islam as educational institutions and have played an important role in spreading Islamic religious, social, moral and cultural values between African populations.  
In the *madrasas* and Qur'anic schools, the Qur'an is learned and memorised by reading and writing at a wooden table. The memorization of the Qur'an is done by copying the teacher a text written on paper, and later recited aloud until memorised. Students were not allowed to pass to another passage until the current passage had been memorized.
c4179abe-6375-58e2-9109-f22b4b9e5ebd.keywords: Photography; education; Egypt; scenes of life

c5abc7e0-07c7-53e5-b0b7-c0930bdd46e4.name: Textiles
c5abc7e0-07c7-53e5-b0b7-c0930bdd46e4.author: Ámparo López
c5abc7e0-07c7-53e5-b0b7-c0930bdd46e4.keywords: Nasrid art; islamic influence; orientalism; collectionism
c5abc7e0-07c7-53e5-b0b7-c0930bdd46e4.description2: These textiles are example of the early Mudéjar production after the defeat of the Nasrid kingdom. The influence of these textiles was great not only in the 16th century but also in the 19th century in the Alhambresque, Moorish and Neo-Mudéjar styles.

c60364d0-48c1-5f1e-9f18-2ee410152391.name: Drawing
c60364d0-48c1-5f1e-9f18-2ee410152391.keywords: Victor Rousseau; Factory; Vista Alegre; Aveiro estuary; master of painting
c60364d0-48c1-5f1e-9f18-2ee410152391.description2: In 1826, Victor Rousseau, French artist living in political exile in London, was hired by Augusto Ferreira Pinto Basto, son of the Vista Alegre Factory’s founder. Regarding the artistic aspect, his hiring allowed for the introduction of new models and decorations, into the eclectic and romantic spirit of those times, and was essential in providing Vista Alegre’s portfolio with a new aesthetic and formal wealth and exuberance. Along with his pedagogical and artistic contribution in the Factory, Victor Rousseau also left as a legacy an interesting drawing album. The drawing, with scenes from the Factory representing the Aveiro Estuary and river Bôco, calls our attention to the specificities needed for the implementation of an industry in the 19th century. The proximity of the estuary represented not only abundance of water, but also offered easy routes for transporting raw materials and other commodities.

en: Valente, Vasco, *Porcelana Artística Portuguesa*, Porto: Imprensa Moderna Limitada, 1949.

c7c7015e-6302-5b17-8d29-534365062bab.name: View of Torre de los siete Picos, the Alhambra Palace
c7c7015e-6302-5b17-8d29-534365062bab.description: In his travels to Granada Joaquin Sorolla was fascinated by the monument of the Alhambra, the palace of Naridd kingdom of Granada. It is, along with the Mosque of Cordoba, the most important monument of Muslim Spain. Sorolla's paintings are far away from the Orientalism topics, and instead it recreates in the beauty of its nooks and gardens, capturing a more personal and intimate perspective of the monument. In this view from afar, highlights the beauty of the building and its surroundings.
c7c7015e-6302-5b17-8d29-534365062bab.author: Covadonga Pitarch
c7c7015e-6302-5b17-8d29-534365062bab.third_name: *Torre de los Siete Picos, La Alhambra*

c96923cb-dba0-5c95-81e1-1742fdb0a515.name: *View of Istanbul*
c96923cb-dba0-5c95-81e1-1742fdb0a515.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
c96923cb-dba0-5c95-81e1-1742fdb0a515.description2: This particular Istanbul painting by Felix Ziem reveals the picturesque aspect of life at sea against the backdrop of the city’s silhouette. The composition of the sailboats and marines in the foreground is balanced by the cityscape with a monumental mosque structure in the background. The artist’s use of vibrant colours and his efforts to capture the shimmering effects of the constant change of light with a fast, dynamic brush stroke technique dominate the painting. This style has led Ziem to be compared with impressionist painters, and even to be regarded as an artist who foreshadowed the emergence of impressionism with his work. The use of brilliant sunlight, which is considered as the major contribution of orientalist painting to European art is evident in the city's cap in the background.

ca59fd60-c057-5dbf-a2fa-484dcab24b97.name: Ring
ca59fd60-c057-5dbf-a2fa-484dcab24b97.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
ca59fd60-c057-5dbf-a2fa-484dcab24b97.author: Huda Kilani
ca59fd60-c057-5dbf-a2fa-484dcab24b97.description2: Thin silver ring with oval-shaped agate stone set in silver with inherent decoration on the soundings. Silver jewellery was the most common, because only rich people could afford gold jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom. The Jordanian economy relied on trades and crafts and new waves of people started to come to Jordan and began to settle for this purpose. This object is an example of how traditional fashion reflected the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is also an example of local personal attire, fashion, costumes and rites.

ca7cde0f-42ef-5233-9987-adf5389bf28f.name: *Ma'ara*
ca7cde0f-42ef-5233-9987-adf5389bf28f.description2: Gold necklace with blue stones made of oval beads on a gold chain with coin print discs and heart-shaped leaves attached to them, with a large heart-shaped gold pendant inlaid with a blue stone and pearls.

caccb7ea-2e4d-5085-b38b-eaad85d82020.name: Bracelet

cb48c75d-bd2a-5fb9-9430-da529ee7f01a.name: Bedstead
cb48c75d-bd2a-5fb9-9430-da529ee7f01a.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
cb48c75d-bd2a-5fb9-9430-da529ee7f01a.description2: This closed bedstead is made of a wooden panel, carved and painted with in an arc. This kind of furniture was a part of the architecture of traditional homes. The bed is made of a wooden plank attached to the wall and sitting in an alcove, sealed by the bedstead. This bedstead is decorated with small flowers and foliage, painted in green on a paler background.

cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.name: Tourbet el Bey
cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.history: The Tourbet El Bey monument is Tunisia's largest and most famous royal mausoleum from Ottoman or Husainid times, notable for its architecture and exterior, as well as for its size and number of cupolas and tombs. It was built by 'Ali Pacha Bey II, the fourth bey of the Hussainid dynasty, around 1770. A *kouttab*, a *sabil*, and a large *madrasa* were also founded in association with this mausoleum. This necropolis for the Beys of Tunis holds the tombs of the Husainids and their families, as well as those of a few important members of the nobility or loyal servants and ministers.
cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.keywords: Architecture; Andalusian style; Italian style; stucco; necropolis
cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.description2:
This funerary complex, composed of eight spacious rooms, is set around two courtyards, one surrounded by porticos and another open-air. The rooms and patios contain the tombs of 165 different beys who had governed Tunis from 1759 to 1942. The room for the ruling beys is notable for by its Arab-style cupolas, similar to those in the Sidi Mahrez Mosque.  
A second room is covered by a barrel vault - unique to Tunisia - decorated with wonderfully carved stuccos. The walls, on the other hand, are decorated in an Italian style with slabs of coloured stone or marble marquetery. The rooms are all decorated with faience ceramics, which are evidence of this necropolis' European and Arab influences as they were both imported from Europe and locally produced. This monument-cum-museum houses one of the most important collections of funerary inscriptions.

cbc34421-cbf1-565d-b4bd-d91bdc792930.name: Rosette shaped part of the *minbar* of the Mosque of Ibn Tulun
cbc34421-cbf1-565d-b4bd-d91bdc792930.description:
The mosque of Ibn Tulun was built in Cairo in the 9th century AD, and was restored and renovated during the reign of the Mamluk Sultan Hosam al-Din Lajin in 1296. One of the most important items of the equipment of a mosque is the *minbar* – originally a raised seat – used as a pulpit, but having also a symbolic meaning as the "Throne of Muhammad". The *minbar* was decorated with stone or wood inlays.  
  
The *minbar* of the mosque of Ibn Tulun was one of the most precious. Its wooden decoration was exhibited at the World Trade Exhibition of 1867 in Paris as one of Egypt’s most significant craft works. After that, important pieces of the *minbar* reached numerous European collections.
cbc34421-cbf1-565d-b4bd-d91bdc792930.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
cbc34421-cbf1-565d-b4bd-d91bdc792930.dates: 1296; exhibited at Paris World Trade Exhibition in 1867

cc3eb98f-be74-5f38-85da-465d5c36d52e.name: Headdress
cc3eb98f-be74-5f38-85da-465d5c36d52e.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
cc3eb98f-be74-5f38-85da-465d5c36d52e.author: Huda Kilani
cc3eb98f-be74-5f38-85da-465d5c36d52e.keywords: Ottoman coins; silk cloth; Atlas; cotton
cc3eb98f-be74-5f38-85da-465d5c36d52e.description2: A rectangular piece of Syrian silk cloth (*atlas*) with a small piece of coloured cotton cloth on the front on two sides. There is a line of Ottoman coins sewn together with three tassels dangling at the end with different stones. Silver was the most common jewellery, given by the groom to the bride as dowry. The use of Ottoman coins as pieces of jewellery – shown by women to friends and relatives – was an indirect reference to the financial status of their husbands. Silk was imported from Syria. Its trade in the Syro-Palestinian area was common because of the lack of geographical and political boundaries; some cities were like twins because of their close proximity and exchange of trade goods and business.

cc673275-b5d7-50ff-bc5e-1a4f9c06e998.name: The Celebration of the Prophet Muhammad in Tangier
cc673275-b5d7-50ff-bc5e-1a4f9c06e998.author: Marina Minozzi
cc673275-b5d7-50ff-bc5e-1a4f9c06e998.keywords: Orientalism; reinvention; historical events in paintings; exoticism; diplomatic mission; Morocco; Mulay al-Hasan; travel; travelling artist; Italian travellers; Italian painters; Edmondo de Amicis; Marocco; travel book
cc673275-b5d7-50ff-bc5e-1a4f9c06e998.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
cc673275-b5d7-50ff-bc5e-1a4f9c06e998.description2: Stefano Ussi lived between Florence and Rome and studied at the Academy of Fine Arts of Florence before enrolling as a volunteer in the first Italian War of Independence, during which he was taken prisoner by the Austrian troops. In 1875 Italian King Vittorio Emanuele II sent an embassy to Morocco which included the writer Edmondo De Amicis and the painters Ussi and Cesare Biseo. The innovative international relations policy of the young Sultan Mulay al-Hassan fostered relations with the Italian King. During his trip, Ussi sketched drafts on Arab every-day life scenes which later inspired his larger paintings.
cc673275-b5d7-50ff-bc5e-1a4f9c06e998.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

cd05b644-c357-52ab-89b2-eb3a5e54560e.description2: Figurines based on the Assyrian sculptures were popular collecting pieces. Owners displayed their interest current events. Buyers included the rich and famous, as well as museums. These Parian ware figurines were also exhibited. Winged bull.

cd6b2c88-0a74-5d2f-8cba-5b3ea7174b9c.name: Tympanum made of 16 tiles from the palace of the grand vizier Piale Pasha (c. 1515-1578)
cd6b2c88-0a74-5d2f-8cba-5b3ea7174b9c.description: These tiles decorated the palace of the Ottoman Grand Vizier Piale Pasha, or possibly the mosque the Vizier commissioned. Both buildings were completed in 1573 and richly decorated with tile panels. The palace and the mosque were restored after an earthquake in 1890, and the tile panels were sold all over the world. At least nine identical tympanums are now in American and European museums.

cdba4d4e-0b47-593b-9836-4ab0f782f5e0.description2: A silver, oval-shaped box with a prominent carving of a couchant lion; an object which was common in both Jordan and Palestine.

The damascening was an Arab technique for the decoration the metallic artworks.

ce15a428-c117-5ec8-bdb2-e57a6da94a62.name: Villa Crespi
ce15a428-c117-5ec8-bdb2-e57a6da94a62.holder: Since the 1980s, Villa Crespi has been transformed in a 4-star hotel owned by the 'Villa Crespi-Ca.pri srl'
ce15a428-c117-5ec8-bdb2-e57a6da94a62.author: Ignazio Galella
ce15a428-c117-5ec8-bdb2-e57a6da94a62.history:
Cristoforo Benigno Crespi was a successful businessman active in the cotton industry. In 1879, he bought an estate near Lake d’Orta (Piedmont, Northern Italy), to build a vacation house in honour of his wife, Pia Travelli.  
Crespi had fallen in love with the architecture of Baghdad, where he went to buy cotton, and asked architect Angelo Colla to build for him a villa in Moorish style. Architect Enrico Combi designed the magnificent park.  
After it was inaugurated, the villa became a centre of high-society life: it hosted members of the Italian royal family and even the King of Spain. The Crespi organised theatre performances in the park and invited nobles, industrialists and bankers. At the end of the 1980s, Villa Crespi was transformed into a four-star hotel.
ce15a428-c117-5ec8-bdb2-e57a6da94a62.description2: An astonishing three-storey villa in Moorish style, near Lake d’Orta in Piedmont, Northern Italy. It features a 48-meter high minaret and has richly decorated interiors made with lavish marbles imported from several countries. Construction lasted 12 years. The estate includes a greenhouse, a wet dock, stables, a big fountain, an annex, and is surrounded by walls with valuable wrought iron gates.

ce58ba5d-a393-5547-95fe-76c5d627ffcf.name: Governor Ben Anda's Son with His Escort of Honour
ce58ba5d-a393-5547-95fe-76c5d627ffcf.author: Marina Minozzi
ce58ba5d-a393-5547-95fe-76c5d627ffcf.keywords: Orientalism; reinvention; historical events in paintings; exoticism; diplomatic mission; Morocco; Mulay al-Hasan; travel; travelling artist; Italian travellers; Italian painters; Edmondo de Amicis; Marocco; travel book
ce58ba5d-a393-5547-95fe-76c5d627ffcf.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
ce58ba5d-a393-5547-95fe-76c5d627ffcf.third_name: *Il figlio del governatore Ben Anda con la scorta d’onore*
ce58ba5d-a393-5547-95fe-76c5d627ffcf.description2: Stefano Ussi lived between Florence and Rome, studied at the Academy of Fine Arts of Florence and then enrolled as a volunteer in the first Italian War of Independence, during which he was taken prisoner by the Austrian troops. The painting represents the arrival of the Italian embassy, of which Ussi was part, in Morocco, in the province of Seffian better known as Ben-Anda, which was the old governor’s family name.
ce58ba5d-a393-5547-95fe-76c5d627ffcf.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

en: Villari, A., in Elena di Majo and Mateo Lafranconi (eds), *Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Moderna. Le Collezioni. Il XIX secolo*, Milan: Electa, 2006, cat. 8.33.

cf7760c0-6a87-5a55-85b5-9801367d91fb.name: Necklace
cf7760c0-6a87-5a55-85b5-9801367d91fb.description: Three strings necklace, with forty-three cylindrical beads of coral, alternating with five spherical silver, tubular finials and smooth; six spherical in silver, with finials decorated with circles of piping and tubular; six biconical accounts also in silver, with tubular trims and cording foot circles; and six ‘*alconciles*’ in silver.

d000e4f8-141c-5c31-bc47-44557dd76807.description: Large, blue, glazed terracotta dish, dated 1864 and made in Fez.
