d0201dc5-b133-5197-929c-a269917b72e1.name: *L'art arabe d'après les monuments du Kaire depuis le VIIè siècle jusqu'à la fin du XVIIIè*
d0201dc5-b133-5197-929c-a269917b72e1.author: Mina Moraitou
d0201dc5-b133-5197-929c-a269917b72e1.description2: A publication in three volumes *L'art arabe d'après les monuments du Kaire depuis le VIIè siècle jusqu'à la fin du XVIIIè* is a monumental work by archaeologist and architect Prisse d'Avennes. It was published in parts by V.A. Morel et Cie. from 1869 to 1877. In 200 plates he reproduced illustration on the art and architecture of Islamic Cairo.

d182a16f-df1f-5ece-848d-95d8514da95e.name: Glazed tile 'Butterflies'
d182a16f-df1f-5ece-848d-95d8514da95e.author: DGPC
d182a16f-df1f-5ece-848d-95d8514da95e.keywords: Azulejo; glazed tile; butterflies; Portuguese culture
d182a16f-df1f-5ece-848d-95d8514da95e.description2: The glazed tile or azulejo is a particularly expressive component of Portuguese art that is constantly being renovated. Between the end of the 19th century and beginning of the 20th century, it is strongly influenced by art nouveau, as is shown by this tile by Rafael Bordalo Pinheiro, made in one of Portugal’s main ceramic centres, the town of Caldas da Rainha.

d199debb-1836-5a98-80c3-90ef128b824b.name: Glass Mosque Lamp
d199debb-1836-5a98-80c3-90ef128b824b.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
d199debb-1836-5a98-80c3-90ef128b824b.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
d199debb-1836-5a98-80c3-90ef128b824b.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
d199debb-1836-5a98-80c3-90ef128b824b.materials: Etched and gilt, light green glass
d199debb-1836-5a98-80c3-90ef128b824b.description2: This mosque lamp may have been made in 19th century Hebron, a century-old Palestinian centre for glass manufacture that managed to survive despite the increasing influx of cheap, mass-produced goods from Europe. While its shape continues a style already popular in Mamluk times, its etched and gilt decoration relates closely to other neo-Mamluk artefacts produced for European tourists at the time.

d1b0dbb9-a089-5201-b98d-4ec5ca02951f.name: Bracelet
d1b0dbb9-a089-5201-b98d-4ec5ca02951f.description: This superb bracelet is decorated with diagonal strips in the middle and decorated floral motifs on each side.
d1b0dbb9-a089-5201-b98d-4ec5ca02951f.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes, Cristina Giménez

d1dd52e7-9117-58ed-9803-87a620891cda.name: Moorish gunpowder flask
d1dd52e7-9117-58ed-9803-87a620891cda.description: This gunpowder container, along with other pieces, was taken by Salvador de Foronda, a member of the Spanish Army, awarded for his actions in battle. He was a relative of the Marquis of Cerralbo and donated to his uncle’s museum these exceptional pieces in 1918. These kinds of pieces typically display rich decoration that in this case is hand made in local workshops. As with the other two pieces, both the Moorish dagger and musket, the flask has a fabric rope for the rider to carry it more easily.
d1dd52e7-9117-58ed-9803-87a620891cda.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes

d2105247-15f5-56b4-9a41-1c51ab776885.name: Lamp
d2105247-15f5-56b4-9a41-1c51ab776885.author: Ballian 1992, 80, no. 41
d2105247-15f5-56b4-9a41-1c51ab776885.keywords: neoclassical; Greeks; vegetal decoration; coin; currency; numismatics; tughra; tuğra; monogram; Ottoman monograms; Ottoman imperial symbols; metalwork
d2105247-15f5-56b4-9a41-1c51ab776885.description2: The lamp has a rounded, pierced body covered in foliate scroll with acorns and ribbons that form interlocking circles. The tall, convex neck is decorated with large acanthus leaves with wind-blown tips. From the base hangs a tassel made up of chains attached to Ottoman coins. The three suspension chains are attached to cast caryatids in softly pleated drapery holding plinths on their heads. The influence of Neoclassicism is obvious in the shaping of the neck, which is reminiscent of a vase, and in the use of caryatids instead of the angels which usually decorate lamps. The acanthus, though another Neoclassical motif, is used here with the naturalism and movement characteristic of Venetian lamps of the previous century (cat. no. 71). The lip is stamped with a semi- obliterated *tugra*.

en: Ballian, Anna, *Treasures from the Greek Communities of Asia Minor and Eastern Thrace. Collections from the Benaki Museum*, Athens: Benaki Museum, 1992.

d2153895-57ef-583f-b177-30f75fa578f2.name: *Study of an Excavation (Pompei)*
d2153895-57ef-583f-b177-30f75fa578f2.author: Marina Minozzi
d2153895-57ef-583f-b177-30f75fa578f2.keywords: Painting; Italian painters; archaeology; documentation; research; history painting; celebration of the past; Roman past; post-unitarian Italian society; realism; rediscovery of the past
d2153895-57ef-583f-b177-30f75fa578f2.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
d2153895-57ef-583f-b177-30f75fa578f2.description2: Filippo Palizzi came from a large family and, along with his three brothers, all painters, introduced in Italy a realistic style of painting which breaks away from academic tradition of religious, mythological or history painting. He depicted real landscapes, people and animals. In 1864 the painter went to Pompei and Paestum where he made a series of studies of archeological ruins discovered in that period from excavation campaigns promoted by the new Italian State.
d2153895-57ef-583f-b177-30f75fa578f2.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

d27f7bc1-9e5e-581e-a7d7-9666172ce6a8.name: *The Cock Fight*
d27f7bc1-9e5e-581e-a7d7-9666172ce6a8.author: Petar Petrovic
d27f7bc1-9e5e-581e-a7d7-9666172ce6a8.description2: Among the best known of his Orientalist paintings from the Balkans are those of domestic life, such as *The Cock Fight*. In this painting Jovanović builds a credible, believable scene. The spectators are fully engaged, each one reacts in his or her own particular way, consistent with their age and appearance. The singularity of Jovanović’s approach is even more evident when contrasted to Western European Orientalist paintings such as Jean Léon Gérôme’s famous *The Cock Fight* of 1847 or Ferentz Eisenhut’s depiction of a cock fight in 1894. Awarded the first prize at the Wien Künstlerhaus exhibition 1898, and having a great success at the Paris Salon in 1906, it was widely reproduced in subsequent years and was surely known to Jovanović. It is evident that studies of the figures directly from nature inform this painting. Jovanović was not only providing a new and authentic category of genre paintings but speaking specifically to a culture that was his own. In the process, he was giving significance to an area and ethnic groups heretofore ignored.

d2c53ee5-ac01-5efd-bfd6-0baaae928208.name: *View of Zaytuna Mosque, Tunis*
d2c53ee5-ac01-5efd-bfd6-0baaae928208.description: One of 389 photographs taken by the Tunisian Service of Antiquities. These photographs were exhibited in the European Historic Exhibition held in Madrid in 1892-1892. After the exhibition closure the photographs were donated to the National Museum of Archaeology.

d3abd1eb-d054-57dc-92dc-e1b2ea8806d5.name: Carpet
d3abd1eb-d054-57dc-92dc-e1b2ea8806d5.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
d3abd1eb-d054-57dc-92dc-e1b2ea8806d5.author: Stefan Weber
d3abd1eb-d054-57dc-92dc-e1b2ea8806d5.second_name: Put together of burned fragments of the original masterpiece
d3abd1eb-d054-57dc-92dc-e1b2ea8806d5.description2: Rugs and carpets are an essential artwork category within the Islamic culture. In the late 19th century, Oriental carpets became collectible and valued art objects. The Museum of Islamic Art’s collection of carpets is one of the most important in the world. It was started in 1904 with the gift of 21 carpets from Wilhelm von Bode. The important carpet no 1 burned partially 1945 and was restored partially with fragments later. This specific artwork was created in the North West of Iran before the middle of the 16th century and shows an animated scene featuring animals and trees.

d467849e-57d5-56af-821f-861425864b86.name: Pair of tables
d467849e-57d5-56af-821f-861425864b86.description: Little tables like these ones had an important place in typical oriental rooms for the tea and coffee, and in *fumoirs* (smoking rooms), masculine intimate spaces that proliferated all around Europe, like the Arab Room in the Cerralbo Museum. These tables decorated with geometrical patterns could have been produced in the East Mediterranean, but more likely is an Indian production for the Arab market. The second one, a two-level table, could have been produced in a south Spain or Morocco workshop.
d467849e-57d5-56af-821f-861425864b86.provenance: Near East or India/ Spain or Morocco
d467849e-57d5-56af-821f-861425864b86.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes, Cristina Giménez
d467849e-57d5-56af-821f-861425864b86.keywords: Production of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode; Neo-mudejar; moorish style

d62a8aad-7189-5f2c-a39f-c9a6febe7aa4.name: *Ancient Istanbul Houses*
d62a8aad-7189-5f2c-a39f-c9a6febe7aa4.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
d62a8aad-7189-5f2c-a39f-c9a6febe7aa4.keywords: Painting; Hoca Ali Rıza; orientalist Turkish painters
d62a8aad-7189-5f2c-a39f-c9a6febe7aa4.description2: Hoca Ali Rıza is known as the first painter who used landscapes in Turkish painting. A study of the artist’s works also readily reveals architectural structures which have changed since his time. Such structures included mosques, fountains, dervish monasteries and lodges, tombs, *sebils* (public fountains installed by charities), ruins, cemeteries, bridges, stately homes new and old, towers, old houses and other subjects which architecturally and historically speaking might have been considered ordinary in his day, but which he pursued with a passion. Riza is completely realistic in his works and he specialized in depicting landscapes using light and shadow.

d6ede956-3098-5ac6-8afc-b9788d8dd31f.name: The first postmaster's office in Tunis, 1892
d6ede956-3098-5ac6-8afc-b9788d8dd31f.holder: Musée des Postes, Télégraphes et Télécommunications
d6ede956-3098-5ac6-8afc-b9788d8dd31f.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
d6ede956-3098-5ac6-8afc-b9788d8dd31f.keywords: Painted wood; floral decoration; Turkish influences; European influences
d6ede956-3098-5ac6-8afc-b9788d8dd31f.description2: The objects assembled in this room all date to the late 19th century and belong to a set of urban Tunisian furnishings. These articles were all part of Tunis' first municipal postmaster's office. They consist of four chairs and a bench in painted wood, centred around a two-layered desk, painted in a floral motif on a pale blue background. Behind, a shelving unit, painted in the same style. This furnishing set shows evidence of traditional Tunisian, Turkish and various European influences.

d70e9882-8463-5f48-be2a-a1278275395f.name: *The Art of the Saracens in Egypt*
d70e9882-8463-5f48-be2a-a1278275395f.author: Mina Moraitou
d70e9882-8463-5f48-be2a-a1278275395f.description2: A publication on the history of the arts in Egypt by Stanley Lane-Poole (1854-1931). Each chapter is dedicated to one aspect of the arts: architecture, stone and plaster, mosaic, woodwork, ivory, metalwork, glass, heraldry, ceramics, textiles and illuminated manuscripts.

d747ca97-275a-501b-b4a0-acb9af093d12.name: Powder box
d747ca97-275a-501b-b4a0-acb9af093d12.description: A powder box – a receptacle for gunpowder – decorated with geometric and floral motifs and crafted in southern Morocco in the 19th century. The decorative style is influenced by European designs, seen particularly in the suspension loops.

d7624db0-56ea-5f6c-a4ec-671242a3d4eb.name: Illuminated Qur’an manuscript
d7624db0-56ea-5f6c-a4ec-671242a3d4eb.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
d7624db0-56ea-5f6c-a4ec-671242a3d4eb.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
d7624db0-56ea-5f6c-a4ec-671242a3d4eb.artist: Calligrapher Hashim al-Kashafi, one of the students of Abd al-Qader al-Rasmi
d7624db0-56ea-5f6c-a4ec-671242a3d4eb.materials: European paper, black ink, pigments, gilding, pasteboard, leather
d7624db0-56ea-5f6c-a4ec-671242a3d4eb.description2: This 19th-century Qur'an manuscript opens with an elaborately decorated and gilt double page giving the first chapter 'Al-Fatiha' on the right and the beginning of chapter 2 'Al-Baqara' on the right. The text, disposed in 15 lines on each page and framed by gold margins, is executed in black naskhi script, with red detailing. The chapter headings are executed in white riqa' script against a solid golden cartouche with blue floral detailing. The verse dividers are rendered as small gold discs. major subdivisions in the text are marked by small red inscriptions or elaborate, colourful medallions in the margins. The last double-page has elaborately coloured and gilt cartouches, the right giving the name of the calligrapher Hashim al-Kashafi, one of the students of Abd al Qader al-Rasmi, in the year 1286 H/ 1865 CE.

d7670c25-7540-57e5-9687-097d572b293a.name: *Moor with oranges*
d7670c25-7540-57e5-9687-097d572b293a.description: Sorolla painted this Moor with oranges in Italy (where he lived on a scholarship), at the end of 1885 or beginning of 1886, long before he travelled to Tiwan, Morocco, in 1919. This is a typical example of Oriental painting made for sale, as Orientalist painting was very fashionable at the time. Sorolla painted mostly Moors and concubines, which conformed to Western ideals of life in the East and not necessarily with reality. Like the main character of this painting, a Moor smoking, wearing the exotic hijab and barefoot, holding an orange in his hand.
d7670c25-7540-57e5-9687-097d572b293a.author: Covadonga Pitarch
d7670c25-7540-57e5-9687-097d572b293a.keywords: Orientalist painting; Spain; Formation of painters

d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.name: Bridal jewellery worn on the breasts (*Mingjuska so vot* and necklace)
d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.keywords: Broad cloth; klashna; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; textile; costume; wedding; marriage
d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.materials: Klashna - thick woollen fabric, silver coins, silver alloy, decorative stones, tiny beads - *monistra*
d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.third_name: Mingjushka so 'vot' – nevestinski ukras za gradi
d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.description2: This piece of jewellery provides evidence on the versatility of articles of adornment worn by women in Macedonia in the 19th century. *Mingjushka so vot* belongs to the group of jewellery decorating the chests, although there is no clear distinction from pieces worn around the neck. This exquisite breast jewellery consists of a rectangular piece of broadcloth – *klashna* – covered with small silver coins reminiscent of fish scales and adorned with decorative stones. It is bordered by a chain, which is additionally adorned with coins. It used to be worn suspended on a chain. Abundant ornamentation with coins was applied on diverse pieces of jewellery and articles of adornment within all ethnic communities in Macedonia.

d7e6c097-9cf8-56b1-b826-78a1e6089691.name: Powder box
d7e6c097-9cf8-56b1-b826-78a1e6089691.description: A powder box – a receptacle for gunpowder – decorated with geometric and floral motifs and crafted in southern Morocco in the 19th century. The decorative style is influenced by European designs, seen particularly in the suspension loops.
d7e6c097-9cf8-56b1-b826-78a1e6089691.type: Fittings; metalwork; arms and armour; munitions

d81a90e8-c3be-5aa0-8a9a-b3efa68184af.name: Portrait Album – Ottoman State Officers
d81a90e8-c3be-5aa0-8a9a-b3efa68184af.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
d81a90e8-c3be-5aa0-8a9a-b3efa68184af.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
d81a90e8-c3be-5aa0-8a9a-b3efa68184af.keywords: Yıldız Album; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Vassilaki (Basile) Kargopoulo
d81a90e8-c3be-5aa0-8a9a-b3efa68184af.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in 19th century. Vassilaki Kargopoulo was of Greek descent. His first studio was opened in 1850 near the Russian Consulate. Between the years of 1859 and 1860, he began to attract the attention of customers from all sections of society. He focused on Ottoman clothing and street vendors in 1860.

d9278f88-7c6f-5ba2-a99d-94b0d6496626.name: Portrait Album – Ottoman State Officers
d9278f88-7c6f-5ba2-a99d-94b0d6496626.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
d9278f88-7c6f-5ba2-a99d-94b0d6496626.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
d9278f88-7c6f-5ba2-a99d-94b0d6496626.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Fotoğraf; Eski Istanbul; Nikolas Andriomenos
d9278f88-7c6f-5ba2-a99d-94b0d6496626.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Born in Costantinople in 1851, Nicolas Andriomenos was an Ottoman Greek who learned photography in the 1870s from Cosmi Abdullah. At that time, Cosmi operated a studio of his own in Beyazıt, but turned the business over to Andriomenos in late 1879, after which its new proprietor soon made it into one of the city's most prestigious portrait studios.

d971e2da-ec43-53d8-9ea9-f48cb8b3eeee.name: Turkish jugs
d971e2da-ec43-53d8-9ea9-f48cb8b3eeee.description: Bought at the 1873 World's Fair in Vienna. The black and white illustration was included in the book edited by C. Lützow: *Kunst und Kunstgewerbe auf der Wiener Weltausstellung 1873*, 1875, S 251.
d971e2da-ec43-53d8-9ea9-f48cb8b3eeee.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
d971e2da-ec43-53d8-9ea9-f48cb8b3eeee.materials: Stoneware, glazed; illustration from a book

d9c388f4-ae74-56f2-b3d4-341eda234a0f.name: Panel with a large bouquet
d9c388f4-ae74-56f2-b3d4-341eda234a0f.description2: This polychromatic panel is decorated with an image of a bowl filled with pears, apples and other fruits, topped by a small vase with flowers such as carnations, tulips, sunflowers and daisies coming out of it, which are interlaced with a rinceau pattern of palmettes, half-palmettes and vine leaves. The main colours are blue, green and brown. The decorative style, colour palette and manufacture all indicate a typical Tunisian ceramic, containing a mix of Andalusian and Ottoman influences.

d9cffa1d-0e9d-59ee-a8f9-0f2a12a3c7dd.name: Dish serving for dried fruits or nuts
d9cffa1d-0e9d-59ee-a8f9-0f2a12a3c7dd.description2: Sultan Abdülhamid II founded in 1891 the *Yıldız Çini Fabrika-i Hümâyûnu* (Yıldız Royal Tile Factory) in the garden of Yıldız Palace in order to revive Turkish tile art and give it a new direction and momentum. Vases, hanging wall plates and many sorts of daily-use wares were produced in the factory, including writing and dinner table utensils, card plates, lidded bowls, pans, *aşure* (a kind of dessert) trays, sugar bowls, tea and coffee cups. Many native and foreign artists have worked in the tile factory of Yıldız. One of them, Halid Naci received training in tile painting in Sevres, France after his education at the *Sanayi-i Nefise Mektebi* (School of Fine Arts) and he was assigned to be head painter of the tile factories after his return.

dbf4dc13-3f6b-5da9-bf05-cfabe7876ad3.name: Headdress
dbf4dc13-3f6b-5da9-bf05-cfabe7876ad3.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
dbf4dc13-3f6b-5da9-bf05-cfabe7876ad3.author: Huda Kilani
dbf4dc13-3f6b-5da9-bf05-cfabe7876ad3.description2: A silver circular disk with inherent decorations in the carving, and prominent dome above; chains dangling with oval shapes at the end. With two different length. This ornament was placed on the top of a high hat worn by al-Druze (Druse) women. Silver was the most common jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom. This object illustrates the variegated social composition and the demographic changes in the Jordanian territory in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The al-Druze tribes migrated from Syria (Hawran) to north east Jordan in the early twentieth century because of their support for the Syrian revolution against the French occupation.

dc620fad-84b0-5474-b1ee-8a583440c84a.name: Textile fragment from Archbishop Ximenez de Rada's burial garments
dc620fad-84b0-5474-b1ee-8a583440c84a.description: The textile fragment was part of the alb which was buried the Archbishop Rodrigo Ximénez de Rada in 1247 at the Monastery of Santa María de Huerta (Soria, Spain). The tomb was opened at the beginning of the decade of 1880 at the request of the Master of Sigüenza. The fragment was found in the coffin and the master give it to the Marquis of Cerralbo, who was present. After this event, because of the importance of the Archbishop garments and the marquis’ interest in the history of the Monastery, the marquis paid all the expenses of two new openings of the grave. The first one in 1886 for the Spanish Royal Academy of the History researches, and the second one in 1907 for his own studio, when he completed the description of the garments and took photographs to his publication in 1908.
dc620fad-84b0-5474-b1ee-8a583440c84a.dates: 13th century, before 1247; discovered at the beginning of the decade of 1880
dc620fad-84b0-5474-b1ee-8a583440c84a.author: Rebeca C. Recio
dc620fad-84b0-5474-b1ee-8a583440c84a.keywords: Spanish Muslim art; islamic influence; orientalism; collectionism
dc620fad-84b0-5474-b1ee-8a583440c84a.materials: Silk, metallic threads; lampas and taqueté weave
dc620fad-84b0-5474-b1ee-8a583440c84a.third_name: Fragmento del alba del arzopispo Ximénez de Rada

dc9bec02-eb7b-5be5-b697-9d2faab3da93.name: *La Mhalla* (painting)
dc9bec02-eb7b-5be5-b697-9d2faab3da93.holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée
dc9bec02-eb7b-5be5-b697-9d2faab3da93.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
dc9bec02-eb7b-5be5-b697-9d2faab3da93.description2: This oil on canvas by Bertrand de Moynier depicts the disembarkment of the *mhalla*, the field army, in the mid-19th century for the collection of taxes. The *mhalla*, a military term, was made up of soldiers, *mamluks*, civil servants, merchants and artisans, which were split into three categories: infantry, cavalry and artillery. This army was supported by informal troops and horsemen from local tribes. The beylical tent has been erected in the centre of the mhalla, next to the service tents for the bey's personnel and the tents for the administrative and fiscal representatives. The future 'Ali Bey III (1882–1902) can be seen in the centre of the painting, in front of the red and green flags.

dcf00ffc-65c1-57d4-a83f-82ea0a6c476a.name: Set of earrings and a necklace
dcf00ffc-65c1-57d4-a83f-82ea0a6c476a.author: Ámparo López
dcf00ffc-65c1-57d4-a83f-82ea0a6c476a.keywords: Nasrid art; islamic influence; orientalism; collectionism
dcf00ffc-65c1-57d4-a83f-82ea0a6c476a.description2: This set of Nasrid jewellery is a good example of collector interest in artworks from the Spanish Muslim period as part of the vernacular identity of Spain. Also, these earrings and necklace are related stylistically to traditional Spanish jewellery stylistically, as we see in the earring and necklace from the Fashion Museum of Madrid.

dd7e299b-4a4e-544f-b652-be813f7bf7be.name: Bowl
dd7e299b-4a4e-544f-b652-be813f7bf7be.description: This bowl with a rich Arab inscription copied models from the Mamluk period. This piece is a Neo-Mamluk artwork possibly made in Egypt.
dd7e299b-4a4e-544f-b652-be813f7bf7be.author: Ana Cabrera

ddd75581-2e37-5baa-8483-63c54f368af5.name: Dress
ddd75581-2e37-5baa-8483-63c54f368af5.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
ddd75581-2e37-5baa-8483-63c54f368af5.author: Huda Kilani
ddd75581-2e37-5baa-8483-63c54f368af5.description2: Long black silk dress (*malas*), narrow at the waist, wide at the bottom, embroidered with cross-stitch dark blue and red on the chest and on the front side, worn by women of the al-Druze tribes, with a shirt underneath. This object illustrates the variegated composition and the demographic changes of the Jordan population in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It also shows how the different populations brought with them their fashion, costumes and rites which contributed to the multifaceted social and cultural heritage of Jordan. The al-Druze tribes migrated from Syria (Hawran) to northeast Jordan in the early twentieth century because of their support for the Syrian revolution against the French occupation.

de834889-8d91-5a45-91c0-917eb5e7de6f.name: Ceramic panel with eight azulejos [tiles] (from the Odescalchi collection)
de834889-8d91-5a45-91c0-917eb5e7de6f.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
de834889-8d91-5a45-91c0-917eb5e7de6f.author: Marina Minozzi
de834889-8d91-5a45-91c0-917eb5e7de6f.keywords: Applied arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; motifs; collector; Spain; Moorish; Islamic art; Islamic influence; Neo-Mudéjar style; production of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode; Manises
de834889-8d91-5a45-91c0-917eb5e7de6f.third_name: Pannello ceramico con otto azulejos (dalla collezione Odescalchi)
de834889-8d91-5a45-91c0-917eb5e7de6f.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". The collections of the M.A.I. included large samples of pottery, wooden objects, fabric, bronzes and ivories dating to Roman, Renaissance and Baroque times. The best part of this collection is on display at the National Gallery of Palazzo Barberini in Rome, while other pieces are housed in Castel Sant'Angelo and Palazzo Venezia. Within the series of the Hispanic-Moorish ceramics are some pottery with azulejos, bought by Prince Baldassarre Ladislao Odescalchi in 1880. The panel with eight azulejos dates from 15th and 16th centuries. It shows both geometric and floral decorations.
de834889-8d91-5a45-91c0-917eb5e7de6f.holding_institution_org: Museo Artistico Industriale presso la Galleria nazionale d’arte antica in Palazzo Barberini

en: Zaccagnini, M., *Arti decorative: Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini*, Rome: L'Erma di Bretschneider, 2011: 13-16.

deea46be-8061-564e-a1de-c2f20389f8a7.name: *Ayasofya (Hagia Sophia)*
deea46be-8061-564e-a1de-c2f20389f8a7.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
deea46be-8061-564e-a1de-c2f20389f8a7.keywords: Painting; Hüseyin Zekai Paşa; orientalist Turkish painters
deea46be-8061-564e-a1de-c2f20389f8a7.description2: The majority of Turkish painters in the 19th century were Ottoman officers who had studied abroad. Hüseyin Zekai Paşa was one of those painters who paints in the western style. In his first works, he followed the painting tradition of 19th century by including thin paint dough and light colours. He made changes in his painting techniques through the Galatasaray Exhibition and turned into an impressionist, his work dominated by thicker brush strokes. In his paintings he combined impressionist colour techniques and a totality of composition with dexterity. Şeker Ahmet Paşa, Osman Hamdi Bey and Hüseyin Zekai Paşa opened the way for other Turkish artists – and in particular impressionists – in Turkey.

df2df39f-10d6-5018-8f8a-0c38e886c096.name: *View of Cairo*
df2df39f-10d6-5018-8f8a-0c38e886c096.author: Dalila Orfali
df2df39f-10d6-5018-8f8a-0c38e886c096.description2: Émile Bernard is known first and foremost for his friendship with the artist Paul Gaugin within the movement often known as the Pont-Aven school. He is known only secondly as an artist of the symbolist movement, along with Odilon Redon. This painting reveals a little-known aspect of the painter's career, namely that he spent some time in Cairo where he mostly painted cafés and theatres. This Egyptian work by Émile Bernard is therefore rare enough to be considered one of the collection's most important works.

df6c527d-f54f-5563-b918-6ec2da8e94f9.name: Tunic (*'aba'a*)
df6c527d-f54f-5563-b918-6ec2da8e94f9.description: Tunic in cotton gauze lined in a red satin. The printed decoration is similar to the Venetian Renaissance printed velvets. This garment is part of the assemble inspired in the travels to North Africa made by Fortuny.
df6c527d-f54f-5563-b918-6ec2da8e94f9.holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
df6c527d-f54f-5563-b918-6ec2da8e94f9.author: Elvira González

dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.name: Dress
dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.author: Huda Kilani
dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.keywords: Dress; machine embroidery; patterns; custmes and rites; Ottoman coins
dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.materials: Chinese cotton, silver coins; machine weaving, machine embroidery
dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.description2: Women's costumes of the central regions of Jordan are characterized by length, dark colours, light vertical strips of embroidery and very long sleeves. This black and blue dress has a very loose fitting, open chest and long flared sleeves pulled over a head band. The length of the dress was adjusted to the height of the woman by a sash. Wide at the bottom, it is decorated horizontally with blue cotton stripes and vertically with embroidery lines and Ottoman coins. The traditional costumes reflect the variegated population composition and demographic changes of the late 19th century-early 20th century Jordanian territory, when new waves of people arrived and settled for the purpose of trades and crafts. Craft was not limited to the everyday life and the profits from crafts were a source of income.

dfd5b69e-9c27-52e5-93bf-9d6d1a4fd259.name: Tekke panel
dfd5b69e-9c27-52e5-93bf-9d6d1a4fd259.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
dfd5b69e-9c27-52e5-93bf-9d6d1a4fd259.materials: Rokoko ornament on paper, art of illumination on bordure
dfd5b69e-9c27-52e5-93bf-9d6d1a4fd259.description2: A *tekke* (dervish lodge) plate with *celi sülüs* calligraphy in the shape of a bird made with black ink. It reads *"Yâ Bâz el-eşheb Kuddise sırruhu Şey'en lȋ'l-lâh"* (religious text, untranslatable). On the upper right corner there is a date and signature together with a bouquet of rose, tulip and rosebuds. The plate is framed in rose colour.

dfe6e123-1970-5707-8279-08002d40fd1f.name: Ottoman Clothing Album
dfe6e123-1970-5707-8279-08002d40fd1f.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
dfe6e123-1970-5707-8279-08002d40fd1f.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
dfe6e123-1970-5707-8279-08002d40fd1f.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
dfe6e123-1970-5707-8279-08002d40fd1f.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

e396b7b2-cb07-51d7-86f1-b131b11dbfe2.name: Portrait of a lady of the court playing the tambourine
e396b7b2-cb07-51d7-86f1-b131b11dbfe2.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
e396b7b2-cb07-51d7-86f1-b131b11dbfe2.keywords: Pierre Desire Guillemet; Orientalism; painting; İstanbul
e396b7b2-cb07-51d7-86f1-b131b11dbfe2.description2: This painting is one of the four half-length portraits painted by Pierre Désiré Guillemet in 1874-1875 depicting a young woman of the Ottoman Court. Her dress has been emphasized by means of a neutral background. She is wearing a *dört etek* (four-skirted) robe, made of *savai* fabric. Part of her undershirt with embroidered borders is visible from her large sleeves and around the edges of the robe. Her robe has a floral pattern with lively colours and her belt has a clasp with a two large stones in a silver setting. Her chestnut-coloured hair flows down to her shoulder. She wears two strands of pearls around her neck and a gold earing with pearls and gems. On her head she wears a cap of blue fabric decorated with small white flowers, plumes and toile.

e3bca328-205b-530c-8cb6-99cd21d8c8dd.name: *Two Musician Girls*
e3bca328-205b-530c-8cb6-99cd21d8c8dd.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
e3bca328-205b-530c-8cb6-99cd21d8c8dd.keywords: Osman Hamdi Bey; Orientalism; painting; İstanbul
e3bca328-205b-530c-8cb6-99cd21d8c8dd.description2: As opposed to the Western Orientalists who emphasize sexuality in their female figures, in Osman Hamdi’s paintings the female figures are often conscious of the period of Westernization in the Ottoman Empire, as well as their individual identities and talents, and are thus open to learning and self-development. In a number of Osman Hamdi’s works, the Ottoman woman is portrayed playing an instrument or reading and she always appears fully clothed. In this painting, which incorporates architectural elements of the Bursa Green Mosque, apart from musical instruments like the *tambur* (lute) and the tambourine, Ottoman decorative elements such as rugs, woodwork, stone carving, and tiles complement the artist’s unique approach to the female identity.

e3f48d7b-3bf0-5b73-ae59-24ec80351340.name: Tantur (woman's headdress)
e3f48d7b-3bf0-5b73-ae59-24ec80351340.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
e3f48d7b-3bf0-5b73-ae59-24ec80351340.author: Vito Lattanzi, Marina Minozzi
e3f48d7b-3bf0-5b73-ae59-24ec80351340.keywords: Woman; photograph; anthropology; ethnology; geography; travel; ethnography; museums; model; genre picture; portrait; representation of the other; costume; material culture; collection; Lebanon; floral decoration; animal decoration; zoomorphism; zoomorphic
e3f48d7b-3bf0-5b73-ae59-24ec80351340.materials: Silver laminate decorated with embossed work
e3f48d7b-3bf0-5b73-ae59-24ec80351340.description2: The Tantur is an example of cultural tradition developed inside the contaminations typical of the Mediterranean world. It is decorated with symbolic images of leaves, flowers and animals and it is engraved with the year of Egira, 1172. Its cylindrical shape is reminiscent of an *asherah*, one of the emblems of the Phoenician goddess of fertility Astarte (the Siriac Atargotis), often represented with cylindrical headgear. The origins in terms of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

e532dd30-df15-5462-88cf-6f2eaa8cf7bd.name: Portrait of David Roberts, Esq., R. A.
e532dd30-df15-5462-88cf-6f2eaa8cf7bd.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
e532dd30-df15-5462-88cf-6f2eaa8cf7bd.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
e532dd30-df15-5462-88cf-6f2eaa8cf7bd.description2: This engraving shows a portrait of David Roberts (1796 – 1864), first completed in the 1840s by Charles Baugniet. Roberts is shown seated on an ancient plinth or capital, holding a drawing board and a pencil. A classical temple structure appears in the background on the left. David Roberts was a Scottish painter especially known for a prolific series of detailed lithograph prints of Egypt and the Near East produced during the 1840s from sketches he made during extensive tours of the region (1838–1839). These, and his large oil paintings of similar subjects, made him a prominent and highly influential Orientalist painter. Charles-Louis Baugniet (1814 - 1886), was a Belgian artist famous for the lithographing of portraits of prominent European figures.

e53bb5a4-b7fc-5802-a8fd-9ee4197aa491.name: Illuminated Qur’an manuscript
e53bb5a4-b7fc-5802-a8fd-9ee4197aa491.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
e53bb5a4-b7fc-5802-a8fd-9ee4197aa491.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
e53bb5a4-b7fc-5802-a8fd-9ee4197aa491.artist: Calligrapher: Hussayn al-Hilmi, a student of Muhammad Amin know as Izzi
e53bb5a4-b7fc-5802-a8fd-9ee4197aa491.materials: European paper, black ink, pigments, gilding, pasteboard, leather
e53bb5a4-b7fc-5802-a8fd-9ee4197aa491.description2: 19th-century Qur’an manuscripts produced in Istanbul and the Ottoman Empire continued many Islamic art traditions, but could not entirely escape the increasing taste for Western aesthetics.The exquisite execution of this manuscript suggests a wealthy patron. The opening double page is set within an elaborate framework of floral and geometric arabesque cartouches, executed in gold, blue and other colours. The design recalls those of early Ottoman manuscripts, which - in turn - took their artistic inspiration from Iranian Qur’an production. The remainder of this Qur’an is executed in black naskhi on 390 gilt-edged folios, with 15 lines to each page. As a rule, Ottoman calligraphers preferred an odd number of lines to each page, be it 11, 13 or 15. The script is enhanced with red detailing, and the verse dividers are gilt. The chapter headings are executed in white riqa' on a golden ground enhanced by delicate floral ornament. Large coloured medallions in the page margins mark important sub-divisions of the text. The signature of the calligrapher – set into an elaborate gold rosette – appears on the last page.

e5b5e193-f08b-5657-b562-1f2add9c333b.name: *Egyptian Landscape*
e5b5e193-f08b-5657-b562-1f2add9c333b.description: This was a good example for the author to derive information from because the author himself did not travel to the Near East. The painter documented his works thanks to books with prints or photographs. It could be located at the Kom Ombo temple in the east bank of the Nile valley.
e5b5e193-f08b-5657-b562-1f2add9c333b.author: Carolina Miguel Arroyo

e64cc958-3eac-53d9-a717-4b4ffea3de31.name: *Interior of Kairouan Mosque, Tunis*
e64cc958-3eac-53d9-a717-4b4ffea3de31.description: One of 389 photographs taken by the Tunisian Service of Antiquities. These photographs were exhibited in the European Historic Exhibition held in Madrid in 1892-1892. After the exhibition closure the photographs were donated to the National Museum of Archaeology.
e64cc958-3eac-53d9-a717-4b4ffea3de31.third_name: *Interior de la mezquita de Kairroun, Túnez*

e6b08b1b-d850-518a-9f8a-7c3f457e761d.name: Palais du Baron d’Erlanger
e6b08b1b-d850-518a-9f8a-7c3f457e761d.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
e6b08b1b-d850-518a-9f8a-7c3f457e761d.history: The history of this monument cannot be separated from its creator's personality. The rich Orientalist painter and Arabic musicologist Baron d'Erlanger moved to Sidi Bou Said in 1911, where he built is palace. He dedicated his life to the preservation of Tunisia's architectural, artistic and musical heritage, and on his death in 1932 was buried in Sidi Bou Said. Notable examples of his work are his vital efforts towards the preservation of Sidi Bou Said, and his remarkable seven-volume work on Arabic music.
e6b08b1b-d850-518a-9f8a-7c3f457e761d.keywords: Architecture; Andalusian style; Italian style; stucco; carved wood; painting
e6b08b1b-d850-518a-9f8a-7c3f457e761d.description2: This palace is built on a hill overlooking the sea, and covers approximately 3,300 m2, occupying just a small portion of the 5-hectare grounds. Built between 1912 and 1922, the palace is notable for its interesting architecture, inspired by Tunisian traditions with elements of Andalusian, Venetian and Arab ornamentation. Behind its huge sea-facing façade, it is organised into three distinct sections. The two main square patios, on two separate floors, are connected by galleries, and all surround a covered central space. The décor consists of wall decorations, ceramic panels, carved stucco panels, stucco carved ceilings, golden or painted carved wooden ceilings, and more.

e6b08b1b-d850-518a-9f8a-7c3f457e761d.responsible_institution_org: Ministère de la Culture et de la Sauvegarde du Patrimoine

e6f7eabb-fc4e-5c98-b6ca-f2544ae496d9.name: Model in plaster
e6f7eabb-fc4e-5c98-b6ca-f2544ae496d9.description: Following on the European fascination for the oriental world and for the famous Nasrid Palaces of the Alhambra (Granada, Spain), a lot of reproductions of its remarkable architectures and decorations were made and spread. José Contreras was commended as restorer and decorator and his son, Rafael (1824–1890), was the leading pioneer of this trend in 1847. His work was continued by the grandson and by a huge number of plaster-cast workshops in Granada, and very likely, in other cities. His plasterworks were very successful in the International Exhibitions and were kept in private collections and museums like South Kensington (London). This polychrome plaster cast res a window in the Mexnar Palace of Granada (Spain).
e6f7eabb-fc4e-5c98-b6ca-f2544ae496d9.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes, Cristina Giménez

e72a56fc-762a-58a7-9573-a53ca4ec40e7.name: Qur'an stand (*kursi*)
e72a56fc-762a-58a7-9573-a53ca4ec40e7.type: Islamic, Indian & Southeast Asian works of art; Metalwork
e72a56fc-762a-58a7-9573-a53ca4ec40e7.holder: Shangri La, Doris Duke Foundation for Islamic Art
e72a56fc-762a-58a7-9573-a53ca4ec40e7.keywords: Qur'an stand; kursi; Mamluk Revival; Egypt; copper alloy; brass; silver; copper inlay; Qur'an; inscription; geometric motifs; furniture
e72a56fc-762a-58a7-9573-a53ca4ec40e7.materials: Copper alloy (brass); inlaid with silver and copper inlay
e72a56fc-762a-58a7-9573-a53ca4ec40e7.description2: This tall, hexagonal brass side table has a flat top, six-sided body, and six baluster-shaped feet. The table is inlaid with inscriptional panels offset by engraved or pierced vegetal patterns. The sides are composed of several panels inset within a frame. This stand may originally have been used to support the Qur’an as it was read. For protection, the Qur’an could be stored inside the stand by opening the small doors and placing the text within.

e733f2a6-8940-5e1d-ba96-bb338e5c87f6.name: Hooded cloak (*burnus*)
e733f2a6-8940-5e1d-ba96-bb338e5c87f6.description: Cloak in green velvet with stencilled decoration of pomegranates and leaves in brown. This velvet is based on the Venetian ones of the 15th and 16th centuries. The cloak has a wide fullness at the bottom and a big hood, formed by four points. The cloak is lined in a green silk, printed in silver vegetal motifs.
e733f2a6-8940-5e1d-ba96-bb338e5c87f6.holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
e733f2a6-8940-5e1d-ba96-bb338e5c87f6.author: Elvira González

e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.name: *Interior of the Great Temple at Baalbec*
e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.artist: Drawn by William Henry Bartlett; engraved by Ebenezar Challis
e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.description2: This view into the interior of the Temple of Bacchus at Baalbek, Lebanon originally formed appeared in 'Syria, The Holy Land, Asia Minor, &c', illustrated views printed in 3 series over 2 volumes (37 plates, 37 plates, and 48 plates for each series respectively) including maps and title pages. The publication resulted from the 1836-1838 collaboration between the painter William Henry Bartlett, the engraver Ebenezer Challis and the Publishers Fisher, Son and Co. The architectural and artistic details they recorded subsequently inspired European Neoclassical architects and artists such as Robert Adam, who based one of the ceilings at Osterley House on the ceiling of the Temple of Bacchus and the portico of St George's, Bloomsbury on its portico. Since the 1860s, many tourists visited the site, including, in 1898, the German emperor Wilhelm II. Struck by the magnificence of the ruins, he dispatched a German archaeological team, whose subsequent work resulted in a meticulous, illustrated publication that further popularised the site.

e80c1234-42a0-5c12-9754-82402e1fca45.name: Umbonate plate
e80c1234-42a0-5c12-9754-82402e1fca45.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
e80c1234-42a0-5c12-9754-82402e1fca45.author: Marina Minozzi
e80c1234-42a0-5c12-9754-82402e1fca45.keywords: Applied arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; motifs; collector; Spain; Moorish; Islamic art; Islamic influence; Neo-Mudéjar style; production of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode; Aragon
e80c1234-42a0-5c12-9754-82402e1fca45.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". The collections included large samples of pottery, wooden objects, fabric, bronzes and ivories dating to Roman, Renaissance and Baroque times. The best part of this collection is on display at the National Gallery of Palazzo Barberini in Rome, while other pieces are housed in Castel Sant'Angelo and Palazzo Venezia. The series of the Hispanic-Moorish ceramics, bought by Prince Baldassarre Ladislao Odescalchi in 1880, were among the models often reproduced by the training school inside the M.A.I. The umbonate plate (inv.n. 2828) is an aragonese manufacture dating from the first half of 16th century. It shows concentric strips with blue and red tones.
e80c1234-42a0-5c12-9754-82402e1fca45.holding_institution_org: Museo Artistico Industriale presso la Galleria nazionale d’arte antica in Palazzo Barberini

en: Zaccagnini, M., *Arti decorative: Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini*, Rome: L'Erma di Bretschneider, 2011: 13-16.

e80dfa93-78f5-57ec-a258-0a31de9fef63.name: *The daughter of the English ambassador riding in a palanquin*
e80dfa93-78f5-57ec-a258-0a31de9fef63.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
e80dfa93-78f5-57ec-a258-0a31de9fef63.keywords: Fausto Zonaro; Guillemet; Orientalism; painting; İstanbul
e80dfa93-78f5-57ec-a258-0a31de9fef63.description2: Until he was appointed as the court painter in 1896, Zonaro was predominantly commissioned by European embassies in Istanbul. In his memoirs, the artist reveals that British Ambassador Sir Philip William Currie (1894-96), who was one of Zonaro’s clients, commissioned a painting depicting his stepdaughter on the palanquin on her way to the church to marry a diplomat. Sir Currie also requested the view of the Golden Horn – as seen from the garden of the embassy – to be included in the background of the painting. The palanquin carriers, two embassy officials smartly dressed in their uniforms and the young woman sitting on the palanquin in her bridal veil, posed for the artist for several days.

e8fc4581-ee8f-583c-a11e-54b1e44bda1a.name: Arabic eye liner, *kohl* and perfume container
e8fc4581-ee8f-583c-a11e-54b1e44bda1a.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
e8fc4581-ee8f-583c-a11e-54b1e44bda1a.author: Huda Kilani
e8fc4581-ee8f-583c-a11e-54b1e44bda1a.description2: Padded bag to hold three small brass bottles of Arab eye-liner, perfumes and essential oils. It was used as a wall decoration. Decorated with silk tassels, glass beads, Egyptian and Ottoman coins. The Jordanian economy relied on trades and crafts and new waves of people started to settle in the Jordanian territory for these purposes. This object is an example of how traditional fashion reflected the variegated population composition of the area in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is also an example of local personal attire, fashion, costumes and rites.

e903b036-cf17-5703-8d28-f9c9700f9acc.name: Dagger
e903b036-cf17-5703-8d28-f9c9700f9acc.description: A dagger decorated with geometric and floral motifs and crafted in southern Morocco in the 19th century. Dagger blades were imported from Europe.
e903b036-cf17-5703-8d28-f9c9700f9acc.keywords: Trade; arms; armours; metalwork; European influence; geometric motifs; geometric decoration; floral decoration; vegetal motifs; vegetal decoration; craftsmanship; war; warfare; military objects
e903b036-cf17-5703-8d28-f9c9700f9acc.materials: Silver; gemstones; copper, wood, horn; cord

e9d20fa0-c214-51e8-a022-980c7d31384c.name: Tekke panel
e9d20fa0-c214-51e8-a022-980c7d31384c.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
e9d20fa0-c214-51e8-a022-980c7d31384c.description2: *Hüsn-i Hat* is a type of calligraphy. Turks probably started to get interested in calligraphy after their arrival to Anatolia. The brightest period was during the Ottoman era. Calligraphy developed well beyond its functional role; it almost played a similar role to the paintings in Western art in terms of the level of its aesthetics. The script *"Ya Hazreti Şeyh Sultan Yusuf Sümbül Sinan Kaddes Allahu sırrahu"* (religious text, untranslatable) is written on a black background with *Zerendud* (gilded) calligraphy and designed as the *sikke* (tall felt hat) of the Sünbüli order. It stands over a small table in Rococo style and there are hyacinth flowers on either corner of the upper part. The sides of the plate are surrounded by two borders that are Rococo in design.

e9e0d077-22ec-5da6-8968-784248276025.name: Palais Kasr el-Said
e9e0d077-22ec-5da6-8968-784248276025.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
e9e0d077-22ec-5da6-8968-784248276025.history: Located near the Bardo palaces, this palace had belonged to a noble of the Husainid court until 1867. It was then subject to a series of adjustments and expansions under the reign of Sadok Pacha Bey, who took up residence there once the works were completed. It was in this palace that, on 12 May 1881, Sadok Pacha Bey added his signature to the treaty which would impose a French Protectorate on his country, headed by General Bréart. The building was restored and taken over by l'Institut National du Patrimonie in 1988, and now houses the first landmarks of the Musée d'Histoire de la Tunisie Moderne et Contemporaine, whilst also preserving its Husainid foundations. It also holds many historically valuable paintings, thrones and coaches which had belonged to the bey.
e9e0d077-22ec-5da6-8968-784248276025.keywords: Architecture; art; painting; stucco; mosaic; marble; ceramics
e9e0d077-22ec-5da6-8968-784248276025.description2: This palace is an excellent example of a typical beylical palace, with an architecture, décor and furnishings that show distinct signs of European, and particularly Italian, influences. The large, tall building is surrounded by trees and orchards. The grand staircase, the marble columns, the marble, ceramic and faience mosaics on the walls, the Italian-style window frames and the Andalusian-style carved stucco all contribute to the decorations' opulent and varied quality, which characterised the 18th and 19th centuries.

ea56c676-8f35-5489-88dc-00a76f28ef9d.name: *Turkish ladies buying jewellery*
ea56c676-8f35-5489-88dc-00a76f28ef9d.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
ea56c676-8f35-5489-88dc-00a76f28ef9d.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
ea56c676-8f35-5489-88dc-00a76f28ef9d.description2: This watercolour, completed in 1873, shows three elegantly dressed society ladies, their faces concealed by a light veil, visiting the shop of a jeweller, his wares displayed in a small multi-tiered glass case placed on the low platform in front. While one of the ladies is seated on a carpet at the entrance to the shop to examine a pearl necklace that the old, bespectacled proprietor has offered her, her two companions wait outside and shield her to some extent from curious eyes. Vittorio Amadeo, 5th Count Preziosi (1816-1882) was an artist of Maltese origin, who left for the Middle East in the early 1840s. He settled in Istanbul as a diplomatic translator and artist, specialising in touristic scenes, vistas and types

ea69f41d-1b91-5ee4-8097-8aba9db33c0f.name: *Le consul Joseph Raffo* (painting)
ea69f41d-1b91-5ee4-8097-8aba9db33c0f.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
ea69f41d-1b91-5ee4-8097-8aba9db33c0f.author: Bechir Yazidi
ea69f41d-1b91-5ee4-8097-8aba9db33c0f.materials: Canvas, wood, coloured pigments, gold leaf
ea69f41d-1b91-5ee4-8097-8aba9db33c0f.description2: Giuseppe Maria Joseph Raffo, the subject of this painting, was born in Tunis in 1795 and is depicted here in full uniform with the air of an important Turkish dignitary. He entered service as a secretary to Bey Hassine, and later served as Tunisia's Minister for Foreign Affairs under his rule as well as that of his successors, despite being a Sardinian subject all the while. He made a fortune by taking over a tuna farm in the Cap Bon region in the form of private concession. This painting is evidence of an active diplomatic relationship between the Palais du Bardo and the European chancelleries.

eae0553a-c677-57b1-9a70-eda8e6211616.name: The Belvedere (Wilhelma Park)
eae0553a-c677-57b1-9a70-eda8e6211616.holder: Wilhelma, Zoological and Botanical Garden Stuttgart
eae0553a-c677-57b1-9a70-eda8e6211616.history:
King Wilhelm I of Württemberg commissioned to Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1837 the design of Moorish style buildings for his Wilhelma garden. The architect planned and built all the buildings with the exception of the Damascene Hall.  
The idea was not to reproduce faithfully the Islamic art but to lend an “oriental” flair to the garden. The mention of an “oriental garden” conjured up visions of elegance, luxury, colourful brilliance, seduction and eroticism.  
The Moorish style recalls the Islamic art of Spain and North Africa between the 12th and 15th centuries which reached its zenith in the Alhambra. It was fashionable in 19th century: Wilhelma is also known as the “Alhambra on the river Neckar” and other buildings – synagogues in Berlin and Vienna for example – were built in the Moorish style.
eae0553a-c677-57b1-9a70-eda8e6211616.description2: The Belvedere is situated on the Rosenstein slope and, as the name signifies (it is Italian for "lovely view"), it is one of the loveliest viewing spots at Wilhelma. From 1851 onwards it served King Wilhelm I of Württemberg as a place to enjoy the view across to the Burial Chapel on Rotenberg Hill and over the Swabian countryside. The Belvedere forms the upper limit of the Sub Tropics Terraces and also of the entire historical Wilhelma, The pavilion itself is closed to the public, but the view can still be enjoyed.

eb5033cb-f5e6-537a-88bb-7d6bf116bf69.name: Laledan
eb5033cb-f5e6-537a-88bb-7d6bf116bf69.description2: It is known that there were workshops producing glass vessels around Beykoz in Istanbul in the 19th century. The first glass workshop was founded by Mevlevi Dervish Mehmed Dede during the reign of Selim III (1789-1807). There were European glass craftsmen working in those workshops as well. Cups, bottles, jugs etc. made of colourful, colourless and opal glass were among Beykoz' productions. This is a *laledan* made of dark blue opaline. On the body there are white vervain motives with green leaves. There are three circles with stars and crescents.

ebdb2818-1d18-5e45-8ad1-bf0b9bc145ab.name: Mosque lamp
ebdb2818-1d18-5e45-8ad1-bf0b9bc145ab.keywords: Orientalism; decorative arts; glass; calligraphy; inscription; mosque interior decoration
ebdb2818-1d18-5e45-8ad1-bf0b9bc145ab.description2: Decorated mosque lamp made in Syria.

ec198745-bf85-5cf3-a025-264676b49e2d.name: *Histoire de la Princesse Boudour (Conte des mille et une nuits)*, Translation by J.C. Mardrus of *The Story of the Princess Boudour: Tales of a Thousand and One Nights*
ec198745-bf85-5cf3-a025-264676b49e2d.description: François-Louis Schmied (1873–1941) and Jean Dunand (1877–1942) worked together on *Histoire de la Princess Boudour*, the French translation of one of the tales from *The Arabian Nights* by J.-C- Mardrus. The painter, illustrator, engraver, bookbinder and publisher François-Louis Schmied was primarily responsible for producing the graphic design and handling of the text, the illustrations and their wood interpretations. Dunand produced a lacquered metal plaque that transmitted the eroticism and voluptuousness revealed throughout the text. Using warm colours, Princess Boudour is portrayed on a red ground sprinkled with gold, and appears as a very elongated, tubular figure holding a flower with both hands. It’s a limited edition, just twenty copies, it’s a extremely rare Art Deco book.
ec198745-bf85-5cf3-a025-264676b49e2d.author: Manuela Fidalgo
ec198745-bf85-5cf3-a025-264676b49e2d.keywords: Orientalism; Literature;  François – Louis Schmeed; Jean Dunand George
ec198745-bf85-5cf3-a025-264676b49e2d.materials: Binding: black and green morocco by Georges Bretté (1893–1969), with one lacquered plate by Jean Dunond (1877–1942)

en: Carvalho, Pedro Moura (ed), *The World of Lacquer. 2000 years of History*, exhibition catalogue, Lisbon: Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation, 2001, p.241.

ec7fd0d9-9cc8-500f-9c45-55773ae4604c.name: *The Tortoise Trainer*
ec7fd0d9-9cc8-500f-9c45-55773ae4604c.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
ec7fd0d9-9cc8-500f-9c45-55773ae4604c.keywords: Osman Hamdi Bey; Orientalism; painting; İstanbul
ec7fd0d9-9cc8-500f-9c45-55773ae4604c.description2: Rather than depicting the “other” as a number of foreign painters did, Osman Hamdi portrayed his own culture and propounded his own cultural perceptions. The architectural decor suggests that the scene takes place in one of the upper-story chambers of the Bursa Green Mosque. Dressed as a dervish and slightly bent over, a man is examining in a contemplative fashion the tortoises roaming the floor. He sports an *araqiyya*, a flattish skull cap commonly worn by dervishes with a *destar*, or sash wrapped around it. He wears a belted, long red robe the borders of which are embroidered; his feet are clad in *çedik*, or slippers for indoor wear, made of yellow *sahtiyan*, Moroccan (goatskin) leather. He holds a ney in one of the hands he has clasped behind; a *nakkare* or a small kettledrum hangs down from his back.

ecda8323-4cc5-5e96-a034-122e8ca1bb6c.name: Textile from the Prince Felipe of Castile burial
ecda8323-4cc5-5e96-a034-122e8ca1bb6c.description: This fragment came from the set of garments wore by the Castilian Prince Phillip in his burial at Villalcázar de Sirga (Palencia). The fragment is a very good example of the richness of the textile from al-Andalus. The textile has an inscription in Arabic that could be translated as “Glory to our Lord the Sultan”. This an early example of the interest in collecting important textiles, even before the important research made by Gómez-Moreno in the Royal Convent of the Huelgas (Burgos).
ecda8323-4cc5-5e96-a034-122e8ca1bb6c.author: Ámparo López
ecda8323-4cc5-5e96-a034-122e8ca1bb6c.keywords: Nasrid art; islamic influence; orientalism; collectionism

edab323b-dc63-5faf-a178-579bc04253cd.name: Pitcher
edab323b-dc63-5faf-a178-579bc04253cd.description2: Kütahya was the second most important ceramic production centre after İznik due to the rich clay deposits in the area. Although there was a decline in ceramic production at the beginning of the 19th century, in the last quarter of that same century production was revived and new designs inspired by İznik ceramics were produced.

ede0b2ce-0710-54bf-ab1e-1d03d63a1f3d.name: *View of the Arab Courtyard: National Museum of Archeaology, Madrid*
ede0b2ce-0710-54bf-ab1e-1d03d63a1f3d.description: View of the "Arab courtyard" in the National Museum of Archaeology before 1920. This room displayed different pieces including the Alfajería arch and a copy of the fountain of the Lions of the Alhambra palace. This room was one of the first museum gallery focused in the Arab or Islamic pieces in Europe.
ede0b2ce-0710-54bf-ab1e-1d03d63a1f3d.keywords: Museums; Spanish Muslim art and Archaoelogy; Madrid

ef67fa8c-4ff1-55bf-83f3-ae6118113aaa.name: *Sorolla in Tetouan*
ef67fa8c-4ff1-55bf-83f3-ae6118113aaa.description:
This picture was taken in Tetouan during a trip of the painter Joaquín Sorolla and his friends to Morocco in 1919. Sorolla's family and friends were portrayed with local people, a highlight of which is the Moor Selam and other characters and exotic animals, such as the monkey. Especially interesting is her daughter Helena who appeared in a Moorish costume.  
This travel appeared in the newspapers El Confidencial and ABC which also published this photograph.  
This family trip brought back memories and objects. The painter's daughter, Helena, had their little Moorish corner on the stairs of the house which is now the Sorolla Museum. A table, a chest, tambourines, fabrics, jewellery were bought back as souvenirs.
ef67fa8c-4ff1-55bf-83f3-ae6118113aaa.author: Covadonga Pitarch

f03672a7-5a8f-5216-8d53-07817c3aa415.name: *The Prayer in the Desert*
f03672a7-5a8f-5216-8d53-07817c3aa415.author: Marina Minozzi
f03672a7-5a8f-5216-8d53-07817c3aa415.keywords: Orientalism; imaginary trips; reinvention; Egyptomania; Egyptology; architectural trends in painting; exoticism; diplomatic mission; Mulay al-Hasan; travel; travelling artist; Italian travellers; Italian painters; Edmondo de Amicis; Marocco; travel book
f03672a7-5a8f-5216-8d53-07817c3aa415.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
f03672a7-5a8f-5216-8d53-07817c3aa415.description2: Stefano Ussi lived between Florence and Rome and studied at the Academy of Fine Arts of Florence before enrolling as a volunteer in the first Italian War of Independence, during which he was taken prisoner by the Austrian troops. He developed a model of history painting characterised by a quick application of layers (almost a rough draft) and by a sharp chiaroscuro. In 1875, along with the painter Cesare Biseo, and Edmondo De Amicis, he accompanied an Italian diplomatic delegation to Morocco. At the opening of the Suez Canal the artist went to Egypt and created his first version of *The Prayer in the Desert* which is exhibited at the Accademia di Belle Arti in Florence. From that moment on, Ussi made both history and oriental-themed paintings.
f03672a7-5a8f-5216-8d53-07817c3aa415.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

en: Villari, A., in Elena di Majo and Mateo Lafranconi (eds), *Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Moderna. Le Collezioni. Il XIX secolo*, Milan: Electa, 2006, cat. 1.35.

f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.name: Headdress
f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.author: Huda Kilani
f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.keywords: Ottoman; Russian coins; pendent; red and green silk
f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.materials: Silver, fabric, glass beads, coins; casting, welding, weaving
f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.description2: Three bands of silver chain fitted around the sides and over the crown of the head and attached to a surrounding fabric patterned in minute beadwork and sewn with various Ottoman and Russian coins. From this head-piece hangs a long piece of cotton sewn with coins of the Ottoman Empire with a rectangular pendant and multiple red and green silk tassels on the back. Headdresses like this one were worn by married women, as silver was the most common jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride. The Ottoman and Russian coins reflect the social and economic situation of Jordan between the end of the 19th century and the early 20th century, when it was part of the Ottoman empire and it was influenced by population movements, demographic changes and trade with distant countries.

f16ca057-a0e1-511d-9754-d9f37c51ca07.name: Kız Kulesi, Galata and Fındıklı Residential Areas
f16ca057-a0e1-511d-9754-d9f37c51ca07.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; Pascal Sebah
f16ca057-a0e1-511d-9754-d9f37c51ca07.description2: Pascal Sébah (1823-1886) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. In 1857 he opened his first photography studio, *El Chark Societe Photographic*, in Istanbul and by 1873 was successful enough to open another studio in Cairo. In 1860 he moved to another studio next to the Russian Embassy in order to work with A. Laroche, who worked in Paris. He continued to work with Laroche until 1873.

f1858928-5bad-513c-bdc1-bfdf93efecdb.name: Pair of boots (*tmeg*)
f1858928-5bad-513c-bdc1-bfdf93efecdb.description: A pair of Boots (*tmeg*) crafted in Meknès in the 19th century, but making use of British imports such as velvet (*nta‘a*) and gold thread.
f1858928-5bad-513c-bdc1-bfdf93efecdb.keywords: Craftsmanship; traditional craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmen; leather; leatherwork; trade; raw material; finished products; British in Morocco; fashion

f2797aad-043c-51e6-ba00-d9f4afd964a3.name: *Recherches sur l' origine du Blason et en particulier sur la Fleur de Lis*
f2797aad-043c-51e6-ba00-d9f4afd964a3.author: Mina Moraitou
f2797aad-043c-51e6-ba00-d9f4afd964a3.description2: The illustrated publication *Recherches sur l' origine du Blason et en particulier sur la Fleur de Lis* is a study on emblems with references to Mamluk blasons. It contains the ex libris of Antonis Benakis.

f30a52d1-4558-58b4-bdf7-91782044f03c.name: Brooch
f30a52d1-4558-58b4-bdf7-91782044f03c.author: Ámparo López
f30a52d1-4558-58b4-bdf7-91782044f03c.keywords: Nasrid art; islamic influence; orientalism; collectionism
f30a52d1-4558-58b4-bdf7-91782044f03c.description2: This brooch is part of the contemporary pieces from North Africa collected by Lázara Galdiano. It is important to point out that most of the Spanish collectors and museums not only acquired early Arab pieces of the Middle Ages, but also pieces from the North African or Near Eastern workshops of the mid-19th century or early 20th century, as part of the interest in these countries.

f310be0c-2e4a-5a7a-ab0c-baaa41091e32.name: *Dokhla* (wedding dress)
f310be0c-2e4a-5a7a-ab0c-baaa41091e32.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
f310be0c-2e4a-5a7a-ab0c-baaa41091e32.keywords: Embroidery from Nabeul; sequins and gold thread
f310be0c-2e4a-5a7a-ab0c-baaa41091e32.materials: Embroidered fabric with gold-plated silver thread
f310be0c-2e4a-5a7a-ab0c-baaa41091e32.description2: This tunic is entirely embroidered with gold-plated silver thread. This is the most important element of the marriage ceremony (jelwa) in Nabeul (Tunisia). The rectangular tunic's splendour comes from its incredibly rich embroidery, which is made of various different silk ribbons, all embellished with tal. In fact, the embroidery entirely covers the fabric itself. The breast and belt areas are embroidered with sequins and gold thread. The tunic is calf-length, and a luxurious pair of silk trousers can be seen beneath, covered in gold embroidery to match the sleeves. In addition to this, one of the bride's many items of jewellery is a great chain of golden rings, a rihana, which she wears with a large necklace made of a scented material. Lastly, the bride's head is covered by an embroidered veil made of muslin and silk.

f3955418-aaed-57fc-96f9-18195a4d076b.name: *Atik Valide Mosque*
f3955418-aaed-57fc-96f9-18195a4d076b.keywords: Painting; Hüseyin Zekai Pasha; orientalist Turkish painters
f3955418-aaed-57fc-96f9-18195a4d076b.description2: The majority of Turkish painters in the 19th century were Ottoman officers who had studied abroad. Hüseyin Zekai Pasha was one of those painters. Following his education at the Kuleli Military High School, he continued his studies at the Military Academy (*Mektebi Harbiye*), where he had a chance to learn technical drawing and perspective. His first period was realistic and his pictorial representation includes scenes or events from everyday life. In his first works, Hüseyin Zekai Pasha followed the painting tradition of 19th century, including thin paint dough and light colours. He made changes in his techniques through the Galatasaray Exhibition and eventually he turned into an impressionist whose work was dominated by thicker brush strokes.

f4606868-6540-5152-bd07-486c73a7f541.name: Jug
f4606868-6540-5152-bd07-486c73a7f541.description2: Çanakkale was a pottery production centre between the end of 17th century and first quarter of the 20th century where pottery with interesting and original forms was produced. Mostly coarse red clay and occasionally beige-coloured paste was used. This vase has pear-like shape with a long neck. On its neck there are three horn-like projecting forms. On the sides and in the front there are embossed decorations.

f54c0c7c-ee1e-50ca-aed8-8e94a72d0f30.name: *Exposition d' art Musulman*
f54c0c7c-ee1e-50ca-aed8-8e94a72d0f30.author: Mina Moraitou
f54c0c7c-ee1e-50ca-aed8-8e94a72d0f30.description2: A catalogue of the *Exposition d’ Art Musulman* which was organized by Gaston Migeon and held in Alexandria in 1925. For each object it contains a description and provenance with no illustrations.

f672a566-07c0-5def-83e1-f7239ef4cf19.name: Cup with *merletto* ('lace') decoration
f672a566-07c0-5def-83e1-f7239ef4cf19.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
f672a566-07c0-5def-83e1-f7239ef4cf19.author: Marina Minozzi
f672a566-07c0-5def-83e1-f7239ef4cf19.keywords: Applied arts; minor arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; decoration; motifs; collection; collector; glass; Murano glass; glasswork; zoomorphysm; zoomorphic; lace; Venice; Victorian; Quattrocento
f672a566-07c0-5def-83e1-f7239ef4cf19.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. The tendency of Murano's industries in using bizarre shapes, often of zoomorphic inspiration, gave life to manufacts not so much functional as decorative. It was very successful. The cylindrical cup in green glass with white glaze and “lace” decoration is the result of a combination of common design details in the second half of the 19th century: while it shows a Victorian decoration, the structure of the object recalls a late 14th century model.
f672a566-07c0-5def-83e1-f7239ef4cf19.holding_institution_org: Museo Artistico Industriale presso la Galleria nazionale d’arte antica in Palazzo Barberini

f6a4d871-3bbf-5f91-943b-4fb7cd618871.name: Saddle (*serj*)
f6a4d871-3bbf-5f91-943b-4fb7cd618871.description: A saddle (*serj*) crafted in Rabat in the 19th century, but making use of British imports such as velvet (*nta‘a*), leather and gold thread.
f6a4d871-3bbf-5f91-943b-4fb7cd618871.keywords: Craftsmanship; traditional craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmen; leather; leatherwork; trade; raw material; finished products; British in Morocco; horsemanship

f7fde934-bd37-5990-9d4a-995069413fad.name: Textile
f7fde934-bd37-5990-9d4a-995069413fad.description: Textile with stencilled decoration with Arab calligraphy. The textile surface has different shades.
f7fde934-bd37-5990-9d4a-995069413fad.holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
f7fde934-bd37-5990-9d4a-995069413fad.author: Lucina Llorente
