f88cd52e-27ec-5aee-beba-ea252bcda254.name: *Gunsmiths at the Palace of the Alhambra*
f88cd52e-27ec-5aee-beba-ea252bcda254.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
f88cd52e-27ec-5aee-beba-ea252bcda254.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
f88cd52e-27ec-5aee-beba-ea252bcda254.description2: This painting, entitled 'Gunsmiths at the Palace of the Alhambra, Granada' is a romantic, Orientalist phantasy designed to pander to the taste of 19th-century Europeans fascinated by the palace complex in particular since the publication of Washington Irving's 'Tales of the Alhambra' after his stay in Granada in 1828, and that of the British artist and designer Owen Jones, entitled 'Plans, Elevantions, Sections and Details of the Alhambra',  published in twelve parts between 1836 and 1845. Owen's work in particular, with its numerous precise architectural drawings and detailed speculations regarding the Alhambra's original colour schemes, was to exert a revolutionary influence on the European artists of his time, and there is little doubt that the Italian artist Filippo Baratti, too, consulted Owen's work in elaborating his painting's colour scheme, depicting especially the stuccoed walls in hues familiar from Owen's reconstructions.

f8cd2cbd-0428-53e7-a7ce-f3ee1f3011f9.name: Shelving unit
f8cd2cbd-0428-53e7-a7ce-f3ee1f3011f9.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
f8cd2cbd-0428-53e7-a7ce-f3ee1f3011f9.description2: This unit is made of two shelves, one in an arch shape and the second topped by small hooks and a perforated decoration. The name of its maker, "Becghtache" is written on its underside, flanked by two six-point stars.

f913a36e-6a1b-5710-a0b7-52e815a3703a.name: Arab Room
f913a36e-6a1b-5710-a0b7-52e815a3703a.description: The Arab Room shows the collections of the Marquis coming not only from Arabia but also from China, Japan, the Philippines, Turkey, Morocco and New Zealand. He collected and displayed these works, similar to other European palaces of the 19th Century, because his taste ran to oriental, exotic, foreign or ancestral cultures. This room was also known as *fumoir*, associated with smoking, essentially thought for masculine use. The ceiling is decorated with interlacing designs and six-pointed star in the middle, from which hangs a superb Arab lamp. There are kilims on the walls and carpets on the floor and furniture. Among all, we can also find arms and armouries, musical instruments and six scale-model reproducing walls and windows from some rooms of the Alhambra palace.
f913a36e-6a1b-5710-a0b7-52e815a3703a.author: Cristina Giménez

f92e54e2-12d0-5aaf-9ae2-ccb42b9f2df7.name: The monuments in the Hippodrome surrounded by protective fences
f92e54e2-12d0-5aaf-9ae2-ccb42b9f2df7.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
f92e54e2-12d0-5aaf-9ae2-ccb42b9f2df7.description2: Robertson’s Istanbul photographs are concerned primarily with the city’s historical monuments. They reveal the city’s magnificent Byzantine and Ottoman structures from different angles and with close-ups taken in an approach that is usually quite aesthetic. A frequently employed device in Robertson's photographs is the inclusion of the one or more human figures in the foreground – indeed, this is something of a trademark of Robertson’s work. In this photo, the monuments in the Hippodrome are surrounded by protective fences.

f95568b2-4453-57ae-8628-5bcd17d70b23.name: Tray with Oriental landscape
f95568b2-4453-57ae-8628-5bcd17d70b23.description: Following the Turkish style, this tray is depicted with an Orientalist landscape that might be related to the Greek War of Independence. The man on the left is dressed in the Greek skirt called *fustanella*, worn to fight against the Ottoman Empire. The different clothes of the man on the right who is turning his back may be identified with those of a Turkish warrior or janissary.
f95568b2-4453-57ae-8628-5bcd17d70b23.author: Isabel Ortega Fernández
f95568b2-4453-57ae-8628-5bcd17d70b23.materials: Moulded; enamelled, painted and gilded earthenware

f9783bd6-7a5b-5ca2-8a70-781a2af32872.name: Cross chain
f9783bd6-7a5b-5ca2-8a70-781a2af32872.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
f9783bd6-7a5b-5ca2-8a70-781a2af32872.author: Huda Kilani
f9783bd6-7a5b-5ca2-8a70-781a2af32872.description2: A cross of silver on a silver chain known with the folkloric name “heal of gazelle”, worn by Christian women. Silver was the most common jewellery; only rich people used gold. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom. This object illustrates the variegated religious composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It also demonstrates personal attire, fashion, local costumes and rites.

f986df26-3b71-5c3e-8d5b-1a8c60864ea5.name: Yemeni dagger
f986df26-3b71-5c3e-8d5b-1a8c60864ea5.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
f986df26-3b71-5c3e-8d5b-1a8c60864ea5.author: Huda Kilani
f986df26-3b71-5c3e-8d5b-1a8c60864ea5.keywords: double edged blade; hilts; geometric designs; silver filigree; suspension rings; arms; armours; metalwork; fashion; accessories
f986df26-3b71-5c3e-8d5b-1a8c60864ea5.description2: A dagger with a double-edged blade, an oblong-head hilt and silver filigree work in geometric designs; it is carried on a woollen belt with leather strap-work, usually with six asymmetrical suspension rings. Yemeni and Hijazi daggers have different shapes and their diffusion on the territory of Jordan shows how population movements, trade and exchange were common in the area.

f9c5a022-ba1e-5b5b-a490-3b54263c0271.name: *Daffah khachyya*
f9c5a022-ba1e-5b5b-a490-3b54263c0271.description2: This was purchased from Sheikh Sa\`ud’s family collection in 2001. The cloak is handmade and hand embroidered, made from heavy black wool. It is estimated to be older than 1960, between the 1940’s and the 1950’s. It is speculated that it was used by the Bedouins from eastern Saudi Arabia. It is called *daffah khachyya* and not *bisht*. *Khachyya* is the man who would have been involved in making the cloaks.

f9f0db9c-6034-5d02-b5c8-8b68a3f973f3.name: Beykoz glass - cup
f9f0db9c-6034-5d02-b5c8-8b68a3f973f3.author: Mina Moraitou
f9f0db9c-6034-5d02-b5c8-8b68a3f973f3.description2: Cup decorated with a stripped band, floral motifs and in the centre a circular medallion with a basket of fruits. It was made in the workshops of Istanbul on the Asian side. The basket with the fruit motif is a known motif of the 18th century as for example in the decoration of the private chambers of sultan Ahmed III (1703–1730) at the Topkapi Palace, and on the fountains of Istanbul. Ottoman glass of the 19th century was developed in order to compete with the imported glass from Venice and Bohemia. The technique is European but the decoration Ottoman.

fa113d57-874f-5262-96a7-d769cd7f7fd8.name: Tunic (*Djellaba*)
fa113d57-874f-5262-96a7-d769cd7f7fd8.description: *Djellaba* made in tabby or plain weave, with a striped decoration from the different wefts thread colours. The origin of this design was travels by Fortuny to North Africa in the 1930s.
fa113d57-874f-5262-96a7-d769cd7f7fd8.holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
fa113d57-874f-5262-96a7-d769cd7f7fd8.author: Elvira González
fa113d57-874f-5262-96a7-d769cd7f7fd8.materials: Cotton; tabby or plain weave, printed

faa81141-8f06-589d-906c-e5429a4e007b.name: Pipe
faa81141-8f06-589d-906c-e5429a4e007b.description: Meerschaum, sepiolite or écume de mer, is a porous mineral founded chiefly in Anatolia. Highly valued in pipe manufacturing since the late 18th century, the most famous meerschaum pipes in 19th century were those from Vienna or Paris. Due to commercial competition, new techniques were introduced. This pipe is an example of a patented French production that reproduced meerschaum pipes and cut the production price. This pipe in the shape of a young man’s head is not functional and merely decorative, and was collected by Antonio del Valle y Serrano, marquis of Villa-Huerta, in Mâcon (France), were he also collected souvenirs related to the famous poet Lamartine.
faa81141-8f06-589d-906c-e5429a4e007b.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes

fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.name: Portrait of the Marquess of Cerralbo in a Turkish Garment
fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This vignetted bust shot albumen portrait of Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, marquise of Cerralbo, shows the playful and aesthetic use of typical Turkish costume in the Abdullah Frères studio, perfect to satisfy the European desire of exoticism.
fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes
fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.third_name: Retrato de la marquesa de Cerralbo a la turca

fc95a324-d1b6-5cb0-852e-73608ea38c07.name: *Marco Polo in front of the Khan of Tartars*
fc95a324-d1b6-5cb0-852e-73608ea38c07.author: Marina Minozzi
fc95a324-d1b6-5cb0-852e-73608ea38c07.keywords: Orientalism; painting; Orientalist paintings; artistic exchange; travel; imaginary trips; reinvention; historical events in painting; history painting; neo-Gothic; architectural trends in painting; exoticism; Italian painters; travel
fc95a324-d1b6-5cb0-852e-73608ea38c07.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
fc95a324-d1b6-5cb0-852e-73608ea38c07.description2:
Tranquillo Cremona studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Venice and then at Brera Academy in Milan. He is considered the “grand bohémien of Italian painting”. This painting was the artist’s first public success. He was fascinated by history paintings and Hayez’s manner as shown in his placement of Marco Polo in front of the Khan of Tartars.  
The artist’s hope to join the Italian embassy – which never happened – was the reason for his interest in the oriental theme. In the ideal recreation, oriental ideas, which were internationally shared, are linked to neo-gothic themes which were fashionable in Italy from the beginning of the 19th century.
fc95a324-d1b6-5cb0-852e-73608ea38c07.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

fcdce33b-73b5-5f44-b815-567a60b30ab7.name: The Welcome to the Italian Delegation in Morocco
fcdce33b-73b5-5f44-b815-567a60b30ab7.author: Marina Minozzi
fcdce33b-73b5-5f44-b815-567a60b30ab7.keywords: Orientalism; reinvention; historical events in paintings; exoticism; diplomatic mission; Morocco; Mulay al-Hasan; travel; travelling artist; Italian travellers; Italian painters; Edmondo de Amicis; Marocco; travel book
fcdce33b-73b5-5f44-b815-567a60b30ab7.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
fcdce33b-73b5-5f44-b815-567a60b30ab7.description2: Stefano Ussi lived between Florence and Rome and studied at the Academy of Fine Arts of Florence before enrolling as a volunteer in the first Italian War of Independence, during which he was taken prisoner by the Austrian troops. In 1875 he, along with the painter Biseo and the writer De Amicis, followed a diplomatic delegation to Morocco. The painting represents the solemn meeting in Fez between the Alauita sovereign and the Italian delegation from the Consular Office in Tangier. The bright colours and the treatment of the young Sultan appealed to Italians viewers. This episode was masterly described by the writer De Amicis in his book “Marocco” published in 1876.
fcdce33b-73b5-5f44-b815-567a60b30ab7.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

fcf42d5a-d05c-5ebc-88f3-195d584999e1.name: Vase with curved handles
fcf42d5a-d05c-5ebc-88f3-195d584999e1.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
fcf42d5a-d05c-5ebc-88f3-195d584999e1.author: Marina Minozzi
fcf42d5a-d05c-5ebc-88f3-195d584999e1.keywords: Applied arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; motifs; collector; Spain; Islamic art; Islamic influence; Romanticism; Neo-Mudéjar style; Alhambra vase; production of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode
fcf42d5a-d05c-5ebc-88f3-195d584999e1.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans. The idea was part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Spanish and Arabian motifs became fashionable in the mid-19th century. The Spanish medieval pottery showed a very strong representation of Romantic Orientalism and inspired a beautiful production of "winged vases"(18th to 19th century). The majolica vase with curved handles is painted in blue and red-brown metallic lustre over a white background. It has a long neck, imitating the Hispanic-Moorish tradition, and its decoration shows a stylised floral motif. It can be dated around mid-19th century for its form and decoration technique.
fcf42d5a-d05c-5ebc-88f3-195d584999e1.holding_institution_org: Museo Artistico Industriale presso la Galleria nazionale d’arte antica in Palazzo Barberini

fcf825c0-6979-528e-9ead-d92db4b19652.name: Vase
fcf825c0-6979-528e-9ead-d92db4b19652.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
fcf825c0-6979-528e-9ead-d92db4b19652.author: Huda Kilani
fcf825c0-6979-528e-9ead-d92db4b19652.keywords: Copper tin; coated; enamelled; birds; floral decoration; Arabic script
fcf825c0-6979-528e-9ead-d92db4b19652.materials: Copper, tin niello; casting, carving and niello
fcf825c0-6979-528e-9ead-d92db4b19652.description2: A copper tin-coated enamelled vase decorated with birds, floral and Arabic script on a dark blue coloured base with orange, red and green. The Jordanian economy relied on trade and crafts. New waves of people began to settle in Jordan for the purpose of trade and crafts. This object reflects the diverse population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It also demonstrates personal attire, fashion, local costumes and rites.

fd18c679-e2d9-58bf-b89d-424355f03bbd.name: Dar Bach-Hamba
fd18c679-e2d9-58bf-b89d-424355f03bbd.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
fd18c679-e2d9-58bf-b89d-424355f03bbd.history: The Bach Hamba family, a noble military family of Turkish origins, gave their name to their home which stood here until 1923. Dar Bach Hamba is therefore a reminder of Tunisia in the first decades of the 20th century. It became the home of the Bach Hamba brothers, Mohamed and 'Ali, who had been co-founders of a part of the Young Tunisians (al-Harakat al-Shabab al-Tunisi) and of the first Tunisian French-language newspaper, *Le Tunisien*. After having served as the headquarters of the Sœurs Franciscaines du Christ Roi, Dar Bach Hamba became, in the year 2000, the seat of a Mediterranean cultural centre - the Fondazione Orestiadi - whose headquarters are in Sicily. The current building also houses a museum with an impressive collection of ceramics, textiles and clothes, which are all evidence for the links between the various Mediterranean cultures.
fd18c679-e2d9-58bf-b89d-424355f03bbd.keywords: Architecture; art; painting; stucco; mosaic; marble; ceramics
fd18c679-e2d9-58bf-b89d-424355f03bbd.description2: Behind a beautiful arched door, marking the entrance to Dar Bach Hamba, lies a vestibule leading to a central patio. Today's *dar* has kept only its huge proportions, ground floor and first floor galleries and symmetrical distribution of doors and windows on the surrounding apartments. The paving, door and window frames, neo-classical columns, and central fountain in the great hall are all made from marble imported from Carrara. The wooden ceilings in the bedrooms are painted in an Italian style. A smaller courtyard on the first floor is covered by a glass roof. The bedrooms generally open out onto balconies, with magnificent wooden coffered ceilings decorated with a rich floral pattern.

fd62bb2a-82f4-581c-9414-fac77a74a469.name: Coffee pot
fd62bb2a-82f4-581c-9414-fac77a74a469.keywords: Arts and Crafts; Daily utilitarian ware; Portugal; Vista Alegre; Factory
fd62bb2a-82f4-581c-9414-fac77a74a469.description2: This coffee pot is part of a set ordered by the King Fernando of Saxe Coburg, husband of queen Maria II. The lid bears the king’s monogram “F”, positioned underneath the crown. This set was painted by Gustave Fortier, master of panting in the Factory between 1852 and 1857 and again between 1861 and 1869. He introduces a lyrical and romantic style, manifest in the painting of flowers, in the introduction of delicate patterns and pale shades, tendencies which will define the factory’s decoration during his stay.

fd93bf8a-d085-595a-a14f-c616a5d43a58.name: Gülabdan (rose water bottle)
fd93bf8a-d085-595a-a14f-c616a5d43a58.description2: It is known that there were workshops producing glass vessels around Beykoz in Istanbul in the 19th century. The first glass workshop was founded by Mevlevi Dervish Mehmed Dede during the reign of Selim III (1789-1807). There were European glass craftsmen working in those workshops as well. Cups, bottles, jugs etc. made of colourful, colourless and opal glass were among Beykoz' productions. This Beykoz-produced *gülabdan* (a small flask for sprinkling rose water) is made of green glass, in the shape of an ewer. There are cut floral decoration on the body. There are yellow, brown, blue, green and pink flower motifs.

fdf4838a-7764-5f27-afc8-32377c84dfbc.name: *The interior of Mustapha Pacha's palace*
fdf4838a-7764-5f27-afc8-32377c84dfbc.author: Dalila Orfali
fdf4838a-7764-5f27-afc8-32377c84dfbc.description2: In the early 19th century this palace, located in the Algiers kasbah, housed the collections of the first library museum. It was also the home of one of the regency's most famous deys, Mustapha Pacha, who ordered many of the old town's monuments to be built during his reign. One example of these is the great palace of Menzel el-Mahalla in east Algiers, which was later partly destroyed, with the rest being used as a hospital for the French expeditionary corps. The dey was assassinated in 1805.

fe6cec92-b619-55f4-a18b-3a0f8fd470af.name: Palais-Musée du Bardo
fe6cec92-b619-55f4-a18b-3a0f8fd470af.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
fe6cec92-b619-55f4-a18b-3a0f8fd470af.history: The museum occupies just a part of the entire Palais du Bardo, a collection of buildings constructed from the early 15th century onwards. It was built in the style of Andalusian princely residences, but also shows traces of North African Tunisian and Italian architectural influences dating to the Husainid period when it underwent a series of modifications. The museum was opened and received its first archaeological collections on 7 May 1888 by the Bey of Tunisia and the French Resident-General. It remains, to this day, one of the most important archaeological museums in the world, and is particularly renowned for its excellent collection of Roman mosaics.
fe6cec92-b619-55f4-a18b-3a0f8fd470af.keywords: Architecture; art; painting; stucco; mosaic; marble; ceramics
fe6cec92-b619-55f4-a18b-3a0f8fd470af.description2: The Musée du Bardo receives more than 500,000 visitors each year. It is divided into three floors, each holding thousands of exceptionally valuable items, all of which tell the story of a country at the crossroads of multiple civilisations. Visitors can admire mosaics on the floors and walls, the statues, funerary steles, ceramics, jewellery, works of art and bronze and marble sculptures, ranging from the prehistoric era to Punic, Roman and Byzantine times.

fe898d65-6a28-56fc-93fb-7e1ee70f830f.name: *A landscape of Bazaar from Istanbul*
fe898d65-6a28-56fc-93fb-7e1ee70f830f.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
fe898d65-6a28-56fc-93fb-7e1ee70f830f.description2: At the beginning of the 19th century, romantic painters who appreciated eastern mysticism brought newly discovered eastern landscapes with their paintings which contained fiery colours and interesting landscapes. One of those painters coming to Istanbul from Malta and affected by eastern mysticism was Amadeo Preziosi. He usually painted scenes from daily life, such as shops between streets, coffeehouses, baths, peddlers passing the street, a woman filling water from a fountain and figures from different ethnic groups. Like many of his contemporaries, Preziosi had been lured to the exotic city of Istanbul. He also tried to reflect the cultural diversity of the city in his paintings. Especially in his watercolour paintings he loved expressing the blue water of the Bosporus with its caïques, pavilions, palaces, boats, mansions, residences, bazaars and cemeteries.

feb4b0a1-063e-5d7c-b120-acf74338a57d.name: Glass bowl
feb4b0a1-063e-5d7c-b120-acf74338a57d.keywords: Orientalism; blue; coloured glass; floral decoration; revival
feb4b0a1-063e-5d7c-b120-acf74338a57d.description2: Glass produced in Bohemia in a European form but with a strong Middle Eastern influence. Acquired by Franks.
